1k7b1jt.title: Энтузиасты запустили проект Leonida для нативного переноса консольной GTA 6 на ПК
1k7b1jt.content:
На платформе GitHub появился открытый проект Leonida, авторы которого пытаются перенести консольную версию Grand Theft Auto VI для Xbox Series на Windows методом статической рекомпиляции. Инициативу возглавил разработчик под ником ItsNotRexed, ранее получивший известность благодаря проекту Hookshot для нативного запуска ремейка The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time с Nintendo Switch 2 на ПК.
В отличие от классических эмуляторов, Leonida использует сходство процессорных архитектур. Поскольку консоли Xbox Series работают на базе x86-64, авторы инструмента планируют исполнять игровой код нативно, подменяя системные библиотеки и прослойки консоли аналогами под Windows. Для графики разработчики реализовали конвейер извлечения и перевода прекомпилированных шейдеров RDNA2 в формат SPIR-V для Vulkan через дизассемблер LLVM. По данным репозитория, инструмент уже успешно обработал и проверил все 26 503 шейдера из версии 1.0.2.1, включая 2 236 вершинных, 12 101 пиксельный, 2 689 вычислительных, 9 282 меш-шейдера и 195 геометрических программ.
Главным техническим нюансом остаются 21 545 шейдеров, рассчитанных на режим wave64. На видеокартах AMD с поддержкой 64-поточных подгрупп они работают точно, тогда как владельцам ускорителей NVIDIA и Intel с 32-поточными подгруппами требуется специальная эмуляция, при которой часть операций выполняется приблизительно. Помимо шейдеров, инструментарий уже умеет извлекать 3D-модели в OBJ, текстуры в DDS с пропуском отдельных сжатых записей BCPack, а также звуковые банки AWC и 1 589 записей конфигурации радиостанций. Сам репозиторий не содержит игровых файлов или ключей шифрования, а для локальной сборки из собственной копии версии 1.0.2.1 пользователям потребуется около 350 ГБ свободного места на диске.
Несмотря на громкий ажиотаж в сети, на данном этапе игра не запускается. Слой трансляции вызовов Xbox D3D12 в Vulkan и загрузчик PE находятся на начальной стадии без поддержки рендер-пайплайнов и вывода изображения, а главное препятствие заключается в отсутствии у команды основного исполняемого файла игры.
Проект находится на ранней стадии, и игра пока не запускается. Все, что можно сделать без исполняемого файла, уже готово, поэтому работа над запуском начнется сразу, как только он окажется в руках разработчиков.- ItsNotRexed, создатель проекта Leonida

1fi166u.title: Рютте: НАТО захищатиме «кожен сантиметр» території Польщі
1fi166u.content:
Альянс захищатиме «кожен сантиметр території Польщі», зазначив генеральний секретар НАТО Марк Рютте. Його слова пролунали наступного дня після повідомлень Варшави про порушення російськими об’єктами польського повітряного простору.«Я можу гарантувати, що НАТО захищатиме кожен сантиметр території Польщі», – сказав Рютте у Варшаві.За його словами, командувач об’єднаних сил НАТО в Європі генерал Алексус Гринкевич «зробить усе необхідне, щоб виявити будь-які загрози обороноздатності та можливостям стримування Альянсу». За потреби він внесе відповідні корективи.

Росія завдала чергового масованого удару по Україні вночі і вранці 20 листопада. Зокрема, Повітряні сили фіксували пуски ракет по західних областях. У Львівській, Закарпатській та Івано-Франківській областях запровадили аварійні відключення світла. Польща заявила про порушення свого повітряного простору трьома об’єктами з боку Росії. За попередніми оцінками, йшлося про дві ракети та безпілотник.Порушення сталося на тлі військових навчань у Польщі за участю країн «Коаліції охочих», які підтримують Україну. Польські посадовці заявили, що збіг у часі не був випадковим.У понеділок, 23 листопада, у Брюсселі відбудеться засідання Північноатлантичної ради НАТО, на якому обговорять порушення польського повітряного простору російськими ракетами.Міністр оборони Польщі Владислав Косіняк-Камиш заявив, що країна отримає від союзників по НАТО суттєву підтримку для посилення захисту східного кордону.

1mb4kto.title: Пророссийские хакеры запустили кампанию против журналистов
1mb4kto.content:
Пророссийские хакеры запустили новую фишинговую кампанию в отношении журналистов и политиков. Об этом в субботу, 21 ноября, сообщила газета Le Monde, а ранее - расследователь Христо Грозев.

Атаке подвергся его собственный аккаунт в мессенджере Signal, а также немецкого журналиста и одного из авторов "Панамского досье" Бастиана Обермайера (Bastian Obermayer), трех сотрудников Le Monde и французского депутата Эрика Ботореля.

По словам Грозева, в его случае фишинговое сообщение пришло в Signal, якобы от одного из его контактов. Это был немецкий журналист, с которым он не общался уже несколько лет. Как уточнил Грозев, был выбран один из его контактов, но настолько отдаленный, что можно было поверить, будто у него появился новый номер в Signal.

Журналисты Le Monde получили приглашения на видеоконференцию о войне в Украине

Журналисты Le Monde получили в Signal приглашения на видеоконференцию о войне в Украине - якобы от знакомого европейского журналиста. Депутату Боторелю со взломанного Signal-аккаунта знакомого предложили вступить в группу в Telegram.

Источники Le Monde в европейских службах безопасности отнесли атаки к деятельности хакерской группы UNC5792, известной также как Frontier Blizzard и Sentry Bear. Христо Грозев написал, что речь идет о "новой фишинговой кампании от наших друзей Fancy/Cozy/GummyBear".

Ранее телеканалы CNN и NBC News сообщили, что хакеры могли взломать Национальный центр криминальной информации (NCIC) - центральную базу данных Федерального бюро расследований США (ФБР), через которую федеральные, региональные и местные органы власти обмениваются информацией об ордерах на арест, судимостях и проверках биографических данных.

rpza7s.title: Public-access television is born anew in NIGHT EYE TV, a digital goggle box filled with art game curios
rpza7s.content:
Channel hop aboard

Image credit: NIGHT EYE TV

I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own shows through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.

NIGHTEYE.TV is a strange little place. I call it a place, it's a fake TV floating in a Unity default texture void, lending it a Backroomsian vibe, but even if there's not much there to ground yourself in, the goggle box is enticing all the same. It beckons you to turn it on, a series of buttons all linking to different "channels." What awaits you isn't television, however. Instead you'll find games, mostly of the weirdo, freako, sicko variety, quickly setting the tone.

🌕NIGHT EYE TV’s initial form is live!🌑

Check out the site and follow our Indiegogo campaign at www.nighteye.tv![image or embed]— NIGHT EYE TV (@nighteye-tv.bsky.social) October 14, 2026 at 2:05 AM
In its current incarnation, it's mostly just a collection of clips of these various art games, with direct links to them hidden away in a menu, but a good collection it is. You'll find Nathalie Lawhead's Everything is Going to Be OK, Jeremy Couillard's more recent Soul Injector Commando, and Taylor McCue's He Fucked The Girl Out Of Me. Some clips are longer than others, acting as sort of segments of playthroughs, but it all feels like an exciting evolution of what public-access television was.

The ultimate goal is for it to be a curated platform where you can buy a rotating selection of games. Most of the sale goes back to the original artist, and 15% gets put into a community pool to be split amongst all of the contributors, with the last 15% going towards keeping everything running. As it stands, that's not quite ready yet. You can help make it happen, though, as right now an Indiegogo campaign is running to help it all get fully operational. Worth chucking a few quid I reckon!

1h7i7n.title: How Movies Are Making Politics Personal in 2026
1h7i7n.content: For years, Simon Rich wanted to sound the alarm about AI.Rich’s childhood friend Dan Selsam worked as a researcher at OpenAI; Selsam showed Rich, a writer known for humorous essays and for the film “An American Pickle,” an early version of the software, and the two friends discussed its ramifications.“It seemed to have real contempt for mankind,” Rich says. “It scared the hell out of me.” Rich published a book, “which was completely ignored,” and found himself striking out in his attempts to get attention with magazine articles. “So, in desperation,” he recalls, “I was like, ‘Maybe if I got a movie star…’”He got Andrew Garfield. In “Artificial,” Garfield plays OpenAI CEO Sam Altman as a blithely destructive sociopath who manipulates his way into the center of a potentially civilization-ending technological advance. Rich uses the juicy character to tell a story about the most consequential political issue of the present moment.“I’ve been living with knowledge of this danger for at least five years, due to my fluke friendship with this scientist,” he says. (Selsam issued a public warning about AI’s increasingly uncontrollable behavior in September.) “I wrote this film out of a desperation to communicate to the world this information.”That desperation may be unique to Rich. But the desire to use the tools of screenwriting to illuminate political concerns is certainly not. Had “Artificial” simply been an enumeration of AI’s dangers, it’d likely have attracted as much attention as Rich’s book; instead, it’s a well-told story with a sharp argument at its core. That makes it one of several movies this year that use character and incident — the stuff of quality storytelling — to illuminate their writers’ very real political concerns.That goes for the year’s most-discussed blockbusters: Writer-director Christopher Nolan has imbued “The Odyssey” with a rueful sense of what it means to lose one’s humanity in wartime, while, if it’s anything like its two predecessor films, “Dune: Part Three,” written by Denis Villeneuve and Brian K. Vaughan, promises to examine the uses, and misuses, of power.But it’s showing up across more human-scale dramas this fall, as well. Take “I Play Rocky.” The film depicts the writing and production of “Rocky,” which — before it was an Oscar-winning smash — was the Hail Mary attempt of unknown actor Sylvester Stallone (played by Anthony Ippolito) to write himself a place in the industry. For screenwriter Peter Gamble, the story has resonances well beyond Hollywood history.“‘Rocky’ came out right after the Vietnam War, and it was a time when people needed to believe,” Gamble says. Stallone, in the film’s telling, is the ultimate underdog; Gamble, who himself yearned for a screenwriting breakout, could relate. The message of the film, the writer says, is intended in part for his children: “They’re like, ‘We’re all going to die from global warming. If not, AI is going to kill us next week.’ What power do I have in the universe at all? We need to believe in ourselves again.”American history provides many stories that feel akin to the charged atmosphere of recent years: One, as Gamble notes, is the demoralization of the Vietnam War, and another is the cataclysm of the Great Depression. “The Weight,” written by Matthew Booi and Shelby Gaines, is a rip-roaring adventure film in which unjustly imprisoned convict Samuel Murphy (Ethan Hawke) has the chance to win his freedom by transporting gold bricks across an unruly wilderness. The viewer roots for Murphy in part because he’s compellingly played by a movie star, and in part because the boot under which he struggles looks, at a moment of increased attention to mass incarceration and wealth inequality, familiar.“You don’t want it to be didactic and message-y or preachy in any way,” Gaines says. “But the idea was to try and tell a good story on a personal, individual level and hope that it would echo sympathetically with things that happen on a larger social level — both during the Great Depression and today.” Murphy’s journey depicts the stakes of its historical moment in frankly personal terms — his loss of freedom means the loss of access to his daughter, a crisis the film treats with gravity and righteous anger.“Abstraction doesn’t help you as a writer much,” Gaines says. “If you want to convey something, the heart is the place to start.”Or you can go for the gut. “Ink,” which James Graham adapted from his own stage play, makes the case that Rupert Murdoch (Guy Pearce) and newspaper editor Larry Lamb (Jack O’Connell) created the venal media world we live in today. The dawning realization that Lamb, especially, is a force for evil hits particularly hard because Graham has, in the film’s early going, taken pains to make him so charming and his exploits so rootable.“You need these people to surprise you,” Graham says, “so that you want to be in that newsroom — and suddenly, weirdly, for a brief moment, you might even want them to get one over on the establishment.” How did tabloid culture gain such purchase? Because, as the film’s characters make clear, we’re willing to pay for it.“Being Heumann” makes us root for its band of rebels, too — but, in this case, they’re working to bring about a better world. The biopic, written by Sian Heder and Rebekah Taussig, tells the story of Judith Heumann (Ruth Madeley), the activist who led the 1977 demonstration over the government’s failure to enforce disability-rights legislation. By its nature, the film is explicitly political, but its screenplay is also the product of a thoughtful, careful approach to representation and inclusivity.Taussig, who, like the late Heumann, uses a wheelchair, saw a certain power in learning about — and then writing about — the many activists Heumann helped organize. “What was so exciting about the research,” she says, “was this gold mine of learning about these absolutely compelling people.”The first-time screenwriter had grown up seeing “very little disability representation — and [when there was], it always felt so flat. There is a richness to the experience of disability that gets missed if you don’t live it and you can’t portray it.”Taussig’s ability to mine her own insights enriches the film, one that Heder, an Oscar-winner for “CODA,” intended to inspire and delight audiences, as well as educate them. “It’s very important to me that this story reach the widest audience possible,” Heder says, “because the events of the story actually were about a triumph. In a time where a lot of us are feeling really helpless, it was so important to express disabled joy and humor. I wanted to take the audience on a really entertaining ride, where they could leave seeing the world differently.”“Fjord” has a similar reframing effect — though its true-life basis is substantially more downbeat than Judith Heumann’s story. Cristian Mungiu took inspiration from the story of the Bodnariu family, an immigrant couple whose five children were taken away by the Norwegian state amid accusations of child abuse. “Fjord” presents the story of Mihai and Lisbet Gheorghiu (Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve) in a who-do-you-believe social drama, one with painful repercussions.“What I’m looking into, in the stories that I pick up,” Mungiu says, “is this possibility of speaking about something bigger than just that story.” For its writer-director, “Fjord” addresses the painful consequences of globalization, as people from different traditions find that they cannot in fact understand one another. “It’s not a reenactment” of the Bodnariu story, he says: “That’s the starting point of a story in which everything is structured to speak about the relationship between the majority and the individual.”“Fjord” won the top prize at this year’s Cannes; the runner-up, “Minotaur,” also places a family drama in counterpoint with a story of major import. Here, a story of marital infidelity (based on Claude Chabrol’s 1969 film “The Unfaithful Wife”) plays out in 2022 as Russia is scaling up its military actions against Ukraine.Writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev had been working to put the film together for years — and, as he wrote, the mobilization against Ukraine was all over the news. “It was a very logical thing,” he says through a translator. “I started to fill gaps in the script with the realities of what was happening.” Like Simon Rich trying to spread the word against AI, Zvyagintsev used his script to convey what he was hearing, like local mayors asking businesspeople to choose which of their employees will be conscripted. “This is not something I took from the air,” Zvyagintsev says. “This is real information that came by phone. People would be afraid to speak up about those situations.”For Zvyagintsev, this use of character to explore the world around him is what screenwriting is all about. “The whole ocean,” he says, “can be reflected in one ocean drop.”

16l2r7b.title: Toyota обвинили в продаже заведомо дефектных гибридных седанов
16l2r7b.content: Иск к Toyota подал житель штата Иллинойс. По его версии, японский производитель знал о неисправности гибридной системы в Camry Hybrid 2026 года, однако продажи не остановил. Об этом сообщает Autoblog.Свою машину мужчина купил в декабре 2025-го. Минуло всего несколько дней – и компания объявила отзывную кампанию, под которую попали свыше 55 тысяч автомобилей, включая Camry Hybrid и Corolla Cross Hybrid. Причина – гайка внутри гибридного инвертора, которую на заводе затянули недостаточно плотно.Чем это грозило на практике? Крепление со временем могло ослабнуть, машина теряла мощность, а в худшем случае не исключались замыкание и даже возгорание.Истец настаивает: о проблеме в Toyota знали еще с ноября 2025 года. Именно тогда поступил первый сигнал – про неисправный автомобиль, который не заводился. Дилеры же, по его словам, продолжали продавать потенциально дефектные машины. Сам он остался без колес на несколько месяцев: с конца февраля до августа 2026-го автомобиль простоял у дилера, пока компания готовила решение.Теперь Toyota добивается закрытия дела. Аргументы такие: покупателю бесплатно предоставили подменные автомобили на весь срок ремонта, да и сам ремонт выполнили без оплаты – значит, никакого ущерба не было. Мужчина с этим не согласен: машина, утверждает он, упала в цене, а права потребителя оказались нарушены.Toyota CamryО том, какие автомобили реже требуют серьезного ремонта, «За рулем» уже рассказывал.Понравилась публикация?Тогда добавьте «За рулем» в список интересных источников: 1. Откройте https://google.com... 2. Поставьте галочку напротив нашего изданияГотово – остаемся на связи! «За рулем» можно читать и в Телеграм

c91sp.title: После 13 лет попыток в GTA 5 игроки наконец смогли остановить поезд в GTA 6
c91sp.content:
На протяжении 13 лет игроки GTA 5 пытались остановить грузовой поезд, но безуспешно. В ход шли грузовики, десятки танков, НЛО и даже попытки затопить Лос-Сантос. Однако поезд продолжал двигаться, игнорируя любые препятствия. С выходом GTA 6 давняя загадка наконец получила ответ: в новой игре поезд можно не только остановить, но и пустить под откос.
Пользователь X под ником jax_caine опубликовал видео, на котором поезд в GTA 6 сходит с рельсов после бокового столкновения. Если дождаться следующего состава, он может столкнуться с уже сошедшим с путей поездом.
В GTA 6 железнодорожный транспорт стал гораздо динамичнее и теперь реагирует на происходящее вокруг. Если игрок стоит на путях, поезд затормозит перед ним. То же самое происходит, когда впереди оказывается другой состав. Даже обнаружив на рельсах тело, поезд останавливается и подаёт сигнал.
В GTA 5 всё работало иначе. Поезда фактически представляли собой неподвижные с точки зрения физики объекты, положение которых обновлялось по координатам. Они следовали заранее заданным маршрутам и не реагировали на физические взаимодействия с окружающим миром. Поэтому состав мог проехать сквозь сотню танков или продолжить движение даже при затоплении Лос-Сантоса.
В GTA 6 поезда, судя по всему, взаимодействуют с миром на тех же принципах, что и другие транспортные средства. Например, столкновение с самолётом может сбить состав с пути, а не заставить его продолжать движение без каких-либо последствий.
Пока неизвестно, как именно Rockstar реализовала новую систему, но возможность схода поездов с рельсов уже открывает игрокам гораздо больше вариантов взаимодействия с железной дорогой. Впрочем, автор TheGamer сомневается, что это остановит сообщество от дальнейших попыток найти ещё более необычные способы остановить состав.

zce0j4.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
zce0j4.content:
Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person. 

You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.

While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.

Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.

Ask Proxy

Image Credits:Ask Proxy

Ask Proxy’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website. 

It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party.

Unlike a typical chatbot, Ask Proxy also takes a proactive approach. It can reach out when it notices something you might forget or when it comes across a new activity, restaurant, or experience you might enjoy. 

There’s also a work-focused version, which the company explains “gets employees back to work faster, while keeping personal data off company systems.”

The personal version costs $1 per day. For businesses, pricing starts at $15 per employee per month for large companies and $23 per employee per month for small teams with fewer than 49 employees.

Ask Proxy works over SMS. You can text “start” to 820-732-2625. 

Caddy

Image Credits:Caddy

Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone users and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check.

For instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you. 

Caddy has been available in public beta since April 2026.

Comma

Image Credits:Comma

Comma is designed to manage tasks across both work and everyday life. Comma carries tasks through to completion, checking its own work and determining when a task is finished. 

Completed work is surfaced for review when a decision or approval is needed. It also proactively notifies users and recommends the next steps.

It can work across a user’s browser, computer, and files, while remaining accessible remotely through messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram, and WeChat. Comma maintains context and memory across devices and conversations, and can deliver daily briefings, flag urgent matters, and summarize recorded calls.

Comma is free to start and open source.

Fambot

Image Credits:Fambot

Fambot is an AI-powered “chief of staff” for families, designed to bring together the many moving parts of family life, including school communications, sports activities, meal planning, calendars, and other day-to-day responsibilities, and turn them into an organized plan.

The service is designed to work across both an app and text messages. Fambot is available on iOS devices, Android devices, and the web, and families can also interact with it directly over SMS. Every night, Fambot automatically sends a summary of the following day, including upcoming events, to-dos, and details such as school uniform or packing requirements. Parents can reply to those messages to ask questions, check information, or make changes to their calendar.

Fambot currently connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, and WhatsApp, with support for Apple Calendar planned for the future.

The company launched in beta in early September 2026 and has raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding. The service is currently free during the beta period, but Fambot expects to eventually charge roughly the equivalent of a Netflix subscription.

Folk

Image Credits:Folk

Folk is designed to be an AI assistant you can reach through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram. It can remember personal context, manage reminders, research topics, track flights, handle email, and perform real-world tasks such as restaurant reservations.

One distinction is that Folk runs on its own private cloud computer. It can also run code and execute multi-step tasks rather than merely responding conversationally. 

Folk launched its beta in May 2026, and it’s available for free but also offers a Pro subscription for $8.33/month if you want unlimited tasks running in the background.

Haven

Image Credits:Haven

Haven distinguishes itself by presenting the concept of a “digital twin” rather than merely serving as a text-based AI assistant. 

According to the company, Haven understands and adapts to your preferences, routines, and decision-making styles, creating a personalized memory graph based on your interactions. As the company describes, “A personal assistant knows what you asked it to do. Haven knows what you would do and how you would do it.”

Notably, the company envisions future features that customize your experiences across devices, like TV and car. 

Currently, Haven is available for free in beta on iPhone and Android devices, and the web. You can also reach Haven by calling or texting (435) 260-6500.

Instinct

Image Credits:Instinct

Instinct first made headlines after raising $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. In September 2026, it raised $1 billion, valuing it at $10 billion.

The always-available agent can take actions on your behalf, rather than simply answer questions. Users can communicate with Instinct by text or voice and connect it to the apps and services they already use, such as email, calendar, Google Workspace, and more. The company says early users have used Instinct for tasks ranging from planning trips and buying groceries to booking tickets and canceling subscriptions.

In September, Instinct began giving users dedicated email addresses for their assistants. The idea is to let Instinct create and manage accounts on a user’s behalf without filling the user’s personal inbox. The agent can use its address to sign up for services, contact businesses, follow up on requests, and handle tasks that require an email account. (However, this level of autonomy has also raised concerns about privacy and security.) It’s also begun rolling out support for placing calls.

The company remains in private beta.

Iris

Image Credits:Iris

Powered by Hermes Agent, Iris is designed to let users delegate tasks to an AI assistant directly through iMessage. Users can connect the apps they use and hand over a task with a simple message. The agent then works through the required steps, while retaining relevant context from previous interactions. It’s also designed to follow up with users proactively rather than waiting for another request.

Martin

Image Credits:Martin

Martin is a general-purpose personal assistant reachable through SMS as well as phone, WhatsApp, email, Slack, and its own iOS app.

It can help manage calendars, email, reminders, tasks, notes, and communications. It can also act on behalf of users by sending messages or making phone calls, while providing daily summaries of what needs attention.

It’s a bit on the pricier side, with subscriptions starting at $21 per month.

Maverick

Image Credits:Maverick

Maverick describes itself as an “AI companion who lives in your texts,” acting as a personal assistant that helps manage everyday tasks directly from your messages.

It can fix typos, cancel subscriptions, schedule meetings from voice notes, and help group chats settle on a date for an event. One notable feature is that Maverick asks for your permission before taking action.

The platform also offers hundreds of integrations, including Discord, Gmail, and Slack, allowing it to connect with the apps you already use.

It’s currently in beta and free to use on iMessage. There’s also a Pro version for €27 per month (or approximately $30.25 USD), which includes 500 tasks a month,  20 connected apps, scheduled tasks, and memory.

Miso

Image Credits:Miso

Miso takes the personal-assistant concept and applies it specifically to travel. 

It operates through iMessage and combines AI trip planning with support from a dedicated travel team. Users can arrange flights through messaging while Miso takes into account their travel preferences, loyalty points, and other priorities. Miso also gives travelers access to trip details and flight updates, along with personalized recommendations.

Ohai

Image Credits:Ohai

Ohai is another family assistant focused on helping households manage the constant stream of information and tasks involved in everyday family life.

Users can send messages, forward emails, or make voice requests, and the assistant can transform them into schedules, reminders, and plans. It can also coordinate calendars, household chores, and meals across multiple members of a family.

It includes a free basic option, but also offers different subscriptions based on family size, starting at $9.99 per month.

Orbits

Image Credits:Orbits

Orbits also has an AI assistant that is focused on the household.

It works through both the Orbits app and text messaging, and can bring together calendars, lists, and conversations while also carrying out tasks for you. That can include searching the web, making purchases, booking restaurants, changing appointments, and requesting quotes for household services.

Additionally, Orbits can remind family members about chores, communicate with service providers, and help coordinate responsibilities beyond the immediate household.

Orbits is backed by investors like Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Speedrun fund, N49P, and Garage Capital.

Pally

Image Credits:Pally

Users can interact with Pally as they would with a friend while giving it access to the apps they already rely on. The assistant can connect information spread across services such as WhatsApp, Gmail, calendars, and Google Drive, helping users keep track of plans, receipts, dates, files, and other details. 

There’s a free plan available. It works over iMessage, RCS, and Telegram.

Poke

Image Credits:Poke/The Interaction Company of California

Poke launched in March 2026 as a general-purpose assistant that you can reach through text messaging. It can handle tasks involving calendars, planning, health and fitness, smart-home controls, photos, and other everyday activities. 

Poke became particularly notable in June 2026 when Apple approved Poke as the first AI agent on the Apple Messages for Business platform. A month later, parent company The Interaction Company of California was acquired by AI coding startup Cognition in a deal valued in the low nine figures.

Rene

Image Credits:Rene

Rene is an AI personal assistant designed to be a user’s “best contact” rather than another productivity agent. It’s text-based and can turn natural-language conversations into tasks, reminders, summaries, and other follow-up actions. Rene also maintains context across conversations, allowing it to remember details and surface things that may need attention later.

Additionally, it has a browser, can write code, shop for you, as well as create slides and images.

Rene is currently available on iMessage, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

Skye

Image Credits:Skye

Instead of waiting for users to open an app, Skye is an “agentic homescreen” for the iPhone that analyzes information from connected services and surfaces what it thinks is relevant through contextual cards, suggestions, and daily briefings. The assistant can generate audio briefings, prepare information ahead of meetings, surface reminders, and identify potentially useful information. 

The company, Signull Labs, raised about $3.6 million in seed funding in 2025. It entered private testing and beta in April 2026, and hasn’t yet announced a public release date.

Stanley

Image Credits:Stanley

Stanley is an AI content assistant aimed at content creators rather than general personal productivity. Available through iMessage, Telegram, and the web, it acts as a kind of AI head of content, helping users come up with ideas, turn them into posts, and maintain a consistent publishing schedule.

For instance, Stanley can connect to a user’s Instagram account, using that context to suggest content based on what the user has actually been doing. Users can also send voice notes, which Stanley turns into scripts, captions, and other social assets. It includes a content calendar and can schedule posts, with the broader goal of making content creation a more continuous, automated process rather than something users have to sit down and plan from scratch.

Szn

Image Credits:Szn

Szn is designed to coordinate tasks and follow-ups through a single conversation thread. Users can send text messages, voice notes, photos, or forwarded emails, and the assistant takes action on their behalf, including making calls, sending emails, and managing follow-ups.

According to the company’s website, Szn has served more than 7,500 businesses across 16 countries, completed over 10,000 jobs, and handled 95 hours of calls.

Tab

Image Credits:Tab

Tab allows users to delegate everyday tasks through familiar messaging platforms. Users can send requests to the assistant via iMessage or WhatsApp, ranging from ordering groceries to finding birthday gifts, and Tab handles the process on their behalf.

The company emerged from stealth in early October with a valuation of $300 million. Its investors include SV Angel, Valar Ventures, and American Spirit.

Tomo

The biggest differentiator with Tomo’s personal assistant for iMessage is that, instead of being a private assistant that only you interact with, Tomo can become part of group conversations. 

Also, like other agents, it’s designed to help with goals, accountability, scheduling, and everyday organization. It also has the ability to send reminders, search the web, work with calendars and email, watch videos, and edit photos.

The basic plan starts at $19.99 per month.

Town

Image Credits:Town

Town is aimed more at professional life. It gives users a “Townie,” an AI assistant designed to learn how they work and handle recurring professional tasks. It can work with email, calendars, documents, Slack, and other platforms. 

In June 2026, the company raised a $55 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and Forerunner.

Underdog

Underdog is a privacy-focused AI assistant that launched an invite-only beta in early October 2026. Unlike cloud-based AI services, the model runs entirely on the user’s device, keeping personal data on hardware they already own. The initial release supports Mac and Windows computers, with Linux, iPhone, and Android versions planned for the future.

The company plans to offer the app for free initially and has stated that it will never include advertising.

Wajo

Image Credits:Wajo

Wajo’s first consumer agent, Fo, can call businesses, send emails, join group chats, make bookings and purchases, and coordinate with people to complete everyday tasks.

A key part of Wajo’s approach is giving Fo its own identity. The agent has its own email address, phone number, and payment card, allowing it to interact with businesses without requiring users to hand over their own credentials. 

Notably, when Fo encounters something it cannot handle on its own, Wajo says it can bring in a human assistant to finish the task.

Fo launched publicly in September 2026 with a free tier, while heavier workloads and custom agents are available through a paid Pro offering.

6tsg3z.title: GTA 6 Kingpin Bowling Alley safe code and location: How to find and open the safe
6tsg3z.content: Wondering how to open the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6? There are two methods to open it that I’ve explained in this guide. You can either find the code for the safe, or blow it up.While you can do one of these methods in Chapter 2 when you’re likely to encounter the bowling alley safe, the other way will require an item that is more rare. Below, I’ve explained where the bowling alley safe is, where the bowling alley safe code is, and much more.This is one of our dozens of GTA 6 guides which can be found in the GTA 6 walkthrough hub. They’re all spoiler free, so feel free to explore them at any point in your GTA 6 journey.Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.GTA 6 Kingpin Bowling Alley safe codeThe GTA 6 Bowling Alley Safe Code is 0300. You don’t have to find the code in the world before you’re able to enter it, so if you just want to enter it without finding it, it’s 0300. If you want to find the code in the wild, you can do so at Brooks Boatworks. You may remember this place from the Slam Dunk mission. It’s the large compound in Port Gellhorn on the north of the town. The code is in a building to the right of the main compound. There’s a ship with a cover over the top of it, and it’s next to the fence on the right of the area.Head up the stairs on the outside of the building, and blast the Kolts you find in there, the code is on wall in an office. But if you’re reading this guide, you already know the code at this point, so going back for it originally is just salt in the wound.GTA 6 Kingpin Bowling Alley safe plant explosiveTo Plant Explosive on the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe, you’re going to need sticky bombs. I first found them on a table in the bowling alley, behind where the pins are dispensed at the bottom of the lanes. I’m unclear if they always spawn here, but in GTA 6, it’s typical that the game will leave some sticky bombs near a safe.You can later buy sticky bombs from Ammunation once you reach chapter 3.That’s everything you need to know about opening the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe. Happy hunting!

jxcp0f.title: VW’s ID.Polo GTI Clubsport Concept Is a Track-Focused EV
jxcp0f.content: Volkswagen revealed a concept car that stuffs a larger, more powerful electric motor into a performance-focused version of the ID.Polo GTI.The two-door ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept makes 362 horsepower and wears an aggressive front splitter, diffuser, and rear wing.The one-off concept won’t reach production, but it’ll be displayed next week at the Essen Motor Show in Germany.The Volkswagen GTI badge has been a staple in automotive culture for 50 years, and it’s clearly not getting sidelined anytime soon. VW just released the ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept, an electric track-focused GTI that slots in as the automaker’s fourth new GTI variant this year.VolkswagenWhile it’s not heading to production, the Clubsport concept is a peek into the possibilities riding on the electric ID.Polo GTI, which became the first EV to wear the GTI badge when it was released earlier this year. The standard ID.Polo GTI, which isn’t sold in the United States, reaches 62 mph in 6.8 seconds thanks to a 223-hp electric motor mounted to the front axle.For Sale Near YouSee all results for near 60526The Clubsport concept ups the ante, with VW claiming it will hit 62 mph in just 4.7 seconds with the help of launch control and a more powerful APP550 electric motor. The upgraded motor, which is typically used to power the rear wheels of larger models like the ID.Tiguan and ID.7, sends 362 horsepower to the front wheels and nearly doubles the standard electric GTI’s torque output from 213 to 406 pound-feet.VolkswagenVolkswagen also equipped the concept vehicle with an electronically regulated front differential lock, a performance-tuned adaptive suspension system, and ceramic brakes with a one-box brake setup. The high-performance powertrain fits into an equally aggressive two-door build, complete with a large front splitter, diffuser, and a flared rear wing.Rather than the typical five-seater setup, the Clubsport concept houses two Recaro bucket seats with red five-point harnesses. A Tornado Red roll bar replaces the rear seats, and the cockpit is solely reserved for racing needs, meaning the standard infotainment system is also omitted. The cabin is finished in a dark microfiber material and trimmed with red stitching.VolkswagenVolkswagenVolkswagen calls this concept the “perfect match of heritage and future,” and the automaker says its young employees were involved in much of the concept’s realization. The ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept won’t ever make it to VW showrooms, but it’ll be displayed next week at the Essen Motor Show in Essen, Germany.➡️ Skip the lot. 1ln6uur.title: Darkest Dungeon 2's next bit of DLC is a short run, combat focused gauntlet where you must do everything in your power to please the audience
1ln6uur.content:
Don't butcher this

Image credit: Red Hook Studios

The original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some new DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel. No, in fact the next bit of DLC for Darkest Dungeon 2 was teased only a couple of weeks ago, with a new trailer shared today actually showing off what it's all about.

It's called The Butcher's Asylum, as pleasant a name as any other, and it's a "stand alone gladiatorial arena game mode," that's due for release sometime in 2027. "The long-silent bells of the remote Asylum ring once more - souring the valley below with discordant and unsettling vibrations," the DLC's Steam page describes. "Garish heraldry, hastily stitched by unskilled hands, festoons the hilltop. Deep within the crumbling masonry of the Asylum, frenzied inmates compete in merciless bloodsport with monsters corralled the kingdom over. And to the victors of these debauched contests, the Butcher’s favour: a cure for their madness."

Watch on YouTube

This DLC isn't veering too far away from its roguelite origins, as it is still run-based, just on the shorter side and focusing more on the combat system. On your runs you'll need to prepare for the fights ahead, come across "insane enemy combinations never before possible," and spin a fun wheel which nets you prizes like new battle modifiers, charms and jinxes. There's also a new crowd meter, "a unique feature to the Asylum, can grant powerful effects to your team if you cater to the Crowd's demands. Failing to do so will only earn their scorn which raises the stakes and puts your success in jeopardy!"

The Butcher's Asylum also introduces a new playable character, The Ringmaster. You pick her up by winning bouts in the arena, and then you can recruit her in any game mode. She also serves as the narrator for the DLC, likely because of the passing of the main game's narrator Wayne June; Red Hook made clear earlier this year that they would never use generative AI to recreate June's voice, so I'm glad to see they haven't backstracked here.

qwemem.title: Энтузиаст портировал ПК-версию "Шрек 2" 2004 года на Android
qwemem.content:
Разработчик под ником Player1444 выпустил неофициальный порт компьютерной версии "Шрек 2", созданной студией KnowWonder в 2004 году, для смартфонов и планшетов на базе Android. Проект получил название Shrek2-android_edition и уже обзавёлся свежей тестовой сборкой 0.1.0-27 на GitHub. Для запуска требуется устройство под управлением Android 7 или новее, а размер установочного APK составляет 56.2 МБ.
Мобильная версия построена на открытых исходниках экспериментального проекта shrekNX от энтузиаста Ananasiy, который изначально разрабатывался для Nintendo Switch и macOS на чипах Apple Silicon. Вместо привычной эмуляции вроде Winlator авторы применили статическую рекомпиляцию кода: оригинальные модули x86 переводятся в код на языке C и собираются напрямую под архитектуру ARM64. За работу системных вызовов Win32, графики Direct3D 8, звука и ввода отвечает специальная прослойка совместимости, транслирующая рендер через OpenGL ES 3.0. Автор мобильной версии Player1444 отдельно отметил заслуги создателя исходного проекта, подчеркнув, что без него Android-порта бы не было.
Если ранняя тестовая сборка поддерживала исключительно русскую версию игры, то в свежем обновлении 0.1.0-27 порт стал универсальным и научился работать как с английским оригиналом, так и с локализацией от издателя Новый Диск. Разработчик добавил настраиваемое сенсорное управление с иконками в стиле Шрека, а сам лаунчер автоматически подстраивает интерфейс под язык системы. Кроме того, игра получила поддержку плавных 60 FPS с переключением частоты обновления дисплея и полноэкранный режим без чёрных полос на вытянутых экранах с соотношением сторон 20:9 и 21:9. В редизайне окна О порте автору помог пользователь под ником base64E.
В базовом репозитории shrekNX мобильная версия по-прежнему числится как несобранная, тогда как билд для Nintendo Switch при разрешении 720p и частоте процессора 1020 МГц показывал в сцене на болоте около 38-38.8 FPS и страдал от фризов при появлении новых материалов. Энтузиасты уже тестируют свежую сборку на портативных консолях вроде Retroid Pocket, однако некоторые владельцы таких устройств столкнулись с некорректной работой правого стика на геймпаде. При этом сам код проекта распространяется по лицензии MIT и не включает защищённые авторским правом ресурсы Shrek 2, поэтому для самостоятельной сборки пользователям потребуется собственная копия игры на PC.
Примечательно, что компьютерная "Шрек 2" на движке Unreal Engine 2 представляет собой совершенно самостоятельную игру, заметно отличающуюся от консольного экшена тех же лет от студии Luxoflux, который позже перенесли на компьютеры с подзаголовком Shrek 2: Team Action. Недавно компания Aspyr выпустила официальное переиздание DreamWorks Shrek 2 Remastered для PC и современных консолей, основанное именно на консольной версии Luxoflux. Однако этот ремастер получил прохладный приём в Steam, собрав около 47% положительных отзывов на старте из-за технических недоработок и вылетов, тогда как ностальгический платформер KnowWonder до сих пор не имеет официального переиздания.

ogh4sj.title: ‘Percy Jackson’: How A Quest To Save Annabeth Makes Everyone Reevaluate Their Relationships In Season 3
ogh4sj.content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains some details from the first two episodes of Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3.

If there is one thing that the kids of Camp Half-Blood can count on, it’s that their lives are only going to get more complicated.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians returned to Disney+ for Season 3 on Friday, and already the dynamics have shifted. The first episode opens with Percy (Walker Scobell) and Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries) recruiting the recently revived child of Zeus, Thalia (Tamara Smart), to help them rescue two younger demigods — Nico and Bianca di Angelo, the children of Hades — and the tension is palpable.

“I think that Annabeth’s presence is actually incredibly divisive between the two of them,” Smart tells Deadline of the dynamic between Thalia and Percy.

In terms of sowing that division on screen, she adds that “a lot of it is based in our actual relationship in the best of ways.”

“Walker also has the exact same personality and sense of humor. So, right right off the bat, we were definitely going back and forth and joking, and I think the only thing we had to do was just up the stakes and be serious about it, which was actually more difficult than we planned,” she says.

Percy and Thalia can’t agree on almost anything, except their loyalty to Annabeth, who has unwittingly been thrown in the middle of their power struggle at the start of the season.

So, when Annabeth is captured and brought to an enemy stronghold where she’s forced to bear the weight of the sky (the eponymous Titan’s Curse), those two have to set aside their differences quite quickly.

“She kind of kept them at a safe distance away from each other, because, as I guess we’ve seen the trailer, bad things happen when they’re not at that safe distance,” Scobell says. “So I think without her there, they’re forced to actually work together and try to figure each other out and attempt to understand each other.”

Adds Smart: “They actually have to be forced into proximity to work together to get her back, because that’s their mutual interest. So, it’s really beautiful in a way that her absence brings them closer, which is a very human thing for us. I think as people, we’re just always brought closer by tragedy. But I think that for them specifically, a lot of ego has to get out the door for them to work together to achieve their mutual goal.”

Rather than put a wedge in Annabeth’s relationship with either, Jeffries thinks that the tension between Percy and Thalia also provides some clarity for the daughter of Athena. Whether she’s ready to face that realization yet is another story.

“I honestly feel like you get to see more Percabeth when it’s between Percy and Thalia,” Jeffries says. “I feel like her eyes open up a little bit. Annabeth is very smart. Even though she’s making it look like she’s not noticing, she knows [she’s developing feelings for Percy]. I don’t know if that’s more of like a denial between her of like, ‘No, no, I’m working right now. I’m on missions. I don’t have time to be falling in love…’

She continues: “You get to see the fight [in her] more, not physically, but just like ‘No, I love this person. You’re not gonna take him away from me.'”

fzpjj1.title: GTA 6 Brooks Boatworks safe code and location: How to find and open the safe
fzpjj1.content: Looking for the Brooks Boatworks safe code in GTA 6? The illegal operation has a hidden safe you can find to collect extra cash. However, finding the safe and discovering its combination can take a little exploration.Fortunately, you don’t need to spend too long searching. This Brooks Boatworks safe code guide will explain where to find the code, what the code is, and what rewards you can expect.This is one of our dozens of GTA 6 guides that you’ll find in our GTA 6 Guide Hub. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.What is the GTA 6 Brooks Boatworks safe code?The Brooks Boatworks safe code in GTA 6 is 6823.You’ll need to enter this code into the safe’s keypad to unlock it and collect what’s inside.You can enter the code straight away without finding the combination first. You can also blow the safe up by planting an explosive. You need sticky bombs to do this. You can purchase sticky bombs from the start of Chapter 3, but if you look around the Boatworks you can find them sitting around.Where to find the Brooks Boatworks safe in GTA 6Brooks Boatworks is an illegal operation associated with Kolt & Associates in Port Gellhorn.  You actually visit this area in the Slam Dunk mission. You may remember having to reverse out of there at 200 miles per hour.Once you get back the compound, you’ll need to deal with the gang members guarding the bottom floor of the building. The safe is in an office to the left of the building. There are drug pickups on pool table that you should also pick up. Keep in mind there are always multiple Kolts in this office, and when we robbed it, they had shotguns, so be careful.How to find the Brooks Boatworks safe codeIf you want to find the combination yourself, head to the eastern side of the Brooks Boatworks compound.Look for a  building with an external staircase. Climb up the stairs and follow the path around the building until you reach the office. There are Kolts here, so expect a proper fight. Here you’ll find three safe codes, one for the Brooks Boatworks safe, another for the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe and finally the La Cascara Motel safe.GTA 6 Brooks Boatworks safe rewardsThe reward for opening the GTA 6 Brooks Boatworks safe is cash.There are also other items worth collecting around the compound. These include a unique Clunker 556 assault rifle and a Smuggler Caracara 4×4. You can return at any time to collect the rest of the items. You can check the map to see what valuables you’re missing, via the small icons under the location name.

1kt8zkq.title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Feasting With $120M+ in Franchise’s Box Office Comeback
1kt8zkq.content:
Logo text

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has begun to ignite the box office.

Lionsgate released the sixth film in the dystopian franchise in 4,018 North American theaters, and it grossed $56 million on Friday, including Thursday previews, as it heads for more than $120 million for the weekend. This would give it the third-best debut Friday in franchise history, besting the two Mockingjay titles ($55.1 million for 2014’s Part 1, $45.6 million for 2015’s Part 2) and 2023’s The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ($19 million) but behind 2013’s Catching Fire ($70.9 million) and 2012’s The Hunger Games ($67.2 million). Sunrise earned an A- CinemaScore from audiences, putting it below the A grades of the Jennifer Lawrence-led initial 2012 movie that kicked off the series and 2013’s Catching Fire but matching the A- grades of the two Mockingjay films.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will notch the fifth-biggest opening in Lionsgate history, as it also stands at No. 5 among 2026 domestic openings for all studios. It represents the highest-grossing launch for the careers of stars Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning. This weekend’s haul also brings the Hunger Games franchise’s box office total to roughly $3.437 billion to make it the studio’s highest-grossing franchise ever, topping The Twilight Saga.

Lionsgate had projected The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to gross north of $80 million, but other sources expected that it would collect between $100 million and $130 million, which now looks to be the case. Adapting author Suzanne Collins’ prequel novel that was published last year, director Francis Lawrence‘s movie carries a production budget of roughly $150 million as it revitalizes the franchise in telling a story set 24 years before the events of Collins’ original 2008 book.

This opening represents a major comeback for the series after registering its lowest-performing entry with 2023 prequel The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, given that Sunrise on the Reaping is looking to open with more than double its launch. Starring Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer, Songbirds & Snakes — telling the backstory for the villainous President Snow, played by Ralph Fiennes in the new movie — disappointed, opening to $44 million domestically for the weekend before ending its run with $166.4 million domestically and a global sum of $361.8 million. It earned a B+ CinemaScore, the lowest for the franchise.

Joseph Zada and Whitney Peak in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Murray Close /Lionsgate / Courtesy Everett Collection

Sunrise on the Reaping holds a 67 percent critical score on Rotten Tomatoes, lagging behind the franchise’s first four movies but besting the 64 percent approval for Songbirds & Snakes. The new film has a franchise-best 95 audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter, chief film critic David Rooney wrote that it “delivers on emotion and brutal spectacle.”

The movie opened the day after the launch of the hotly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto 6, which does not appear to be preventing the film from thriving. Joseph Zada stars as Haymitch Abernathy, providing the backstory for the character whom Woody Harrelson brought to life in the first four movies. The cast for Sunrise on the Reaping also includes Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak and Maya Hawke.

Among other weekend titles, Amazon MGM Studios expanded I Play Rocky to 2,477 North American locations after two frames in limited release. Peter Farrelly’s Rocky origin story earned $3.8 million on Friday, including Thursday previews, as it heads for an estimated $9.3 million. Starring Anthony Ippolito as a young Sylvester Stallone, I Play Rocky landed a rare A+ CinemaScore, becoming only the second release this year to do so (after April’s A Great Awakening).

I Play Rocky holds an 89 percent approval rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes and a 98 percent audience score. Rooney’s review described it as a “big-hearted movie about moviemaking, if not an artful one.”

Anthony Ippolito and Stephan James in I Play Rocky.

Claire Folger/Amazon Content Services

In its sophomore frame, Paramount’s horror-tinged holiday offering Ebenezer is likely to claim third place with roughly $8.2 million for a decline of around 57 percent, bringing its domestic cume to $33 million. Johnny Depp marks his studio comeback vehicle with director Ti West’s reimagining of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, which opened atop last weekend’s box office.

Continuing to draw families in its third weekend is Warner Bros.’ The Cat in the Hat, as the animated adaptation of Dr. Seuss’ classic children’s book is expected to gross around $7 million for a domestic total of $47.2 million. This marks a respectable decline of roughly 38 percent for directors Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni’s movie that features the voice of Bill Hader in the lead role. It is set to face fresh competition in the animated space from Disney’s Hexed over the forthcoming Thanksgiving frame.

Gkids and Toho’s Godzilla Minus Zero is likely to close out the top five with $2.9 million in its third weekend to reach a domestic cume of around $54.7 million.

Focus Features opened Elsinore in six theaters in New York and Los Angeles, with director Simon Stone’s Oscar hopeful likely to collect approximately $240,000 to average $40,000 per screen. Andrew Scott stars in the biographical film about Scottish actor Ian Charleson, who navigates personal challenges while preparing for a pivotal performance of Hamlet. After earning acclaim at Telluride and TIFF, Elsinore holds an 87 percent rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes, with Rooney deeming it “a hymn to the theater, powered by a towering lead turn.”

Andrew Scott in Elsinore.

Anthony Dickenson/Focus Features

Toward the bottom of the top 10 is Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, with Sony Pictures distributing the Prime Focus Studios religious epic that is expected to gross $2 million for its third weekend to bring its domestic take to $28.3 million through Sunday. Director Nitesh Tiwari’s project becomes the highest-grossing Indian film ever at the North American box office.

With Thanksgiving arriving next weekend, the holiday frame brings an array of new options, including Disney’s Hexed, Universal’s Meet the Parents sequel Focker-in-Law, Netflix’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth and Angel’s biographical Hershey.

6rzlt0.title: Lindsay Hubbard Teases ‘Summer House’ Spinoff ‘In the City’ Season 2: “Better Than Season One”
6rzlt0.content:
Logo text

Amid filming season two of Bravo‘s In the City, being a mom and her charitable efforts, Lindsay Hubbard is having a busy fall.

Hubbard’s latest venture is partnering with No Kid Hungry’s Amplify Impact campaign ahead of Thanksgiving. The reality star served free breakfast sandwiches to New Yorkers at Give Back Bodega alongside season 21 Top Chef winner Danny Garcia at a pop-up event in Manhattan earlier this week. The campaign aims to help 10 million more kids access meals by 2032.

“One in five kids faces hunger every day in the United States, and as a kid, they should just be kids. They should be playing and having a good time, and they shouldn’t have to think about where their next meal is coming from,” she told The Hollywood Reporter.

The cause has taken on an even greater significance for Hubbard as a mother. Her daughter, Gemma Britt Kufe, turns two next month, and she explained how motherhood has changed her perspective on childhood hunger.

“When I’m with Gemma, I have no nannies. I’m single mom-ing it hard,” she said. “I am spending my days feeding her, caring for her, making sure she’s eating. That’s the one thing that I’m always constantly thinking about. Even me growing up, I didn’t have to worry about where my next meal is coming from, so of course my perspective changes because it’s sad that we live in a world where one in five kids doesn’t have meals.”

Lindsay Hubbard with Top Chef season 21 winner Danny Garcia on Nov. 18 in New York City.

Courtesy of Give Back Bodega

Hubbard’s transition into motherhood has also been documented on Bravo’s Summer House and its spinoff, In the City, which was recently renewed for a second season.

While she remained tight-lipped about the upcoming season because the show is currently in production, she teased that fans will be satisfied with what’s to come.

“We’re in the middle of filming it right now, and let me tell you, it’s got all of the elements of a great season two, better than season one,” Hubbard said.

Page Six reported in October that the sophomore season will feature a cast shake-up. According to the outlet, new castmembers include Brittany Whitfield, Robert Morrison, Reagan Baker, Natasha Parker and Barthelemy Jallet. Meanwhile, season one stars Amanda Batula, Danielle Olivera and her partner, Eoin Heavey, as well as Andrea Denver and his wife, Lexi Sundin, will not be returning.

Batula’s departure comes amid a particularly eventful period for the Summer House cast. She also exited ahead of season 11 of the original series amid the controversy surrounding her relationship with co-star West Wilson, who previously dated her close friend and fellow castmember Ciara Miller. Batula and her husband, OG Summer House star Kyle Cooke, had separated before the reports surfaced. Cooke was also close friends with Wilson. In alleged Instagram DMs, Batula cited intense online “hate” and “bullying” over her relationship with Wilson as her reason for not returning. Bravo has yet to officially announce the cast for In the City season two and did not respond to THR’s request for comment.

Meanwhile, Hubbard herself has made headlines amid filming for the upcoming season. Earlier this month, Page Six reported that Cooke made out with Hubbard over Halloween weekend while filming a cast trip in Cancun, Mexico. The pair have been friends for more than a decade, and Cooke is also best friends with Carl Radke, Hubbard’s ex-fiancé and another OG Summer House castmember.

Hubbard addressed the speculation with a laugh, telling THR, “No, Kyle’s like a brother to me. We just have a lot of fun, you know.”

From left: Carl Radke, Hubbard and Kyle Cooke at Bravo Fan Fest in Charleston, South Carolina, on Oct. 24, 2026.

Jessica Yurinko/Bravo via Getty Images

With Summer House season 11 and In the City season two on the horizon, Hubbard isn’t expecting to step away from reality television anytime soon.

“I’ll do it as long as they’ll have me on all these shows. I live a really big, full life that rarely ever stops. Things happen, and I have a lot to share at all times,” she said. “So until that stops, then maybe the TV portion would stop for me, but I don’t see that stopping anytime soon.”

Also forthcoming is Hubbard’s memoir, Activated, which will be released May 18. Despite spending a decade on television, she said she still has plenty of stories she hasn’t shared with audiences.

“I don’t need to rehash things that you can go back and rewatch,” she said of what readers can expect from the book. “So it’s all the stories that happen in life. I turned 40 this year, so you haven’t seen the first 30 years of my life. This is childhood, high school, college, my early PR days in New York, me living in L.A., me coming back to New York.”

Hubbard added that she’s “actually really nervous” about readers discovering some of those previously untold stories.

“I have been giggling and crying. It’s a lot of vulnerability,” she said. “I’m actually really nervous to open up some of these stories that people have never heard before, and it’s also the wildest moments of my entire life. There’s no holding back.”

eyb1jr.title: Геймеры уничтожают GTA VI — игра получила 5,6 балла от пользователей на Metacritic
eyb1jr.content:
Несмотря на восторженные отзывы критиков,  Grand Theft Auto VI столкнулась с волной негативных оценок от геймеров. На Metacritic рейтинг составил всего 5,6 балла из 10. При этом журналисты выставили проекту Rockstar среднюю оценку 99 из 100.На момент публикации материала пользователи оставили более 60 тысяч оценок, из которых 44 % оказались отрицательными. Ранее рейтинг GTA VI даже опускался в красную зону, но затем немного восстановился.Причины недовольства у игроков разные. Некоторые критикуют ограничение частоты кадров до 30 fps на консолях, другие недовольны тем, что значительная часть сюжета посвящена отношениям Джейсона и Лусии, а не криминальным приключениям, которыми славились предыдущие части серии.

Есть только два стула.
Отдельные пользователи считают, что Rockstar слишком увлеклась реализмом. По их мнению, гипердетализированный мир и новые механики сделали игру медленной и скучной, а некоторые ограничения лишили её привычной свободы. Один из авторов отрицательной рецензии даже назвал GTA VI симулятором повседневной жизни, который не позволяет отвлечься от реальности.Другие жалуются на сюжет, диалоги, технические проблемы и обилие сексуального контента. Встречаются и отзывы с обвинениями в «воукнутости» проекта и продвижении повестки DEI. Некоторые пользователи считают, что подобные решения испортили сценарий и ограничили свободу игрока.Напомним, оценки на Metacritic может выставлять любой пользователь — играть в оцениваемый проект площадка не требует. Так что любые идеологически заряженные группы людей могут прийти и снизить рейтинг игре, какой бы качественной она ни была на самом деле.Оценивать качество Grand Theft Auto VI можно на Xbox Series и PlayStation 5 с текстовым переводом на русский язык.

l1907a.title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
l1907a.content:
For the most part, the content offered by the microdrama startup Shortical is indistinguishable from the rest of its industry. The company produces soapy, melodramatic storylines — almost always risqué romances — that, in bite-sized two-minute episodes, compel viewers to stay glued to their phones so as not to miss the latest twist in a tawdry, cliff-hanger-happy saga.

The primary way that Shortical — which was founded last January — makes money is through subscriptions. Typically, the first 7-10 episodes of a micro-drama are free. After that, if the user wants to finish the series, they have to pay a small monthly fee which unlocks access to all of the site’s content.

Over the past year, the company has churned out a gush of popular live-action romances like “Crossing the Line with My Neighbor,” “Accidentally Married My Boss,” and “Spoiled by My Billionaire Sugar Daddy.”

Lately, however, the company’s homepage is covered in AI-generated content. The reason isn’t exactly hard to figure out: the production overhead for AI content is substantially less than live-action. The profit potential, meanwhile, is substantially higher, if you can draw an audience.

Its latest microdrama premiered in Los Angeles last week. The series, called “Inevitable,” stars Aki Avni, an Israeli film and television star who has been visible in American TV shows for years (he had a stint on Fox’s 9/11-era thriller “24” years ago) but is now trying something largely unheard of in modern Hollywood: licensing his face to Shortical for the sake of its AI content.

The project, which is wholly AI, used Avni’s face to create a digital avatar of him. In “Inevitable,” he plays himself – in a very meta plot in which he — the actor Aki Avni — licenses his face to a film studio, after which thriller-like antics ensue.

This is Shortical’s first foray into such a licensing deal, but it likely won’t be their last.

In a phone interview, Avni told TechCrunch that he found the project both nerveracking and exciting. “Look, it’s a new era for artists,” the actor said. “AI is a new kind of art. It’s a new format. It’s always great to be the pioneer in something.”

Guy Shimoni, the CEO of Shortical, emphasized the creative potential of the new tool. “One of the things that AI does is it enables smaller teams to be able to produce these movie-scale productions,” Shimoni said. “When we were doing mobile-first live action, we were limited by budget, but now we can serve them with epic fantasies. We have kingdoms and dragons. We have superheroes. We have werewolves.”

But AI-generated romances involving werewolves — who, exactly, is watching this kind of thing?

Apparently, a lot of people. While China boasts the biggest microdrama audience globally, Shimoni says that most of his platform’s viewers are actually in the U.S. The industry’s viewer demographic skews heavily female. Many viewers may watch them to wind down at night, getting minor dopamine hits as they drift off to sleep. Many of the AI-generated programs that already exist on the company’s website appear to have millions of views.

Now, Shortical is betting on the creation of a new generation of creators — those who, like Avni, are willing to surrender their likenesses for compensation. “LICENSE YOUR FACE” Shortical’s website advertises, explaining that interested parties can submit their social media handles to the company, which will then decide whether to offer them “a contract setting out the terms” of using their persona in the company’s AI-generated content.

A company rep told TechCrunch that this “offering is still in its early days and hasn’t yet resulted in any signed contracts.” They added: “The series with Aki is the first time Shortical has used a real person’s likeness, and it was done through a direct agreement with him rather than through the platform. Shortical hopes the series will draw more attention to face licensing and plans to promote the offering more actively following this launch.”

Much of this trend has already taken hold in China where the microdrama industry originated, where AI-generated content is big, and where face-licensing is already a trend. Although the trend may not be a particularly profitable one for creators. A recent report in Rest of World found that Microdrama firms were paying people “between US$15 to US$700 to license their facial likenesses.”

How much money is Shortical offering for its face-licensing deals? The company isn’t saying. As for if Shortical will offer royalty-based compensation for creators — like the residual system in television, “It’s a case by case [basis],” Shimoni answers vaguely.

A Shortical representative further explained to TechCrunch that the company didn’t want to “share a specific figure” for Avni’s particular contract. However, the person said, he came “on as a partner in the project, and his compensation was in line with industry standards for a comparable non-AI acting role.”

For other actors, however, the deals may be quite different. Plus, many creatives are understandably unsettled by signs of automation creeping into their industry. Until recently, microdramas seemed like a safe, entry-level gateway into the entertainment industry, where young actors could gain experience on sets and hone their craft. Now, companies are downsizing and producing content that doesn’t even require real actors.

Jennifer Cooper, a longtime fan of the industry and founder of the consultancy firm Vertical Drama Love, notes that there’s a lot of distrust of AI — both from audiences and within the microdrama industry itself.

“Everyone’s been impacted by AI,” she said. “A lot of us have either lost work to AI or can see that it’s devastated this industry — [taking microdramas] from something that was a rare thing in the world, that was in growth, and providing work, particularly for young people…[and now] you know, it’s been decimated.”

Questions of consent with AI likenesses have also dogged the industry (some creators claim they have had their likenesses stolen), which is something that Shortical is obviously trying to address with its new face-licensing endeavor.

Yet these licensing deals could also help to gig-ify the industry, creating a scenario in which creators pay a distributor for the chance to platform their content (or their face), then receive payouts based on the audience engagement they’re allowed to generate. Shortical recently partnered with a company called Payouts.com, which describes itself as a “payout infrastructure platform powering creator and gig economy disbursements at scale.” The plan is to create a system by which creatives can seamlessly interact with Shortical’s platform and get paid.

Cooper believes the push towards AI in the industry is driven by broader financial trends. Most of the microdrama business is led by startups, and VCs love to hear a growth game plan involving automation. “For anyone to get investment at the moment in microdramas, they’ve got to mention the word AI,” she says. “It’s like AI equals gold in everyone’s eyes.”

Despite all the investment in this space, Cooper seems skeptical that there is actually a huge audience for this kind of content. “Some of it does get views. A lot of it doesn’t,” she said, of the AI content. “I think it’s being pushed on an audience more than there is an audience demand or wish for it.”

16wof9n.title: Психологический хоррор Baptiste про жуткую куклу перенесли на 25 марта 2027 года
16wof9n.content:
Трейлер с анонсом новой даты релиза Baptiste.
Студии Digital Dreams и Firenut Games отложили выход психологического хоррора  Baptiste. Вместо осени 2026 года игра появится на ПК и консолях 25 марта 2027-го.Сюжет Baptiste рассказывает о Саре и её сыне Томе, которые пытаются оставить семейную трагедию позади и начать новую жизнь в уединённом доме на британском побережье. Однако вместо долгожданного спокойствия их ждёт кошмар. В пыльном шкафу они находят жуткую куклу по имени Батист. Рядом с ней лежит предупреждение: «Никогда не выпускай его из его стеклянной темницы».Игроки возьмут на себя роль Тома, который тяжело переживает смерть отца. Переезд должен помочь ему и матери справиться с потерей, но происходящее в новом доме постепенно подрывает его рассудок. Чтобы разобраться в происходящем, герой будет исследовать мрачный особняк, искать подсказки и раскрывать его кровавые секреты.Авторы обещают густую атмосферу и повествование через окружение. Записки и загадочные шёпоты помогут восстановить историю дома. Также заявлены выразительное звуковое сопровождение и необычная визуальная эстетика, в которой красота переплетается с гротеском и ужасом.Пытаться не сойти с ума в Baptiste позволят на ПК (Steam) Xbox Series, PlayStation 5 и Nintendo Switch 2. Заявлена текстовая русская локализация. На платформе Valve можно пощупать демоверсию проекта.
