⬇️ Install
The easy way, on Windows 10 or 11:

Download GT5-Installer.bat
and double-click it. If Windows warns about a downloaded file, choose Run (or More info, then
Run anyway).
In its window, pick two things and press Install:

your GT5 game: the folder of your disc dump (the one with PS3_GAME in it) or an .iso;
PS3UPDAT.PUP, Sony's free PS3 system software (the window has a button that opens Sony's page).

That's all, and it all happens in that one window: the steps, a progress bar, and what went wrong if
something does. Nothing is installed into Windows. It downloads this code and, into the install folder,
its own copies of Git (38 MB, only when the PC has none), Python (17 MB) and the compiler tools
(about 1.5 GB, into the install folder: no Visual Studio is installed or changed), unlocks your game's executable and the system software (with the port's own small tool; RPCS3 is fetched
only if that fails, as a tool:
the game itself runs natively as gt5.exe, not in an emulator), builds the game (about an hour the
first time) with both renderers (DirectX 12 and Vulkan), adds AMD FSR 3 frame generation and, on a PC with
an NVIDIA RTX card, NVIDIA DLSS, and puts Gran Turismo 5 (PC) on your desktop, which opens the
launcher. Nothing from the game is ever uploaded or shared. Some of what it downloads comes
under another company's licence (Microsoft's C++ libraries in the compiler tools, when it fetches those;
NVIDIA DLSS): the line by the Install button names them, with links, and pressing Install accepts them.
Rather do it by hand? See Setup. On Linux? See Linux.

🎛️ The launcher

Gran Turismo 5 (PC) on your desktop (or GT5Launcher.exe in your gt5-recomp folder) opens the
launcher: every setting in one window, then Play. No more editing play.bat.

Display: the renderer, resolution, anti-aliasing (NVIDIA DLSS, on an RTX card), shadows, frame
generation, borderless full screen (the default), a maximized window or a window size, screen shape
(ultrawide), the frame rate (60 or 30 fps) and asynchronous shader loading. The rows say
what the game's own menu says; a row that
means nothing with another setting's value is left out, as in the game (no Multiplier while frame
generation is off), and with Vulkan chosen the rows it can't do yet are greyed.
Controls: the controller's triggers (throttle and brake, or as on a PS3 pad), steering wheel on/off,
wheel rotation, force feedback strength and direction, pad in the background, mouse clipping,
mouse steering, keyboard keys.
Game: the cockpit view (field of view, seat position), the game's language (as far as
your disc has it), the volume and muting in the background, your mods from GT5\mods, the launcher's
own language (English or 中文).

The game's own settings menu (F1 in the game, or Select + Start held on a controller) has the same
settings and writes the same file; the launcher reads it again when the game ends.

Updates: shows your version and the newest one with what's new, and Update now does the
whole update for you in its own window (your newest Photo Mode pictures behind it, a car on the
progress bar, Details for the full text) and opens the launcher again.
Help: Save logs for a report puts one report file (GT5-report-<date>.zip) on the desktop,
plus the logs folder, the problem form, this FAQ and Clear the shader cache (also
ClearShaders.bat in the install folder; see the FAQ).
After a crash or a freeze the line at the bottom says so, with Save a report (the same file,
shown in Explorer) and Open the report page (the problem form with your version and PC filled in:
drag the file into it). The report holds the parts of the logs that matter, your settings and your
PC's parts; your Windows user name, PC name and every folder outside the game's are taken out, and
there's no save data or game file in it. Nothing is sent by itself.

It's built on your PC from launcher/GT5Launcher.cs with the C# compiler that
comes with Windows, every time the game is built, so it updates with the game; its picture is the logo
from your own disc. Settings are saved in GT5\settings.bat, which play.bat reads, so play.bat
still works and starts the game the same way. (GT5Launcher.exe --play starts the game straight away.)

🔄 Updating
Every change to the port comes out as a numbered version (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, ...) on the
Releases page, with what changed. To hear
about new ones, click Watch at the top of this page, then Custom and tick Releases.
The easy way

The launcher checks for a new version when it opens: its Updates page shows what's new, and
Update now does everything below in an update window and opens the launcher again. If the update
stops, the window shows why and keeps the full text in GT5\logs\update.log for a report.
Or double-click Update.bat in your gt5-recomp folder.

Both run update.ps1, so everything below applies. (No launcher or Update.bat yet? Your next update
brings them: run the command below once.)
Are you out of date?
Close the game, open PowerShell in your gt5-recomp folder and run:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -List

It lists every version and marks the one you have (<- installed) and the newest ([newest]).
If they're different, you're out of date.
Update to the newest version
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1

That one command does everything:

It downloads the new version.
It swaps the old ps3recomp patch for the new one.
It re-generates the game code only if that version needs it (about 10 minutes).
It rebuilds only what changed.

Kept as they are:

your saves (GT5\gamedata), a game update's data (GT5\hdd0) and game files (GT5\input, GT5\vfs, GT5\dev_flash);
the shader cache;
edits you made to files such as play.bat.

The previous gt5.exe is kept as GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe. If one of your edits clashes with a
change in the new version, the new version's file is used and your edit is saved in backups\ so
you can copy it back.
If you're several versions behind, run the same command. It goes straight to the newest version;
there's no need to step through the ones in between.
Installed before update.ps1 existed?
If your folder has no update.ps1 (you set up before v0.1.0), get it first, then update:
git pull
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1

If git pull says your local changes would be overwritten (usually play.bat), run git stash,
then git pull, then git stash pop, then the update. Your first update re-generates the game code
once (about 10 minutes), because older installs have no record of what their code was made from.
Downloaded the ZIP instead of cloning?
A ZIP download can't update itself. Clone the repository fresh as in Setup, step 1. Then
move these folders over from your old copy and run update.ps1:

your game files: GT5\input, GT5\vfs, GT5\dev_flash;
your saves: GT5\gamedata (and GT5\hdd0, if you set up a game update).

Go back to an older version
If a new version gives you trouble, switch back to the one that worked (see -List for the names):
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Version v0.1.0

To play the previous build right away instead, copy GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe over
GT5\build\gt5.exe (the last update kept it). Please also
report what went wrong.

Test builds
Changes still being tried out go to a test build first: the test branch of this repository, with
no version number and no release. Releases, new installs and the launcher's Update never use it. To try it:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Test

A plain update (update.ps1, Update.bat or the launcher's Update now) goes back to the newest
release. What the current test build changes is at the top of
its CHANGELOG (the entries above
the newest "Released as" line), and each new one is announced in
Announcements and in
the Discord's releases channel. Expect rough edges, and say "test build" and its date when you report
something.
Other options

Command
What it does

update.ps1 -Test
The test build: changes still being tried out. A plain update goes back.

update.ps1 -Dev
The newest changes, before they're released.

update.ps1 -NoBuild
Switch versions without building; build later with GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5.

update.ps1 -Force
Re-generate and rebuild everything, even when nothing changed.

🎮 Controls
A DualSense, DualShock 4 or XInput pad works, and so does the keyboard, with a pad connected or without one.
On a pad the buttons are the game's own, as on a PS3 pad: ✕ / A accelerates, □ / X brakes, R2 / L2
shift (change them in the game's own options). The in-game menu's Controls page has Triggers:
Throttle and brake makes the right trigger the throttle and the left the brake while you drive, both
by how far you pull them, with the bumpers shifting up and down, the left stick press looking back and
the right one working the lights; the face buttons still accelerate and brake fully, and it follows the
buttons you set in the game's own options. At the menus, in replays and in the in-game menu the pad is
always laid out as a PS3 pad. Every pad gets the same small round dead zone on its sticks.
The game's menus show PlayStation symbols. The Controls page has Button symbols: Xbox shows
A / B / X / Y, LB / RB, LT / RT in their place, Keyboard shows the keys you have bound, and
Automatic follows what you used last (checked on the European 1.00 release; a release whose
pictures differ keeps the game's own).
Keyboard: Z = Cross, X = Circle, A = Square, S = Triangle, arrow keys = D-pad, Enter = Start, Tab = Select.
An arrow-key tap moves one place in the menus, and in a race Left/Right steer as the D-pad does on a PS3
pad, eased in by the game (PS3_KEYS_ARROWS under Switches has the other ways).
Esc quits the game, after asking (set "PS3_ESC_CONFIRM=0" in play.bat quits at once).

Your own keys (new): the launcher's Controls page has a Keyboard keys list, one row per PS3
button, labelled with what that button does in GT5. Click a row and press the key you want (Esc
cancels); right-click a row to give it a second key, × to clear it, Reset to defaults to start
over. A key that's already used moves to the row you picked. Or put it in GT5\settings.bat (or
play.bat) yourself, button:key pairs split by commas:
set "PS3_KEYS=cross:W,square:Space,l2:Q,r2:E,circle:LAlt"
That one is W = accelerate, Space = brake, Q / E = shift down / up, Left Alt = handbrake. A bound
button takes only its new keys, and a key you bind stops doing its old job (above, W no longer works
the headlights and Z no longer accelerates). Two keys for one button: cross:W/Up; no key: l1:none.
With nothing set, the keys above are unchanged. On Linux the same line goes in GT5/settings.sh:
export PS3_KEYS="cross:W,square:Space,l2:Q,r2:E,circle:LAlt" (letters are where they are on a US
keyboard there).

Buttons: cross circle square triangle l1 r1 l2 r2 l3 r3 start select,
the D-pad up down left right, and the sticks pushed all the way: lstick_up lstick_down
lstick_left lstick_right rstick_up rstick_down rstick_left rstick_right.
Keys: A-Z, 0-9, F1-F24, Space Enter Tab Backspace CapsLock, LShift RShift
LCtrl RCtrl LAlt RAlt, Up Down Left Right, Insert Delete Home End PageUp
PageDown, the number pad Num0-Num9 NumPlus NumMinus NumMultiply NumDivide NumDecimal,
Comma Period Slash Semicolon Apostrophe LBracket RBracket Backslash Minus Equals
Grave IntlBackslash (the extra key next to Left Shift on European keyboards), and the mouse's side
buttons Mouse4 Mouse5. Any case. Esc stays the quit key. A name the game doesn't know is left out,
with a [keys] line in logs\play.err.
With Alt or F10 bound, the game window no longer opens its window menu (or beeps) on them; Alt+Tab and
Alt+F4 work as before.

What each button does is GT5's own setting (in the game: Options > Hardware > Change Button
Assignments). Its defaults, as the game shows them:

Button
GT5 does (default)
Default key

Cross
Accelerate (OK in the menus)
Z

Square
Brake
A

R2 / L2
Shift up / Shift down
2 / 1

Circle
Handbrake (Back in the menus)
X

Triangle
Reverse
S

L1
Rear view (look back)
Q

R1
Flash and toggle high/low beam
W

L3 / R3
Horn / Windscreen wipers
none

Select / Start
Change view / Pause
Tab / Enter

D-pad up
Ghost

D-pad left/right, left stick left/right
Steering
Left / Right

Right stick up / down
Accelerate / Brake
none

Left View, Right View, Flash Lights (on its own) and Toggle High/Low Beam have no pad button by
default: give one of the free buttons (D-pad down, the left stick's up/down, the right stick's
left/right) that action in GT5's Change Button Assignments, then bind a key to that button here. The
keys press the pad's buttons, so they follow whatever you set there. With mouse steering (below) GT5
still takes the pad's buttons, so the keys work the same.
A steering wheel works too, with force feedback (new; one real wheel tried so far): see the
FAQ.

Mouse steering (new, off unless you turn it on): tick Steer with the mouse on the launcher's
Controls page, or set "PS3_MOUSE_STEER=1" in play.bat. In races, move the mouse left and right to
steer: left button = throttle, right button = brake, middle button = straighten the wheel. The
keyboard and pads keep working alongside (Z still accelerates). While you steer, the cursor is hidden
and kept inside the window. At the menus and when paused the mouse doesn't steer: there left click = OK
(Cross), right click = back (Circle) and the mouse wheel moves the cursor up and down, and the keyboard
and pads work as before (set "PS3_MOUSE_MENU=0" leaves the mouse out of the menus). Alt+Tab frees the
mouse at any time. The game sees a steering wheel
(the same emulated G27 a real wheel uses, with its fine steering), so a real wheel isn't used while
mouse steering is on.

Setting (launcher, or play.bat)
Default
What it does

Mouse steering speed, PS3_MOUSE_STEER_SENS
100
Percent, 1 to 1000, decimals allowed (2.5); the launcher steps it by 0.5. At 100, mouse movement about the width of a 1080p screen (at Windows' default pointer speed) turns the wheel from straight ahead to full lock; 200 is twice as quick. GT5 turns sharply on little wheel, so small movements go a long way. Windows' pointer speed and acceleration don't change it.

Wheel straightens by itself, PS3_MOUSE_STEER_CENTER
off
Once you stop moving the mouse, the wheel goes back to straight ahead, at this percent of full lock a second (the launcher's Slowly / Medium / Quickly are 50 / 100 / 200). Off: it stays where you left it.

📋 Current state

Playable. Races run at 45 to 58 fps on the tested rig, and most of the game's modes work. The full
board (tested rig, what works, what's being worked on, known issues, recent changes) is in
STATUS.md; updates are also posted in
Announcements.
Everything done on the port since the first day, with dates, is in CHANGELOG.md.

🏁 Try it, then tell me how it went
If you own the game, please set it up and play. Every result helps decide what gets fixed next,
whether it runs great, half works, or doesn't build at all. Laptops, integrated graphics and AMD cards
especially: the port was tuned on one desktop with an NVIDIA card.

You want to...
Go here

Say how it went (takes two minutes, mostly quick picks)
Tried it: here's how it went

Report something broken
Something's broken

Ask for a change
Suggest a change

Post quick results, screenshots of it running, or ask for help
Discussions

Chat, get help live, share results
The Workshop Discord: #gt5-help, #gt5-test-reports, #gt5-chat (I'm mormonftp there)

❓ FAQ

Question
Short answer

Steering wheels?
🧪 New. First real wheel: a Genius Speed Wheel 3 Vibration (0458:3017, tested by brocolison, #29) attaches as an emulated G27; since 13 Nov it's found by itself and its one-axis pedals work as throttle and brake (a full race on v0.1.39). Logitech, Thrustmaster and Fanatec wheels are picked up by themselves but still untried: wheel owners wanted

Force feedback?
🧪 New, with wheel support, also untried on a real wheel

Widescreen (16:9)?
✅ Yes, GT5 is a 16:9 game

Ultrawide (21:9, 32:9)?
✅ New: a wider view, with the HUD kept 16:9 in the middle

Wider cockpit view, seat position?
✅ New: the launcher's Game > Cockpit view (more)

Which controllers?
✅ DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox pads, keyboard; new: keys of your choice, steering with the mouse

US copy (BCUS98114)?
✅ Yes, players have raced on it

Version 1.02, or a game update (2.xx)?
🧪 New: game updates run: 2.17 (the last) tested on the US and European releases, 2.01 on the Asian one, 2.11 with the Master Mod on the US one by a player (how to set one up); 1.02 untried

Settings without editing files?
✅ New: the launcher

Full screen?
✅ New: borderless full screen in the launcher (Alt+Enter is switched off since v0.1.17: it used to freeze the picture)

Vulkan instead of DirectX 12?
🧪 The launcher's Display > Renderer: built in, slower than DirectX 12 for now (more)

Higher than 1080p (4K)?
⚠️ The game's top mode is its 1080p one (races drawn at 1728x972), scaled up to your window; drawing above that isn't there yet

Japanese or Asian release (BCJS, BCAS)?
✅ Hong Kong / Asia (BCAS20108) runs, reported by a player, and its disc 01.00 and update 2.01 race in tests too; Japanese untried, please report

Slow PC or laptop?
🛠️ Laptops now use their dedicated graphics card. On most PCs the CPU sets the pace (the game's own threads), so the launcher's Speed: 30 fps rarely helps: it's for a graphics card at its limit. On a laptop: plug it in and set Windows' power mode to Best performance (and the maker's performance mode, e.g. in HP Command Center or Lenovo Vantage): a tester's i5-1135G7 ran into its power limit 88% of the time, which held its cores at 2.9 GHz instead of 4.2, while its graphics were only 30% busy. Speed-ups for 4-6 core CPUs are being worked on

Linux?
🧪 New and early: a native Linux build. First test (no graphics card) reached the race start; races on a real GPU untested

Steam Deck, Proton, Wine?
🟡 Steam Deck: the Linux build in a distrobox runs (menus ~25-30 fps, races ~8-10; Steam Deck). Proton and Wine not tried. Reports welcome

Android?
🛠️ Being worked on

Online?
❌ No

Is it legal?
✅ No game files here: you build it from your own disc

Ready-made download?
❌ No, but GT5-Installer.bat builds it for you

Errors during setup?
🛠️ Use GT5-Installer.bat, or run setup.ps1 (see below)

Black screen, draws: 0?
🛠️ Fixed: update; if it's still black, GT.VOL may be missing or in pieces (see below)

Clear or refresh the shaders?
✅ New: launcher Help > Clear the shader cache, or double-click ClearShaders.bat (see below)

Q: Does it support steering wheels and force feedback?
A: Yes, new in v0.1.2, a

ph90lp.title: Sheila Mangubat Dies: ’90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days’ Star Was 35
ph90lp.content:
Sheila Mangubat, who appeared in TLC’s 90 Day Fiancé franchise, has died. She was 35.

David Dangerfield, whom Mangubat dated on 90 Day Fiance: Before the 90 Days, announced that she died on Saturday in the Philippines, according to her family.

“It breaks my heart to share the news from her family that Sheila passed away on Saturday in the Philippines,” Dangerfield wrote on Instagram. “I am devastated and still trying to process this loss. Please keep her son, her family, and me in your prayers. Thank you for all your love and support.”

In 2023, Sheila and David appeared on Season 6 of Before the 90 Days, having met through an online sign language group. They bonded over the fact that Sheila was hard of hearing and David is deaf, communicating primarily through ASL.

David followed Sheila to the Philippines, where she lived with her mother, her father and her son Jhonreil. The season ended with Sheila accepting David’s proposal.

e2alkb.title: Sunrise on the Reaping Box Office: Hunger Games Prequel Stun in Debut
e2alkb.content:
“Sunrise on the Reaping” caught fire at the domestic box office, collecting a sensational $120 million in its opening weekend while reinvigorating Lionsgate’s “Hunger Games” franchise.

Overseas, “Sunrise on the Reaping” generated $105 million from 84 territories for a towering launch of $225 million globally.

The dystopian prequel is one of just five movies this year to launch above $100 million in North America, joining the company of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” ($360 million), “Toy Story 5” ($159 million), “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” ($131 million) and “The Odyssey” ($123 million). All of those films eventually surpassed the $1 billion mark globally.

“‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ posting an impressive $100 million-plus [domestic] debut reinforces just how vital ‘The Hunger Games’ remains as a movie franchise,” says Paul Dergarabedian, Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends.

“Sunrise on the Reaping” coincided with another big release — albeit not at the movies. Rockstar’s video game “Grand Theft Auto VI” launched after years of anticipation, earning a staggering $3.79 billion on its first day. It’s expected to set a sales record for entertainment across any medium.

“Many have speculated as to whether the release of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ would hurt ‘The Hunger Games’ at the box office, and I think the marketplace has already spoken,” adds Dergarabedian. “There’s plenty of time to play ‘GTA VI’ and make it to a theater to see ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ this weekend.”

On top of pitched competition at home, initial ticket sales for “Sunrise on the Reaping” are notable because they’re not far off from the original saga. For reference, 2012’s “The Hunger Games” ignited to $152 million, followed by 2013’s “Catching Fire” ($158 million), 2014’s “Mockingjay Part 1” ($121 million) and 2015’s “Mockingjay Part 2” ($102 million). Nearly a decade after those movies, starring Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson, concluded their run, the studio revived the young-adult property with 2023’s “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” an origin story about Panem’s cruel leader, President Coriolanus Snow. That film, set during the 10th Hunger Games, bowed significantly below its predecessors with $44 million. However, the movie stuck around through the holidays and eventually climbed to $363 million globally, registering as a win against a (comparatively leaner) $100 million budget and justifying another prequel for the studio. “Sunrise on the Reaping,” which returns to Panem for the 50th Hunger Games, carries a larger price tag above $150 million, not including the many millions spent on worldwide marketing efforts.

That “Sunrise on the Reaping” managed to recapture the spark of the initial series is impressive as the sixth installment in any property. And the film earned a strong “A-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls, which bodes well for box office longevity. Analysts attribute the strong debut to several factors, including the franchise’s multi-generational appeal as well as the excitement for the return of fan-favorite characters. This chapter, based on the novel by Suzanne Collins, has a stronger connection to the original saga; the story follows a young Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada takes on the role originally played by Woody Harrelson) — who eventually mentors Katniss (Lawrence) and Peeta (Hutcherson) in their Hunger Games, a Battle Royale for teens. Francis Lawrence returned to direct, having helmed all but the first chapter in the YA-centric franchise.

“The last ‘Hunger Games’ stumbled when the story went back 64 years without Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson,” says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “This is a strong return.”

“Sunrise on the Reaping” is Lionsgate’s second major theatrical victory in 2026 following “Michael,” which captured a huge $97 million in its debut and became the first biopic ever to cross the $1 billion mark. With this weekend’s haul, the “Hunger Games” series has collectively generated $3.43 billion in global ticket sales, making it the studio’s highest-grossing franchise ever—above “The Twilight Saga” ($3.3 billion worldwide across five films).

“This success is a testament to their remarkable film, the performances of our incredibly talented cast, and ultimately, the love of ‘Hunger Games’ fans worldwide, who embraced a film that told a story they had been asking to see for many years,” said Adam Fogelson, chairman of the Lionsgate Motion Picture Group.

Second place went to “I Play Rocky,” which earned $9.3 million while expanding nationwide to 2,477 theaters. The Amazon MGM movie, which depicts the real-life story of Sylvester Stallone bringing the 1976 classic “Rocky” to the big screen, has generated $10.4 million after two weekends in limited release. Audiences, roughly half of whom were over 45 years old, awarded the feel-good film a rare “A+” grade on CinemaScore. “I Play Rocky,” which hopes to find itself in the Oscar race, cost about $30 million to produce.

Last weekend’s champ “Ebenezer” dropped to third place with $7.7 million from 3,545 venues, a steep 60% decline from its opening. Paramount’s PG-13 take on “A Christmas Carol,” starring Johnny Depp in his first major Hollywood role in eight years, has generated $32.5 million in North America and $78 million globally. It’s not quite a resounding embrace of Depp amid the actor’s return to studio fare. However, it’ll be decently positioned in its theatrical run against a modest $38 million budget. (Theater owners keep half of ticket sales.)

In limited release, the Focus Features drama “Elsinore” earned $240,000 from six locations in New York and Los Angeles, translating to $40,000 per theater. To compare, another awards hopeful, A24’s drama “Club Kid” had a $65,097 per-screen average from six venues, while “I Play Rocky” averaged $49,200 per location in its initial frame. “Elsinore” stars Andrew Scott as the Scottish actor Ian Charleson who secretly battles AIDS while playing “Hamlet” in London. Focus will continue to roll out the film through December.

“Sunrise on the Reaping” provided a nice jolt to the box office ahead of Thanksgiving. This Turkey Day might not cement any theatrical records, but the holiday should be busy for theater owners. “Hunger Games” will continue to draw crowds alongside new offerings like Universal’s comedy “Focker in Law,” with Ariana Grande joining Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro, Disney’s animated “Hexed” and Netflix’s Imax release of “The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”

“This is a very good weekend,” Gross says. “The weekend before Thanksgiving sets up 10 very strong days. Moviegoing is back on track.”

gh-1453786236.title: GitHub - luisbraganca/ps2n: Converts PlayStation 2 games into native applications by ahead-of-time static recompilation, with PCSX2's core as the console.
gh-1453786236.content:
PlayStation 2 games as native applications, by static recompilation.

luisbraganca.github.io/ps2n
·
Releases

PS2Native (ps2n) converts a PlayStation 2 game into a native application.
The game's code is translated to C++ ahead of time and compiled on your own
computer, by the compiler PS2Native brings, into a folder that plays the
game. The console around that code (graphics, sound, storage, timing) is the
core of PCSX2: the translated code takes the place of
PCSX2's recompilers for the console's two processors and its two vector
units.
You provide your own game and your own BIOS dump. Neither is included here,
and nothing generated from them is.
Download
PS2Native 0.2, a pre-release, published on 2026-11-22:
the release, with its notes.

File
Runs on

Windows
PS2Native-0.2-windows-x64.zip
Windows 10 (version 1803 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit

Linux
PS2Native-0.2-linux-x64.tar.xz
64-bit Linux with glibc 2.35 or later (Ubuntu 22.04, Linux Mint 21 and later)

Nothing to install: unpack it and start PS2Native. Its wizard takes five
steps: the game's disc image, in any format PCSX2 plays; the BIOS; the
settings, which are PCSX2's own pages for the game; the recompile, a few
minutes; and the game's folder, which plays the game from then on. A game
made with 0.1 is brought up to date from the wizard's first step ("Games made
earlier...").
It needs a processor with SSE4.1, a graphics driver with Vulkan (or another
renderer chosen in the game's settings), and about 1 GB of disk for each game
on Windows, 1.5 GB on Linux: each game's folder has its own copy of the
compiler.
Status
A preview. It has been tried with five games, the European releases of
Killzone, 007: Agent Under Fire, Gran Turismo 3: A-Spec, Jak and Daxter: The
Precursor Legacy and Silent Hill 3. Every other game is untried and may not
work.

Windows x64. Everything measured was measured there, on Windows 11. On
the maintainer's own sessions played back, a compiled game takes 0.98 to
1.00 times the time stock PCSX2 takes with its recompilers (Killzone 0.92,
with counts of a session that is nearly the one timed). That is against
stock PCSX2 with the console's second vector unit (VU1) on the main
processor thread, as PS2Native runs it. PCSX2 itself gives VU1 a thread of
its own by default, on a computer with three cores or more, and so set it
takes 2% to 40% less time on those sessions: a compiled game then takes
1.02 to 1.65 times its time. Carrying VU1 out on a thread of its own is
PS2Native's next step.
Linux x64. Built and tested only inside WSL 2 (Ubuntu 22.04) so far,
every test passing there, and games made and played there. One game was
timed, Jak and Daxter: as 0.2 has it, 1.05 times stock PCSX2's time, and
about 2.2 times the time of stock PCSX2 with its VU thread on. Most of what
it takes more there than on Windows was PCSX2 waking a thread PS2Native
does not use, which the next release leaves out (0.75 and 1.59 then).
Nothing is known to work on a Linux machine of its own yet.
What a compiled game is held to. A run on PS2Native is compared with
the same run on stock PCSX2 at every point where the two can be compared,
and with recordings made on a console: 534 tests.
No recompiler for PS2 code is in a game's folder. Code a session meets
for the first time (some games load theirs from their data) runs
interpreted, slower, with a notice over the picture, and is compiled when
you close the game.

What was done and measured, step by step: the proof of concept
(docs/poc-log.md), the first games
(docs/game-log.md, docs/phase3-report.md)
and the application (docs/app-log.md).
Building it
PS2Native builds inside PCSX2's own CMake project, with PCSX2 v2.9.170 as a
submodule that is never edited (git submodule update --init --depth 1).
What PS2Native changes of PCSX2's code is in patches/pcsx2,
applied to copies of the files concerned when it is built.

Windows: Visual Studio or its Build Tools with clang-cl, CMake and
Ninja, and PCSX2's Windows dependency package in deps\windows-x64
(docs/poc-log.md says where it comes from).
scripts\windows\build.ps1 builds, and scripts\windows\test.ps1 -Bios <BIOS image> runs the tests.
Linux: CMake 3.25 or later, Ninja, and clang and lld (LLVM 22.1.3 in
deps/llvm-22.1.3-linux is taken when it is there). scripts/linux/build.sh
builds, PCSX2's dependencies with PCSX2's own script the first time, and
PS2N_BIOS=<BIOS image> scripts/linux/test.sh runs the tests.

The tests that boot the console need a BIOS image of your own, and are
skipped without one. Each script's header says what its options do.
scripts\windows\kit.ps1 and scripts/linux/kit.sh put together the folder
a release is made from.
Documentation

Document
What it holds

docs/brief.md
The project's goals and rules

docs/phase1-feasibility.md
The feasibility assessment and the architecture

docs/execution-model.md
How compiled code, the interpreter and the PCSX2 core run a program together

docs/poc-log.md
The proof of concept: what was done and measured

docs/game-log.md, docs/phase3-report.md
The first games, and the report on them

docs/phase4-proposal.md, docs/app-log.md
The application: its design, and what was done and measured

docs/adr/
The decisions, one file each

assets/branding/README.md
The logo files, the colours and how to use them

docs/site/README.md
The website: which files in docs/ are its own, and where its numbers come from

License
PS2Native is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3
or later (LICENSE). It builds on PCSX2 (GPL-3.0 or later,
Copyright PCSX2 Dev Team), which is included as PCSX2 released it, as a
submodule under third_party/pcsx2. PS2Native's own changes to PCSX2's code
are the patches in patches/pcsx2, each saying what it
changes and why; 0.2 and 0.1 have none. Each download's licences folder has
the licence of everything in it, and where the source of each is.
PS2Native is an independent project. It is not affiliated with the PCSX2
project or with Sony Interactive Entertainment.

gh-1433661775.title: GitHub - cheviman/robotech-decomp: Robotech: Battlecry (Xbox, 2002) statically recompiled into C and ported natively to PC with Direct3D 11, without emulation. Bring your own copy: no game data included. Not affiliated with Harmony Gold or TDK Mediactive.
gh-1433661775.content:
Robotech: Battlecry — native port
A native port of Vicious Cycle's 2002 Xbox game Robotech: Battlecry — not an emulator. The original
Xbox executable is statically recompiled into C with xboxrecomp
and linked against a runtime that stands in for the Xbox kernel, its GPU, its sound and its controllers.
Where it is going:

Windows, Xbox Series, Linux and Mac. Direct3D 11 first, for Windows and Xbox Series; Vulkan after,
for Linux and Mac.
The game brought up to date: higher resolutions, widescreen, frame rate, and DLSS.
New to it: multiplayer and mods.

This repository contains no game data and none of the game's machine code. The recompiled C the game
runs on is generated on your machine from your own copy of the game, which the build reads and never
changes; nothing generated from it is committed. What the repository holds of the game is the C written by
hand as it is decompiled (src/game/) and the names of symbols/symbols.txt.
Status

XBE analysis: title TM-002 (NTSC, linked 2002-08-05), XDK 4721 (XAPILIB, XBOXKRNL, LIBCMT, D3D8 not
LTCG, DSOUND), Bink 1; 115 kernel imports, all of them covered by the runtime
The whole executable recompiled into C: 6,590 functions, 5,203 of them the game and its engine
(Vicious Cycle's own, vc* engine classes and gc* game classes, no RTTI), the rest the XDK's D3D8,
DirectSound and peripheral libraries and Bink
Native build with MSVC (x64)
The XDK library code named: XbSymbolDatabase finds the entry points (all 77 Direct3D ones the game
calls, DirectSound, XAPI; symbols/xdk_symbols.json), and matching the XBE against the XDK's own
.lib files names the rest that did not change from 4721 to 5849 (symbols/lib_matches.json,
with the libraries' variables); the engine's 35 object classes and their callbacks come from the
descriptors the game registers (symbols/classes.json); the game's own object system (families
of types, handles, messages and state machines) and 239 of its 370 object types, named from their
own strings or from what makes them, their functions in bulk (symbols/registries.json and the
type lines); with the engine named as it is decompiled, 2,239 functions with a real name, and
2,951 more named from their decompiled C by two models, one drafting and one reviewing (tools/naming)
Boots: creates its Direct3D device and plays the legal screen and the TDK, Harmony Gold and
Vicious Cycle logo movies, whole frames, through xboxrecomp's pushbuffer executor (slowly: the GPU
is drawn in software)
The logo movies through Direct3D 11 (ROBOTECH_D3D11=1): the device, Clear, Swap, textures and
DrawVerticesUP routed, at the movies' speed
The menu and the first mission through Direct3D 11: render states, vertex and index buffers, the
engine's own 2D draws, vertex programs (on the CPU by default, on the GPU with
ROBOTECH_VP_GPU=1); sound, the pad and the keyboard,
saves on the hard disk (PENDING.md has
what is wrong and what is missing)
The first of the engine decompiled into C (src/game/engine/): the object system (27 functions
and the classes' default callbacks), the files, the formatted strings, the rectangles, the random
numbers, the screen (the Direct3D device, the viewport, clearing and showing it), the text
(fonts, measuring and laying out strings), the render state setters, 19 classes'
registrations and the scene objects' tree, 134 functions, every name real; the menu, the first mission and a save as the recompiled ones played them, frame for frame
The structured decompiler: arcade-decomp's (SegaSonic's), with an x86 frontend of this project's
(tools/x86); 4,374 of the game's functions in its C (src/decompiled/), with no goto, in the
recompiled ones' place, calling the ones still recompiled and through a pointer as the
recompiled code does, their
x87 floating point as C doubles rounded as the x87 rounds them, a float handed back a double
returned; the nine scenarios frame for frame as before
Every byte of the XBE classified (tools/coverage.py, analysis/coverage.txt): code, data whose
layout is known, data the code reaches, fill, unknown. Of the game's own (its and the engine's code,
and the data its code reaches in .rdata and .data), 1,237,883 bytes of code with none unknown;
130,634 of data described, 827,995 reached but not yet typed, 38,093 of fill and 3,855 unknown, all
of them in its data; tables of records in place by their fields in the decompiled C (Levels, the
pads with a field for each control, the object system's families and types, the screens' sprites,
the entity types' records of where their constants are and the constants, the weapons', the guns',
the heavy cannons', the turret cannons', the missiles' and the chunks' records and constants, the
veritechs' constants by model, mode and pack, the mechs' motions, the pad's items a mission has off), the players and what 82 types get by name
(their models, nodes, scenes, materials and sounds) by name, a float with a name read and written
by it; 947 of the texts the code hands on by the words they say (tools/symbols.py texts);
the decompiled C reads or writes 8,692 places at a raw address; Ghidra, headless, as a
second reading of the whole program with the project's names and types (tools/ghidra)
(11-11-2026)
Native sound: the 29 DirectSound entries the game and its Bink call answered on the host
(src/dsound_bridge.c, with the XDK's own behaviour), the Xbox ADPCM decoded and mixed to 48 kHz
stereo (src/sound_mixer.c) and played through xboxrecomp's audio output (XAudio2); the 3D is a
distance and a pan, and the reverb is not heard yet
The original game as the reference: the scenarios played in xemu on the port's clock and pad, its
frames set against the port's; the menu, the first mission and a save the same on both, the flight
and the shots included, at a mean difference of 1.23 of 255 or less (1.5 fails), and the training,
its shadow drawn to a texture, at 3.2 (its dialogue waits for voice lines, which end on other
frames in xemu); the code that unlocks every mission typed with the pad, and a mission of each
chapter as close (Force of Arms in space, Ambush Hills, Rebel Revenge, Goodbye Graystone,
Besieged; their fog too)
The rest of Direct3D 8 routed to Direct3D 11 (docs/d3d.md maps how the game uses it): vertex
programs on the GPU by default, pixel shaders, render targets
Higher resolutions, widescreen, frame rate
Xbox Series (UWP, Direct3D 11)
Vulkan, for Linux and Mac
DLSS
Multiplayer
Mods
The game's code decompiled into readable C, and its formats (the VC2 resource containers of
levels, packs and textures, the Xbox ADPCM sound and music) as editable files

Getting started
Requirements: Python 3.10 or newer with capstone (pip install capstone), CMake 3.20 or newer, and
Visual Studio Build Tools (MSVC, x64).

The toolkit: clone xboxrecomp next to this repository (../xboxrecomp), as it is released; this
project uses it unchanged (built and run with v0.16.0, f0f8a46). What the game needs from it is
set up from here: src/main.c and src/recomp_manual.c.

Your game: the game's folder (default.xbe, dsstdfx.bin and Media/), from the Xbox disc or from
the Xbox 360 "Xbox Originals" package, at game/: a copy, or a link to where you keep it:
mklink /J game "D:\Games\Robotech Battlecry"

Recompile the XBE into C (src/recomp/gen/). The analysis goes to analysis/:
py -3 tools/pipeline.py

Build:
cmake -S . -B build -A x64
cmake --build build --config Release --parallel

Run, from the repository's root (where game\ is):
RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 RECOMP_VBLANK=paced RECOMP_FB_WINDOW=1 build/Release/robotech_battlecry.exe
RECOMP_PB_EXEC executes the game's GPU commands, RECOMP_VBLANK=paced gives it a 60 Hz vertical
blank and RECOMP_FB_WINDOW shows what it draws in a window. The runtime's other switches are in
xboxrecomp's documentation.
Or through the Direct3D 11 bridge, which is where the port is going (src/d3d11_bridge.c; not with
RECOMP_PB_EXEC). ROBOTECH_WINDOW_SCALE sizes its window, 2 by default:
ROBOTECH_D3D11=1 RECOMP_VBLANK=paced build/Release/robotech_battlecry.exe
ROBOTECH_VP_GPU=1 runs the game's vertex programs on the GPU instead of the CPU (PENDING.md has
what it was measured at).
The sound is the game's DirectSound answered on the host; RECOMP_AC97_READY=1 plays it through
xboxrecomp's emulated APU instead, and RECOMP_AUDIO_WAV=<file> records what is played.

symbols/xdk_symbols.json comes from scanning the XBE with
XbSymbolDatabase's command-line tool; to make it
again:
XbSymbolDatabaseCLI analysis\default.xbe -e > analysis\xbsymbols.txt
py -3 tools/xdk_symbols.py analysis/xbsymbols.txt

symbols/lib_matches.json comes from matching the XBE against the static libraries of an XDK (5849
here: d3d8.lib, dsound.lib, xapilib.lib, libcmt.lib, libcpmt.lib, xboxkrnl.lib, in one folder);
to make it again:
py -3 tools/match_libs.py --libs D:/xdk/lib

Changing the decompilation
The game's C is written by hand, a function at a time, into src/game/ by subject; each takes its
recompiled version's place. Everything else under src/recomp/gen/ is generated and never edited by
hand.

Names, descriptions, files, types: symbols/symbols.txt, the one place they live (its header says
how to read it); struct, field and var lines become symbols.h's accessors for the C written by
hand (vcClassDesc_create(p), vcClassByType(type)). A var whose type is a structure is records of
it in place (var Levels Level[76]), which the decompiled C reads by field (Level_chapter(Levels(level)));
an address of a place with a name goes by it where the C uses it as a value (ecx = Levels_VA;). tools/symbols.py merge and layout write the tools' findings into its generated sections;
a line written by hand wins. Then py -3 tools/pipeline.py names regenerates the C. A function the
decompiler writes that gets a name needs the decompiled C first: py -3.14 tools/decompile.py build,
then py -3 tools/pipeline.py hand (or names after it), or the recompiled code still calls it by its
sub_ name and the link fails (sub_0001A700_entry unresolved).

A function written by hand: C in src/game/, by its name in symbols.txt and with a signature
of its own, the guest's memory read through symbols.h's accessors. Beside it, its entry
(ENTRY_CDECL2(vcObjectFind), src/game/decomp.h) is the function as the recompiled code calls
it, its arguments on the guest stack (or in the registers the compiler used,
ENTRY_REGISTERS_VOID(vcSceneObjectUnlink, g_eax, g_esi, g_ebx)) and its result in eax; the pipeline's hand step hands the
entries to the recompiler, which generates no body for them and calls the entries instead. It calls
the functions still recompiled with CALL(vcFileReadU32, file, at) and a callback with
CALL_AT(address, ...), and one written by hand directly (the build takes C4113 as an error, so a
CALL left on a function that has become C fails); a local it hands them by address lives in the
guest's stack.

Checking that nothing changed, after every change:
py -3 tools/verify_c.py
py -3 tools/scenario.py
py -3 tools/noise_report.py
verify_c.py runs each function written by hand against the game's own machine code with
xboxrecomp's conformance harness (it needs a 32-bit MSVC): eax and the memory, the game's variables
included, and names any function it compared with nothing.
scenario.py plays the scripted scenarios
of tests/scenarios/ (the menu, the first mission, a save, the training, and a mission of each
chapter, reached with the code that unlocks them) with every clock the game reads tied to the
frames and an empty save folder of its own, so runs repeat frame for frame, and compares every dumped
frame and saved file with the reference the build before wrote (--save records it). noise_report.py
counts what keeps the generated C from reading as written, the XBE's bytes of the game's own that are
unknown or not yet typed among them (tools/coverage.py), and fails if a count went up (--save after a
round that brought some down). The scenarios run alone: under another heavy process, two of them
went their own way once at frame 2880 (the race the clock tied to the frames does not cover).

Checking against the original: the same scenarios run on the original game in xemu, patched to
dump its frames with the port's numbers and to answer the game's clock and pad as the port does
(tools/reference/xemu/ has the patch, how to build it and what it needs of your own console), and
each frame is set against the port's; it fails when a frame is further than the scenario's original
line allows:
py -3 tools/xemu_reference.py

Layout
game/ your game's folder (ignored by git)
src/main.c host entry: loads the XBE, brings up the runtime, calls the recompiled entry point;
names the Direct3D device's GPU fence
src/game/ the game's C written by hand, by subject (engine/objects.c, files.c, format.c,
rects.c, random.c, screen.c, text.c, render.c, classes.c, scene.c, vector.c); decomp.h and
decomp.c, what joins it to the recompiled C
src/recomp_manual.c the bridges' wrappers around recompiled functions, by the functions' names
src/d3d11_bridge.c the Direct3D 11 bridge: what the game's D3D calls draw, through xboxrecomp's
D3D8 layer
src/input_bridge.c the pad and the keyboard answered from the host's XInput, and the pad scripts
src/dsound_bridge.c the game's DirectSound answered on the host: buffers, their 3D, the listener
src/sound_mixer.c mixes the game's sounds from its memory (PCM, Xbox ADPCM) to the audio device
src/clock_bridge.c the clock tied to the frames, for runs compared frame for frame
tests/scenarios/ the scripted scenarios and their reference frames (tools/scenario.py)
src/recomp/gen/ the recompiled C, laid out by subject: xdk/, bink/, engine/, game/ (ignored by git;
tools/pipeline.py writes it)
symbols/xdk_symbols.json the XDK library symbols XbSymbolDatabase finds in the XBE (names and addresses)
symbols/lib_matches.json the XDK library functions and variables matched against the XDK's .lib files
symbols/classes.json the engine's object classes and their callbacks
symbols/registries.json the game's object types and their functions, by family
symbols/symbols.txt the one place of the names, descriptions and files of the C
tools/pipeline.py xboxrecomp's pipeline, with every output inside this repository
tools/symbols.py writes the tools' names and the file lines into symbols/symbols.txt
tools/string_table.py lists the game's texts by their number, from main.pak's string table (into analysis/)
tools/apply_names.py writes the names of symbols.txt into the disassembly before recompiling
tools/apply_files.py tells the recompiler each function's file, from symbols.txt
tools/organize_gen.py lays the recompiled C out in its files, each function with its description
tools/noise_report.py counts what keeps the generated C from reading as written (baseline beside it)
tools/coverage.py classifies every byte of the XBE: code, data described or reached, fill, unknown
tools/conformance.py runs xboxrecomp's oracle: the game's machine code and the C side by side
tools/hand_functions.py lists the functions written by hand (src/game/) and wrapped (src/recomp_manual.c),
for the recompiler
tools/verify_c.py checks each function written by hand against the game's machine code
tools/scenario.py plays the scenarios and compares their frames with the references
tools/xdk_symbols.py makes symbols/xdk_symbols.json from XbSymbolDatabase's scan
tools/match_libs.py makes symbols/lib_matches.json from the XDK's .lib files
tools/find_classes.py makes symbols/classes.json from the class descriptors the game registers
tools/find_registries.py makes symbols/registries.json from the game's object type registries
tools/make_xiso.py packs the game's folder into an Xbox disc image (XDVDFS) for xemu
tools/xemu_reference.py runs the scenarios on the original game in xemu and sets its frames against the port's
tools/reference/xemu/ the patch that makes xemu the reference (GPL-2.0-or-later, as xemu), and its build
tools/decompile.py the game's functions through arcade-decomp's decompiler: lifted, their stack and
data flow followed, their signatures found, their C written into src/decompiled/
tools/x86/ the decompiler's x86 frontend: the functions decoded, lifted to its IR, made graphs,
their C written; recompiled.py, what each function left recompiled reads, writes
and takes, read from its machine code, for the decompiled C that calls it
src/decompiled/ the decompiled C (tools/decompile.py build), each function in its recompiled
version's place, and x86.h, what it calls for the x86's own arithmetic and to call
the recompiled code
tools/core/ arcade-decomp (a git submodule), the decompiler the frontend feeds
docs/d3d.md how the game uses Direct3D: the map for the Direct3D 11 path
analysis/ the pipeline's data: a copy of the XBE, disassembly, function and ABI databases
(ignored by git)
licenses/ licenses of the code this project starts from

How the port works

Game code. xboxrecomp lifts the XBE's x86 code into C, a function per function, with the CPU's
registers and flags as variables and the Xbox's memory at the addresses the game expects; the C is
compiled into a native executable. That includes the libraries the game linked statically (Direct3D,
Bink), which run as recompiled code too.
Kernel. The Xbox kernel calls the game imports are answered by the runtime with the host's
operating system: files from game/, threads, events, memory.
Graphics. For now the game's own Direct3D runs and writes GPU commands, which the runtime's
pushbuffer executor draws in software. The port's way is to route the game's Direct3D calls to
Direct3D 11 instead (docs/d3d.md).
Sound. The game's DirectSound is not run: each of its entries is answered on the host, as the
XDK's own would answer it, and each buffer the game fills is a voice of a mixer that reads it in the
game's memory, decodes the Xbox's ADPCM and plays it through the host's audio device.
The game's files are read where the game asks for them, from your copy, unchanged.

Legal

This project is licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License; see LICENSE.
CMakeLists.txt, src/main.c and src/recomp_manual.c started from xboxrecomp's
templates/new-game (MIT); see licenses/xboxrecomp.txt. xboxrecomp itself is not part of this
repository.
src/vertex_program_hlsl.c translates the vertex programs to HLSL after XboxXBERecomp's
runtime/gpu/shaders.cpp (MIT); see licenses/XboxXBERecomp.txt. XboxXBERecomp itself is not part of
this repository.
tools/reference/xemu/xemu-reference.patch changes xemu and is licensed as xemu is, GPL-2.0-or-later;
xemu itself is not part of this repository, and neither are the console's MCPX ROM, BIOS or hard disk
it runs with.
symbols/xdk_symbols.json is the output of XbSymbolDatabase (MIT): names and addresses, no code.
symbols/lib_matches.json holds names and addresses only: the XDK's libraries are read on your
machine, and no XDK code or file is part of this repository.
No game data and none of the game's machine code is distributed by this project: the recompiled C is
generated from your own copy of the game and stays on your machine. The decompiled C in src/game/ is
written by hand for this project.
Robotech is a trademark of Harmony Gold USA, Inc. Robotech: Battlecry was developed by Vicious Cycle
Software and published by TDK Mediactive. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by them or by
Microsoft.

1tqqd5d.title: GTA 6's strong and silent Jason was inspired by Steve McQueen and former Army Rangers, says Rockstar
1tqqd5d.content:
Man of few words.

Image credit: Rockstar

If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.
Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 1.Watch on YouTube
"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries said. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves."
Game writer Michael Wiafe said Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly.
"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them."
Fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it."GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.
Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.
Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

w3iupj.title: At Least 4 Killed in Russian Drone Attacks on Kyiv Region, Officials Say
w3iupj.content:
Nov. 22, 2026

Emergency workers lead away a woman in distress from the site of an apartment block that partially collapsed after it was hit during a night of Russian missile and drone attacks.

Reuters/Thomas Peter

At least four people were killed in Russian drone attacks on Ukraine's Kyiv region on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky and local officials said.
The bodies of three people were found and about 10 people may still be trapped under the rubble of a residential building that was struck by a Russian drone on Sunday morning in the small town of Dymer near Kyiv.
"Part of a five-story apartment building has collapsed following a Russian drone attack," Zelensky said on X. "I thank our first responders for acting quickly: nine people have already been evacuated, and the fire has been contained."
Local officials said four people, including a teenager, were injured.
Later on Sunday, one person was killed when a Russian drone struck a grocery store in Vyshneve, southwest of Kyiv, the local governor said on Telegram, adding that three people were injured.

Emergency service footage showed rescuers searching through a large pile of rubble, helping residents descend from the damaged building by ladder and crane platform.
At 3:35 p.m. (13:35 GMT), rescuers had to stop their search for survivors because of an incoming aerial threat.
Shortly after, three explosions rang through the town of Dymer, with Reuters footage showing an unidentified aerial object on fire falling from the sky. Civilians and rescuers were seen taking shelter in nearby buildings.

uz4u6k.title: This 1991 Mercedes-Benz 560SEC on BaT Has an Extra Bit of Euro-Snob Appeal
uz4u6k.content: Here’s a big Mercedes cruiser with a European-market V-8 that gives it a bit more punch.Euro-spec cars also got slimmer bumpers and sleeker headlights, so this one also looks great.It has relatively low mileage and is set up to do plenty of stately touring.A Mercedes-Benz executive coupe from the early 1990s is a grand tourer par excellence, and you could hardly do better than this well-traveled machine. Currently on Bring a Trailerr (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos), this is a European-spec 1991 560SEC that was imported first to Japan before being brought to the United States seven years ago. The mileage is reasonable at the equivalent of 78K miles, but if you like to travel, here's your beast.Bring a TrailerThis generation of Mercedes coupe was the two-door sibling to the wunderbar W126 S-class, designed by the legendary Bruno Sacco. The first of these C126 coupes launched in 1981, kicking off a decade-long run that ended with the 1991 model year. These are truly great cars from the brand’s “The best or nothing” era.Bring a TrailerU.S.-market 560s came with a fairly emissions-strangled version of Mercedes's 5.5-liter V-8, but this car benefits from higher compression and slightly freer-flowing exhaust. There were more powerful versions available, but here you can expect around 275 horsepower and mountains of creamy torque, fed through a four-speed automatic gearbox.Bring a TrailerIt's not an AMG under the hood, nor are the stately looks here anywhere near as boisterous as the wide-body versions of the 560SEC that Affalterbach dreamed up. Here, the tailoring is more discreet, set off by a set of 17-inch Lorinser wheels and a slightly lower ride height on H&R springs with Bilstein dampers up front.Bring a TrailerIt looks understated and reserved in a way Mercedes doesn't really do anymore. Inside, it's just as cushy as you would hope, with leather heated seats, plenty of wood trim, and a stereo that has been updated with Bluetooth connectivity.There’s an issue with the air conditioning that a specialist could probably address, but this example has had plenty of mechanical work done. The fuel system was overhauled with new injectors and a new distributor a few years ago, and larger work including valve seals and a new timing chain was done two years ago. At that time, perishables like vacuum lines were also replaced.Basically, this well-fettled big coupe is an idealized version of the top-dog Mercedes from the brand’s glory days.The auction ends on November 24.Brendan McAleer is a freelance writer and photographer based in North Vancouver, B.C., Canada. He grew up splitting his knuckles on British automobiles, came of age in the golden era of Japanese sport-compact performance, and began writing about cars and people in 2008. His particular interest is the intersection between humanity and machinery, whether it is the racing career of Walter Cronkite or Japanese animator Hayao Miyazaki's half-century obsession with the Citroën 2CV. He has taught both of his young daughters how to shift a manual transmission and is grateful for the excuse they provide to be perpetually buying Hot Wheels.

gh-1408068472.title: GitHub - NoRain211/doa3-re: Native Windows port of Dead or Alive 3 (Xbox), built by static recompilation with a hand-written runtime. Requires your own copy of the game.
gh-1408068472.content:
A native PC port of Dead or Alive 3 (Windows, macOS & Linux), built by static recompilation, with the goal of rewriting it into readable source.

Status ·
Report a bug ·
Code signing policy

ImportantThis project ships no game files. You need your own legally obtained copy
of the Xbox game: the Japan 3.1 disc, the main build, or the USA 3.0
disc. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's rights holders.

About
The original Xbox executable is lifted to C with a static recompiler, then
linked against a hand-written runtime that replaces the Xbox kernel imports
and, one entry point at a time, the Direct3D 8 and DirectSound APIs with native
equivalents: Direct3D 11 (or Vulkan through SDL_GPU) and XAudio2 on Windows,
SDL_GPU (Metal or Vulkan) and SDL3 audio on macOS and Linux. The rest of the
game, including its statically linked libraries, runs as generated code. The
plan is to replace game logic with readable, hand-written source one
data-structure cluster at a time once the game runs.
The runtime comes from the sister project
doaxbv-re, which is fully playable on
the same approach.
Status
NotePlayable, in early testing. Intro movie, title, menus, Story, Time
Attack, Watch and Sparring fights with audio, stage transfers, continue and
attract mode run on the whole-program recomp. See
bring-up for run evidence, history
for how the port got here, and runtime options
for settings and runner flags.

The main build is the Japan 3.1 disc (XDK 4134), with 3.1's moves, balance
and costumes; the USA 3.0 disc still builds. tools/build_game.py and the
launcher tell them apart by default.xbe, keep each in its own extraction and
play folder (so saves never mix), and the launcher shows which one is
installed. Japan specifics are in Japan 3.1.

Area
State

Whole-program lift
Runs from boot to fights, paced to 60 Hz

Kernel imports
Shared with doaxbv-re

D3D8 3925
Device, frame, draws, textures, vertex programs and viewport bound to DOA3

DirectSound 3936
Bound; XAudio2 (Windows) or SDL3 (macOS, Linux) output with 3D distance, Doppler and HRTF

macOS and Linux
Native builds; see building on macOS and Linux

CRI Sofdec movies
Play natively

Hand-written game logic
Stage boundary and danger-zone collision

DOAXBV swimsuits
Every DOA3 woman can wear her DOAXBV swimsuits, switched live in a fight, built from your own DOAXBV disc

Free camera
Take the game's camera and fly it through fights and cutscenes, freeze and step the game, hide the HUD, change swimsuits (with your DOAXBV disc) and save screenshots; see Free camera

DOAXBV swimsuits
With your own Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball disc (an .iso or its
extracted folder), Kasumi, Ayane, Christie, Tina, Hitomi, Helena and Lei Fang
can each wear any of her 307 DOAXBV swimsuits. They keep their DOA3 heads,
hair and moves; the suit is built on the fly from your disc, and skirts swing
and clear the legs, and tassels swing, with DOAXBV's own cloth motion. In a fight, click
L3 (the left stick) on any controller to open the swimsuit menu (click
again to close): its left half dresses P1
and its right half P2. LB / LT and RB / RT change the
swimsuits (hold to scroll), X / B mark a favorite (saved per girl),
and Y browses only favorites. A panel lists the controls
while the menu is open, and the keyboard's 1 / 2 switch too. Works on
Japan 3.1 and USA 3.0. The game finds
a DOAXBV .iso or extracted folder in private/ (or in a doaxbv-re
checkout beside this one); otherwise choose or drop it in the launcher (steps
in Getting the swimsuits). The
suit recipes (recipes/doaxbv-suits.pack.gz) ship with the
port; no DOAXBV data does. See
DOAXBV swimsuits.
Free camera
Tick Free camera in the launcher, then in a fight or cutscene press
F1 or click the right stick to take the game's camera and fly it: the
sticks or WASD and the arrow keys move and look, the triggers or Q /
E go down and up. Start or P freezes the game and the right
shoulder or . steps it a frame, the left shoulder or H hides the
HUD, and the d-pad's left or \ turns to a fighter whose swimsuit the
d-pad's up and down change. F12, or the d-pad's right while flying,
saves a screenshot to DOA3 in your Pictures folder. It works on both
Japan 3.1 and USA 3.0. F3 turns on, or off again, a readout of the frame
rate, the average frame time and the slowest frame of the last second; it
starts off. No control uses Back, which DOA3 acts on first. See Free camera.
Offline, hold Back (Backspace on the keyboard) for two seconds on any
controller to quit to the desktop: A quits once any save in progress is
written, B keeps playing. The game still sees the held Back before the
panel opens, so it can reset training or skip a cutscene on the way. A netplay
session keeps the prompt closed. The main menu's last entry, Quit Game, asks the same.
recomp-runtime/ started from doaxbv-re at f6ad13e. Its DOAXBV address
bindings are gated off; DOA3's D3D8, DirectSound, XAPI and CRI functions are
re-bound in its adapters.

Library
DOA3
DOAXBV

XAPILIB, D3DX8, XGRAPHC, XBOXKRNL
3911
4928

D3D8
3925
4928

DSOUND
3936
4928

Both games carry CRI Sofdec (PSGSFD*), XPP and DOLBY sections and ship AFS
archives and SFD movies.
Build the tests from source
The runtime tests build without any game files or submodules:
git clone https://github.com/NoRain211/doa3-re.git
cd doa3-re
# Windows: put llvm-mingw and CMake on PATH, downloading them into private/ the first time.
$env:PATH = (python -c "import os, sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'tools'); import build_game; print(os.pathsep.join(map(str, build_game.windows_tools())))" | Select-Object -Last 1) + ";$env:PATH"
cmake -S recomp-runtime -B build/recomp-runtime -G "MinGW Makefiles" -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++
cmake --build build/recomp-runtime
ctest --test-dir build/recomp-runtime --output-on-failure
The $env:PATH line uses the llvm-mingw
Clang and mingw32-make and the CMake that tools/build_game.py pins; on
macOS and Linux skip it and use -G Ninja without the compiler options.
Visual Studio 2022 also works: configure with -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"
and pass --config Release to the build and -C Release to ctest.
This produces test executables, not the game runner. Passing tests does not
establish game accuracy.
Set up a local build
git submodule update --init
python tools/extract_iso.py <your-doa3.iso> # -> private/imported-disc/disc
python tools/xbe_info.py private/imported-disc/disc/default.xbe
extract_iso.py needs XboxDev
extract-xiso on PATH or at
tools/artifacts/extract-xiso.exe. The lift and runner build are in
docs/bring-up.md.
Play
Download the ZIP from the latest
release and extract it
to a folder with a short path. Drag a DOA3 ISO or extracted disc folder onto
Launcher.exe, or choose it on the launcher's BUILD GAME page, to build
the game; START GAME
plays with the resolution, anti-aliasing, widescreen and volume you pick; see
docs/test-release.md. After that, DOA3.exe starts
the game with those settings. In a checkout,
python tools/package_test.py --launchers . builds both exes. On Windows the build needs
only Python 3.12+; its first run downloads
llvm-mingw (Clang and make) and
CMake (245 MB, about 850 MB unpacked) into private/.
On macOS and Linux, extract the release's
DOA3-<version>-macOS.tar.gz or DOA3-<version>-Linux.tar.gz and run
./build_game.sh with your ISO, then ./launcher.sh or ./run_game.sh, or
open ./launcher.sh and build from its BUILD GAME page; see
docs/building.md. The game keeps its cache and
saves in private/play-disc and each session's log in private/play-logs.
To uninstall, delete the folder; free camera screenshots stay in
Pictures/DOA3.
Controls
The first connected controller, or the keyboard, drives player 1: arrows are
the D-pad, Enter is Start, Backspace is Back, A and S are X and Y, Z and X
are A and B, Q and W are White and Black, and E and R are the triggers.
To rebind the keyboard, create private/keyboard.json with the buttons to
change, for example {"a": "Space", "b": "Ctrl", "start": "Tab"}. Buttons are
up, down, left, right, start, back, a, b, x, y, white, black, ltrig and rtrig;
keys are A-Z, 0-9, F1-F9, F12, Up, Down, Left, Right, Enter, Backspace,
Space, Tab, Shift, Ctrl and Esc. Buttons you leave out keep their keys,
except that a key you give to one button leaves the button that had it. F10
is a Windows system key and F11 is reserved, so neither can be bound. With
the free camera on, F1, backquote, F12 and P keep their jobs, so a button
bound to one of those does both.
Display settings
RECOMP_D3D_SCALE (1-8, render height multiplier; 3 renders 1920x1440
natively), RECOMP_D3D_MSAA (sample count, for example 4) and
RECOMP_D3D_SMAA=1 (built from the third_party/smaa submodule; Direct3D 11
only) work as in doaxbv-re.
F11 or Alt+Enter switches between a window and borderless fullscreen.
Widescreen defaults off because DOA3's box lists no 16:9 support, but the
game honors the dashboard flag that RECOMP_D3D_WIDESCREEN=1 reports: its 3D
view renders anamorphic 16:9 with a wider horizontal view, and the window
shows it at 16:9. The game leaves its 2D layer at 4:3, so the presenter
narrows screen-space quads that are narrower than the centered 4:3 area by
3/4 toward the center. The HUD, menus and subtitles keep their 4:3 shape;
full-screen fades, backdrops and the already pillarboxed movies are left as
drawn.
RECOMP_D3D_WIDESCREEN=16:10, or any W:H from 4:3 to 4:1 such as an
ultrawide monitor's 3440:1440, makes the game render that shape itself:
the runner rewrites the 16:9 constants of its projection and fight camera,
and the presenter narrows the 2D layer to 4:3 of the shape. Wider than 16:9,
the fight camera keeps its 16:9 framing and the view widens around it.
Movies come in a centered 4:3 frame the game sized for 16:9; the presenter
keeps the film's shape, letterboxing 16:9 endings on 16:10 and pillarboxing
them on ultrawide. The launcher's Ultrawide screen uses the primary
monitor's own shape when it is wider than 16:9, up to 4:1, and 64:27
(2560x1080) otherwise.
Repository layout

Path
Contents

recomp-runtime/
Runtime, kernel and input adapters, audio, D3D8 replacements, presentation, tests

xbe/
XBE parsing and hashing

tools/
ISO extraction, XBE info, lifter submodule, DOA3 function lists, build, launcher, packaging and export checks

third_party/
SMAA submodule

docs/
Bring-up status, lift and build steps, D3D8, audio, input and fiber research

private/
Ignored local game inputs, generated output and run evidence

Contributing
Read the contribution guide first. Translation defects are
fixed in the lifter and regenerated; generated game C is never patched by hand.
When reporting a bug, include
your build version, steps to reproduce, what happened, your hardware and
controller, and the stop or crash message
(how to read logs).
Remove private paths from logs, and never upload game binaries, generated game
C, assets, extracted filenames, saves, BIOS data or private run evidence.
AI assistance
This project uses large language models and AI coding agents extensively for
code, reverse-engineering analysis, debugging, tests and documentation. Their
output can contain mistakes; changes are reviewed and tested, and unverified
behavior is tracked as such.
Code signing policy
Free code signing provided by SignPath.io,
certificate by SignPath Foundation.
The signed files are Launcher.exe and DOA3.exe in the Windows release ZIP,
from the first release after SignPath Foundation accepts the project; 0.6.6
and earlier are unsigned. GitHub Actions builds them from this repository
(sign-launchers), and an approver signs
off on each release. The game itself is not in the ZIP and is not signed: your
computer builds it from your own disc.

Committers and reviewers: NoRain211.
Pull requests from anyone else are reviewed before they are merged.
Approvers: NoRain211

Privacy
This program will not transfer any information to other networked systems
unless specifically requested by the user or the person installing or
operating it.

Build: the first build on Windows downloads llvm-mingw, CMake, SDL3,
Dear ImGui and miniupnpc from GitHub, shaderc from Maven Central and the
Capstone package from PyPI. Those sites see the requests, as with any
download.
Online play: only the Versus netplay menu goes online. It talks to the
other player and to the matchmaking server set in its settings (the
project's server by default). The server sees your public and local network
addresses, a random player ID this install made, your room and the game
build, and relays the session's packets when the two players cannot reach
each other directly. Hosting asks your router, through UPnP, to forward the
game's UDP port.

License
Original code and documentation are licensed under
GPL-3.0-or-later; see also NOTICE. Third-party components
keep their own licenses. The license grants no rights to the game or its assets.

gh-1464649491.title: GitHub - Drashi/sacred-native: Sacred Gold running natively on Apple Silicon Macs and Linux ARM64. Bring your own copy of Sacred Gold 2.28.
gh-1464649491.content:
A native port of Sacred Gold for Linux ARM64 and macOS on Apple Silicon. Play your copy of the game without Windows,
Wine or an emulator, at any screen size and frame rate.
This is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to the owners of the Sacred
trademark or the game's original developers and publishers. "Sacred" is their trademark.
You need your own copy of the game
Sacred Native contains no game code and no game data. It needs an installed Sacred Gold 2.28 (English, the GOG or
Steam release): the folder that holds Sacred.exe, granny.dll and tincat2.dll. On macOS or Linux you can copy that
folder from a Windows installation. The installation is only read, never changed.
On the first start the launcher translates the game's own Sacred.exe, granny.dll and tincat2.dll into native code
on your machine (a few minutes, once per update). What ships is the runtime that replaces Windows, DirectDraw/Direct3D,
the Miles sound system and DirectShow, and a translation recipe that lists where the game's instructions are, without
any byte of the game.
Download and play

Download the bundle for your system from the releases page and unpack it.

macOS: remove the download quarantine once: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine sacred-native-macos-arm64
(the binaries are signed ad hoc, not notarized).

Start ./sacred-launcher. It finds your installation (or lets you pick its folder), checks the version, and
starts the game with Play. The first Play builds the game module; later starts are immediate.
From a terminal the same works with ./sacred-gold "/path/to/Sacred Gold".

Settings and saves live in your profile: ~/Library/Application Support/Sacred Native/Sacred Gold on macOS,
~/.local/share/Sacred Native/Sacred Gold on Linux. The log is sacred-native.log in the same folder.
HD and widescreen
The launcher's Settings page holds the port's options, each with a short explanation. A new profile starts
fullscreen at the display's size and refresh rate with sharper rendering and textures already on.

Any resolution. The game runs at the window's or display's size instead of 1024x768, including wide screens.
Menus and loading screens designed for 4:3 are scaled to the screen height; the main menu and character select extend
their sky and water to the full width, and the bundle's menu pictures fill the sides of the other screens.
Render scale (1-4x) draws the 3D scene at a multiple of the window size and filters it down.
HD textures (2-4x) upscales the game's own textures in the background; texture packs can replace them.
Frame rate limit up to 240 FPS, or the display's refresh rate. Movement and game logic keep their speed.
Original Sacred look: the classic UI skin, menu art and menu music that Sacred Gold ships but does not use.

All options are keys in the profile's Settings.cfg too; the bundle's README.md lists them.
Building from source
See CONTRIBUTING.md. In short, with the game installed:
export SACRED_ASSETS="/path/to/Sacred Gold"
tools/build_macos_deps.sh # macOS only: SDL2, FreeType, pkg-config in build/
tools/bootstrap.sh # Python venv, LGPL FFmpeg, generated C
cmake -S . -B build/game -DSACRED_BUILD_GAME=ON && cmake --build build/game -j
build/game/sacred-native --assets "$SACRED_ASSETS"
tools/dist/make_bundle.sh builds the same bundle the releases carry.
How it works
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describes the translator, the runtime and the CPU semantics. In short: every x86 instruction
of the game becomes a few lines of C over an explicit CPU state, compiled by your C compiler. The x87 FPU keeps its
80-bit registers; the Windows, DirectDraw, Miles and COM APIs the game imports are implemented natively on SDL2,
OpenGL, FFmpeg and FreeType.
License
Copyright (C) 2026 Sacred Native contributors.
Sacred Native is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public
License as published by the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later
version (GPL-3.0-or-later, full text in LICENSE). It is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but
WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY. Third-party components keep their own licenses; they and the LGPL relinking notes are listed in
