Building & Verification

Prerequisites

Compiler: Modern C/C++ toolchain (GCC 13+ / MSYS2 UCRT64 GCC 14.2+ / Clang 15+)
Build Tool: GNU make or mingw32-make
SDL2: MinGW-w64 development libraries are self-contained in lifted/third_party/SDL2/, with SDL2.dll provided for runtime execution.

1. Compilable Decompiled Legacy Suite (decompiled/Compilable/)
Because Little Fighter 2 artwork, sprite sheets, sound effects, and stage backgrounds are proprietary freeware created by Marti Wong and Starsky Wong, they are not distributed in this source code repository.
# Build the legacy static library (decompiled/Compilable/build/liblf2_legacy.a)
mingw32-make -C decompiled/Compilable

# Run the decompiled verification test suite
mingw32-make -C decompiled/Compilable test

# Clean legacy build artifacts
mingw32-make -C decompiled/Compilable clean
Verification Suite (test_legacy.exe) checks:

1:1 Fast integer absolute value computation (0x004034e0)
2D Bounding box overlap arithmetic (0x004171c0)
Deterministic 3,000-byte circular PRNG table lookup (0x00417170)
Exact sizeof and offsetof alignments for all 10 domain structures
Rudolf teleportation gameplay positioning logic (0x00403270)

2. Modernized Source Lift Engine (lifted/)
The modernized source lift builds an independent executable and static engine library:
# Build the modernized game executable (lifted/build/lf2.exe)
mingw32-make -C lifted

# Run all 16 unit test suites and the 30-frame verification test (17 tests total)
mingw32-make -C lifted test

# Clean lifted build artifacts
mingw32-make -C lifted clean
Running the Game:
# Launch from the lifted directory
cd lifted && ./build/lf2.exe

# Launch directly in fullscreen mode
cd lifted && ./build/lf2.exe --fullscreen

Controls & Player Mapping: Player keys are configured via control.txt.
Fullscreen Toggle: Press Alt + Enter to switch between windowed (794x550) and fullscreen.
Secret Cheat Codes:

Type lf2.net on the main menu to unlock Julian, Firzen, LouisEX, and all enemy henchmen.
Type herofighter.com to enable stage debug function keys.
Type ABC to unlock the internal frame and hitbox inspector.

3. Setting Up Authentic Game Assets
Little Fighter 2 artwork, character sprites, sound effects, and stage backgrounds are proprietary freeware created by Marti Wong and Starsky Wong, and are not distributed in this repository.
To run the lifted engine with full audio and visual assets:

Obtain an authentic Little Fighter 2 installation (v1.9c, v2.0, or v2.0a) from lf2.net or LF-Empire.
Copy the authentic game folders (data/, sprite/, bg/, sound/, bgm/) into lifted/build/ (or run lf2.exe directly inside an existing LF2 directory).
All frontend menu and character selection UI images are pre-baked directly into the binary (lifted/src/graphics/embedded_ui.cpp), exactly mirroring the Win32 PE resource architecture of the original binary.

Reverse-Engineered Secrets, Ciphers & Easter Eggs

Ghidra decompilation and binary disassembly revealed several fascinating, historic internal mechanics and easter eggs embedded directly into the machine code of lf2.exe:
1. The Legendary Resource Decryption Key: "SiuHungIsAGoodBearBecauseHeIsVeryGood"

Memory Location: Hardcoded in the .rdata section at virtual address 0x0044892c (file offset 0x4792c).

Origin & Fun Fact: "Siu Hung" (小熊) is the Cantonese pseudonym of Marti Wong (黃小熊), co-creator of Little Fighter 2 alongside Starsky Wong. Translated from Cantonese, it means:

"Little Bear is a good bear because he is very good."

The Cipher Architecture: LF2 encodes all game resources (.dat files) using a byte-wise additive/subtractive variant of the Vigenère cipher operating modulo 256.

The 123-Byte Header Trick: Every .dat file begins with a 123-byte (0x7B) padding header. In FUN_004148a0, the decryptor steps through the key (key_idx + 1) % 37 for each of the 123 dummy bytes before decrypting any payload data. Since 123 % 37 = 12, payload decryption always begins at key index 12 (the character 'G' in "GoodBear..."):
$$\text{plaintext}[i] = (\text{ciphertext}[i] - \text{key}[k] + 256) \pmod{256}$$

Modding Community Nostalgia: For over two decades, this hardcoded string has been celebrated among LF2 modders who reverse-engineered the binary to create data decrypters (e.g. LF2 Data Changer).

2. The Replay (.lfr) Secondary Obfuscation Cipher (0x0043DD60 / 0x0044D7A0)

Two-Layer Protection in LF2 v2.0: While legacy versions saved raw frame records, Little Fighter 2 v2.0 introduced a dual compression and encryption pipeline in 0x0043DD60 to protect replay recordings (.lfr files in recording\) from tampering and desynchronization.

zlib Deflation: The memory buffer containing all recorded battle input frames is first compressed using a statically linked build of zlib 1.1.4 (compress() / deflate() at 0x0043F4B0).

The Obfuscation Pass: Immediately after deflation, the engine loops through the compressed payload byte-by-byte and applies an additive character cipher using a hardcoded 1,345-byte ASCII digit key stored in .data at 0x0044D7A0:
Key = "15456611235456134545631153456894056897..." (1,345 bytes)

Transformation Formula: Each of the first $\min(N, 1345)$ bytes of the compressed stream is transformed using its corresponding key digit:
$$\text{byte}[i] = (\text{byte}[i] + (\text{key}[i] - \text{'0'})) \pmod{256}$$

This custom secondary cipher explains why third-party replay editors from the LF2 1.9c era failed to open or parse replays generated by version 2.0.

3. Secret Cheat Code State Machines in WindowProc (0x0043b3d0)
The original window procedure maintains static state counters that detect sequential keystrokes typed anywhere in the application:

"lf2.net" (Roster Unlock): Typing L -> F -> 2 -> . -> N -> E -> T increments state tracker DAT_0045857c and sets DAT_00455471 = 'd' (ASCII 0x64). This unlocks Julian, Firzen, and LouisEX on the character selection screen along with other enemy characters, which are non playable by default.

"herofighter.com" (Sequel Easter Egg): Typing H -> E -> R -> O -> F -> I -> G -> H -> T -> E -> R -> . -> C -> O -> M advances tracker DAT_00458578 and sets DAT_00455470 = 'd'. Marti Wong embedded this secret domain name in later versions of LF2 as a nod to his next major project, Hero Fighter! It enables the user to use function keys in the Stage mode of the game.

"ABC" (Internal Data Debugger): In FUN_0043e9a0, pressing A -> B -> C sequentially sets DAT_00450bec = 1, unlocking mode switching via keys '1', '2', '3' to access the built-in frame/weapon inspector mode.

4. Window & Platform Identity Artifacts

Window Class Name: The Win32 window class is registered as "Marti" at 0x00447634.

Window Title: Defined as "Little Fighter 2" at 0x00447620.

Authentic Viewport Resolution: Hardcoded in the .data segment at DAT_0044d78c (width = 794) and DAT_0044d790 (height = 550).

5. Deterministic Multiplayer PRNG Table

Standard C library rand() implementations vary across compiler runtimes, which would desynchronize peer-to-peer multiplayer.
LF2 completely avoids rand() during gameplay: at 0x0044FF90 in .data, it embeds a static, precomputed 3,000-byte pseudo-random table.
The PRNG routine (0x00417170) simply advances a circular index:
$$\text{index} = (\text{index} + 1) \pmod{3000}$$
guaranteeing 100% deterministic lockstep synchronization across network clients.

6. Fixed-Step 30 FPS Timing & Spiral-of-Death Protection (0x0043cf40)

Tick Step: In battle (DAT_0044d02c != 0), the step is 33 ms (0x21), yielding ~30.3 FPS. In menus, it steps at 3 ms.

Spiral of Death Clamp: If system lag causes the accumulator to fall behind by more than 100 ms, the game drops excess accumulated time:
$$\text{if } (t[\text{now}] - t[\text{last}] > 100\text{ ms}) \implies t[\text{last}] = t[\text{now}] - 100\text{ ms}$$

CPU Yielding: To prevent 100% CPU core starvation, the timing loop yields via sleep in chunks of at most 5 ms.

Key State Table: A raw 256-byte static array at 0x00455378 is initialized to 'u' (0x75 = up) in WinMain and toggled to 'd' (0x64 = down) on WM_KEYDOWN.

Engine Quirks, Desyncs & Known Binary Bugs

Through Ghidra decompilation and binary disassembly of lf2.exe, we reverse-engineered the exact root causes of legendary Little Fighter 2 engine quirks, multiplayer desync crashes, and long-standing community mysteries:
1. The Anatomy of the Infamous "Synchronisation Error!" (0x0041CAD9 / 0x0041CCB5)
For over two decades, Little Fighter 2 players experienced sudden match freezes with a "Synchronisation Error!" modal dialog. Disassembly of the lockstep network routine in 0x0041C5F0 revealed the exact mechanism:

The 22-Byte Lockstep Packet: At 0x0041CB80, every frame exchange transmits a compact 22-byte packet (net_packet_t) containing 8 packed player controller states (Up 0x02, Right 0x04, Attack 0x08, Jump 0x10, Defend 0x20, Down 0x40, Left 0x80, with 0x01 idle bit), frame sequence counter, version byte, and active HP checksum.

Three-Tier Desynchronization Checks: Disassembly at 0x0041CB50–0x0041CCD0 reveals the exact single-byte checks:

Offset +9 (Sequence Counter): Frame counter modulo 50 (idiv $0x32, DAT_00450bf0). Checked at 0x0041CC27; a mismatch halts with "Connection Lost!" (0x004493B4).

Offset +11 (Version Tag): Game version byte (DAT_0044d03c). Checked at 0x0041CC78; a mismatch halts with "Version not matched!" (0x0044939C).

Offset +13 (HP Checksum): Cumulative active player HP checksum (DAT_00450bf4). Checked at 0x0041CCB5; if remote and local checksums differ by even 1 HP, execution halts with "Synchronisation Error!" (0x00449384).

The 3-Phase Handshake Pipeline:

Phase 1 (14 Bytes): Host transmits "u can connect\0" (hardcoded at 0x00448900).

Phase 2 (77 Bytes): Slot negotiation ("11110000" host slots 1–4 vs "00001111" client slots 5–8) + four 10-byte player name strings delimited with _.

Phase 3 (3,001 Bytes): 1-byte command tag + 3,000-byte precomputed circular PRNG table (0x0044FF90) so both peers share identical pseudo-random sequences.

2. The 400-Slot World Object Array & Screen Overflow Crash (0x0042E100 / 0x004061D0)

Static Allocation Ceiling: Little Fighter 2 manages all entities on screen through a fixed global array in global_t (0x00458B00) capped at exactly 400 object slots (objects[400] at offset 0x194–0x7D4, matching is_object_exists[400] at 0x004–0x194).

Shared Pool Competition: Player characters (slots 0–7), enemy minions, dropped weapons (knives, baseball bats, rocks), projectiles (energy balls, ice swords), and transient particle effects (blood splatters, smoke puffs) all compete for these 400 slots. In object_t, the victim rest array vrest_of_objects is also exactly 400 bytes (0x0F0–0x280).

A native engine for the PC games Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (2001)
and Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2002).
macOS, Windows and Linux. The original games, checked against the originals.

HPEngine is an unofficial, open-source replacement for the engine behind the first two Harry Potter games for PC by
KnowWonder / Electronic Arts, both built on Unreal Engine 1:

Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone / Sorcerer's Stone (2001), "HP1" below;
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2002), "HP2" below.

It contains nothing of the games: it reads the maps, UnrealScript code, textures, sounds and music from a copy you own
and runs them on new code. Both games run on the same engine.
A legally obtained copy of the game is required. See Requirements.
Status
Version: beta (0.5.0).

playable: the full campaign was completed on 0.1.0

Harry Potter 2 (Chamber of Secrets)
first beta, new in 0.5.0: it starts, plays and saves, but its campaign has not yet been played through to the end on HPEngine (see Known issues)

Coming from 0.1.0? See CHANGELOG.md for how to move your saves.
Quick start

Download the package for your system from Releases:

macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel): HPEngine-Launcher-macOS.zip
Windows: HPEngine-win-x64.zip
Linux / Steam Deck: HPEngine-linux-x64.tar.gz

Add your game. Start the launcher (macOS: HPEngine Launcher; Windows: HPEngine Launcher.exe; Linux: HPEngine-Launcher),
pick the game's tab (Harry Potter 1 or Harry Potter 2) and add your copy. The launcher never changes your
files.
Play. Press Play (HP2: New Game or Load Game) in the launcher.

Step by step, with the first-launch warnings of macOS and Windows: Install.

Highlights

Native, without a compatibility layer. Built for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, Windows x64 and Linux x64; no Wine, no
virtual machine. The CD check and SafeDisc protection of the 2001 release are not involved, so modern Windows
versions that refuse SafeDisc are no obstacle.
The games' own code, unchanged. The shipped UnrealScript bytecode runs as it is in HPEngine's virtual machine; the
engine's native functions are ported from the original binaries. Game logic, physics, timing, animation and saves
behave as in the original release.
One engine for both games. Code the two games share is written once; where Chamber of Secrets' engine differs from
the first game's, HPEngine follows that game's own binaries.
Measured against the original. Ported functions are run side by side with the original machine code in an
emulator, frames are compared draw call by draw call with the running original game, and whole levels are played in
both and their state compared. Every difference found so far has been fixed; please report any you notice.
Modern displays. Any resolution and aspect ratio: on a wide screen you see more to the sides, the interface is
scaled by whole pixels, and fast displays get up to 120 interpolated frames per second while the game logic keeps
its native 60 Hz.
Easy setup. A launcher on macOS, Windows and Linux installs the games, switches mods on and off, starts the game
and keeps itself up to date. It works with the mouse, the keyboard or a gamepad.

Screenshots
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone

HPEngine at 1920x1080 with the US 1.53 game files.
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

Improvements over the original releases
The games themselves are left as they were. Where HPEngine deliberately does something differently, it is listed here
and in detail, marked "not original", under Differences from the original. They apply to both
games unless the list says otherwise:

Picture: wide-screen view without stretching (menus and 2D screens stay 4:3), sharp interface at every size,
smooth motion up to 120 fps, 16x anisotropic and trilinear filtering, models at full detail at any distance, no dark
band on glasses, light flares hidden behind Harry instead of shining through him, Harry's robe not showing through
his neck at high resolutions (HP1).
Timing: the game logic is locked to 60 Hz, as its scripts assume; it never runs fast on high-refresh displays,
and torch flames do not stop above 128 fps as they do in the original.
Sound: mixed at 44.1 kHz (the original HP1 mixes at 22 kHz); music continues from the same place after Alt-Tab;
in HP1 also after the pause menu, songs are no longer cut short and lowering the sound volume no longer silences the
music.
Menus and input: mouse-wheel scrolling in lists, an open list closes when the page changes, every resolution
offered in every window mode, readable key names, the mouse is captured in a window without an extra click; gamepad
support, with the controller's own button names on the Controls page and the d-pad stepping between menu controls,
sliders and list items. Chamber of Secrets: B skips a cut-scene, Back opens the map, the d-pad picks the duel spell,
and the options input page shows Difficulty for every player.
Bugs of the original fixed (HP1): some Bertie Bott's beans flew away from Harry at a steady frame rate; Mrs Norris
could not climb the library bookcases above about 30 fps.
Saves: HPEngine's own save files stay loadable across HPEngine versions.

What we learned about how the original engine works, with addresses in the original binaries: docs/.
Requirements
Your copy of the PC game, and one of the systems below.
Harry Potter 1: tested editions

US English 1.53: the reference; the port is checked against it.
UK English 1.1: plays through.
Russian (EA): plays through; menu text in a substitute font (Philosopher for MS Sans Serif, not original).
Nordic multilingual CD (HARRY_POTTER_NORD_2210: English, Danish, Finnish, Norwegian, Swedish): startup and
localized menus on Windows 11; the campaign not yet.

Other releases (European English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, ...) and modified copies (the fan "1.55" patch,
modded re-releases such as the 2002 "City" disc) install and run with a warning: nobody has checked them yet.
HP1Setup detects the edition from the files and shows it. For a release it does not recognise it shows a warning
with the SHA-1 hashes of System/HP.exe, Engine.dll, Render.dll and HPBase.u (HPEngine prints the same warning
at start): please open an issue with them and say whether the
game works. More: docs/editions.md.
Harry Potter 2: tested editions

English retail CD (build HPCos_021009_1205-1): the release the port is built against.
Russian (EA "Hit-Parade"): the same build and data as the English release, with its Russian dialogue and text.

Re-releases with changed game scripts install and run with a warning.

Install
You need your own copy of the game: see Requirements. HPEngine never changes it: it only reads it and
copies the game data into a folder of its own.
The launcher installs both games, each from its own tab, and each tab refuses the other game's copy:

Harry Potter 1 takes the CD, the game's installer, an installed game folder, a .zip of the game folder (and, on
macOS, a disc image).
Harry Potter 2 takes the installed game folder or the English retail CD (its InstallShield setup is unpacked,
never run: the English files are installed); then start a New Game or Load Game from the tab.

Pick your system. The launcher is the easy way; the last ways are for people who prefer the terminal.
macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel)

Download HPEngine-Launcher-macOS.zip from Releases and unpack it.
Move HPEngine Launcher to Applications and open it. It is not signed by Apple, so the first time macOS blocks
it: open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway
(or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/HPEngine Launcher.app").
Pick the game's tab, drop your copy of the game onto the launcher window (or click Choose…), click Install,
then Play.

The launcher keeps itself up to date and only installs updates signed by HPEngine.
Windows

Download HPEngine-win-x64.zip from Releases and unpack it into an empty folder. Inside are
HPEngine Launcher.exe, README.txt and the folder HPEngine\; keep them together. No admin rights needed.
Run HPEngine Launcher.exe. The files are not signed: if SmartScreen warns, choose More info → Run anyway.
Pick the game's tab and drop your copy of the game onto the launcher window, or add it with Choose folder… (an
installed game, or the CD drive) or Choose files… (HP1: the game's Setup.exe or a .zip); click
Install, then Play. A disc image: double-click it to mount it, then add the new drive.

Linux / Steam Deck

Download HPEngine-linux-x64.tar.gz from Releases and unpack it into an empty folder
(tar -xzf HPEngine-linux-x64.tar.gz, or Extract in the file manager). Inside are HPEngine-Launcher,
README.txt and the folder HPEngine/; keep them together.
Run HPEngine-Launcher (double-click; if the file manager asks, choose Execute, or allow running it in the
file's properties). Needs a Vulkan driver.
Pick the game's tab and add your game with Choose folder… or Choose files… (or drop it onto the window),
click Install, then Play. A disc image: mount it first (Steam Deck: right-click in Dolphin → Mount),
then add the mounted folder.

Steam Deck: in Desktop Mode, close Steam and choose Menu → Add to Steam… in the launcher (it keeps a backup of
Steam's shortcut list), or in Steam → Add a Game → Add a Non-Steam Game… → browse to HPEngine-Launcher. Then
start it from the Steam library (in Game Mode, and in Desktop Mode too). Started from Steam, the Deck's controls work
as a gamepad; started from a desktop shortcut, Steam keeps its desktop layout (trackpad as mouse, triggers as clicks)
until you hold the ≡ (Options) button.
The launcher keeps itself up to date on Windows and Linux too (signed updates only; the game data, saves and settings
are in your user folder and stay). A 0.2.0 launcher on Windows or Linux does not update itself: download and unpack
the new archive over it once.
Without the launcher: Harry Potter 1 (Windows, Linux)
From the unpacked folder, in a terminal:
HPEngine/HP1Setup <game folder, CD, installer or .zip> # checks the copy, copies the data into HPEngine/game/
HPEngine/HPEngine # plays
(Windows: HPEngine\HP1Setup.exe, HPEngine\HPEngine.exe.) A game installer (Inno Setup Setup.exe with its .bin
files, or InstallShield data1.cab) is unpacked, never run. HP1Setup prints the edition it found and refuses to write
into a folder that holds a game it did not install.
Without the launcher: Harry Potter 2
HPEngine/HP1Setup --game hp2 --dest <folder> <game folder or CD>
HPEngine/HPEngine --root <folder>
Manually, into your game folder: Harry Potter 1 (all systems)
If you already have the game installed (or its installed folder copied from a Windows PC), HPEngine can run it in
place. The game folder is the one with System/ and Maps/.

Download the archive for your system from Releases: HPEngine-win-x64.zip,
HPEngine-linux-x64.tar.gz, or for macOS HPEngine-osx-arm64.tar.gz (Intel Mac: HPEngine-osx-x64.tar.gz).
Unpack it into the game folder. Nothing in it overwrites a game file.
Run it:

Windows: HPEngine Launcher.exe (unpacked into a game folder it works with that game: nothing is installed and
it never removes your folder), or HPEngine\HPEngine.exe directly.
Linux / Steam Deck: ./HPEngine-Launcher, or ./HPEngine/HPEngine. On a case-sensitive file system keep the
original file names exactly (System, Maps, Lev_Tut1.unr, ...).
macOS: this archive has no launcher and no wrapper folder: tar -C <game folder> -xzf HPEngine-osx-arm64.tar.gz,
then xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <game folder> and run ./HPEngine from Terminal.

The engine also takes the game folder as --root <game folder>. If the game is not found, HPEngine shows what is
missing and exits with code 4.

Harry Potter 2 is installed into HP2Data/game beside the first game's folder; its saves and settings are in
HP2Data/Save and HP2Data/HPEngineData, kept when you install again or remove the game (unless you ask to delete
them too).
Without the launcher the HP1 game folder is HPEngine/game/ (HP1Setup) or your own game folder (manual install). The
launcher's Menu opens the saves and the logs folder (This game). The shipped .ini files are never rewritten. Saves are in
HPEngine's own format: they stay loadable across HPEngine versions, but saves of the original games are not read.
Game language
The launcher's Language row lists the languages included in your game files (it is shown only when there is
more than one). Select one before pressing
Play; the choice is remembered. For multilingual discs, the language is read from each numbered System folder's
Default.ini, rather than assuming folder 0 is the language you want. The corresponding text, dialogue, menu art
and splash are used together. Game default restores the original data selection.
No language files are downloaded. If your copy contains only one language, you need your own game data containing
another language to use it. Original files stay unchanged: the engine builds a working copy (links where available) in
HPEngineData/modroot, and applies enabled mods after the selected language. As in the original game, a package with
the language's suffix (such as AllDialog.fin_uax) is opened before the plain one (AllDialog.uax). Saves stay in the
normal Save folder; selecting a language does not change the list of script mods recorded in saves. Removing a
selected language is reported as an error until you select an available language or Game default.
The launcher separates multilingual data from its engine family. For example, the Nordic language set shares the
engine family called UK 1.1; that match does not identify a UK disc. Different data means the Nordic files
differ from that family's reference manifest, which alone does not establish that a disc was modified. The language
set is detected from installed files; identifying an exact source image requires its volume information and hashes.
Controls and settings
Keyboard and mouse work as in the original (rebind keys in Options → Controls); Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen.
A gamepad works out of the box (not original): left stick moves, right stick looks, A jumps, X or the right trigger
casts, B skips, Start opens the book; Options → Controls shows and rebinds the gamepad's buttons while you use it.
Chamber of Secrets differs: A also does the broom action, B skips a cut-scene, Back / View opens the map, the d-pad
picks the duel spell; its Controls page shows the gamepad but cannot rebind yet.
HP1: any key skips the start-up splash screens, and Space turns a story-book page once it has been shown for 2 seconds (not
original: the original allows both only in its hidden debug mode, and never from a story's first page).
The full layout, interface size, the original-look mode and the other HPEngine settings:
docs/settings.md.
Mods
Existing mods can be switched on and off without changing your game copy, for both games in the same way. Each game
tab has a Mods row that opens its Mods page:

Add Mod… (or drop the mod onto the Mods page) takes the mod's folder, its .zip, .7z or .rar archive, or a
single game file such as a map (.unr). The launcher copies it into Mods/<mod name>/ in that game's folder; one
wrapper folder around the mod (as in Mod-v1.zip/Mod-v1/System/...) is dropped. A mod's installer (.exe) is
never run: unpack the mod first. You can also put the files into the folder yourself (Open Mods Folder). Loose
packages such as HPBase.u are fine: each file goes where the game itself looks for that kind of file.
Switch the mod on (or add Enabled=<mod name> under [Mods] in Mods.ini; see Where things are).
When two mods change the same file, the launcher numbers the enabled mods in apply order and the higher number wins;
the Mods page names two enabled mods with the same file. × on a mod's row removes it (to the Trash / Recycle Bin).

A mod that adds its own maps: choose the map in Start map next to Play (without the launcher:
--map <map name>).
Your saved games stay in the same place with or without mods. A save made with a different set of script mods
restarts its level from the beginning, with the progress you had when you entered it; the game says so at the top of
the screen. A save made by 0.1.0 loads only with the mods off.
This is a beta: a mod may not work. Small mods (changed scripts, textures, translations, single maps) are the ones to
expect to work. Checked on 0.3.0: every map of 11 popular mods, including Restored + Free Play, loads, except two maps
named Entry (they have no player start; the original stops on them too) and Sofas and Armchairs, which needs a class
from Harry Potter 2. Mods made for the fan 1.55 may misbehave on 1.53. If a mod fails, the launcher shows the reason:
please report it with the mod's name. Check any other bug without mods before reporting it.
Chamber of Secrets: the mods published so far (maps, cutscene and script mods) are made for Metallicafan212's later HP2
engine and editor; their packages have a newer format than the retail game's, and HPEngine cannot open them yet. The
Mods page says so under such a mod, and Play refuses while it is on. A mod for the retail game is expected to load.
Known issues
Both games:

macOS and Windows builds are not signed: Gatekeeper and SmartScreen warn on first launch.
No .app bundle in the manual archive on macOS; run from Terminal or use the launcher.
Please report anything that differs from the original: see Reporting a bug.

Harry Potter 1:

Native Windows startup and localized menus were tested on Windows 11 Pro 26H2 (OS build 26300.9818) with the Nordic
multilingual CD. A full campaign and save/load on Windows still need verification; earlier tests were under CrossOver.
Mods are in beta: a mod not listed in Mods has not been checked and may not work.
UK 1.1 and Russian: they play through, but are not yet proven exact against those builds. Russian menu text uses a substitute font
(not original). Other releases (European English and the other languages) are unverified: they install and run with
a warning, and nobody has checked them yet. Modified copies (patches, mods, modded re-releases) also install and run
with a warning; please check a bug with the unmodified game before reporting it.

Harry Potter 2 (first beta):

Its campaign has not yet been played through to the end on HPEngine; please report anything that stops you.
Rebinding keys or buttons on its Controls page is not available yet.

1r3717i.title: ВС РФ атаковали Киевскую область: в Вишневом под обстрел попал магазин, есть погибшие
1r3717i.content:
В городе Вишневое в Бучанском районе Киевской области в результате атаки российских войск погибли два человека, еще восемь пострадали. Об этом сообщила Киевская областная военная администрация (ОВА) в Telegram в воскресенье, 22 ноября.

По ее данным, удар пришелся по магазину, в котором находились покупатели. Один из пострадавших - в тяжелом состоянии. Пожар в здании ликвидирован. Украинские Telegram-каналы пишут, что российский беспилотник попал в торговый центр "Новус".

В Белоцерковском районе пожар

Глава Киевской ОВА Тимур Ткаченко также рассказал, что в Белоцерковском районе Киевской области из-за атаки ВС РФ возник пожар в частном доме. Погиб мужчина, его тело спасатели извлекли из-под завалов. Еще четыре человека пострадали. Одну женщину госпитализировали с черепно-мозговой травмой, еще одна получила травмы в результате взрывной волны.

В Белой Церкви в результате падения обломков российского БПЛА возле магазина ранены два человека, они госпитализированы. Повреждены частный жилой дом, два автомобиля и предприятие, добавил Ткаченко.

В поселке Дымер спасли ребенка

В поселке Дымер Вышгородского района из-под завалов жилого дома, согласно последним данным, извлечены тела трех погибших, но удалось спасти ребенка.

Подъезд пятиэтажного жилого дома был разрушен в результате ночного удара российской армии. Ранее сообщалось о двух погибших и вероятности нахождения под завалами до 15 человек. Поисково-спасательная операция на месте удара продолжается.

1j0dobu.title: CD Projekt RED не собирается копировать GTA 6 в Cyberpunk 2, несмотря на масштаб игры Rockstar
1j0dobu.content:
Выход GTA 6 произвёл огромное впечатление на игровую индустрию. Многие разработчики восхищаются масштабом, детализацией и техническими достижениями проекта Rockstar, однако считают, что другим студиям не стоит пытаться повторить его успех любой ценой.
Креативный директор Cyberpunk 2 Игорь Саржиньский признал, что новая Grand Theft Auto может вызвать у разработчиков открытых миров чувство подавленности. Он с иронией назвал GTA 6, возможно, величайшим художественным достижением в истории, отметив её масштаб, насыщенность деталями, целостность и продуманность.
«Это технологическое и творческое чудо», — написал Саржиньский в Bluesky, пошутив, что Cyberpunk 2 отменена, а сам он теперь собирается подметать осенние листья во дворе.
Впрочем, разработчик быстро уточнил, что CD Projekt RED не собирается отказываться от проекта или пытаться напрямую конкурировать с Rockstar.
«На самом деле, я думаю, мы создаём что-то своё, с другим уникальным характером», — добавил он. По словам Саржиньского, GTA 6 впечатляет так же, как и любое великое произведение искусства: она расширяет представления о возможном и воплощает захватывающую творческую задумку практически безупречно.
С ним согласен и руководитель издательского направления Larian Studios Майкл Доуз. Он отметил, что в непростое время особенно приятно видеть, как игра объединяет людей разных поколений и интересов вокруг общего культурного события.
«Не каждая игра должна быть GTA. Это оставляет пространство для других типов проектов и делает такие редкие события ещё более особенными», — написал Доуз.
Дизайнер Naughty Dog Майкл Барклай также сравнил впечатления от GTA 6 с тем, как Bugatti Veyron могла бы выглядеть в глазах испуганного ребёнка викторианской эпохи.
В индустрии уже звучали подобные заявления после выхода Baldur’s Gate 3 в 2023 году. Тогда разработчики предупреждали, что не стоит пытаться повторить масштаб ролевой игры, её интерактивность, объём озвучки и множество сюжетных развилок.
При этом GTA 6 не должна становиться обязательным ориентиром для всех студий. Руководитель издательского направления Rockstar Дженнифер Колбе недавно опровергла слухи о бюджете в 2 миллиарда долларов, уточнив, что затраты на игру составили менее 1,5 миллиарда. Даже эта сумма остаётся недоступной для большинства разработчиков, особенно если учитывать, что Rockstar может рассчитывать на огромные доходы от GTA Online.
На фоне растущих бюджетов разработка крупных игр становится всё более рискованной: неудачный релиз способен привести к массовым увольнениям или закрытию студии. Поэтому стремление превзойти GTA 6 может оказаться опасным для индустрии.

1cfq8dn.title: David Leitch Gives ‘Ocean’s 14’ Update, Notes “Lot Of Motivation” To Make Sequel
1cfq8dn.content:
Nearly 20 years later, Danny Ocean is trying to get the gang back together for Ocean’s 14, which was expected to begin filming in 2026.

David Leitch, who is attached to direct the fourth installment in the heist film franchise, recently noted that George Clooney and his Smokehouse producing partner Grant Heslov have delivered a “great script,” but scheduling issues stand in the way.

“Oh, I mean, there’s a great script and I think everybody’s excited about moving it forward,” he told People. “I think it’s always been about getting all those people together, and their schedules are always the issue.”

Leitch added, “Look, there’s a lot of excitement around it and … George and Grant did incredible work on the script. So, yeah, a lot of motivation to make it happen.”

Clooney starred as Danny Ocean in the 2001 Steven Soderbergh-helmed remake of the 1960 Rat Pack film, reprising the role in Ocean’s Twelve (2004) and Ocean’s Thirteen (2007).

In January 2025, Leitch was in early talks to direct the next installment. Last October, the 2x Oscar winner Warner Bros. approved the budget for Ocean’s 14, which he expected to begin filming this year.

Ocean’s 14 will mark the first installment in the main franchise not directed by Soderbergh, after Gary Ross helmed the 2018 female-led spin-off Ocean’s 8, starring Sandra Bullock as Danny’s sister Debbie Ocean.

Meanwhile, Bradley Cooper is attached direct an Ocean’s 11 prequel, which will star himself and Margot Robbie as Danny Ocean’s parents.

nxa5tf.title: Rockstar сэкономила $600 тысяч на музыке GTA 3 благодаря неожиданной сделке с Sony
nxa5tf.content:
Rockstar Games предусмотрела более 600 тысяч долларов на музыкальное сопровождение Grand Theft Auto 3, однако эти деньги так и остались нетронутыми. Бывший руководитель Take-Two Келли Самнер рассказал, как благодаря сделке с Sony разработчикам удалось получить лицензии на музыку бесплатно.

Музыка давно стала одной из визитных карточек серии Grand Theft Auto. Благодаря играм GTA такие композиции, как «I Ran (So Far Away)» группы A Flock of Seagulls и «The Rhythm of the Night» Corona, получили новую популярность среди нескольких поколений игроков. GTA 3 также запомнилась своими радиостанциями, включая Flashback FM, целиком посвящённую музыке из фильма «Лицо со шрамом».
В интервью The Game Business журналист Кристофер Дринг поговорил с бывшими руководителями PlayStation и Take-Two о соглашении, благодаря которому GTA 3 вышла эксклюзивно на PlayStation 2. Во время беседы Самнер поделился подробностями о музыкальном бюджете игры.
По его словам, сотрудник Rockstar по маркетингу Терри Донован сумел связаться с Томми Моттолой, который в то время возглавлял Sony и был одной из влиятельных фигур музыкальной индустрии. Моттола лично приехал в офис компании в нью-йоркском районе Сохо, где Донован договорился о необычной сделке.
«У GTA 3 был музыкальный бюджет более чем в полмиллиона долларов, но Терри каким-то образом связался с Томми Моттолой. Моттола буквально сел в машину и приехал к нам в Сохо, где мы тогда находились. Терри заключил сделку: мы получили музыку бесплатно. Взамен мы предоставили им права на CD», — рассказал Самнер.
По словам бывшего руководителя Take-Two, соглашение оказалось выгодным для обеих сторон. Rockstar получила необходимые композиции для радиостанций GTA 3, а Sony — права на выпуск музыки на компакт-дисках. В результате разработчики смогли сохранить весь предусмотренный музыкальный бюджет.
Недавно вышедшая GTA 6 также использует лицензированные композиции на игровых радиостанциях. Кроме того, для игры выпустили отдельный музыкальный альбом с участием таких исполнителей, как Лана Дель Рей и Cardi B.

14lpole.title: The Hotel Bel-Air’s Menu Returns to Tradition
14lpole.content:
Since Wolfgang Puck’s 2023 departure from the Hotel Bel-Air and its eponymous restaurant, the luxury lodging has been tweaking its Cal-Med menus with classical French techniques and hyper-seasonal ingredients. The approach was ambitious, evolving, at times even experimental. Yet the largely local dining clientele — 70 percent of weekly regulars are neighbors — who treat the place as a second home (or maybe a fourth, given their net worth) have made it clear they prefer familiarity over ingenuity. Under new executive chef Ralf Schlegel (far left), previously of The Peninsula in Beverly Hills, the kitchen has turned back toward the classics.

The bill of fare has long had a dedicated section of “Bel-Air Classics”: the tortilla soup, the club sandwich, the chopped salad named for late No. 1 fan Nancy Reagan. Now, the restaurant has restored several other salads that had been relegated to off-menu, only-by-request status — Thai-style chicken, soy ginger BBQ salmon, burrata with squash — along with the house burger.

“When you go home, you want what you remember,” explains Hotel Bel-Air manager Tiffany Lai, who insists the restaurant’s back-to-basics pivot won’t condemn it to culinary ossification. “We’re still busy creating new favorites.” She points to the German-born, Austria-raised Schlegel’s signature dish: chicken schnitzel with lemon paprika (left). “Maybe in 15 years that’ll be the next classic.”

This story appeared in the Nov. 18 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Click here to subscribe.

1uuct8.title: After 114 Years, the Beverly Hills Hotel Gets a (Night)life
1uuct8.content:
Wearing a hard hat and a tailored suit, Beverly Hills Hotel general manager John Scanlon surveys the most significant expansion in the iconic Pink Palace’s 114-year history. Amid the BRRRAAAP! of drills and SKREEEE! of scraping metal, he outlines a slate of new amenities, a decade in the making, including a supper club, a screening room and a cocktail bar.

“I’m going to bed at night dreaming about this and waking up thinking about it,” says Scanlon, a Dorchester Collection veteran who previously ran London’s 45 Park Lane. “It’s the first thought that comes into my head in the morning: ‘Where are we at? What have we got to do today?’ ”

Right now, in the lead-up to their simultaneous debut in the coming weeks, the answer is: a lot. Finalize the menus. Hire more staff. Approve the live acts. Close out permits. Eyeball every aesthetic detail. On a terrace, among the property’s paddle-shaped banana leaf plants, Scanlon says in his Irish brogue, with traces of exhilaration and exhaustion, “I’m obsessed.”

The Beverly Hills Hotel, which opened in 1912.

Courtesy of Hotel

Later, over a lunch of McCarthy salads at the Polo Lounge, alongside the hotel’s new food-and-beverage head Megan Doherty, Scanlon explains that this is all an attempt to better serve guests, especially locals. A consultant — in his accounting, a “social anthropologist” — asked regulars what they wanted as the hotel considered renovations to a sizable swath of neglected, interconnected square footage, on the lobby level to the left of the red carpeted entrance, ranging from an unpopular bedroom suite to a ’90s-era business center that “nobody was using anymore.”

Foremost, it turned out, was a desire for a real nightlife option for party-hardly Beverly Hills. The solution is The Supper Club: a 94-seat, high-glam ovular room with skyline views of Century City that aims for neo-retro, akin to Delilah in West Hollywood. Open until 1 a.m., it will feature a no-photos policy, throwback palm tree motifs, coastal Italian dishes from chef Mattia Agazzi (previously of Gucci Osteria) and a sequence of live evening performances, including five-piece bands, which are curated by music director Alex Le Roux, an in-demand industry booker for events like the wedding of Brooklyn Beckham and Nicola Peltz. “This concept perfectly fits into the heritage of this hotel, but allows us to do something fresh,” says Doherty, who previously ran operations for star L.A. chef Evan Funke.

The scene at the hotel in 1921.

Courtesy of Hotel

The research also produced a 14-seat screening room, which is tricked out for sound to handle record-release listening events. Its design by Ken Fulk (clients include Pharrell Williams and Gigi Hadid) is inspired by the Holmby Hills screening room of , Louis B. Mayer’s daughter and Hollywood’s preeminent hostess, where she showed films to friends before release.

For his part, Scanlon seems perhaps most enthused about a new, yet-unnamed cocktail bar — “very intimate, very elegant” — which he promises will rival the Dorchester’s offerings, as well as a lobby-oriented lounge, boasting a wraparound veranda, which will present afternoon tea service: “We’ll have bespoke teas and hand-painted china from Royal Crown Derby and custom sterling silver tea stands that have been made by Arthur Price. It’s a Claridge’s-level experience.”

A rendering of the hotel’s new 14-seat screening room.

Ken Fulk International for The Beverly Hills Hotel

A key challenge for the new spaces is competing with the landmark existing ones, chiefly the Polo Lounge, the Fountain Coffee Room and the Cabana Café. “Our guests know and love and really connect with them, and there’s this nostalgia there,” Scanlon explains. “They are tractor beams. So, with what we’re doing now, it’s been about, ‘What can we do that’s distinctive?’ They need to shine on their own.” He adds, looking up from his McCarthy salad, “a lot of places take the most popular dish off the menu. That’s crazy to me. Make another popular dish!”

This story appeared in the Nov. 18 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Click here to subscribe.

151gyw7.title: Sheila Mangubat Dead: '90 Day Fiancé' Star Was 35
151gyw7.content:
Sheila Mangubat, who appeared on the reality series “90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days,” has died. She was 35.

David Dangerfield, Mangubat’s former fiancé, announced her death in an Instagram post shared on Saturday. A cause of death was not shared.

“It breaks my heart to share the news from her family that Sheila passed away on Saturday in the Philippines,” he wrote. “I am devastated and still trying to process this loss. Please keep her son, her family, and me in your prayers. Thank you for all your love and support.”

Dangerfield and Mangubat first connected in 2021 through a Facebook group for deaf singles, and dated long-distance (Dangerfield lived in Omaha, Neb. at the time, while Mangubat was born and raised in the Philippines). The two went on to get engaged, and their relationship was documented on the sixth season of TLC’s “90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days,” which aired in 2023. The couple split in Oct. 2025 following K-1 visa issues.

“90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days” follows Americans who believe they’ve found their soulmate online, per TLC’s official description. They then travel abroad to meet them in person for the first time, navigating cultural differences while deciding whether or not to get engaged. “90 Day Fiancé” follows already engaged couples who must decide whether to ultimately get married or break up.

Mangubat’s sister, Grace, also shared a tribute to the reality star, as was reported by People. “Rest in peace my beloved sister Shiela Mangubat… fly high my sister we will miss you,” she wrote in a Facebook post.

Mangubat is survived by her son, Jhonreil.

h0qere.title: GTA 6: Full Alien UFO questline walkthrough
h0qere.content: Grand Theft Auto 6 is hiding an incredible alien easter egg, and it goes further than anything we’ve previously seen in the series.Rockstar Games has always had a fascination with aliens and cryptids, and GTA 6 is no different. Only this one goes a step further and has a full alien questline for you to uncover if you keep your eyes open.In this guide, we’re breaking down how to start the new Alien UFO questline easter egg and the surprisingly amazing rewards you get for finishing it in Grand Theft Auto 6. When it’s all done, you’ll get The Truth Is Out There trophy and achievement.Starting the alien questline, UFO easter egg – GTA 6The first step is finding a car on the side of the road with its doors open and lights flashing. This will only happen at night, but can happen in a large variety of locations around Leonida. It will only be possible after starting Chapter 2. We found this first step of the alien questline while searching for all of GTA 6’s Meditation Spots.A good place to start looking is the quiet roads to the East of Port Gellhorn and North Kelly County. There’s no guaranteed way to spawn the encounter, but sleeping until night and driving around the darkest and quietest roads in Leonida is a good place to start.Once you’ve found the car, you’ll also find a trail of clothes leading away from it. Follow them, and you’ll find a bright light with a naked woman hovering in the air. Interact with her to speak with her, and she’ll ask you to bring her car over. Try to, and your player character will have a close encounter before waking up in the same place during the daytime. You’ve been gone for three days.Alien UFO dream, light puzzle – GTA 6When you go to sleep as the protagonist who got abducted, you will eventually have a nightmare about being aboard the UFO.Inside, you’ll first be greeted with the solar system in alignment. Inspecting Earth will show you a location that you can find in Leonida. Make note of the fenced-off, angular building, and the large tower, as those are the most recognizable bits of the scene.Next you’ll find a keypad, and the solution is written above the keypad, only with lines instead of numbers. Two horizontal lines are a 2, four lines are a 4, etc. In our case, the code was “2431”, though it may change with playthroughs.In the next room is a light puzzle you must complete. You have access to four buttons connected to four lights, and each light has three stages: off, red, and blue. You must light them all blue to continue; only some of the buttons control more than one light. The buttons work as follows:First button: Light #1 onlySecond button: Light #1 and #2Third button: Light #2 and #3Fourth button: Light #3 and #4It’s an awkward puzzle to complete. You should aim to light all lights red, and then press the Second and Fourth buttons to activate them all once, turning them all blue. This will allow you to continue.This will allow you to access three doors. This mini-puzzle is simple: you must take the “milk” from the left room and place it in the machine in the right room. The center door leads to radiation that will damage you.Eventually, you will wake up from the nightmare, safe in bed. But you will wonder where the location shown to you in the dream actually is, and you can find it within Leonida.Alien dream location solution – GTA 6The building shown to you in the dream can be found in the swamp to the South of Hamlet, in Pelican Valley. It’s just West of the main road leading North from Key Lento that goes over the Shoeless Keys.Finding it is pretty easy; getting in is harder, as the place is surrounded by barbed wire fences and gates that won’t open. Make sure to take a large vehicle, and then drive around to the rear of the building. There’s a metal structure that forms a path over the barbed wire fence, but you’ll need leverage like a truck or van to jump on top and get inside the compound. You can use the nearby metal structures to climb up and over the metal rail, but it’s more difficult than it’s worth. Once inside, the character that was abducted will remark that this is the place from their dream, “the place in the orb”.Once inside, you’ll find a door locked by a keypad, and you’ll already have the code, as it’s the same as the one from your dream. Go down the elevator, and follow the linear path forward to find a control room with the same light puzzle from the dream, and the same three doors.Complete the puzzle and carry the milk precisely as in the dream, and the way forward will open.You will meet an alien. Like, no, actually. An alien in Grand Theft Auto. Take it to the surface, and it will be taken to its people. Unfortunately, the cops arrive shortly after. They’re the unfortunate ones, though, as the UFO will help you get your freedom as a parting gift.Alien UFO easter egg quest rewards – GTA 6As a reward for finding the cryptic location and freeing the alien, both Jason and Lucia will be given permanent buffs to their Health, Stamina, and Focus. A nice thank-you from the aliens before they go home. Cal would love to hear about this.

6irlro.title: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
6irlro.content:
In his new book “Hyperscale,” journalist Paris Marx investigates the impact of data centers and generative AI, taking readers inside the data centers themselves and explaining how computing infrastructure that goes back decades recently became a political landmine.

The book is well-timed, to put it mildly, as data center backlash seems to have been one of the motivators for the massive blue wave seen in the recent midterm elections. And those debates are likely to continue as Democrats wield more governmental power.

In an interview with TechCrunch, Marx described the data center buildout as “fundamentally unsustainable” and “completely out of line with a livable planet,” while also arguing that these facilities make for an obvious target amidst broader anger at the tech industry. After all, if a data center is being built in your community, “it’s very physical, it’s very material.”

“It doesn’t matter what side of the political spectrum that you’re on,“ Marx said. “You are going to feel the effects of that in your quality of life, in your power bill, potentially in your access to water, potentially in what you hear around your community, if these air conditioning units on the roofs of data centers are making a lot of noise.”

He also suggested that data center opposition is only the most visible piece of a wider movement targeting “the physical manifestations of the tech industry, […] whether it’s the opposition to Flock cameras rolling out across the United States, or the smart glasses that Meta is trying to put on people’s faces, or even the self-driving cars that Waymo is rolling out.”

During our conversation (which I’ve edited for length and clarity), Marx and I discussed data centers’ environmental impact, how tech companies are responding to community resistance, and what it’s actually like inside a data center.

I liked your description of trying to get access to the inside of a “hyperscale” data center and then eventually taking a tour [of one]. Could you talk a little bit more about what that experience was like? How did you get in? What surprised you when you actually got in? 

Getting inside of a hyperscale data center was not the easiest task in the world. I spoke to some researchers who have been doing research on data centers for a number of years longer than I had, and they told me that before the generative AI moment, and before all the attention that has been put on data centers recently, that it was quite a bit easier to do so. 

I sent emails to a number of companies asking if I could get inside, often didn’t get a response, other times got a no. I ended up, after visiting the outsides of some data centers in places like northern Virginia and Ireland and spots like that, I actually went down to New Zealand to go inside of a data center itself.  And the thing that struck me most was the level of security. 

Obviously, you would expect that this is an infrastructure that is really securitized, because the data inside needs to be kept safe, obviously [they] have these big fences and all the security cameras around the data centers. But to go inside, I had to send my passport in advance. Then when I got there, they had to check the passport, and then as we were going through the data center itself, every single door in the data center was locked unless you had a key card to unlock it.

Then, when you get inside of the server room itself, where all this computer hardware is stored in tall racks that look like cabinets — you can imagine, in your mind, that this would be kind of a sinister location, with some eerie lighting or something like that. But in truth, it’s just quite utilitarian. It’s a warm room with some air conditioning blasting into the servers from vents that are nearby. 

It was really loud as well, because you have all these fans running from all these servers, it was really kind of piercing. To be inside of this room, if you were going to be in there for a while, you’d probably want earplugs or something like that.

Before I read your book, I thought of data centers as something that’s important, but a little bit boring. How did you decide they were interesting and rich enough to sustain an entire book? 

I felt the same. I was aware that data centers had been out there, but it was not something that I was paying particularly close attention to. But then there were a number of stories that of tipped me off to the fact that there might be more here, and that it was worth looking deeper into what was going on — the first being hearing about the water pressures created by data centers in Chile around the capital of Santiago, where companies like Google and Microsoft were building data centers, and communities were concerned about their access to water and started organizing around that.

And then hearing about how much electricity data centers were consuming in Ireland, to the point that now they consume more than 20% of the country’s electricity, and that was obviously pushing up power prices. It was putting pressures on the grid, such that the grid operator actually put a moratorium in place for grid connections for data centers around the Dublin area, back in 2022. This was even before the generative AI moment that caused a surge in construction of data centers.

And then the other one was in The Dalles, Oregon, where Google had actually built its first company-owned data centers about 20 years back. In that case, its water deal was coming up for renewal. It wanted to build more data centers there, so it needed more water. And when the residents started asking, “How much water is Google actually using?” a journalist at The Oregonian went to the city and essentially asked, “Hey, how much water is Google using? Our readers would like to know this,” he was hit with a lawsuit instead of being given that information. Because Google did not want it to be public. And then, of course, when it did come out about a year later, Google revealed that it was using 29% of the city’s water, which seemed quite significant.

That was around when ChatGPT was being released and generative AI was starting to take off. It felt like, okay, there are these pockets of places where a lot of data centers have already been constructed, where they are putting pressures on the communities that are causing people to respond, and it felt like that was going to start coming to a lot more communities. It was a good time to really start to dig in and pay attention.

You don’t just talk about the data centers’ environmental impact, but also, they [become] your way in to talk about this broader tech moment. They represent to you — particularly the hyperscale data centers — represent to you how these tech companies are doing business now. 

Absolutely. The hyperscale data centers and just the scale of the construction — whether it’s the the size of the actual facilities themselves or the number that these companies are trying to build out, just feels fundamentally unsustainable. 

They’re just demanding too much from the communities where they’re being located, whether that’s because of electricity or because of water use or what have you, or just the fact that they’re building out so many, that when you think about the cumulative impact and you look at the demand for water, but particularly for energy from fossil fuels, that means that it’s just completely out of line with a livable planet and an amount of computation that feels like it makes any degree of sense for us to have constructed.

I think it really goes back to the hubris of the tech industry and of these major tech companies and the tech billionaires that run them, and the fact that they have these particular visions of the future that are based on fantasies, but also on expanding their own power and influence over the world, and they don’t seem to mind that everyone else then has to pay the cost that comes with their ambitions and what they are seeking to do.

And I feel like it’s become particularly egregious with generative AI and the data centers to power them, where many of the benefits that were supposed to come of generative AI do not appear to have materialized — whether those are the economic benefits, the productivity benefits, but also the the benefits of delivery of services like healthcare and education to the public, as we heard Sam Altman saying a lot in the in the early days of ChatGPT.

Paired with that, there has been this massive environmental cost […] but there’s also this massive and growing social cost, when you think about the mental health impacts of chatbot dependence, of all the false information that pervades social media platforms now, of the deepfake crisis, and I could go on and on and on.

It’s not surprising that there has been backlash. But I have been surprised at how widespread it’s been, and also how bipartisan — you talk about Ron DeSantis and Bernie Sanders both being opposed to data centers. Why do you think it’s become such a unifying issue? 

Because it’s not an abstract issue, right? I think even when we think about generative AI or social media or something like that, [it] can feel abstract. It’s a service that you access from your phone or from your computer. It’s not something that is tangible in the world. 

But when a data center is coming to set up shop in your community, it’s very physical, it’s very material. It doesn’t matter what side of the political spectrum that you’re on. You are going to feel the effects of that in your quality of life, in your power bill, potentially in your access to water, potentially in what you hear around your community, if these air conditioning units on the roofs of data centers are making a lot of noise.

I think that there was already a pre-existing frustration with the tech industry that came from the quality of the products, the effects that they’re having on our society and our lives. For some people, [they have] frustration with the way that the tech industry has been collaborating with the Trump administration and with right-wing political groups in different parts of the world. But then you add on top of that the actual effects that come of having one of these infrastructures be planned or located in your community, and that anger gets kind of directed into that physical manifestation of this thing that you have an issue with.

Obviously, the data centers are at the forefront of this, and it’s what we pay the most attention to. But we also see this increasingly with other aspects of the tech industry, whether it’s the opposition to Flock cameras rolling out across the United States, or the smart glasses that Meta is trying to put on people’s faces, or even the self-driving cars that Waymo is rolling out.

There’s a lot of frustration with the physical manifestations of the tech industry, because that is something that can really be felt more directly, but can also be challenged more directly. You can delete an app on your phone, but what difference does that really make to the company? It doesn’t often seem like very much. 

The tech companies have reacted to this backlash in a few different ways. One is that Microsoft, Amazon, and  OpenAI have all talked about [their commitment] that they’re not going to use NDAs anymore in their negotiations with local governments. How big a difference do you think that will make? 

Not a huge difference.

I do think it’s going to be good that it will be easier for people to access information on these projects that are being located in their communities. But part of the reason why we’re seeing these shifts is exactly in response to that opposition.

We’re seeing the tech companies propose to pay for more of the electricity infrastructure that will be required for their data centers to reduce the pressure on ratepayers, because people are angry about that. They’re promising to use different water-based cooling systems in their data centers, to say that they’re able to use less electricity. 

When we look at the NDAs and the decision or the announcement that they’re not going to use those anymore, I think it’s also because it’s working against them. People know what a data center is now, and if people find out that a data center is coming to town and they have questions and they’re not getting answers, that’s only going to further fuel the opposition to those data centers.

So, it’s not really a surprise to see [the tech companies] do this, and it’s a way that they can get a positive PR thing by saying, “We’re not going to use these NDAs that are working against us anyway. “

One of the other ways they’ve responded is by saying that there’s a lot of misinformation about the environmental harms, or that they’re being overstated, or that they can mitigate them with renewable technology. How valid do you think those arguments are? 

I think that the industry recognizes that there is a lot of concern and they’re trying to basically move into the discussion with narratives of their own to have people question whether data centers are really a problem or not.

I feel like we don’t see the industry doing as much on the energy side anymore, particularly on the fossil fuel side, because they realize that they have kind of lost that argument. If you look back a year and a half, two years ago, they were talking a lot about renewables, about nuclear energy, you don’t hear so much of that discourse anymore.

They have pivoted, instead, to focus on the water question, where I think that they feel that they can use more abstract national figures in order to confuse the public about what’s going on. They can say, “If you look nationally, agriculture and golf courses also use a lot of water. So you don’t need to be worried about a data center coming to tow,n because they don’t use as much, in aggregate.”

But the issue with data center water use is not a national issue. It’s a local issue. There are unquestionably going to be communities where they seek to locate data centers that are going to have plenty of water and that are not going to be concerned about a data center coming to town. But they’re also locating [data centers] in a lot of communities that are experiencing high degrees of water stress, which means that they don’t have the water to really provide to these infrastructures.

We have also seen them pivoting to move away from the evaporative cooling systems, the ones that require a lot of water — because you need to take in a certain amount of water as it gets too hot, it evaporates away, and so you can see why you need a consistent flow of water into the data center for that type of cooling system —  to a closed loop system, where you basically have a certain amount of water, it stays within the data center, you keep cooling it down by using electricity to do that, and so you clearly don’t need as much water.

That is their new way to say, “Hey, don’t worry about the water use. We’re going to switch to this other system.” But the issue there, of course, is that it does require more electricity in order to keep that water cooled down, and that is often not part of what they talk about or discuss when they are proposing that as an alternative.

Then the other thing is that it’s not just water that is in those pipes or tubes going through the data center. There’s also a lot of coolant in there, a lot of chemicals, and communities where these projects are being located with closed loop cooling systems are becoming increasingly concerned about those coolants leaking out into their water supply and what that is going to mean.

In the book, you say repeatedly that you’re not against technology itself or even data centers in general, but [against] this hyperscale approach. The book is called “Hyperscale.” The last chapter is called “Human Scale.” Why do you see scale as such an important part of the problem? 

Because scale is what creates the pressures, whether those are the pressures on the communities or you know the pressures on our wider electricity system and whatnot.

I don’t think that the inherent problem is data centers, because we have had data centers for a long time, and sure, there have been occasional concerns about specific projects, but data centers as a whole have not been an issue that the public has felt merited this degree of attention. So that is why I feel the hyperscale data center, and particularly the acceleration that we’ve seen in the expansion of the size of these hyperscale data centers, but also the number of data centers that these companies are building out, is notable in this moment.

Linked to that is not just the scale of the demand created by these hyperscale data centers, but also, what they are supposed to be powering? That is where the other disconnect lies. They’re demanding a lot, but if we were actually getting something good for it, this might be justified. I think that for a lot of people, and I feel like we see this reflected in polling, they’re not actually seeing the benefits from generative AI.

So then the question becomes: “Okay, we’re expending all of these resources, we’re pushing up emissions such that climate change is going to be accelerated just to build out all these data centers to meet the ambitions of generative AI that the tech companies have, but then we’re not actually getting much benefit out of that technology. So what are we actually doing here?” 

One other thing that really struck a chord with me was your description about how tech executives often talk about the future as if there’s [just one] inevitable future. The only thing that’s in question is how quickly we arrive there [and] who’s going to make the most money off of it.

This is so important for me, because I do feel like how we think about the future then shapes decisions that we make. The tech billionaires, they see the future in a certain way […] and I think that they have been very successful in getting us to buy into their vision of the future for the past several decades. But that does not mean that that is the only way that the future has to be.

We can imagine a very different kind of future, and that would mean that we place our resources in different places and actually develop technology in a different way, toward different outcomes, with different incentives driving that work. 

There are interesting conversations happening in different parts of the world right now around things like digital sovereignty, getting off of these technologies from the U.S. tech companies. But in some cases, those conversations are quickly captured by industry in those different parts of the world to say, “Okay, we want to get off U.S. technology, but let’s have our local companies do effectively the same thing, and just let them do the same exploitative practices and make the money that the U.S. tech companies would be making.” And I don’t think that that is the right way forward.

I also think that there is a role for public sector development of technology in a way that we’ve eschewed or even looked at skeptically for the past number of decades, because the idea was that technology had to be left to the private sector. What we’re starting to see in Europe is a bit more funding of public technology, in order to develop the services that government itself depends on, and I think that that is a good first step.

But especially when we’re looking at the Microsoft outage that happened just recently, and we’re looking at Google threatening schools with their access to Google search if they don’t accept Google AI tool, I think that there’s a real moment right now to put resources into developing something different, that doesn’t come from these major tech companies, and that hopefully can have much more public benefit than what these companies now provide us.
