gh-1423433613.title: GitHub - skuza-oss/downhill-revived: A PC port of Downhill Domination (PS2), built on a matching decompilation. Bring your own disc.
gh-1423433613.content:
A PC port of Downhill Domination.
Downhill Revived is a native 64-bit Windows port of Downhill Domination (PlayStation 2, Incognito
Entertainment / SCEA, 2003), with experimental builds for Macs with Apple silicon and for 64-bit
Linux. It is built on a matching decompilation: C/C++ source that compiles back to the original
game program byte for byte, built for the PC with the PS2 hardware replaced by native code.
Download ·
Discord (news, help and races) ·
Players' guide (controls, online, texture packs, settings) ·
Support on Ko-fi
Features

A launcher with the settings, updates, release notes and the public online races.
A native renderer (Direct3D 12, Vulkan or Metal), 60 fps or more (up to 240) with even frame
pacing, 1x to 8x resolution, Hor+ widescreen at any shape, windowed, borderless or fullscreen.
Online races for 2 to 10 players (experimental), public or private with a code; after your
finish you watch the others ride to the line.
REVIVED SETTINGS in the game's own OPTIONS menu, a sharp font, Unlock All, the movies, memory
card saves, PCSX2 texture packs, mouse in the menus, Discord Rich Presence.
Controllers (Xbox, DualSense, DualShock 4, Switch Pro, 8BitDo and most others) and full
keyboard play, with your own keys and buttons (in the game or the launcher).
Automatic updates that never touch your settings or saves.

The full list and the known gaps: docs/PLAYING.md.
Getting started

Download the installer DownhillRevived-<version>-win-setup.exe from the
Releases page and run it (no
administrator rights needed). It isn't code-signed, so SmartScreen may ask: More info >
Run anyway. Or take DownhillRevived-<version>-win.zip and unzip it into a folder you can
write to (not Program Files) for a portable copy.
Start Downhill Revived and press PLAY.
The first time, choose your .iso of the USA disc (SCUS-97177). It is checked and
remembered.

Mac and Linux (experimental): the -mac-experimental.dmg (drag the app to Applications) or the
-linux-experimental.AppImage (one file, with the launcher's libraries inside; Steam Deck too),
or their zips. None of the downloads is signed by a developer certificate:
docs/PLAYING.md says how to allow them and where your files go. You
need Windows 10/11 64-bit (or an Apple silicon Mac, or Linux with glibc 2.35+ and Vulkan) and a
Direct3D 12 or Vulkan graphics card: minimum and recommended specs for every platform are in
docs/PLAYING.md.
Android (experimental): the -android-experimental.apk for arm64 phones and tablets on Android 10
or later (minimum: a Helio G80 / Snapdragon 680 class phone with 4 GB RAM), with touch controls;
every online race, as on the PC. The release page says how to install it.
Legal notice

This is a fan project. It is not made, endorsed or supported by Sony Interactive
Entertainment, Incognito Entertainment or anyone who holds rights to the game.
This repository and its releases contain no game data: no disc image, no game executable
or data from it, no IOP modules, no textures, sound, music or movies, and no BIOS. dhd.exe is
the translated code only; at every start it reads the game's data from your disc image, after
checking it is the unchanged original.
To play you need your own dump of the USA disc. Other regions and modified images are not
supported (why: docs/findings/100-other-releases.md).
The project sells nothing. Donations on Ko-fi are voluntary and unlock nothing: every release
is free and the same for everyone.

rh5qdb.title: Rockstar незаметно поменяла внешность персонажу GTA VI, который был похож на Мао Цзэдуна
rh5qdb.content:
Опрос

3DNews Новости Software PlayStation Rockstar незаметно поменяла внешность пе...

реклама

Новости Software

Самое интересное в обзорах

23.11.2026 [12:20],

Изменение дизайна второстепенного персонажа перед релизом — событие зачастую заурядное, но в случае с нашумевшим криминальным боевиком в открытом мире GTA VI от Rockstar Games привлекло к себе особое внимание.
Источник изображений: Rockstar Games

Напомним, прошедший в конце августа расширенный показ GTA VI обернулся небольшим скандалом среди китайских игроков вокруг детали, которая могла быть воспринята как оскорбление в адрес восточной страны.
Мелькнувший на 12-й минуте владелец ограбленного магазина напомнил китайским геймерам Мао Цзэдуна (Mao Zedong) — основателя Китайской Народной Республики и бывшего председателя Коммунистической партии Китая.

В Китае очень трепетно относятся к изображению «великого кормчего» в популярной культуре, так что ситуация рисковала вызвать вокруг GTA VI ещё и политическую напряжённость, но Rockstar уладила конфликт до его появления.
Как подметил пользователь SilentPanda с форума ResetEra, в преддверии релиза Rockstar изменила дизайн «двойника» Мао Цзэдуна и лишила его характерных черт лица бывшего китайского лидера (см. изображение ниже).

Тем временем стриминг GTA VI в Китае может привести к блокировке аккаунта, если не следовать установленным правилам: никаких откровенных нарядов, кровавых сцен, нападений на прохожих и полицейских или угонов транспортных средств.

GTA VI вышла 19 ноября на PS5, Xbox Series X и S. В преддверии релиза новинка заслужила звание самой высокооценённой игры за всю историю, но пользователи агрегатора Metacritic устроили проекту иной приём.

pf616z.title: Recipe for one of the world's most important cancer drugs uncovered: Tobacco plants could produce the medicine
pf616z.content:
This is the yew tree, which is the original source of the cancer drug Taxol (paclitaxel). Credit: Feiyan Liang, University of Copenhagen

More people around the world will receive a cancer diagnosis at some point in their lives. As this trend is expected to continue, researchers have been working to crack the code of how the widely used cancer drug Taxol (paclitaxel) is naturally produced, with the aim of making its production cheaper and more efficient in the future.

Today, Taxol, which is used to treat breast cancer, ovarian cancer and lung cancer, is produced through a long process that extracts related plant compounds from plants and converts them to the drug through a series of complex chemical reactions. This makes Taxol one of the most expensive medicines available.
"That is why it has been essential to understand how Taxol can be produced biosynthetically, so that treatment can become more accessible to patients around the world," says professor Sotirios Kampranis from the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, who is also the senior author of the study published in Nature Chemical Biology.
Taxol originally comes from the yew tree, where the active compound is produced in the bark. Although Taxol has long been produced for cancer treatment, there has never been a complete manual describing the process that the plants use to make it. Now, researchers have assembled that missing guide.
"We have tested numerous hypotheses to uncover the complete biological pathway for producing Taxol from start to finish. We now have a blueprint, essentially a recipe, that can be used to produce Taxol in plants, yeast or other systems. This could pave the way for new methods of producing Taxol that make manufacturing easier and the final product more affordable," says Kampranis.

This is the tobacco plant that the researchers have used to produce Taxol. Credit: Feiyan Liang, University of Copenhagen

Tobacco plant can produce cancer drug
In the study, the researchers took candidate genes responsible for Taxol production from the yew tree and introduced them into another plant, the tobacco species Nicotiana benthamiana. This plant grows quickly and is widely used in research.
"We introduced more than 20 of the yew tree genes into tobacco plants to demonstrate the entire biological process of Taxol production step by step," says Zhen Fan, a postdoctoral researcher at the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences and co-first author of the study.
The researchers succeeded in getting the tobacco plants to produce Taxol at levels comparable to those found naturally in yew tree bark.
"The tobacco plant is an effective platform for growing Taxol because it provides the same cellular environment as the yew tree but is a lot faster to grow and easier to engineer," says Kampranis.
For tobacco plants to be used in large-scale production in the future, the yew tree genes will need to become a stable part of the plant's own genetic makeup.
"That is the next major challenge. Large-scale production, for example in greenhouses, requires stable plants that permanently contain the yew genes, so that we do not have to introduce them every time," says Kampranis.
The key to cheaper treatment may lie in the new blueprint
In addition to using tobacco plants to produce the cancer drug, the researchers point to other possible production methods.
"Now that we have the crucial blueprint for biosynthetic Taxol production, there is potential to produce it in many different ways. We also see fermented yeast cells as a promising solution," says Kampranis.
Regardless of the method used, other researchers can now build on this blueprint to produce Taxol, opening up new possibilities.
"In Denmark, hospitals and patients are not as dependent on low-cost Taxol. But in many other parts of the world, affordable Taxol treatment is crucial. Our discovery could ultimately contribute to cheaper Taxol, making treatment more accessible in low-income countries," concludes Kampranis.

Publication details
Feiyan Liang et al., Complete biosynthesis and production of paclitaxel in a plant host, Nature Chemical Biology (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41589-026-02376-x

1u6i079.title: Bela Bajaria Reflects on Netflix, Says 'Stay Tuned' at Emmys
1u6i079.content:
Former Netflix executive Bela Bajaria put the emphasis on her belief in the transformative the power of storytelling in accepting the Founders Award Monday night at the International Emmy Awards in New York.

Bajaria was ousted from her role as chief content officer of Netflix in a very public fashion last month amid a larger shake-up of content leadership at the streaming giant. In her speech, her first major public appearance since her departure, Bajaria reflected on her career journey to the top echelon of Hollywood as a senior executive at CBS and Universal Television prior to joining Netflix in 2016.

In a nod to the Thanksgiving holiday this week, Bajaria opened by expressing her gratitude for the opportunities she’s been afforded since her family relocated to Southern California in the late 1970s when she was in grade school.

“Gratitude isn’t passive or soft. It’s earned. Gratitude is strength in knowing nothing is guaranteed and nothing can be taken for granted. Gratitude is the appreciation for both struggle and success, and sharing the journey with others,” Bajaria told the crowd.

During most of the past decade, Bajaria was focused on building out Netflix’s local-language TV content operation at a scale never before seen in the industry. The experience was profound as the regional teams set off on a search for new creative voices.

“Whether I was in Mumbai or Madrid, Bangkok or Berlin or anywhere in between — there’s nothing like being on the ground finding that original voice — in their homes, or sharing a meal, and looking eye to eye with openness, curiosity and respect,” Bajaria said. “I’ve seen firsthand how the saying is true: to paraphrase, you can ‘travel the world and never be a stranger.’ ”

Bajaria indicated pride the legacy of her role having greatly expanded the global village of television during her tenure at Netflix.

“I’m full of gratitude for how far that idea — that belief — has forever transformed storytelling allover the world and not just in entertainment but in sports, brands and fandoms of all kinds,” she said. “Gratitude to all of you — you tell your stories from your own country and in your own language.Someone far away, who you will never meet, will watch and remember your work in the mostunexpected ways. You will stay with them forever.”

Bajaria’s kudo was presented by Keri Russell, star of Netflix’s “The Diplomat” and was preceded by a video with compliments on her leadership and creative instincts from such notable stars and creatives as Kate Hudson, Hasan Minhaj, Peter Morgan, Lee Sung Jin, Shonda Rhimes, Tan France, Ricardo Darín, Alex Pina, David Beckham and Hwang Dong-hyuk.

In closing, Bajaria more than hinted to the audience that there is another chapter of her career to come.

“I’ve never been more excited for the next season. You know I love to surprise an audience,” she said. “So stay tuned.”

qtxwh5.title: Is Vanity Fair’s Hit Piece on Taylor Swift Really Journalism?
qtxwh5.content:
After word hit the street some days back that Vanity Fair was imminently going to publish an extensively reported hit piece on music’s biggest superstar, there was some anticipation that Monday might turn out to be a bad day for Taylor Swift. Instead, it was just a bad day for journalism. As attention-seeking magazine articles go, it’s hard to remember one that landed with quite such an unanticipated — but very loud — thud as “The Mastermind,” which has even hardened anti-Swifties wondering whether May Jeong slipped it through without editorial oversight, sneaking an alleged year’s worth of work onto the internet in the dead of morning.

The alternative scenario was unthinkable. You would have to imagine that the author had actually been encouraged by editors to puzzle readers with a reported op-ed in which the subject of the piece — apparently, some top-tier celebrity! — is never named, yet still is subject to accusations that she picks her own friends, harbors ambitions, owned three pairs of Ugg boots while posing as a teenage commoner, and, most slanderously, was actually popular in school.

When was the last time a high-profile magazine piece got ratio-ed this badly? That would have been one year and one week ago, when an exclusive excerpt from Olivia Nuzzi’s memoir, “American Canto,” was released to an incredulous world. And if there’s something that feels a little bit familiar about Jeong’s oddball tactic of not naming names in her piece (or at least not the big ones), it’s because this “you know who it’s about, but we’re not gonna say anyway” technique was a weird conceit last grafted into big-time American journalism by Nuzzi. That author referred to RFK only as “the Politician,” her ex-boyfriend as “the man I did not marry,” and so on. Nuzzi walked so that Jeong could run. Although this new piece is not any kind of roman a clef, she still feels compelled to euphemize Swift as “The Star,” her former label as “The Machine,” Scooter Braun as “The Manager,” Charli xcx as “The Brat” and even a secondary source as “The Person Familiar.”

You would think Vanity Fair’s editors would recall the horrible reviews Nuzzi got for employing this gambit in “American Canto,” especially since the excerpt that introduced that annoying running gag to the world was published in… Vanity Fair. (How quickly they forget, but monthly journalism is a grind.)

The article aims to unload secrets, but the secret we really need revealed is: Why do that? An interview with Jeoing is in order. Or perhaps she is saving the rationale for her journalism class at Princeton, which may be the only one destined to have “The Mastermind” as ciriculum. On first blush, a journalism non-pro might imagine that it was done to skirt libel laws, although that explanation holds no water, since the writer does quote several of her lowest-level sources by name, like the kids from Swift’s school who are ready to call her out now for not having been friendless or unmoneyed. (The former classmates will pick up some notoriety now, but will they regret that they could have become even more legendary if they’d been ID-ed as “The Girl Who Noticed The Star’s Uggs”?) No, it seems more likely that Jeong did it because we are, all of us, just archetypes in a fable. Except for the music teacher at Wyomissing Area Junior/Senior High, who is un-archetypical enough to require a first and last name.

Or perhaps Jeong refrains from naming Swift because she is the female equivalent of two other characters who are often referred to as He Who Must Not Be Named: Voldemort and Trump. Certainly the article seems to see Swift as an exemplor of the banality of evil, or, more to the point, a modern-day, real-life Regina George from “Mean Girls.” (No, not making that up, the journalist really goes with that.) Nearly every sentence is intended as a slap. Most journos writing a piece remotely in this vein — a reported one, as opposed to a straight opinion — would try to leaven it at least once or twice with a positive or just neutral observation, before dropping the next bomb. “The Mastermind,” to its honest credit, dispenses with any “See, I went into this with an open mind” niceties.

The Star is found to be “making herself a metonym for all women, successfully equat(ing) criticism against her as criticism against womenkind.” Compared to Katy Perry (or “The California Girl”), who is “an adult pretending to be a child,” Swift “might be a child pretending to be an adult.” She “has a reputation for being punitive. She seems too invested in her own victimhood.” For Swift, “all she had ever wanted from the world was that it celebrate her milky goodness, that her altruism not be mistaken for covert narcissism.” And then from there, Jeoing gets to some of Swift’s bad qualities. (Just kidding.)

If this were framed in any way as a commentary, as opposed to Vanity Fair objectively speaking in the voice of God, it wouldn’t catch much notice. But instead, the magazine frames it as an ultimate profile, the result of a year of work and talking to “over 100 sources.” We have to take the editors’ word for that, because the reportage, as printed, only quotes six sources on the record: the mother of a man who directed Swift in her school plays, a guitar teacher, a school music teacher, two girls who sat near Swift in music class, and a poet who is called in to assess how lyrics work. Five others are quoted anonymously: someone who used to be close to Swift called The Person Familiar; a music pro called The Exec; a mystery collaborator with a profession that must be kept secret; a musician who toured with Swift; and a critic who was ostracized after slamming her. Now, reporters do often get great background information from interviews they don’t quote, so the 100-plus figure doesn’t sound unrealistic. But if these dozen or so sources were the best that the story had to actually quote — including a poet and a critic — you do have to wonder who the other 85-plus were, to be less quotable. (An editor’s introduction to the piece says one of the people interviewed was a “lover” of Swift’s, but we’ll just have to guess if the writer got to Joe Alwyn.)

All that said, there are a handful of interesting questions and critical observations scattered through Jeong’s piece. (See? This is the part where you throw in something nice, to show you were objective.) If you removed the promise of fact-finding and this existed as an essay on Salon — RIP — you could credit her with some food-for-thought lines and decently snarky zingers. (Sure, I chuckled when Jeong, alluding to Travis Kelce, wrote, “Regretfully we must call him Redwood.”)

But the veneer of investigative reporting placed upon this piece mostly shows just how low the bar is for an attempted expose anymore. Even without the terminally cutesy names. It’d be nice to suppose that Jeong really did come up with something after a year — there is so much hinted at that is quickly dropped — and that Vanity Fair’s lawyers gutted the piece to within an inch of a life. But more probably it’s an example of snark masquerading as reportage. And it’s a lesson that some journalists (even journalists that teach at Princeton) are too quick to succumb to a sad maxim, when an expensive and exhaustive fishing expedition doesn’t turn up much: If you can’t get the goods, just get cute. But don’t expect readers who expect more out of their hit squads not to notice.

btm8rf.title: Bela Bajaria Calls Time at Netflix a “Fun Chapter” as She Teases Rest and “Conversations” in First Remarks on Exit
btm8rf.content:
Former Netflix chief content officer Bela Bajaria addressed her exit from the streamer in her first public comments about her abrupt departure last month.

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter ahead of the 2026 International Emmys, where she’s set to be honored with the Founders Award, Bajaria called her decade at Netflix “such an amazing, fun chapter” and shared she was “proud of so many of the things” that she and her team had accomplished.

Since her exit, Bajaria said she’s been indulging in “a little rest” and having some “really fun conversations.”

“I’m excited about what’s next, and I think this time is good for a little rest after a lot of global travel,” she told THR on the red carpet ahead of the awards show, adding that she’s “really open” to whatever the future holds.

Bajaria was ousted from her role at Netflix on Oct. 15, with former Fox and Disney exec Peter Rice taking her place as chief content officer.

The former chief content officer previously spoke with THR at the Saban Community Clinic Gala at the end of October but wasn’t yet ready to speak about her time at Netflix. Still she offered, “the outpouring that I’ve received in the last couple of weeks has been so beautiful and amazing. I’ve been in television for 30 years, and at this point I have worked with what feels like nearly every single person from agents and producers to writers and actors. I love it. I’m so grateful for the career I have had to date, with lots more to come.”

Bajaria, who joined Netflix after serving as president of Universal Television at NBCUniversal, left the streamer as it shed 1,000 employees, roughly six percent of its workforce, including execs Doug Belgrad and, days after news broke of Bajaria leaving, film boss Dan Lin. The layoffs came as the company seeks a reset amid slowing viewership growth.

When she left Netflix, co-CEO Ted Sarandos said of Bajaria, “Bela has built and shaped a truly global Content organization, hiring brilliant people and empowering them to make good decisions. I am incredibly grateful to her for everything she’s done.”

He added in a staff memo, “I know this is a big change in a year that has already had its share. But I also see an opportunity to take our slate to the next level, especially in [the U.S. and Canada] where we have an outsize impact in creating big, buzzy hits that our members love and drive conversation around the world.”

1sumrzk.title: ‘GTA 6’ Boss Strauss Zelnick Among First Raft of SXSW London 2027 Speakers
1sumrzk.content:
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick, the man behind Grand Theft Auto VI, is among the first raft of speakers confirmed for next year’s SXSW London.

The conference is set to return to Shoreditch, east London, for its third year from May 24-29, where Zelnick will take to the stage to talk about building one of the world’s biggest entertainment franchises (sales for the latest release have already out-grossed Christopher Nolan’s box office behemoth The Odyssey).

The upcoming installment is built around the theme “The Power of Human Potential,” described by organizers as a deliberate focus on people in a year dominated by what machines can do. Among the speakers making that case is Jon Steinback, the former DeepMind creative lead whose start-up Marker is building an AI writing tool designed to develop, rather than delete, writers.

Elsewhere, David Thornton, president of Genomics Limited, will explore how rapid analysis of large-scale genetic and genomic information will empower us to predict disease risks and improve medicine.

Ilyas Khan, who founded Cambridge Quantum and was the founding CEO of Quantinuum, is also on board to discuss the convergence of AI and quantum computing. His appearance follows Quantinuum’s $1.68bn Nasdaq listing in June 2026, the largest traditional IPO yet for a pure-play quantum computing company.

Two of Britain’s best-known voices in advertising, Martin Sorrell and Rory Sutherland, and media personality GK Barry, will join the festival to explore the future of advertising and the creator economy, while Refik Anadol, founder of the newly opened LA museum, Dataland, will share his artistic vision for AI and data-driven installations.

“SXSW London is a place of firsts — where you see it first, hear it first, and meet the people behind it first,” began Katy Arnander, SXSW London’s chief programming officer. “It’s also where industries converge: where gaming meets advertising, art meets AI, and quantum computing shares a stage with the creator economy. Our first wave of speakers reflects exactly that, and shows what happens when human potential is central to the conversation.”

The event will welcome around 20,000 festival-goers on its walkable Shoreditch campus, engaging in networking, music showcases, international premieres and parties. The 2026 festival drew attendees from 97 countries, 863 speakers (including Michelle Obama, Serena Williams and Brian Eno), 256 music artists across 18 venues and 100 film screenings, 13 of them world premieres.

suxgkl.title: Local measurements reveal global quantum properties in a constant number of experimental runs
suxgkl.content:
Workflow of the certification protocol. Computational-basis measurements on one subsystem produce an outcome and a projected state; randomized Pauli measurements on the small subsystem feed a conditional-fidelity estimator, which is compared with a threshold to accept or reject. Credit: Physical Review X (2026). DOI: 10.1103/rkl6-hfrn

A quantum device with more qubits is harder to verify. Describing a general quantum state takes an exponential number of parameters, and reconstructing it in full—a procedure known as state tomography—becomes impractical as the system grows. Yet most experiments do not need the full description. They need to know a few things: Is the state close to the target? Are the qubits entangled? And does the system carry the resources needed for quantum computation?

In our study published in Physical Review X, we asked whether those questions can be answered with drastically simplified experiments.
The answer came from a phenomenon that at first looked counterintuitive. In many-body quantum systems, global features often survive local measurements on the rest of the system. Measure most of the qubits and the entanglement or other structure does not simply vanish. It becomes concentrated in the small subsystem you leave untouched, leaving traces that can be detected there.
We call this localizable quantumness. The logic is clean: if the original state has no entanglement, measuring part of it cannot create entanglement in the rest. So if we detect entanglement in the projected state of the small subsystem, we have certified that the original state was entangled.
We turned this idea into a practical test. Split the system into a small part A and a large complement B, measure B in the computational basis and record the outcome, then measure the qubits of A in randomly chosen single-qubit Pauli bases. Combine the two data sets into a score we call the conditional fidelity. If the score passes a threshold, the property is certified. The measurement settings are fixed in advance. There is no adaptive feedback, no need to wait for a particular outcome, and no requirement to keep quantum states alive in memory.
What surprised us most was the cost. For certifying global state fidelity, the number of experimental rounds no longer grows with the number of qubits. Earlier protocols with fixed local measurement settings required a number of samples that scaled as n⁴. Doubling the qubit count raised their cost 16-fold. Our scaling is constant. The tolerated deviation from the target state also stays constant as the system grows, which matters for real devices. And the method remains valid for mixed states—the noisy states that experiments actually produce—rather than only idealized pure states.

The same framework reaches beyond fidelity. It certifies multipartite entanglement and circuit complexity using only local Pauli measurements. For properties such as fully inseparable entanglement, it improves the sample complexity from O(n) to O(log n). For quantum magic, the resource behind fault-tolerant quantum computing, we demonstrate certification with a subsystem of just three qubits while the total system grows to 512 qubits.
Our results point to a practical consequence. Quantum technology is moving from small demonstrations toward scaled-up machines, and cheap, reliable certification is a prerequisite for that step. By flattening the cost curve and working with realistic noise, we hope to give experimenters a tool they can use. The broader lesson is that a global quantum state may be too large to describe, yet still leave a local fingerprint that is enough to verify what matters.
This story is part of Science X Dialog, where researchers can report findings from their published research articles. Visit this page for information about Science X Dialog and how to participate.

Publication details
Zhenyu Du et al., Certifying Localizable Quantum Properties with Constant Sample Complexity, Physical Review X (2026). DOI: 10.1103/rkl6-hfrn

Who's behind this story?

Lisa Lock

BA art history, MA material culture. Former museum editor, paramedic, and transplant coordinator. Editing for Science X since 2021.

Full profile →

Robert Egan

Bachelor's in mathematical biology, Master's in creative writing. Well-traveled with unique perspectives on science and language.

Full profile →

Zhenyu Du is a fourth-year Ph.D. student at Tsinghua University, advised by Prof. Xiongfeng Ma. He received his B.S. from the Turing Class at Peking University in 2023. His research focuses on developing efficient quantum information processing protocols, exploring quantum advantage, and quantum error correction.
Xiongfeng Ma is a professor at the Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences at Tsinghua University. His research explores the connections among quantum cryptography, quantum foundations, and quantum computing. He was elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society in 2023.

gh-1462612300.title: GitHub - Alountk/OpenCrown-MAC: Play Dragon's Crown Pro natively on Apple Silicon Macs from your own PS4 dump: a macOS contribution to OpenCrown PC, with a static recompiler, launcher, controllers and online co-op.
gh-1462612300.content:
Dragon's Crown Pro, running natively on Apple Silicon

Getting started ·
How it works ·
Controllers ·
Online ·
Building ·
Credit ·
Full guide

This is a macOS contribution to OpenCrown PC, the project by Nezara that lets you play Dragon's Crown Pro on a computer from a dump of your own copy. It is made with the author's permission. The loader, the PS4 system libraries, the renderer, saves, online play and the launcher are Nezara's work; this fork adds what a Mac needs to run them.
ImportantNo game files are included, and none will ever be. You need your own decrypted dump of Dragon's Crown Pro (CUSA10454): the folder with eboot.bin and sce_module/libc.prx.

What you get

🍎 Native on Apple Silicon. No emulator, no JIT: your dump is recompiled to C++ and built for arm64. Checked at 60 fps on an M2 Pro.
🎮 PlayStation and Xbox controllers work out of the box, with a visual controller view and a setup wizard in the launcher.
🌐 Online co-op through OpenCrown's public lobby, so Mac players join the same rooms as everyone else. Friend codes included.
🔊 Audio and saves, played by hand through menus, characters and several quests.
📦 A normal Mac app: OpenCrown.app in a .dmg, with an icon and a launcher.
🧪 Checked against the original: the recompiler is tested instruction by instruction against Rosetta 2 (1,287 cases, 0 failures).

Getting started

Download the latest .dmg from Releases, open it and drag OpenCrown to Applications.
The app is signed ad hoc and not notarized (that needs a paid Apple Developer account), so the first time right click it and choose Open.
Point it at your dump and press Play. The first run recompiles and builds the game on your Mac (a few minutes; it needs cmake and the Xcode command line tools). After that it starts in seconds.

How it works
A Mac cannot run the game's x86-64 code directly, so this fork statically recompiles your own dump to C++ and builds it natively. The generated code stays on your Mac, outside this repository, and is never shared. Everything else (graphics over Metal, audio, input, saves, online) is OpenCrown's, with Mac fixes. More in docs/MAC.md.
Controllers

In the game, hold touchpad click + Options (PlayStation) or View + Menu (Xbox) for 2 seconds to quit.
Online
Online play is OpenCrown's own. To try it on a single Mac with two copies of the game, see docs/MAC.md.
Building from source
cd linux-port
./play-mac.sh /path/to/your/dump/CUSA10454
Needs a Mac with Apple Silicon, cmake and the Xcode command line tools. Details, the launcher and the .app build are in docs/MAC.md. Releases are listed in the changelog and the plan is in the roadmap.
Credit and licence

OpenCrown is Nezara's project and its code is not relicensed here: this fork uses it with their permission. Please go to the original repository and its Discord for everything about OpenCrown itself, and consider supporting the author.
The fork's own additions (the recompiler and the Mac scripts) are MIT. Details in docs/NOTICE.md.
Dragon's Crown belongs to Vanillaware and Atlus. This is a hobby project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Vanillaware, Atlus, Sony or Nezara.

Upstream's own README, with everything about OpenCrown, is here.

gh-1466540621.title: GitHub - nacholuver1/Blitz-TheLeague-II-Recomp: Native Windows & Linux port of Blitz: The League II (Xbox 360) via static recompilation with the ReXGlue SDK. No emulator, no game data included: bring your own disc dump.
gh-1466540621.content:
An unofficial native Windows and Linux port of Blitz: The League II (Xbox 360, 2008), made
by static recompilation with the ReXGlue SDK.
The game's PowerPC code is translated to C++ ahead of time and compiled into a normal x64
program (blitz2.exe on Windows, blitz2 on Linux). No emulator runs at play time; the SDK
provides the Xbox 360 kernel, GPU (Vulkan / Direct3D 12), audio and input layers.
Companion to Blitz-TheLeague-Recomp
(the first game); most of what that project worked out carried over.
This repository contains no game data. No disc image, no game files, and none of the
C++ that the recompiler generates from the game's executable. To play, you need your own
copy of the game.

AI-assisted project. The code, build scripts, debugging and documentation in this
repository were written by Claude (Anthropic's AI, via
Claude Code), directed and play-tested by nacholuver1.
Every commit carries a Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer. Treat it like any community
project: read the code, and report problems in Issues.

Playing

Download the latest release from Releases: the -win64.zip for Windows or
the -linux-x64.tar.gz for Linux. Extract it anywhere (it's portable).
Dump your own Blitz: The League II disc (USA / Europe release) to an .iso.
Run blitz2.exe (Windows) or ./blitz2 (Linux), choose Use my disc image (.iso) and
pick your dump. It checks the game executable, then unpacks the disc into a game folder
next to the program (about 6.7 GB, one time).
The launcher opens: pick settings, then START GAME.

Runs at full speed (60 fps) at 2x render resolution (2560x1440) with FXAA and 16x texture
filtering on an RTX 4070 SUPER. Keep VSync on: game speed follows the frame rate, and the
game needs the vertical blank to advance.
The player README (release/README.txt) covers controls, settings and
command-line flags (--blitz.iso=, --title.game_root=, --blitz.launcher=false, --blitz.check_updates=false,
--blitz.skip_intro=true, --ui.fullscreen=, --gpu.driver=, and any --section.name=value
from blitz2.toml).
Everything (game files, saves, settings, shader cache, logs) lives in the program's folder.
Building from source
Requirements (Windows x64):

Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (C++ workload, Windows SDK 10.0.26100)
LLVM / Clang ≥ 20 (built with Clang 23) at C:\Program Files\LLVM
Vulkan SDK (built with 1.4.363) at C:\VulkanSDK\1.4.363.0
CMake ≥ 3.25 and Ninja (both come with the Build Tools)
Python 3 (only for the helper scripts in tools/)
Your own dump of the game

Different install paths: set BLITZ_VCVARS (path to vcvars64.bat), LLVM_DIR and
VULKAN_SDK before running the scripts.
git clone --recursive https://github.com/nacholuver1/Blitz-TheLeague-II-Recomp.git
cd Blitz-TheLeague-II-Recomp

rem 1. ReXGlue SDK v0.11.0 (submodule) + this project's patches, then build and install it
git -C deps/rexglue-sdk apply ../../patches/rexglue-dcbz-128.patch ../../patches/rexglue-audio-diag.patch ../../patches/rexglue-vsync-relaxed.patch
tools\build_sdk.bat

rem 2. Put your extracted disc in game\ (must contain default.xex), e.g.
python tools\extract_xiso.py "path\to\your.iso" game

rem 3. Build. The first build runs `rexglue codegen` (reads game\default.xex, writes the
rem recompiled C++ to blitz\generated\), reconfigures, then compiles.
tools\build_blitz.bat release

rem 4. Player zip (blitz2.exe + DLLs + README + licenses, no game data) in dist\
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\make_release.ps1 -Version 1.0.0
tools\build_blitz.bat package builds Release and copies the program files into a local
BlitzPC\ play folder without touching its saves or settings.
Linux (x86-64)
Tested on Ubuntu 24.04 (under WSL2). Build on the oldest distro you want to support: the
binary needs that glibc (2.38+) and libstdc++ (GCC 13+) or newer.
git clone --recursive https://github.com/nacholuver1/Blitz-TheLeague-II-Recomp.git
cd Blitz-TheLeague-II-Recomp
sudo bash tools/linux_deps.sh # cmake, ninja, clang-20 (apt.llvm.org), SDL/GTK/audio dev packages
source ~/vulkan/<version>/setup-env.sh # Vulkan SDK 1.4.313+ from https://vulkan.lunarg.com/sdk/home#linux
tools/build_linux.sh sdk # applies patches/, builds and installs the SDK
python3 tools/extract_xiso.py /path/to/your.iso game
tools/build_linux.sh release # codegen + build: blitz/out/build/linux-amd64/Release/blitz2
tools/make_release_linux.sh 1.0.0 --no-build # dist/BlitzTheLeagueII-1.0.0-linux-x64.tar.gz
With 8 GB of RAM or less, limit parallel jobs (export CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=6).
Game version
The setup screen only accepts the exact default.xex this project was made against (title
4D5707E8, SHA-256 in blitz/src/blitz_setup.cpp). Another
release of the game needs its own addresses in the manifest and hooks, and a new hash.
How it works (and what it took)

Where
What

tools/port_addresses.py
Finds functions from Blitz 1 in Blitz 2 by instruction pattern (whole functions from .pdata, with branch targets and address immediates masked). Ported the CRT setjmp/longjmp, the XAPI fiber functions, the engine's recursive-lock wrapper and XUserCheckPrivilege in minutes instead of re-deriving them.

blitz/blitz2_manifest.toml
Codegen manifest: setjmp/longjmp, XAPI fibers mapped to SDK host-fiber shims, and console-exact vector math — with the SDK's fast vmaddfp/estimates, player faces and arms shot out into long spikes in close-ups.

blitz/src/main.cpp
Vulkan by default — on Direct3D 12 the game ran at ~10 fps in play (the same was reported for Xenia: #1628, #332). Resolve readback fast — full (Blitz 1's setting) stalled the CPU on every resolve and held the game at 30 fps, i.e. slow motion; none left motion-blur ghost trails. Adaptive VSync (relaxed FIFO, SDK patch patches/rexglue-vsync-relaxed.patch) — strict VSync turned a frame just over 16.7 ms into 30 fps, i.e. half speed. Faster heavy scenes — execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu on (Xenia's default) and clear_memory_page_state off: full-field kickoffs at 2x went from ~50 to ~60 fps. Synchronous shader compilation, game-folder discovery.

blitz/src/blitz_hooks.cpp
Offline user-created content (XUserCheckPrivilege grants privilege 247 for campaign create-a-team saves). Optional intro skip: detours CRI Sofdec's mwPlyStartFname so the boot movie can't open, and the game moves straight on. Blitz 1's boot-deadlock fix isn't needed — Blitz 2 ships the corrected lock release.

blitz/src/blitz_setup.cpp
First-run setup: XDVDFS disc-image unpacker, XEX title-ID / hash check, setup screen.

blitz/src/blitz_menu.cpp
Pre-game launcher and in-game options menu (F1 / Guide / LB+RB+Back).

blitz/src/blitz_look.cpp
The menus' look, after the game's own menus (scene and colours in blitz_palette.h): all drawn, no game art; Impact / Bahnschrift from Windows, DejaVu / Liberation on Linux.

blitz/src/blitz_updater.cpp
Updates from GitHub releases: the launcher checks releases/latest, a newer release opens an Update now / Later popup, the package must match GitHub's SHA-256 digest, files are swapped with .old backups (rolled back on failure; *.toml, game, user, cache, logs never touched) and the new version restarts. WinHTTP + tar.exe on Windows, curl + tar on Linux. The version is project(VERSION) in blitz/CMakeLists.txt; BLITZ_UPDATE_URL points it at a test server.

patches/
SDK patches shared with Blitz 1: dcbz clears a 128-byte cache line on Xenon (the codegen cleared 32), and extra audio-stream diagnostics in the log.

tools/
Build scripts (Windows and Linux), release packers, ISO extractor, XEX header dump, and debugging helpers.

Known issues

3x / 4x render resolution is GPU-bound (about 40 / 28 fps on an RTX 4070 SUPER), and the
game slows down below 60 fps. 2x (1440p) holds ~60 fps, including full-field kickoffs.
The first launch shows a black screen for up to a minute while shaders compile; later
launches reach the title screen in about 30 seconds.
Direct3D 12 (--gpu.driver=d3d12) works but runs at ~10 fps in play.
Linux: builds and runs (tested under WSL2 with software rendering); not yet play-tested on
real Linux hardware with a GPU driver.

Credits

Written with Claude Code (Anthropic); project direction
and play-testing by nacholuver1.
ReXGlue SDK by Tom Clay, built on Xenia.
Menu layout adapted from darkuni's outrun-arcade-recomp (MIT).
Xenia testers' compatibility reports for this game pointed at the Direct3D 12 slowdown and
the importance of VSync.
See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Legal
This project's own code is MIT licensed (LICENSE). Blitz: The League II and its
code, assets and trademarks belong to their owners; this project is not affiliated with or
endorsed by them. The repository contains none of the game's files; the release blitz2.exe
contains code recompiled from the game's executable and loads all game data (models,
textures, audio, video) from your own disc. Use it only with a copy of the game you own.

gh-1420121199.title: GitHub - polaco1782/v64recomp: N64 Static Recompiler
gh-1420121199.content:
Your N64 favorites, with room to stretch out.
v64recomp rebuilds N64 games as native Windows and Linux applications. Bring your
own ROM, build the game, and settle in with a wider view, familiar controls and
a few comforts that weren't around in the cartridge days.
Super Mario 64 US also has an experimental browser build using WebAssembly and WebGL 2.

Make it yours
What you can do

Widescreen and ultrawide
Expand the view to fit your window with F7, or keep the original proportions.

Texture packs, built right in
Load a compatible texture ZIP directly, or embed it in the executable so it comes along whenever you move the game.

Adjustable field of view
Find a comfortable view with keypad + / −, from the original angle up to 140° in supported games.

WASD and mouse
Move, look and aim with familiar PC controls in supported games, including mouse menu navigation in GoldenEye.

Steam Deck and preset controls
Play through a native Linux package with a 1280×800 expanded view and the included v64recomp - N64 Steam Input layout.

Low CPU usage
Static recompilation and RT64's optimized Vulkan pipeline are designed to keep CPU work light, including on Steam Deck.

Get started · Games and progress ·
Controls · How it works

Ocarina of Time, captured from the native build with RT64 widescreen expansion.
This is an active porting project. Some games already reach playable levels;
others are still at their first menus. The game notes explain
what has been tried and what still needs work, so you can choose where to start.
Make yourself at home
A little more room to see
Have a wide monitor? Resize the game window and press F7 to expand the view.
Press it again to return to the game's original aspect ratio. Desktop builds
start with the original proportions in a 1280×960 window; Steam Deck packages
start at 1280×800 with expansion already enabled.
RT64 also provides 4× rendering resolution, 4× MSAA to soften jagged edges, and
interpolated rendering targeting 60 FPS. The game's logic and audio keep their
original timing. Widescreen and the adjustable camera FOV are separate settings,
so you can choose your screen shape and viewing angle independently.
On GLES3, F7 uses the game's native projection when a verified aspect
hook is available. Other titles keep their original framing rather than
stretching the picture.
Your favorite textures, in one place
With RT64, pass a compatible Rice/GLideN64 texture ZIP straight to the game. There's no need to unpack it or convert it first:
./build/sm64-us-release/bin/sm64-us --texture-pack /path/to/pack.zip
Want the pack to travel with your build? Embed the texture ZIP in the
executable when you compile it:
cmake --preset sm64-us -B build/sm64-us-release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DRECOMP_EMBED_TEXTURE_PACK=/path/to/pack.zip
cmake --build build/sm64-us-release
The game then loads those textures automatically, without the original ZIP
beside it. This works in Debug and Release, with or without ROM embedding.
You can still choose another pack with --texture-pack.
Press F5 to switch between the original and replacement textures and reload
pack changes. Textures without a matching replacement keep their original look.
To export original textures as PNGs with JSON metadata, pass --texture-dump DIR
to an RT64 game in Debug or Release. The directory is created automatically as needed.
See the texture guide for supported filenames, loose folders,
texture dumps and matching caches.
Desktop GLES3 supports a smaller set of packs. With texture support built in,
F8 opens the thumbnail editor in Debug and Release without loading a ZIP.
See the GLES texture instructions.
Controls that feel familiar

desktop adapters (some opt in). Each one follows the game's own movement
and camera rules; the linked guides cover buttons, sensitivity and controller
fallback.

FOV means field of view: how much of the world you can see at once. In the
games listed with FOV controls, use keypad + / − to change the horizontal
angle one degree at a time, or hold a key to keep adjusting. Each launch starts
at the original view; lowering the setting to its minimum restores that view.
GoldenEye retains its native weapon zoom. These controls work in both builds.
Mouse support is specific to each game and mode. For example, Ocarina of Time's
mouse orbits the normal follow camera; first-person aiming keeps the native
controls. Nightmare Creatures uses horizontal mouse motion to turn the character.
The game guides record these limits and the current testing status, including
FOV changes that still need gameplay validation.
To get your desktop cursor back, press Escape; F4 recaptures it for play.
Use F10 or close the window to quit. Gamepads remain available; release mouse
capture or use the game's documented mouse-disable setting for its original
controller bindings.
Take it to your Steam Deck
The Deck package runs natively on SteamOS and includes a ready-made controller
layout. After the initial setup and ROM import, build it on
an x86_64 Linux PC with:
./tools/build_steamdeck.sh oot-us-v12 4
The Steam Deck guide walks through the container dependencies,
copying the package and your ROM, and adding launch.sh as a non-Steam game.
Keep Steam Input enabled and leave forced compatibility tools disabled.
From the extracted package in Desktop Mode, install the included preset:
./install-controls.sh
Restart Steam, then choose Controller settings → current layout → Templates →
v64recomp - N64 → Apply Layout. Launch through Steam so the layout is active.
You can also start with Steam's built-in Gamepad template.
The preset keeps analog movement and adds convenient C-button shortcuts on the
right trackpad and rear buttons. In the Ocarina of Time Deck package, the
left stick moves Link, the right stick positions the normal follow camera, and
the D-pad handles C-buttons, including ocarina notes. A/X are action/sword, the
left trigger targets, and the right trigger or bumper raises the shield.
See the complete controller layout to
make it your own. Hardware gameplay and performance coverage are still being
expanded; the package is not a claim that every port is fully tested on Deck.
A lighter load on your Steam Deck
The design aims for very low CPU usage on Steam Deck. Static recompilation translates
the game's CPU instructions once, when you build, into native machine code.
During play, your Deck runs that compiled code directly. RT64's optimized Vulkan
pipeline handles rendering on the GPU, with asynchronous upload, rendering and
presentation work that can overlap the game CPU work.
Together, these help keep CPU work light on a handheld. Actual CPU usage depends
on the game, scene and settings; shader compilation and Debug builds can add
extra work. For a look at your own Release build, the built-in profiler
works on Deck without installing extra tools.
Build and play
You'll need your own ROM for the exact revision the game profile expects.
The import tool checks it for you, so there's no need to rename files or convert
byte order by hand. ROMs and texture packs aren't included.
RT64 is the default renderer. For games with verified graphics microcode,
--gles selects the native OpenGL ES 3.0 renderer and statically compiled graphics RSP. Use --wasm for the SM64 browser build, which runs the same shaders on WebGL 2. Supported games and build commands.
1. Get the source and dependencies
Clone with submodules so RT64 and its dependencies come along too:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/polaco1782/v64recomp.git
cd v64recomp
Already have a checkout? Run git submodule update --init --recursive from its
root. CMake uses those local sources; it doesn't download missing submodules.

Platform
What to prepare

Windows
Follow Windows setup for Visual Studio, Python and vcpkg dependencies. Open v64recomp.sln, select your game and build Release.

Linux
Python 3.11+, a C/C++ compiler, CMake 3.25+, Ninja, OpenSSL 3, SDL2, libcurl 7.85+, X11/Xwayland and a Vulkan-capable driver.

Steam Deck
Follow the container build guide on your Linux PC. It uses Debian 12 so the package doesn't depend on newer host libraries.

On Linux, install the Python build dependencies from the checkout root:
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
2. Import your ROM
Here's Super Mario 64 US as an example:
.venv/bin/python tools/import_rom.py \
--profile games/sm64-us/profile.toml --rom '/path/to/Super Mario 64.v64'
For Ocarina of Time, use the US V1.2 ROM and its matching profile:
.venv/bin/python tools/import_rom.py \
--profile games/oot-us-v12/profile.toml --rom '/path/to/Ocarina of Time.n64'
The importer accepts .z64, .v64 and .n64, verifies the exact size and SHA-1,
and copies the normalized ROM into ignored local/. It rejects a mismatched
revision or a destination containing different bytes. On Windows, use
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe in place of .venv/bin/python after setup.
3. Build, then play

python3 tools/build.py sm64-us --debug --gles

python3 tools/build.py sm64-us --debug --wasm

python3 tools/build.py sm64-us defaults to RT64 Release. Replace sm64-us
with a game ID for desktop builds. GLES3 requires a
supported game; the
browser target currently supports SM64 US. The build
reuses Emscripten from an existing Wasm configuration or finds an installed SDK.
Run the executable from its build tree, or serve the browser build locally:
./build/sm64-us-release/bin/sm64-us

python3 tools/serve_web.py --directory build/sm64-us-wasm-release/bin
On Windows, use the Visual Studio solution or VS Code launch entries.
For command-line builds, the Windows guide has the matching
PowerShell commands and executable paths.

Controls and data
Keep these shortcuts handy while you play:

Key
What it does

The default gamepad mapping uses the left stick for analog movement, the right
stick for C-buttons, A/X for N64 A/B, left trigger for Z, right trigger/bumper for
R, and Menu/Start for Start. The D-pad stays the N64 D-pad. Ocarina of Time's
Deck mode uses right-stick camera control and D-pad C-buttons instead.
Without a game-specific mouse adapter, the shared keyboard mapping is arrows
for the stick, A/X/Z for N64 A/B/Z, S for Start, C/V for L/R, and I/J/K/L for
C-buttons. See the individual control guides
for the WASD layouts.
ROMs, saves, texture packs and crash dumps stay in ignored local/. Loose texture
replacements default to local/textures/<game>/replacements;
RECOMP_TEXTURE_REPLACEMENTS selects another location. The texture guide
covers ZIP overrides and disabling replacements. The cheat menu
downloads ROM-specific codes from Mupen64Plus and Project64 and caches them for
offline use.
If something goes wrong, controlled failures in both builds save a JSON report
and RAM snapshot to local/crashes/<game>/. Keep the executable and generated
sources with the report. Run .venv/bin/python tools/analyze.py crash REPORT.json
to inspect it, or use tools/analyze.py --help to list the ROM analysis commands. Host faults
outside those checks need a debugger or core dump. See debugging
and live code repair for the next steps.
More build options

Build presets, compiler selection and the shared RT64 cache
List game workflows with cmake --workflow --list-presets. The flag launcher
runs cmake --workflow --preset <game> with a configuration-specific build
directory. Native workflows promote published live functions and review discovery
before building with four compiler jobs. Browser workflows build the ROM-verified
CPU and graphics RSP code directly.
For a custom configuration, pass CMake cache flags directly and build that directory:
cmake --preset quake2-us -B build/quake2-us-gles-debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DRECOMP_RENDERER=gles
cmake --build build/quake2-us-gles-debug -j 8
A plain cmake --workflow --preset quake2-us uses
build/quake2-us and the project defaults on first configure.
Release builds optimize generated CPU code for size (-Oz, falling back to
-Os; /O1 /Os on MSVC), while the runtime and native adapters retain their
speed optimization. Generated CPU objects avoid LTO, and unused sections can be
discarded. Set -DRECOMP_OPTIMIZE_SIZE=OFF to use the previous compiler policy.
Linux Release executables keep their debug information in a compressed matching
bin/<game>.debug file. Keep that file for source-level diagnostics; it is not
required to play. Set -DRECOMP_SEPARATE_DEBUG_INFO=OFF to retain debug information
inside the executable. MSVC continues to produce PDB files. Native games build
as position-independent executables on Linux, including an explicit PIE link.
See the size measurements.
CMake prefers Clang (clang/clang++), falling back to GCC (gcc/g++) when
the corresponding Clang compiler is unavailable. Explicit CC/CXX,
CMAKE_C_COMPILER/CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER, and toolchain selections take precedence.
Existing build directories keep their cached compiler; use a new build directory
to apply the default to a previously configured build.
The equivalent explicit CMake configuration is:
cmake -S . -B build/quake-release -G Ninja -DRECOMP_GAME=quake-us -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build/quake-release -j 4
cmake --build build/quake-release --target run
CMake selects one game per build tree and regenerates CPU sources when the ROM,
profiles, inventories or generator change. Unchanged generation is cached. Missing
ROMs or generation failures stop configuration explicitly. The generation log is
in the build directory. CPU sources are split into smaller files for parallel
compilation. Use -DRECOMP_GAME=none -DRECOMP_BUILD_RT64=OFF to build shared libraries.
RT64, its shaders and bundled libraries build once under build/shared/rt64/
and are reused by every game and both game modes. The shared build uses
RelWithDebInfo by default; -DRECOMP_RT64_BUILD_TYPE=Release selects another
renderer configuration. Compiler, toolchain and relevant flag changes select a
separate cache directory. Source edits rebuild the affected RT64 files.
-DRECOMP_RT64_JOBS=4 controls its compiler jobs, independently of game build
parallelism. Builds from different game directories serialize ac

fpuxzd.title: ‘Michael’ Director Antoine Fuqua Sued for Assault, Battery
fpuxzd.content:
“Michael” director Antoine Fuqua has been accused of assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress by a Los Angeles bar manager following an incident back in February during which Fuqua allegedly pulled a gun on and struck the employee in the head.

In a 10-page civil claim filed Friday in the Los Angeles Superior Court, William Rosenthal, an assistant manager at the bar Good Times at Davey Wayne’s, is said to have denied entry to Fuqua, his son, Brando, and his daughter because they were “visibly overly intoxicated.” Rosenthal was then spat on by a member of the group, to which Rosenthal told them they needed to leave the bar.

An hour later, Rosenthal alleges that Faqua and his party remained standing outside the bar’s line, and upon noticing their presence, was approached by Faqua and accused of pepper-spraying his daughter. When the manager denied the allegation, Fuqua “pulled out a handgun” and “struck” Rosenthal in the face before directing “a racial and antisemitic slur” at Rosenthal and threatening “to kill him.”

“As Plaintiff staggered back in pain, Defendant Brando Fuqua appeared and approached Plaintiff and forcefully swung a handgun at Plaintiff’s face,” read the complaint. “Defendants Antoine Fuqua and Brandon Fuqua then pointed their handguns at Plaintiff, placing him in imminent fear for his life, before fleeing down the street.”

Rosenthal is seeking $50,000 as a result of his suffering “serious physical and psychological injuries” which include a nose fracture, head injury, skin lacerations, post-traumatic stress disorder, severe emotional distress and severe scarring, all of which continue to cause him “great physical and mental pain and suffering.” The claim noted that Rosenthal believes said injuries “will result in some permanent disability.”

Reps for Fuqua did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment.

sw7l6p.title: В ФРГ будут производить украинские разведывательные БПЛА для Киева - Берлин выделяет на это 34 млн евро
sw7l6p.content:
Германия начнет на своей территории производство украинских разведывательных дронов "Бабка" для Киева. Об этом в понедельник, 23 ноября, сообщил глава Минобороны Германии Борис Писториус (Boris Pistorius) после встречи в Берлине со своим украинским коллегой Евгением Хмарой.

По словам Писториуса, на создание производственных мощностей Берлин выделит около 34 млн евро. Для реализации проекта немецкая компания Wingcopter и украинская Shadow Flytech основали совместное предприятие.

Также Писториус и Хмара подписали меморандум о намерениях использовать бундесвером украинскую систему управления боем Delta. Как пояснил министр обороны Германии, она позволяет свести воедино информацию о ситуации на поле боя в режиме реального времени. В прошлом месяце немецкие сухопутные войска уже протестировали эту систему совместно с украинскими военными, указал Писториус. Теперь ее планируется разрабатывать дальше и готовить для использования бундесвером.

Шесть совместных оборонных проектов Германии и Украины

Со своей стороны Евгений Хмара рассказал о шести совместных оборонных проектах с объемом инвестиций более одного миллиарда евро, а также о новом контракте на производство 1000 ракет IRIS-T.

По словам Бориса Писториуса, в будущем году Германия собирается выделить на поддержку Украины 11,6 млрд евро. В первую очередь, эти средства должны быть использованы для укрепления противовоздушной обороны страны.

Двумя днями ранее министерства обороны Украины и Великобритании сообщили о заключении соглашения, в рамках которого украинские беспилотники для ВСУ начнут производить на территории Соединенного Королевства при финансовой поддержке Лондона.

4spa8f.title: Consumers, oblivious of being targeted, find online ads helpful
4spa8f.content:
A mock web page for a news and opinion blog with banner ads for tote bags on the left and right sides of the page. The banner ads include a transparency cue that takes internet users to an explainer about why they are seeing the ads. Credit: the researchers / Penn State

Most online shoppers know that ads strategically follow them across sites, a mechanism known as "ad retargeting." A new study led by Penn State researchers found that consumers find these targeted ads helpful, but explaining why they are seeing an ad can backfire by increasing concerns about being watched.

The findings, recently published in the Journal of Current Issues & Research in Advertising, suggest that online shoppers see a benevolent intention behind retargeted ads more so than a privacy concern, said senior author S. Shyam Sundar, Evan Pugh University professor and the James P. Jimirro professor of media effects at Penn State.
"We live in an online world where people are reconciled to the fact that ads are part of the package, and the persuasive intent that exists is ever-present," he said. "I think consumers may see targeted ads as an effort by the ad industry to streamline content in a way that would be most relevant or personalized for the user."
Transparency can heighten surveillance concerns
What internet users might find scary, and what might trigger surveillance concerns, are the processes and data collection that occur behind the scenes, Sundar added, noting that online ads usually include a button that takes users to an explainer of how personalized ads work. He said these transparency cues give internet users more agency and are socially responsible on the advertiser's part. However, they remind consumers that their data is being collected and used for showing them specific content.
"Persistent targeting is a double-edged sword," said lead author Sangwook Lee, assistant professor of advertising, public relations and design at the University of Colorado Boulder. Lee completed his doctoral work with Sundar at Penn State.
"It could help people recognize the benevolent intent of the ad system, but on the other hand it makes people aware that they are under surveillance by algorithms. This is why internet browsers now offer users ad controllability, which allows individuals to personalize internet advertising by choosing topics, brands, product types or even the ability to turn off personalized ads."

Testing retargeting across four websites
To see how internet users perceive ad retargeting, the researchers recruited 345 online participants and asked them to evaluate the designs of four websites: an e-commerce platform selling tote bags, a fan blog, an online portfolio and a news site. The researchers created all four websites and designed the experiment so that all participants started on the e-commerce platform and navigated to the other sites, which included banner ads on the left and right sides of the pages.
The researchers randomly assigned the participants to one of four ad targeting conditions: no retargeting or low, medium or high retargeting. Participants in the non-retargeting group saw banner ads on the succeeding web pages, but not ads for tote bags. Meanwhile, participants in the other conditions saw banner ads for tote bags on one, two or all three succeeding websites. Half the participants in all conditions saw banner ads with a clickable transparency cue at the top that took them to an explainer on why they were seeing the ads. Banner ads for the other participants did not include a transparency cue.
After leaving feedback on each website, participants completed a questionnaire to measure variables like how helpful they found the banner ads, their perceived surveillance, their intention to click an ad and their knowledge of online advertising.

Helpful ads, but greater unease
The researchers found that participants perceived persistent retargeting as a helpful tool to show them relevant products and that it led to higher click intention. High persistence, however, increased feelings of perceived surveillance, which had a negative effect on participant attitudes toward ads. Contrary to what the researchers expected, the transparency cue increased perceived surveillance, especially for individuals in the non-targeting condition.
A possible solution, according to the researchers, is to pair transparency cues with tools that allow internet users to control what kinds of ads they see in order to give them more agency.
"The phenomenon of advertisers tracking us is typically cast in a negative light in public discourse, as 'surveillance capitalism,' the idea being that we're all products being sold to advertisers," Sundar said. "Our study allows people to take a step back and think about what advertisers want to achieve. They want to get our attention in an era where our attention is really scattered and is at a premium.
"There could be a benevolent aspect to retargeted advertising, if done well: to lead consumers toward the right product, give them a choice to opt out or customize the kinds of ads they would like to see and in general try to be helpful rather than exploitative."
Yongnam Jung, assistant professor at Soongsil University, South Korea, who completed her doctoral studies with Sundar at Penn State, also coauthored this study.

More information

yn0qx.title: Sanaa Lathan, Terence Blanchard Join ‘Jazz Infernal’ As EP
yn0qx.content:
It’s a “Love and Basketball” reunion!

Sanaa Lathan, who starred in the 2000 film, and Terence Blanchard, who composed the score, have teamed up on Will Niava’s short film “Jazz Infernal” as executive producers.

The short film explores migration, African identity and the bond between father and son as music becomes their language for grief and self-expression, with jazz shaping the film’s rhythm, tension and exploration of belonging in a new country.

Directed by Niava and co-written with Kristelle LaRoche, “Jazz Infernal” premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival before winning the Sundance Short Film Jury Award for International Fiction and earning a place in TIFF’s Canada’s Top Ten.

Lathan made her feature directorial debut with “On the Come Up,” which premiered at TIFF in 2022.

In a statement, she said, “I’m excited for the world to experience this edge-of-your-seat emotional ride, masterfully directed and brought to life by captivating performances.”

Blanchard, an eight-time Grammy winner, is an accomplished composer who has earned Academy Award nominations for his scores for Spike Lee’s BlacKkKlansman” and “Da 5 Bloods.” He has also worked on “The Woman King,” “One Night in Miami” and “Eve’s Bayou.”

He said, “‘Jazz Infernal’ is a moving and inspiring illustration of how powerful music can connect us and maintain the soul and spirit of our loved ones.”

Elegance Bratton and Chester Algernal Gordon have also joined as executive producers. Together, the filmmakers co-founded Freedom Principle, the production company behind work exploring identity, humanity and belonging.

Gordon added, “‘Jazz Infernal’ is a bold reminder that cinema, like jazz, is at its most powerful when it refuses to play by the rules. It’s daring, hypnotic and unapologetically alive.”

The film is produced by Zion Lipstein-Saffer and Samuel Caron.

qgdx79.title: ‘Daredevil’s Charlie Cox Wanted To Audition For James Bond But Was Told He Was “Too Old”: “But Robert Pattinson Is The Same Age As Me!”
qgdx79.content:
Charlie Cox wanted the opportunity to audition for the role of James Bond in the upcoming Denis Villeneuve-directed film.

However, the Daredevil actor was told he was “too old” to play the 007 agent. Amazon MGM Studios ultimately cast Robert Pattinson in the iconic role.

“Can I say something? I asked to audition for that,” said in an interview with Virgin Radio UK. “Do you know what they told me? ‘Too old.’ But Rob is the same age as me! He does look good for it, I have to be fair. Next [month] I am going to be 44… how is 44 too old?”

Pattinson turned 40 this year, while Cox is turning 44 in December. Other names who reportedly tested for the role included Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, Callum Turner and Nicholas Hoult.

“I thought it was going to be Jack Lowden or maybe Callum Turner,” Cox said. “What an amazing career [Pattinson] has carved out. Some of the stuff that guy has done… worked with directors who have gone on to be huge, huge auteurs, but when he worked with them, it was their first film or stuff.”

After Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson would take on the James Bond role, the Dune: Part Three actor said, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

1n24727.title: Глава МЗС Чехії: Вимоги Кремля щодо архітектури європейської безпеки є неприйнятними
1n24727.content:
Вимоги, які Росія висунула Європі стосовно майбутньої архітектури безпеки, є надмірними та неприйнятними.

Про це міністр закордонних справ Чеської Республіки Петр Мацінка сказав під час візиту до Лондона, передає Укрінформ із посиланням на iDnes.

«Російська сторона має певне уявлення про те, якою має бути архітектура безпеки Європи, але вона, звичайно, абсолютно неприйнятна для всіх інших. Теза про те, що Фінляндія повинна вийти з НАТО, і ми повинні повернутися до періоду до 1997 року, - це вже занадто», – цитує видання керівника чеської дипломатії.

Водночас Мацінка зазначив, що Європа повинна мати чітке уявлення про те, якою має бути архітектура її безпеки після закінчення війни в Україні.

Читайте також: Глава МЗС Чехії: Неправильно, що Європа не сидить за столом мирних переговорів

«Європа не повинна просто говорити, що те, чого бажають росіяни, є абсолютно неприйнятним. Вона також має показати, як вона це бачить», – сказав чеський міністр.

На зустрічі з радником британського уряду з національної безпеки Джонатаном Пауеллом в Лондоні він обговорив питання можливих мирних переговорів. Мацінка зазначив, що Пауелл дуже близький до переговорів між Україною, США та Росією, і «майже впевнений», що Велика Британія та інші європейські країни братимуть участь у цих переговорах.

Читайте також: ЄС відмовляється обговорювати архітектуру безпеки до укладення мирної угоди

Як повідомлялося, Євросоюз і Велика Британія зобов’язалися й надалі підтримувати Україну в боротьбі проти російської агресії, а також продовжувати чинити тиск на РФ задля досягнення справедливого й тривалого миру.

6bph39.title: NASA spacecraft data reveal how solar system's tail shifts over 14 years
6bph39.content:
A Southwest Research Institute-led study has shown how the comet-like tail of the heliosphere, known as the heliotail, fluctuates with the 11-year solar cycle. The study analyzed 14 years of data from NASA's Interstellar Boundary Explorer spacecraft to chart the detailed evolution of the heliotail beyond a solar cycle for the first time. This study confirms that the heliotail structure is driven by the solar wind to separate into fast and slow streams. Credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab

A Southwest Research Institute-led study is the first to map out the distinct motion paths of the heliotail lobes across a 14-year period using data from NASA's Interstellar Boundary Explorer (IBEX) spacecraft. By identifying the paths followed by these lobes, the study provides a better understanding of how solar activity shapes the heliotail.

The heliotail is the wake-like, trailing region of the heliosphere, a vast bubble formed by the interaction of the solar wind with interstellar plasma that envelops the entire solar system. IBEX was launched in 2008 to map the outer boundary of the heliosphere from Earth orbit.
Using IBEX-Hi data collected between 2009 and 2022, the study tracks the motion of the heliotail lobes through a full 11-year solar cycle and beyond. IBEX-Hi is a highly sensitive imager that detects and counts energetic neutral atoms (ENAs) produced through charge exchange, when fast-moving ions originating from the solar wind take an electron from cold neutral atoms in the interstellar medium, becoming neutral themselves.
These ENAs then travel back into the interior of the heliosphere where they can be detected, making it possible for scientists to remotely image and map out the otherwise invisible plasma that makes up the heliotail.

A Southwest Research Institute-led study of data from the IBEX spacecraft shows the movement of the four lobes of the heliotail over a 14-year period. The illustration shows how the movement syncs with the activity of the solar cycle, with red highlighting higher levels at solar maximum and blue indicating decreased activity at solar minimum. Credit: Southwest Research Institute

The solar cycle maps the sun's magnetic activity, which waxes and wanes in a cyclical pattern approximately every 11 years. The beginning and end of the cycle are called solar minimum, when the sun is least active. Solar maximum occurs around the midpoint of the cycle when solar activity peaks and the sun's magnetic field becomes complex and disordered.
The study "Evolution and Geometry of the Heliotail Across 14 years of IBEX-Hi Observations (2009–2022): A Baseline for IMAP-Era Heliotail Studies" is published in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series.

"The data show us that the tail's ENA emissions surge, fade and shift position as the solar cycle progresses, with a few years' delay," said Dr. Maher Dayeh, a senior manager in SwRI's Space Science Division and lead author of a paper outlining the results of the study. The study lines up the IBEX data of the heliotail with solar activity during the 14-year period, showing how they sync.
The data show four heliotail lobes arranged in a four-leaf clover pattern with two regions with increased ENA emissions and two regions with reduced emissions. The pattern is shaped by the solar wind and the force of the interstellar magnetic field draped around the heliosphere.
"What we are finding is that the sun reshapes the tail of the heliosphere in a predictable way," Dayeh said. "These paths we have traced provide new information for models to interpret future observations of the heliotail."
The paper summarizes 14 years of data showing where each lobe sits, how it is shaped and its motion path during the solar cycle. Currently, several competing models disagree about the tail's shape. "Our study maps the solar cycle-driven motion of the heliotail lobes to improve models and create a framework for interpreting future observations across different phases of the solar cycle," Dayeh said.
But many other questions can be answered in the meantime. "IBEX data set the baseline for future studies by NASA's Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) mission," Dayeh said. IMAP, which launched in September 2025, is the successor mission to IBEX and operates about 1 million miles (1.6 million kilometers) closer to the sun than Earth.
IMAP uses ENAs to create detailed maps of the heliosphere's boundaries and study how the solar wind interacts with interstellar space. It carries 10 scientific instruments, including the Compact Dual Ion Composition Experiment (CoDICE) built by SwRI to study particles ranging from the solar wind to energetic particles associated with solar storms and driving space weather.

More information
M. A. Dayeh et al., Evolution and Geometry of the Heliotail across 14 yr of IBEX-Hi Observations (2009–2022): A Baseline for IMAP-era Heliotail Studies, The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series (2026). DOI: 10.3847/1538-4365/aea6ba
