sgssf5.title: СМИ: Microsoft хотела отказаться от платного мультиплеера на Xbox Helix
sgssf5.content:
Издание Windows Central со ссылкой на свои источники сообщило, что изначально Microsoft планировала сделать Xbox Helix полноценным гибридом консоли и игрового ПК. Устройство должно было запускать игры для Windows, поддерживать сторонние магазины вроде Steam и позволять играть по Сети без подписки. Однако смена руководства XBOX, рост цен на комплектующие и пересмотр стратегии компании могут помешать этим планам.По первоначальной задумке Xbox Helix должна была работать скорее как обычный компьютер. Геймеры могли бы запускать игры для консолей Xbox, пользоваться полноэкранным интерфейсом в стиле Xbox Ally, а при желании переходить на рабочий стол Windows и устанавливать любые программы. В том числе речь шла о Steam и других сторонних магазинах.Такая открытая платформа потребовала бы от Microsoft отказаться от платного доступа к сетевому мультиплееру. На полноценном ПК подобное ограничение выглядело бы неуместно, поэтому компания изначально учитывала отмену подписки Xbox Game Pass Core (ранее Xbox Live Gold) в финансовой модели устройства.

Но у этого решения была и обратная сторона. Microsoft пришлось бы продавать консоль по высокой цене: в отличие от нынешних Xbox, компания не смогла бы компенсировать стоимость устройства доходами от подписок и продаж игр. При этом первоначальный проект разрабатывали ещё до резкого подорожания оперативной памяти на фоне бума искусственного интеллекта.После ухода Фила Спенсера (Phil Spencer) и Сары Бонд (Sarah Bond) руководство XBOX перешло к Аше Шарме (Asha Sharma). С тех пор компания стала описывать Helix несколько иначе. Судя по последним заявлениям представителей Microsoft, устройство будет ближе к традиционной консоли с привычным интерфейсом, но при этом сможет запускать игры для ПК. Что именно подразумевается под этой возможностью, пока неясно.Windows Central предполагает, что поддержка Steam может оказаться под вопросом. Microsoft сейчас старается вернуть игроков в собственную экосистему и укрепить позиции XBOX. Например, временная консольная эксклюзивность  Forza Horizon 6 уже помогла увеличить активность пользователей на устройствах компании. Кроме того, XBOX вновь возвращается к эксклюзивам и намекает на возможный перенос крупных серий вроде Diablo, Fallout и The Elder Scrolls в число игр, доступных только на её консолях.

По данным издания, внутренний анализ Microsoft также показал, что многие владельцы Xbox Ally предпочитают запускать игры через Steam, когда у них есть такая возможность. Поэтому полноценный доступ к магазину Valve на Helix мог бы увести пользователей из сервисов XBOX. Не исключено, что под запуском «своих игр для ПК» Microsoft в итоге будет подразумевать только проекты из Microsoft Store с поддержкой Xbox Play Anywhere, а не весь каталог Steam.Отмена платы за сетевую игру тоже может оказаться слишком дорогой для компании. Подписка на мультиплеер приносит Microsoft сотни миллионов долларов в год, а возможно, и больше. Точную сумму оценить сложно, потому что свою подробную финансовую статистику XBOX не раскрывает. Эти деньги помогают поддерживать консольное направление, финансировать Game Pass и разрабатывать игры.При этом Microsoft продаёт Xbox Series с убытком, несмотря на недавнее повышение цен. Если компания откажется ещё и от платы за мультиплеер, ей придётся компенсировать потерю доходов за счёт более высокой стоимости Helix. Это может сделать устройство менее привлекательным для покупателей.

Впрочем, у Microsoft остаются варианты. Например, бесплатный мультиплеер могут предложить только владельцам Helix, сохранив подписку для пользователей Xbox One и Xbox Series. Другой вариант — выпустить несколько версий консоли: обычную с привычными ограничениями и более дорогую, открытую для сторонних магазинов и сетевых игр без подписки.Кроме того, подписка и сейчас не нужна для бесплатных игр вроде  Fortnite,  Overwatch и  Roblox. Возможно, доходов от Game Pass будет достаточно, чтобы отказаться от отдельной платы за сетевые функции.Пока неизвестно, какой вариант Microsoft выбрала для Xbox Helix. Источники Windows Central не располагают подтверждением окончательных планов компании. Авторы материала допускают, что первоначальная идея бесплатного мультиплеера могла уйти вместе с командой Фила Спенсера, однако не исключают, что Microsoft всё ещё может к ней вернуться.

ubyonw.title: Первый пострелизный патч для GTA VI починил погоду и автосохранения — подробности обновления 01.002.002
ubyonw.content:
Опрос

3DNews Новости Software PlayStation Первый пострелизный патч для GTA VI почи...

реклама

Новости Software

Самое интересное в обзорах

24.11.2026 [00:31],

Спустя 13 лет ожиданий и восемь лет разработки студия Rockstar Games (принадлежит Take-Two Interactive) наконец выпустила криминальный боевик с открытым миром GTA VI, но почивать на лаврах не стала.
Источник изображений: Rockstar Games

Rockstar Games сообщила о выходе для GTA VI первого пострелизного патча. Обновление 01.002.002 занимает около 1,6 Гбайт (Xbox) / 0,6 Гбайт (PS5) и содержит ряд исправлений. Список изменений включает всего семь пунктов.
В частности, Rockstar устранила несколько проблем, приводивших к вылету GTA VI, и исправила работу автосохранений — до выхода апдейта система не закрепляла прогресс должным образом.

Кроме того, разработчики GTA VI искоренили пять багов, из-за которых:

погода могла не изменяться в течение длительного времени;
телефонные вызовы (в том числе сюжетные) не срабатывали в нужный момент;
игрок не мог сбросить уровень розыска;
игрок не мог использовать штангу для становой тяги в спортзале;
партнёры не могли передать игроку сумки с награбленным на продажу скупщикам.

GTA VI вышла 19 ноября на PS5, Xbox Series X и S, а до ПК, по слухам, доберётся в первом квартале 2027 года. Игра показала рекордный запуск и стала самой высокооценённой в истории, но пользователи Metacritic устроили новинке иной приём.

1letgkn.title: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist
1letgkn.content:
Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.

The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”

Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.

TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds.

After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

1lxrcd.title: YouTube’s iconic iOS app icon may soon return with new customizable icons [Gallery]
1lxrcd.content:
The iconic YouTube app icon that looked like a retro TV found on iOS might be making a comeback, with new customizable icons showing up behind the scenes of a new YouTube update.

In the early days of the iPhone, Apple built a custom app for YouTube on iOS before Google built its own. That included an app icon that looked like a retro TV and it was later replaced when YouTube’s official app launched on the platform.

Now, that icon might be coming back.

Android Authority spotted several new app icons YouTube for Android is testing in its latest beta update (v21.47.483-BETA). These icons seem to be tied to a new feature that would allow users to customize the homescreen icon for YouTube, and includes seven designs in total including two throwback designs. One is the aforementioned retro TV icon used on iOS, which was never on YouTube for Android, and another is an old stacked YouTube logo design.

Users would be able to change the app icon via a new setting in the app near the “Appearance” section, but nothing is live just yet. We also don’t know if this is Android-only, if this is limited to Premium subscribers, or when this might debut.

That said, it’s very fun to get these throwbacks, and we’ll be excited to see this functionality go live.

8p1unr.title: Dakota Johnson to Star in "Tell Me Everything," Lionsgate Lands Hot Spec
8p1unr.content:
Dakota Johnson is set to star in and produce the relationship-dramedy “Tell Me Everything” for Lionsgate.

The studio landed rights to the hot title in a competitive spec sale with multiple preemptive offers. Gaelyn Golde (Netflix’s “Saturn Return,” Hulu’s “Chad Powers”) penned the script and will executive produce the film.

In “Tell Me Everything,” Johnson plays a cynical divorce attorney “who no longer believes in love,” who encounters a celebrity couples therapist “with marital troubles of her own.” As the logline explains, “Their unexpected bond causes both to question everything they know about love in this modern tale about marriage, commitment, and relationships.”

In addition to starring in the film, Johnson will also produce the project alongside Ro Donnelly and Samantha Racanelli will produce for TeaTime Pictures. Since launching TeaTime Pictures in 2019, Johnson has produced and starred in “Daddio,” Sundance audience award winner “Cha Cha Real Smooth,” “Am I OK?” and the upcoming “The Three Incestuous Sisters.” She most recently starred in Amazon’s “Verity”; Neon’s “Splitsville,” which she also produced; and Celine Song’s “Materialists” for A24. Johnson and Tea Time Pictures are repped by CAA and Johnson Shapiro Slewett Kole. Johnson is also represented by Untitled.

Golde most recently wrote and executive produced Netflix’s upcoming film “Saturn Return,” starring Rachel Brosnahan, Charles Melton and Will Poulter. The film is directed by Academy Award nominee Greg Kwedar, with Plan B producing. Golde is also developing a feature at Netflix with Kelly Fremon Craig producing. Her TV resume is highlighted by serving as a writer and producer on both seasons of Hulu’s “Chad Powers,” co-created by Michael Waldron and series star Glen Powell. Golde is repped by CAA and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis.

The deals were negotiated by Dan Freedman on behalf of the studio. Chelsea Kujawa and Maria Ascanio will oversee the project for Lionsgate.

Deadline first reported news of the upcoming project.

1cjwpmu.title: Danny Boyle on ‘Ink’ and Murdoch, the ‘Trainspotting’ Toilet Scene and How ‘Slumdog Millionaire’ Almost Went Straight to Video
1cjwpmu.content:
“Decades before clickbait, before Fox News, before OnlyFans, before Truth Social, before Google, before Facebook, before any of it, something started that we’re still living with the consequences of,” Danny Boyle said while recording an episode of The Hollywood Reporter’s Awards Chatter podcast in front of an audience at the recent SCAD Savannah Film Festival, where he was being honored with the fest’s Maverick Director Award. The Oscar-winning director was referring to the fateful 1969 meeting of Australian businessman Rupert Murdoch and British newspaperman Larry Lamb, and the tabloid journalism that it spawned, which is chronicled in Boyle’s latest film, Ink, which Netflix will release in theaters on Dec. 11 and on its streaming platform on Jan. 8.

The 70-year-old Englishman has directed 15 features over the past 32 years, including 1994’s Shallow Grave, 1996’s Trainspotting, 2002’s 28 Days Later, 2008’s Slumdog Millionaire, 2010’s 127 Hours and 2015’s Steve Jobs. Described by the New York Times as “a cinematic hypnotist” and by The Guardian as “a film director in a class of his own,” he won best director Academy, Golden Globe and BAFTA awards for Slumdog, and an Emmy for his work on the London 2012 Olympic Games Opening Ceremony. And he also was presented with a Britannia Award for Artistic Excellence in 2009 and a BFI Fellowship in 2010.

You can watch the listen to or watch the entire episode above, or read select excerpts below…

On the scene in Trainspotting in which Ewan McGregor swims through “the worst toilet in Scotland”…

“CG was just beginning to emerge in cinemas. In fact, there was a Christmas film out at the time with Tim Allen playing Santa Clause, and they squeezed him into a chimney pot. That’s one of the very first uses of CG in film. It looked terrible, I thought. I thought, ‘We’re not going to do it like that,’ because somebody said, ‘Oh, you could use CG,’ as it was at the time. We wanted to do it live. So we used a theater trick, the trompe l’oeil: you cut the toilet in half and film it from the side. So, obviously, it isn’t a toilet on this side; it’s the slide that McGregor goes down. Then Brian [Tufano, the cinematographer] told Ewan [McGregor, the film’s star] to twist his feet ’round at the end, because then people will think it’s the U-bend that you’re going ’round, which curiously people do. It’s just that illusion that we buy into. If you believe the actors, you’ll believe anything! So people believed it was the worst toilet in Scotland, even though it smelled of chocolate, because all the shit was chocolate, and it was delicious! All the prop girls had candles burning so that everybody felt good about being there all day.”

Trainspotting

Miramax/Courtesy Everett Collection

On how Slumdog Millionaire almost went straight-to-video instead of to the Oscars…

“There was a change of regime at Warner Bros., and there was a change of emphasis. They decided that films that they put a bit of money up for would not be worth the cost of releasing, so they decided to put them straight out on video. And it wasn’t just my film, there was a Guy Ritchie film as well, Revolver, and a couple of others like that, as well. Fortunately, Peter Rice, [who was running Fox Searchlight at the time and] who’s just taken over Netflix, picked it up and bought it off Warners, which normally doesn’t happen. He knew somehow that when you played it with an audience, it would prove itself.”

Slumdog Millionaire

Fox Searchlight/Courtesy Everett Collection

On Ink and Rupert Murdoch…

“The film’s really about truth, so you have to tell the truth about Murdoch and what Murdoch was like. Even though people would prefer you to paint him as a villain, he, in fact, had many reservations about what was going on. But he didn’t act on them, which is as much condemnation as you need, I think, rather than just portraying him as a villain.”

Guy Pearce and Jack O’Connell in Ink

Anthony Dickenson/Netflix

On Ink star Jack O’Connell…

“He is the kind of actor like [Al] Pacino is, who can take you to an impossibly dark place — in Pacino’s case, the ordering of the execution of his brother [in The Godfather, Part II] — and yet you still lean into the character. Jack has that. If you think about he stuff he does in Sinners and in 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple, he’s a monster, and yet you’re drawn into him. That’s a weird duality he has, which not many actors do. He’s a wonderful, wonderful actor.”

Jack O’Connell in Ink

gh-1449527062.title: GitHub - kelvynzucco/majistic-recomp: Native PC port and static recompilation of Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom (Xbox 360) for Windows x64. Direct3D 12, locked 60 FPS, and 4K support.
gh-1449527062.content:
Native PC port and static recompilation of Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom (Xbox 360) for modern Windows x64 PC.

Early Prototype (WIP) · Native C++23 · Direct3D 12 & Vulkan · 60 FPS Target · Custom Launcher

WarningEARLY DEVELOPMENT & EXPERIMENTAL PROTOTYPE:
This project is currently in an early stage of development (work-in-progress). While foundational game systems, rendering, and gameplay sequences are functional, expect bugs, edge-case graphical artifacts, audio glitches, and potential crashes. It is actively being researched and improved, and is not yet a polished or final release.

Legal, Copyright & Fair Use Notice
ImportantSTRICT ZERO-ASSET DISTRIBUTION POLICY:
This repository distributes NO game assets, ISO disk images, executables, proprietary shader microcode, textures, audio, dialogue, video, or copyrighted game binaries.
Users and testers MUST provide their own legally acquired physical disc copy of the original Xbox 360 game (Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom). All executable unpacking, symbol mapping, local shader reconstruction, code generation, and static recompilation steps are executed strictly locally on the user's computer using the automated scripts and launcher tools provided in this repository.

NoteNO AFFILIATION DISCLAIMER:
Majistic Recomp is an independent, non-commercial, experimental open-source preservation and static recompilation project. The authors and contributors have ABSOLUTELY NO affiliation, relationship, association, sponsorship, or endorsement with Bandai Namco Entertainment Inc., Game Republic, Microsoft Corporation, or any of their parent companies, subsidiaries, or affiliates.
All trademarks, service marks, trade names, product names, logos, and registered trademarks appearing in this repository are the property of their respective owners.

Overview
Majistic Recomp is an open-source static recompilation of the classic 2010 action-adventure game Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom (originally developed by Game Republic and published by Bandai Namco for the Xbox 360). It translates original PowerPC machine code into native, optimized C++23, running on modern Windows x64 hardware via the ReIGlue / ReXGlue SDK with dedicated Direct3D 12 and Vulkan graphics runtimes derived from Xenia and Forza Horizon 1: ReImagined.
By translating game logic into native CPU instructions and mapping Xbox 360 GPU calls through a Direct3D 12 runtime, the project currently implements:

60 FPS gameplay target with experimental delta-time normalization hooks.
Multi-threaded startup PSO compilation, significantly reducing runtime shader stuttering.
Native Host Render Target (RTV) rendering, providing direct Direct3D 12 execution without requiring slow ROV interlocks.
Reverse-engineered graphics subsystem, featuring custom hooks for post-processing effects (SysKemumaki), dynamic camera FOV scaling, and Direct3D presentation pacing (analyzed with REA).
Synchronized fast-forward for in-game dialogues and cutscenes with dynamic audio frequency scaling.
Multi-language support with selectable in-game text and localized voiceover (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Korean, and Japanese).
Configurable resolutions (720p, 1080p, 1440p, 4K) paired with built-in AMD FidelityFX FSR 1.0, CAS, and FXAA upscalers.
Desktop Launcher powered by Tauri v2 and Tailwind CSS, featuring configuration controls, automatic build pipelines, and portable game-data management.

Supported Game Editions

Deterministic Shift Law (USA 0.0.0.2)
Analysis of the executable revealed that between the .text entry (0x82150000) and 0x821C0000, 100% of function addresses match 1:1 between European and American releases. Above 0x821C0000, every function is shifted by exactly -0x70 bytes (-112 bytes / 28 PowerPC instructions) due to an alignment padding variation in the PAL compiler toolchain.
All 34,247 PowerPC functions have been mapped and recompiled with zero unresolved branch targets.

Key Technical Highlights
1. Direct3D 12 Renderer & Frame Pacing (60 FPS Target)

Frametime Pacing: Benchmarked on modern GPUs (e.g., RTX 3060 Ti) targeting steady 16.6ms frame intervals.
Default Host Render Target (RTV) Mode: Restored CPU-side vertex height estimation in draw_extent_estimator.cpp, preventing 2D clears from claiming all 2048 EDRAM tiles and resolving the black 3D screen regression in non-ROV mode.
UI Presenter Loop Fix: Resolved an architectural regression where toast dialogs kept the presenter trapped in uncapped UI repaints, restoring true cadence presentation (PaintMode::kGuestOutputThreadImmediately).
GPU Bandwidth Tuning: Emulates gamma render targets with 32bpp (R8G8B8A8_UNORM) saving 50% VRAM bandwidth over 64bpp, restored native anisotropic filtering, and disabled synchronous GPU-to-CPU memexport readbacks.

2. Clean-Room Shader Pre-Compilation & Multi-Threaded Pipeline Warm-Up

100% Clean-Room Shader Distribution: No original shader microcode (.xsh) or proprietary game assets are distributed in the repository or release packages. Instead, the release includes only a portable pipeline state description list (4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpl, containing 64-bit XXH3 hashes and render state bitfields) and a reconstruction recipe map (shader_recipes.json).
Local Reconstruction & GPU Warm-Up: During ISO Setup (or when clicking Precompile Shaders in the launcher), the launcher reconstructs the Xenos shader cache locally on the user's machine directly from the files extracted from their own game disc (static.pak, eff.pak, HexaEngineXbox.knl), verifies every shader via XXH3_64bits, and pre-compiles a monolithic Vulkan driver pipeline cache (.monolithic.vkpc) tailored to the user's specific GPU.
Asynchronous Fallback: Any remaining uncataloged pipelines (such as 2D UI blits or rare effect permutations) are compiled asynchronously on background worker threads to prevent main-thread traversal stuttering.

3. Synchronized Cutscene & Dialogue Fast-Forward

Holding Select/Back (controller) or Tab (keyboard) during in-game cutscenes and dialogues triggers clean fast-forward (2x, 4x, 6x, 8x).
Integrated dynamic audio stream frequency scaling via SDL3 (SDL_SetAudioStreamFrequencyRatio), preserving voice clarity and releasing audio channels naturally without muting or corruption.

4. Scalable Display & Modern Controls

Display Output: Selectable output between 720p, 1080p, 1440p, and 4K UHD.
Draw Scaling: Native 1x (720p), 2x (1440p), and 3x (4K).
Upscaling & Anti-Aliasing: Integrated AMD FSR 1.0 (EASU edge-adaptive scaling + RCAS contrast-adaptive sharpening), Contrast-Adaptive Sharpening (CAS), Bilinear stretching, and FXAA.
Input Profiles: Controller (via SDL3 / XInput) and fully remappable Keyboard + Mouse with configurable mouse look sensitivity.

5. Vulkan Backend (Operational via ReIGlue)

Fully functional Vulkan rendering powered by ReIGlue Xenos GPU emulation and SPIR-V constant-fetch handling.
Resolves texture binding null-descriptors, enabling accurate 2D UI menus, fonts, textures, and 3D geometry rendering.
Includes waitable-timer frame presentation pacing (vulkan_hooks.cpp) and native FSR 1 / CAS post-processing.

6. High Frame Rate Physics & Animation Fixes

Collision Edge Step Scaling (step_fix): At high frame rates (60+ FPS), character movement steps into small lips, ledges, or stair edges could resolve backwards rather than upwards, creating invisible walls. Incorporates root-motion scaling hooks (researched by ArthurMS15) to smoothly scale step distance when blocked, allowing characters to climb edges naturally just like on console.
Sub-Motion & Object Animation Speed Normalization (anim_speed): Fixes partial animations (Majin's facial expressions, Tepeu's gesture commands, healing animations) and certain world objects running 2x to 4x too fast above 30 FPS by dynamically scaling them by frame delta-time.
Frame-Time Smoothing (frame_timer): Evens out frame time steps to keep game delta-time in lockstep with real time, avoiding collision jitter.
Camera FOV & Post-Processing Controls: Configurable field-of-view multiplier (--majin_fov_scale) and switches for pause blur (--majin_pause_blur), depth of field (--majin_dof), and glare/bloom (--majin_bloom). The underlying graphics routines, post-processing pipeline (SysKemumaki), and camera projection matrices were analyzed and mapped with the assistance of REA.

7. CPU Codegen & Compiler Optimizations (Issues #17 & #19)

Non-Volatile Guest Memory Accessors: Modified the ReXGlue codegen template (resources/templates/codegen/pch_h.inja via patches/rexglue-0.10.0/codegen-nonvolatile-memory-accessors.patch) to remove restrictive volatile qualifiers from standard guest memory macros (REX_LOAD_* and REX_STORE_*). This enables Clang/LLVM to perform register promotion, SSA value caching, Common Subexpression Elimination (CSE), and Dead Store Elimination (DSE) without constant redundant roundtrips to host RAM/cache. Multi-thread memory ordering remains strictly protected via std::atomic_thread_fence and std::atomic compare-exchange operations.
x86-64-v3 Target Architecture (AVX2/FMA/BMI2): Translation units compile with modern ISA extensions (-march=x86-64-v3 -mavx2 -mfma -mbmi -mbmi2 -ffp-contract=fast), enabling hardware movbe (big-endian moves folded directly into load/store instructions), single-cycle fused multiply-add for transform matrices, and native 256-bit SIMDe AltiVec (VMX128) skeletal animation lowering.
Link-Time Optimization (ThinLTO): Release builds enable ThinLTO (CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION / -flto=thin), allowing aggressive function inlining and constant folding across all 180+ recompiled translation units without prohibitive link times.

[!IMPORTANT]
CPU Hardware Requirement: Building and running Majistic Recomp now requires a modern 64-bit x86 processor with AVX2 support (x86-64-v3 microarchitecture baseline: Intel Haswell 4th Gen / AMD Excavator/Zen or newer). Older CPUs lacking AVX2, FMA, or BMI2 instructions are unsupported and will crash with an illegal instruction exception (SIGILL).

Directory Architecture: Self-Contained game-data/
All decompiled game files, extracted assets, binaries, and runtime caches are cleanly isolated inside a single self-contained directory:
Majin Recomp/
├── Majistic Launcher.exe # Portable desktop launcher (Release)
├── Majistic Launcher (Dev).exe # Development launcher (with diagnostics & telemetry)
├── branding/ # Official logo & high-resolution icons
├── launcher/ # Launcher source code (Tauri v2 + Tailwind CSS)
├── prototype/ # PAL (0.0.0.3) codegen manifests & translation units
├── prototype-usa/ # USA (0.0.0.2) codegen manifests & translation units
├── src/ # Unified C++ source code & QoL hooks (shared)
├── scripts/ # Automation scripts (extraction, build, run)
└── game-data/ # Self-contained game directory
├── bin/ # Compiled native game binary (majin.exe)
├── unpacked/ # Unpacked executable image (loaded-image.bin)
├── runtime/ # Save files (user/), shader cache, and logs
└── [Game Assets] # Audio, video, textures, level packages from disc

TipIf you ever want to recompile, clean cache, or switch game versions, simply delete or replace the game-data/ directory. The root launcher and project files remain completely untouched and clean.

Building from Source
Prerequisites

Windows 10 or 11 (x64) on a CPU supporting AVX2 / x86-64-v3 (Intel Haswell 2013+ / AMD Zen 2017+ or newer). Pre-AVX2 CPUs are not supported.
Visual Studio 2022 (Community, Professional, or Build Tools) with:

Desktop Development with C++ (MSVC v143 x64, Windows 10/11 SDK)
Clang: Visual Studio component C++ Clang Compiler for Windows, or standalone LLVM 20.1.8+

CMake 3.25+ and Ninja
Python 3.10+, Git, and PowerShell 7+ (or Windows PowerShell 5.1)
Node.js 18+ and Rust (optional, only required to build or modify the desktop launcher from source)

You can install the required toolchain quickly via winget:
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override "--quiet --wait --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Workload.VCTools --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.Windows11SDK.26100 --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.CMake.Project --includeRecommended"
winget install LLVM.LLVM --version 20.1.8
winget install Kitware.CMake Ninja-build.Ninja Python.Python.3.12 Git.Git

Step-by-Step Compilation
1. Clone this repository
git clone https://github.com/kelvynzucco/majistic-recomp.git
cd majistic-recomp
2. Prepare and build the local ReXGlue SDK (v0.10.0)
.\scripts\prepare-sdk-source.ps1
.\scripts\build-sdk-local.ps1
3. Extract your legally owned game data
Extract your Xbox 360 disc dump directly into game-data/:
.\scripts\extract-iso.ps1 -IsoPath "path\to\your_dump.iso" -OutputDir "game-data"
Unpack the encrypted executable:
.\scripts\unpack-xex-usa.ps1
4. Recompile and build the native executable
Generates the C++23 source translation via rexglue codegen and compiles game-data/bin/majin.exe:
.\scripts\build-usa.ps1 -Configuration Release
5. Build and Launch via the Desktop Launcher
The project provides two launcher builds depending on your workflow:

Release Launcher (Majistic Launcher.exe): A clean, silent, streamlined binary for normal players without debug consoles or local logging overhead.
Development Launcher (Majistic Launcher (Dev).exe): Built with --features dev-mode, enabling active process telemetry, verbose startup diagnostics in launcher-debug.log, and developer tooling.

To compile the Release launcher:
.\scripts\build-launcher-usa.ps1
To compile the Development launcher:
.\scripts\build-launcher-usa.ps1 -Dev
You can then run Majistic Launcher.exe or Majistic Launcher (Dev).exe, or develop live with:
cd launcher
npm run tauri dev
Alternatively, you can launch directly via the CLI runner:
.\scripts\run-usa.ps1 -RenderingPath Default -Resolution 1080p -FrameRate 60
Known Issues
Launcher window closes or goes blank with MSI Afterburner / RTSS running (issue #6)
The RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS) overlay hook crashes the launcher's WebView2 browser process a few seconds after startup. The launcher detects this and shows a message with the fix:

Open RTSS and click Add to add Majistic Launcher.exe and msedgewebview2.exe (usually in C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\EdgeWebView\Application\<version>\).
Set Application detection level to None for both.
Open the launcher again.

RTSS keeps working normally inside the game; the exclusions only affect the launcher window. Alternatively, close MSI Afterburner / RTSS before opening the launcher.

Credits & Acknowledgments

GM-0856 / majin-recompile: Original recompilation research and PAL proof-of-concept that served as the initial kickoff inspiration for this project.
ArthurMS15 / MajinRecomp: Research and implementation of physics collision step scaling (step_fix), sub-motion animation speed correction (anim_speed), frame time smoothing (frame_timer), camera FOV scaling, and post-processing toggles.
morluto / REA (Reverse Engineering Assistant): Reverse engineering assistant and toolkit utilized during development to inspect and deconstruct the game's graphics subsystem and rendering pipeline. Specifically aided in analyzing the post-processing effect pipeline (SysKemumaki), tracing camera projection matrix calculations and frustum culling structures, and reverse engineering Direct3D presentation routines.
ReIGlue Project & Forza Horizon 1: ReImagined: Custom ReXGlue fork by Dyotson, Sean O'Connor, Scott, and FH1-ReImagined contributors. Developed essential Xenos GPU emulation accuracy fixes, SPIR-V constant-only texture fetch translations, texture cache barriers, and Vulkan presenter improvements that enabled full Vulkan backend rendering.
Pinyon Shift Project: Presentation and frame submission architecture concepts incorporated in ReIGlue.
ReXGlue Project & Xenia Project: Static recompilation toolkit, PowerPC intermediate representation, and Xbox 360 Direct3D 12 GPU emulation architecture.
Game Republic & Bandai Namco: The original developers and publishers of this classic game.

1jfaljy.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
1jfaljy.content: OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches. In a controlled test⁠(opens in a new window), a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart.We’re inviting developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators across the industry to help develop the project further. The project brings together OpenAI’s frontier AI, security and infrastructure research and Cisco’s infrastructure and security expertise to help protect the systems people rely on every day.Testing and deploying a patch can still take days or weeks. Protecting a service in the meantime can be challenging because an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same Linux operation. Blocking that operation entirely could take the service offline.Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”) is designed to help security teams navigate this tradeoff. Teams can test whether a temporary safeguard, called a shield, blocks the behavior that exposes a vulnerability while allowing legitimate requests through. Once an operator approves the shield, it can be deployed while the service continues running. How Shirudo worksShirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system. This makes it possible to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted security protections to running systems.How the guardian agent observes and protects a running system with eBPF.OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo around four core capabilities:Live protection: eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system. Security teams can monitor how a proposed shield would affect applications before enforcing it.Defense at machine speed: OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo to give agents programmable controls to investigate vulnerabilities, develop targeted shields, and validate their effectiveness against exploits and real workloads. Security teams control what gets deployed.Trusted deployment: Shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading. Linux's eBPF verifier checks eBPF programs against its safety rules, while kernel security controls restrict unauthorized changes.Hardware-backed verification: Shirudo uses a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) to support a verifiable record of protections being loaded or removed. Operators can use this evidence to check whether systems meet their security requirements.The Shirudo technical walkthrough⁠(opens in a new window) from the Linux Plumbers Conference shows how to apply a shield and verify it on the target host⁠(opens in a new window). The Java4Shell vulnerability is another example illustrating how a targeted shield can protect a running application while a permanent patch is being prepared. Using OpenAI's Codex, the team generated a shield that added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder and attached it directly to a running Elasticsearch process. When attempting to exploit the vulnerability, the shield rejected the malicious input, blocking the attack while Elasticsearch continued running. You can read more here⁠(opens in a new window).Rethinking infrastructureShirudo is a first step toward infrastructure that can adapt to emerging threats while remaining reliable. We want to strengthen the operating system foundations needed to deploy these protections at scale, including hardening the kernel and core services, limiting workload permissions, and making updates and recovery safer.Our long-term goal is to enable defenders and AI agents to quickly identify affected systems, validate protections, and deploy eBPF shields that block exploits without disrupting workloads. Applications should run with only the permissions they need, governed by policies that are automatically generated and maintained.We will combine frontier AI with security and infrastructure research to discover vulnerabilities and test defenses against realistic attacks. We aim to make it easier for operators to detect and contain compromises, prevent attackers from moving across systems, and restore services to a verified, known-good state. Hardware-backed attestation and independent network controls provide additional assurance even if individual systems are compromised.Building in the openOpenAI and Cisco are open-sourcing Shirudo⁠(opens in a new window) so developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators can inspect the code, test protections, and contribute to its development. Shirudo is licensed under BSD 2-Clause, with its BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.Our goal is to make tested shields available alongside vulnerability disclosures, giving operators a way to evaluate and deploy temporary protections while preparing permanent patches.Try Shirudo: Follow the VM quickstart⁠(opens in a new window) to sign, load, and verify a test protection.Get hands-on: Explore Shirudo through Isovalent's self-guided lab⁠(opens in a new window).Join the technical deep dive: Register for the December 15 webinar⁠(opens in a new window).We’re building Shirudo in the open with the people who build, run, and secure Linux systems. We welcome contributions to the runtime, new shields, and improvements to Linux and eBPF. If you'd like to get involved, take a look at the code on GitHub⁠(opens in a new window), read the docs⁠(opens in a new window), and let us know what you find⁠(opens in a new window).

gh-1444789806.title: GitHub - spartalos/gothic3-beginning-pc: Fan-made PC port of the 2008 mobile game Gothic 3: The Beginning, with an optional HD-2D 3D renderer. Bring your own jar: contains no game content.
gh-1444789806.content:
A PC port of the 2008 J2ME game Gothic 3: The Beginning, built from renamed and decompiled sources (package g3). It runs on a desktop MIDP implementation (midp/) and is launched through a libGDX launcher (desktop/).
Trailer: https://youtu.be/5WvNaz-iCe4 (the original 2D view next to the optional 3D view; footage shows the original game's art, so it is hosted outside this repository).

The screenshots show the original game's art and are hosted as files of the v0.2.0 release, not in this repository.
Playing: you need your own copy of the game
This port does not contain the game. It builds it on your computer from your own copy of the original mobile game:
Gothic3-TheBeginning_s40v3a.jar (Nokia Series 40 build, 416,549 bytes, SHA-256 0f02bc1b...cb7f, MIDlet "Gothic3TheBeginning" by handy-games.com; use your own
copy, e.g. from a phone backup). Put it in your Downloads folder (or start the app with --jar <path>, or choose / drop it on the setup screen). The first start
builds the game (about 10 seconds), later starts are instant. The 25 sound effects are converted with a small ffmpeg that ships inside the app images (the plain fat jar uses ffmpeg
from PATH; without any ffmpeg the game runs silent apart from the music). Details: docs/byo-jar.md.
The music (MIDI) sounds far better with a SoundFont: the app images ship GeneralUser GS; with the plain fat jar put any General MIDI .sf2 next to the jar
(or set audio.soundfont / -Dg3.soundfont=), see docs/audio.md.
Run the release build with java -jar gothic3-<version>.jar or start the app image (Gothic3/bin/Gothic3, Gothic3.app, Gothic3.exe).
Developing
./gradlew build works on a clean checkout without any game jar: the :game module is then skipped (one log line) and everything else (midp, port, buildtools,
desktop, :desktop:dist, :desktop:packageApp) builds; this is what CI and the release workflow do (no secrets; the release workflow also builds the minimal ffmpeg, scripts/ffmpeg). The decompile tools (Vineflower,
tiny-remapper) are fetched from Maven and SHA-256 verified.
With your jar (original/Gothic3-TheBeginning_s40v3a.jar or -PgameJar=<path>), :game is generated at build time and ./gradlew :desktop:run runs it directly;
./gradlew clean build -PgameJar=... plus the determinism trace is the opt-in integration check (docs/byo-jar.md). Release builds (fat jar, per-OS app
images, GitHub Releases): see "Building & releases" in docs/platform.md; they contain no game content (checked by ./gradlew :desktop:checkNoGameContent, and
scripts/check-no-game-files.sh for the repository). Game code edits: docs/byo-jar.md.
Hotkeys

key
action

F5
switch between the 2D (original) and 3D view (this session; the saved choice is in the F10 options)

F3
status overlay (fps, tick rate)

F8 (gamepad: right stick click)
fast forward on / off (speed in F10 > Display)

F10 (gamepad: Start + Back)
advanced settings (display, 3D, controls, audio incl. Sound effects on/off for music only; Display > HD text switches to crisp window-resolution text, off = original pixel font by default); 3D > Graphics quality picks Low / Medium / High / Ultra at once

F11 / Alt + Enter
fullscreen

On the first start the game asks whether you want sound and whether you want the 2D or the 3D view. Both answers are saved and not asked again; change them in the F10 options (Audio > Sound, 3D > View, Game > Ask startup questions again).
Further documentation:

docs/platform.md: platform notes
docs/audio.md: audio notes
docs/analysis/: analysis of the original game
docs/mapping/: symbol mapping from original to renamed sources

Legal
This repository contains no code or assets of the original game. You need your own legally obtained copy of Gothic3-TheBeginning_s40v3a.jar
(SHA-256 0f02bc1b70c2492b0f08b0d7ef5a3ab6c71d01608a8363b52c77678d3cc6cb7f, 416,549 bytes). Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by
THQ Nordic, Piranha Bytes or HandyGames. Gothic is a trademark of its respective owners.
Third-party components and their licences: see NOTICE. This project's own code is MIT licensed (see LICENSE); the licence does not cover the original game.

1e8ahhu.title: OpenIDE 2026.3: новый главный экран, Git worktrees для работы с агентами и поддержка 14 СУБД
1e8ahhu.content: Уровень сложностиПростойВремя чтения3 минОхват и читатели35ОбзорВышла OpenIDE 2026.3. Это самое большое обновление с выхода 2026.2 в сентябре. В свежую сборку вошли новый главный экран, удобная работа с несколькими ветками Git и новый терминал. А в OpenIDE Pro за эти два месяца появилась возможность работать с несколькими AI-агентами в рамках одного чата, самый удобный визуальный редактор Markdown, 14 СУБД в DB-клиенте и поддержка новых языков.Если вы впервые слышите про OpenIDE, это мультиязычная среда разработки: Java, Kotlin, Go, C#, Python, Ruby, PHP, JavaScript и TypeScript в одном окне. Рядом с кодом есть Git, Docker, базы данных и AI-агенты.Новый главный экранКогда ни один проект не открыт, OpenIDE теперь показывает новый главный экран вместо старого окна приветствия. Раньше это было окно выбора проекта, а теперь можно сразу начать работать, не выбирая какой-то конкретный проект.Можно создать файл или перетащить существующий в окно, и он откроется без проекта. Отсюда же открываются терминал и действия с Git.В списке недавних проектов теперь видно, на какой ветке каждый из них и какие задачи в нём запущены.Несколько веток одновременно: Git worktreesWorktree — это отдельная рабочая папка для другой ветки того же репозитория. Можно работать в двух ветках одновременно: не переключаться между ними и не делать stash. Для агентной разработки незаменимая вещь.В 2026.3 новая рабочая папка сразу готова к работе: в неё переносятся настройки проекта и конфигурации запуска. В файле .worktreeinclude можно перечислить, какие ещё файлы скопировать (например, локальный .env), а после создания запустить скрипт подготовки окружения. ТерминалТерминал переехал на libghostty — движок терминала Ghostty. Теперь вывод программ разбирает и хранит состояние экрана именно он, а IDE только рисует результат. Старый эмулятор пропускал или неверно понимал почти 50 управляющих последовательностей, поэтому консольные интерфейсы в нём иногда разъезжались. С новым движком цвета и интерфейсы отображаются точно: если запускать в терминале Claude Code, Codex или OpenCode, интерфейс агента выглядит так же, как в отдельном терминале.Заодно терминал понимает клавиатурный протокол Kitty: программа отличает Enter от Shift+Enter и Ctrl+Enter, так что Shift+Enter в поле ввода агента переносит строку, а не отправляет сообщение.AI-агенты в одном чатеAI for OpenIDE (MetaHarness) собирает AI-агентов в одном чате прямо в IDE. Это Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, а также «Астра ИИ Код», SourceCraft Code Assistant и ещё больше десятка агентов. Ставить Node.js или Python для них отдельно не нужно.Что можно делать:позвать второго агента через @: пишете в чате с Claude @codex проверь, и Codex отвечает в отдельной ветке с учётом истории;выделить код и задать вопрос прямо из редактора — ответ появится под фрагментом;оставить несколько замечаний к коду или ответу агента и отправить их одним пакетом;отложить задачу на нужное время, а если у агента кончился лимит, запрос повторится сам после сброса.Подробнее с примерами — в статье «Сегодня Claude, завтра Codex: обновления мультиагентной OpenIDE».Самый удобный редактор MarkdownСпецификации, планы, README.md и AGENTS.md теперь можно править как обычный документ. Таблицы редактируются прямо в ячейках, картинки вставляются из буфера, диаграммы Mermaid и PlantUML видны сразу. Выноски и вики-ссылки из Obsidian и GitHub работают без переделок. Файл при этом остаётся обычным .md.Подробнее — в нашем блоге.14 СУБД в DB-клиентеРанее DB-клиент работал с PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, SQLite, Oracle и Greenplum. Теперь к ним добавились MongoDB, Redis, Microsoft SQL Server, Apache Cassandra, H2, Tantor Postgres, Postgres Pro и Reindexer.В MongoDB запросы можно писать в синтаксисе mongosh или на обычном SQL. В Redis есть дерево ключей и команды с подсказками.Ещё одна новая возможность — запросы с параметрами. Вместо зашитого customer_id = 1042 пишете :customer_id, а значение вводите при запуске и до отправки видите итоговый SQL.Подробнее — в разборах про MongoDB и Redis и про шесть новых СУБД.Поддерживаемые языки программированияЗа два месяца мы выпустили много улучшений для разных языков:C# — публичная бета: подсказки, проверки, запуск и отладка, управление NuGet-пакетами;Ruby — навигация, запуск и отладка, RSpec, Minitest и Rails;Python — Django, Flask и FastAPI, а также Jupyter-ноутбуки;PHP — PHP 8.6, профилирование и FrankenPHP;Go — golangci-lint ставится из IDE, отладка в WSL;JavaScript и TypeScript — несколько модулей в проекте со своими Node.js и менеджером пакетов, нативный TypeScript-сервер на Go.Что изменилось в вашем стеке, подробно рассказываем в блоге OpenIDE.Как попробоватьСкачайте OpenIDE 2026.3 или обновитесь прямо из IDE. OpenIDE бесплатна, а Pro можно два месяца пробовать бесплатно и без регистрации.Пишите, что понравилось и чего не хватает, в чате OpenIDE. Новости про обновления — в Telegram-канале.

gh-1439087973.title: GitHub - TheBozos/DC_Recomp: Dark Cloud (NTSC-U, SCUS-97111) static recompilation with PS2Recomp: configs, scripts, notes (no game data)
gh-1439087973.content:
A native Windows port of Dark Cloud (NTSC-U, SCUS-97111), made by statically recompiling the game's PlayStation 2 code to C++ on BozoEngine.
The game's own MIPS R5900 code runs as a PC program, drawing and playing sound through native PC services.
BozoEngine replaces the PS2Recomp fork completely; there is no emulation fallback. A Linux build is planned.

ImportantNo game files are included: no ELF, overlays, IRX modules, data archives, or code generated from them.
You need your own copy of the North American release, PS2 ID SCUS-97111 (disc version 1.02). The port is
built against that disc's files:

File
SHA-1

SCUS_971.11
d9965d6908a334a5dfc982f3384428ad42048d54

TITLE.BIN
8da27dd6a4f8d2090216b17d5d64a0c142cfd6d5

DUN.BIN
ab7e56a4eeb69e178638088de6e57857d48f1d98

For players (Windows)
Download DC_Recomp-0.3.0-bozo.zip from Releases,
check its .sha256, and extract it to a writable folder such as D:\Games\DC_Recomp_Bozo.
Open DC Launcher.exe, select your own USA disc image (.iso or .bin/.cue), click Prepare the game,
then Play. Preparation runs locally with the bundled offline tools; no developer software is needed.
It can be cancelled and resumed. The launcher follows TMB_Recomp's layout and supports English and French.
You need Windows 10 version 1903 or newer (or Windows 11), an AVX2/FMA CPU, OpenGL 3.3 and about 10 GB free.
Only the unmodified SCUS-97111 version 1.02 disc is supported; the executable and both overlays are verified.
The unsigned launcher may trigger Windows SmartScreen. Game files and generated game code are never distributed.
Use the launcher's Settings for display options, logs, maintenance and updates. F2 opens the game's
settings. Saves, controls, video settings and cheats are stored in %APPDATA%\DC_Recomp and survive launcher
updates. Existing development saves are kept separately; copy only the desired card files into that directory.
The in-game pause menu includes Graphics, Cheats and Quit Game. Updates offer a rebuild when the source changes.
See CHANGELOG.md for release changes and the checked routes above for current coverage.
Status
Playable Windows port, under active gameplay testing. Checked routes include Norune,
Divine Beast Cave exploration and combat, the Dran encounter, and region travel to Matataki Village.
Movement, dialogue, party/weapon menus, save/load, native music and effects have been exercised.
A complete story playthrough and full visual parity remain unverified.

Milestone

Map the main ELF and both overlays from the game's own symbol table
✅

Recompile and link with BozoEngine; remove the PS2Recomp build dependency
✅

Boot through native SDK services and reads from the owner's disc
✅

Title screen, attract sequence and native 3D rendering
✅

Norune: movement, interiors, dialogue, HUD and menus
✅

Divine Beast Cave: multiple floors, exploration, combat and the Dran encounter
✅

Travel to Matataki through “Go to Other Area”
✅

Memory-card saving, loading and restart with saved progress
✅

Native music and effects
✅

Controller-operated Graphics, Cheats and Quit Game inside Options; F2 settings remain available
✅

Georama and dungeon play on the current engine
✅

New-game opening on the current engine
🔧

Complete story, all companions, locations and effects
🔧

Linux build
⏳

Widescreen
⏳

Native port. Models, textures, camera, lights and drawing routines feed native PC draws.
BozoEngine supplies the runtime, native SDK services, renderer and mixer.

Layer

Main EE functions and both overlays statically recompiled to C++
✅

Five sound libraries relocated and recompiled offline, without a firmware bootstrap
✅

Pad and memory-card calls answered through native SDK services
✅

Compiled sound drivers and native libsd/mixer; no SPU2 emulator
✅

Frame loop paced by the PC's clock
✅

OpenGL renderer; no GS memory or GS renderer
✅

Models, shadows and cloth drawn from game data; no VIF/VU1 execution
✅

Disc textures converted offline into native images
✅

HUD, menus, text, frame copies, water refraction and depth of field drawn natively
✅

Full range of sprites, particles and scene effects checked against the original
🔧

✅ works · 🔧 in progress · ⏳ not reached yet
Native thread/timer/file contracts and transfer-completion acknowledgements remain as SDK compatibility
services. Some compiled routines still build unused console-format buffers; the renderer does not consume
them. There is no runtime GIF packet renderer, IOP interpreter or emulation fallback.
Still being checked: heavier-scene performance (including Dran's house), the full range of effects and
menus, and broader story/Georama coverage. The Dran face sampler correction passes its pixel regression;
the full encounter still needs a player comparison. Matataki's reported sharp sky boundary was corrected
and confirmed in the player's comparison.
docs/NATIVE_RENDERING_FOLLOWUP.md records recent fixes, playtest
coverage and the move to engine main (the loading-screen vsync callback). docs/BOZO_MIGRATION.md retains the migration
and conditional dispatch audit; docs/RECOMP_NOTES.md records earlier bring-up work.
Screenshots
Captured from the current build at 960x720.

Goal
A fully playable Dark Cloud as a native PC program, from the opening to the ending, drawing and playing
sound directly from the game's data. Accuracy and complete gameplay coverage come first; Linux,
widescreen and additional presentation options follow.
How it works
disc files (game/) ──► tools/dc_bozo_prepare.py ──► resident ELF + TITLE/DUN overlay ELFs
│
BozoEngine's bozo-recomp ──► native C++ in build/bozo/dc_gen/
five sound IRX ──► offline relocation + strict native translation ──► build/bozo/dc_audio_gen/
disc textures ──► tools/dc_texconv.py ──► build/bozo/textures/dc_textures.bin
│
CMakeLists.txt ──► BozoEngine + generated code + DC's own adapters
│
dc_native.cpp: models, lighting, shadows, cloth, menus and HUD ──► native OpenGL renderer ─┐
dc_audio.cpp: compiled drivers + native libsd ──► native mixer ├─► dc.exe
dc_port.cpp: native frame boundary; SDK files, cards and pads ──► native host services ───┘

The retail executable keeps its CodeWarrior symbols. tools/symtab_map.py and the retained function maps define
the resident code and overlays; no Ghidra pass is needed. The offline preparation checks all three disc hashes.
TITLE.BIN and DUN.BIN are MWo3 modules sharing 0x01DABD00. Each has its own generated symbols and function
table; native dispatch checks the resident header before selecting it, including resume entries.
runtime/dc_native.cpp translates the game's MDT models, RenderInfo camera/lights, textures and drawing calls
into native draws. It does not read console graphics packets or run VU1 microcode.
LIBSD, SDRDRV, MODMIDI, MODHSYN and EZMIDI are relocated and compiled offline. Their SDK calls use
reusable native services; libsd uses the native mixer. Pad/card modules are replaced at their SDK interfaces.
The top-level build generates code and converts textures automatically, then links the windowed dc and
dc-headless runners. Game-derived output stays in the ignored build directory.

BozoEngine is the sole engine submodule. Game-specific addresses, formats,
hook choices and module layouts stay in DC_Recomp; engine changes must be generic and reusable by other recompiles.
Requirements

Windows 10/11 with MSYS2 (UCRT64, see below); Linux is not qualified yet
CMake 3.21+, Ninja, GCC with C++20 support; development builds currently use MSYS2 GCC
FFmpeg development libraries (libavcodec, libavutil) through pkg-config, or a compatible build supplied with BOZO_FFMPEG_ROOT
bsdtar (libarchive) to extract the disc, Python 3; the offline texture converter uses only the standard library
OpenGL 3.3 for the window; SDL3 and ImGui are fetched at pinned revisions by BozoEngine
Your own copy of SCUS-97111 (check the hashes above)

Build and run
The following is the developer workflow; players can use the launcher above.
One command, from your disc
The launcher uses this same resumable pipeline. With an installed development toolchain:
python tools/dc_build.py --disc "Dark Cloud (USA).iso" --out build/player
With an extracted release, use kit/python/python.exe -I -X utf8 source/tools/dc_build.py instead; it discovers
kit/ automatically and builds offline. --check verifies the selected disc without preparing anything;
--redo STEP repeats a step and its successors. Detailed logs are in <out>/logs/.
Developer build and regression suites
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/TheBozos/DC_Recomp.git
cd DC_Recomp
scripts/extract_iso.sh "/path/to/Dark Cloud (USA).iso"
scripts/bench_run.sh --alone 20 "native build" scripts/build_runtime.sh Release \
-DDC_ISO="D:/path/to/Dark Cloud (USA).iso"
scripts/bench_run.sh 120 "play" scripts/run.sh --fullscreen
Game runs take one shared benchmark slot; builds and timed measurements take the bench alone.
Use scripts/bench_run.sh when sharing the machine with other recomp projects. Close the game before
replacing its executable. A separate FFmpeg build can be selected with
-DBOZO_FFMPEG_ROOT="D:/path/to/ffmpeg" (containing include/ and lib/).
Code generation, sound compilation and texture conversion are included in the full build.
DC_WINDOW=OFF builds only the headless runner. The validated static build imports Windows system/UCRT
DLLs; for dynamic builds, scripts/stage_dlls.sh stages required MSYS2 DLLs next to the executable.
Windows
Run the scripts in an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell; MSVC is not supported for this port.
pacman -S --needed mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-{gcc,cmake,ninja,pkgconf,ffmpeg,libarchive,python} git
Controls and settings
F2 opens native settings, including the same Cheats controls. F11 toggles fullscreen.
--fullscreen starts fullscreen; --no-vsync disables VSync for comparisons. The default is windowed
with VSync enabled. F8 captures a frame when a capture directory is configured.
Save states: F5 saves the whole game at that moment into the selected slot, F7 loads it back, F6 /
Shift+F6 choose the slot (0–9); F2 → Save states shows them. A state belongs to the build that made it: after
an update, use the game's own memory-card saves. --save-state FILE --save-state-at FRAME and
--load-state FILE [--load-state-at FRAME] do the same from the command line.
The game's Options entry page offers Game Options (the original settings), Graphics, Cheats, and
Quit Game. Up/Down selects rows, Cross confirms and Circle goes back. Graphics sets the display mode,
resolution, render scale and frame rate; Apply and save writes them to video.ini (shared with the launcher's
Settings and F2 → Video). Quit Game asks for confirmation,
with Cancel selected initially. Save through the game's normal save menu before quitting to keep progress;
quitting does not autosave.
Cheats
Open Options → Cheats in the game, or F2 → Cheats in native settings.
The in-game list scrolls with Up/Down.

Cheat
Behaviour

Infinite health
Keeps party HP full

Infinite weapon durability
Keeps equipped weapons at full WHP and prevents wear/breakage

Infinite thirst
Keeps party thirst full and prevents dehydration

Combo stamina
Keeps the bottom-left dungeon attack/combo gauge full

Equipped weapon ATK
One-time edit, 0–999; select Apply weapon ATK

Weapon ABS multiplier
1–16× positive combat rewards; normal full-ABS cap remains

Gilda
Set 0–65,535; select Apply Gilda

Consumable quantity
Set a quantity for one of the three active HUD slots; limited by bag capacity

Movement speed
50–200% horizontal movement, retaining wall collision

Freeze time of day
Holds sky and outdoor lighting; gameplay/story timers continue

Inventory size
Set 1–100 slots; occupied entries cannot be hidden or discarded

Cross toggles on/off rows. Numeric rows use Left/Right for one, L1/R1 for ten and L2/R2 for one hundred,
unless the row's hint says otherwise. Gilda uses 1/100/1000 steps; movement uses 5% steps.
Select the corresponding Apply row for ATK, Gilda, consumable quantity or inventory size.
Those edits apply when Options closes or gameplay resumes, and become part of a game save if you save
afterward. Toggle/multiplier settings are session-only: each launch starts with toggles off,
ABS at 1× and movement at 100%. See the cheat reference for limits and validation.
Memory cards and data paths
The windowed runner uses BozoEngine's per-user memory-card directory. Existing game/mc0 saves migrate
through its application-data service. --card-dir <directory> selects a separate root containing mc0;
copy the card directory before experiments. Headless runs use an in-memory card unless --card-dir is
supplied. Inventory edits reach the active card only when the game performs a save.
The build retains configured asset paths. --elf and --iso override executable/disc locations;
DC_TEXTURES selects a relocated native texture pack. The executable still needs the owner's game files
and converted assets.
Checks and captures
scripts/bench_run.sh --alone 20 "build regression suites" \
scripts/build_runtime.sh Release -DDC_ENGINE_TESTS=ON
scripts/bench_run.sh --alone 10 "regression suites" \
ctest --test-dir build/bozo --output-on-failure
scripts/bench_run.sh --alone 5 "bounded native capture" \
scripts/run.sh --frames 1400 --capture-dir build/captures --capture-frame 1200 --profile-io
Suites cover instructions, runtime/kernel services, ELF/overlay decoding, native libraries/audio,
compiled game boundaries, cheats, menu lifecycle and GPU readback. GPU checks require OpenGL 3.3.
CI uses game-free engine fixtures and offline-tool checks; retail-route tests require the owner's disc.
scripts/engine_tests.sh runs standalone headless engine checks.
--frames 0 runs until shutdown; --frames N bounds a run. --wav <file> records sound.
--pad-script <file> accepts entries such as 1200:START/6,1500:CROSS/6; --live-pad <file> reloads
changed input text relative to the current frame. --capture-dir and repeatable --capture-frame
select native captures. --hidden never shows the window and plays no sound: captures then read the game's offscreen picture, so a
scripted run needs no visible window. --mute alone runs without a sound device. --profile-io reports device-register accesses after a bounded run.
Normal play leaves expensive diagnostic recording disabled.
Recent results live in NATIVE_RENDERING_FOLLOWUP.md.
BOZO_MIGRATION.md retains migration/qualification details and
RECOMP_NOTES.md the earlier bring-up history. Synthetic checks and short
captures do not establish a full-game pass.
Making a release
VERSION declares the release version; CHANGELOG.md contains its release notes. The launcher, offline build
kit and release scripts are adapted from TMB_Recomp under its MIT
licence, retained in launcher/LICENSE. The release includes the pinned BozoEngine source, compiler dependencies,
licences and corresponding toolchain sources, and audits the archives for game data.
python tools/make_build_kit.py --out D:/dc_kit/kit
scripts/bench_run.sh --alone 20 "release package" python tools/make_release.py \
--version 0.3.0 --kit D:/dc_kit/kit --out D:/dc_release --with-sources
Only committed source is exported. Follow the release checklist before publishing;
the version-tag workflow builds and checks a draft release without a disc.
Disc facts

Boot ELF
SCUS_971.11, entry 0x100008, one segment at 0x100000 (1.6 MB of code and data, BSS up to 0x1DABD00), symbols kept

Code
0x100000-0x2452B8 (EE code), 0x245300-0x24FB00 (VU microcode), 0x29FE80-0x2A1010 (static initializers)

Overlays
TITLE.BIN (177 functions) and DUN.BIN (62 functions), CodeWarrior MWo3, both at 0x01DABD00

Video mode
NTSC

IOP modules
MODULES/*.IRX: SIO2MAN, PADMAN, MCMAN, MCSERV, LIBSD, SDRDRV, MODMIDI, MODHSYN, EZMIDI (and the unused network stack: INET, AN986, LIBNET, NETCNF, MSIFRPC, USBD)

IOP image
MODULES/IOPRP211.IMG

Data
DATA.DAT (1.7 GB archive) with its indexes DATA.HED and DATA.HD2

Sharing the machine with other ports
The team's native ports share a local benchmark lock, now provided by BozoEngine's tools/bench_lock.sh. Its
protocol remains compatible with the other ports: a game run takes one slot; a build or timed measurement takes
the bench alone.
scripts/bench_run.sh 5 "boot test" scripts/run.sh
scripts/bench_run.sh --alone 20 "runner build" scripts/build_runtime.sh

hr9hiw.title: Netflix’s French Thriller ‘Elite Force’ Starts Production on Season 2
hr9hiw.content:
Netflix has kicked off production on the second season of “Elite Force,” its hit French action thriller starring Tomer Sisley (“Largo Winch”).

Created by Julien Leclercq and Sylvain Caron and directed by Leclercq, the series spent four weeks in Netflix’s global Top 10 for non-English-language shows and cracked the streamer’s Top 10 in 91 countries.

The second season will see David and Max, after being dismissed from the GIGN – France’s elite counterterrorism and hostage rescue unit — find themselves at the center of an incident that raises suspicions within their unit and threatens its very existence.

“We’re starting filming on Season 2 of ‘Elite Force’ today. Audiences followed us throughout the first season, and it’s with great excitement that we’re embarking on a new storyline with everything dialed up: intrigue, emotion, action… Everything is in place to deliver!” said Leclercq.

Netflix has a track record with French action thrillers, notably “Under Paris,” directed by Xavier Gens, and “AKA,” starring Alban Lenoir and Eric Cantona.

“Elite Force” marks a return to familiar territory for Leclercq, who previously chronicled one of the GIGN’s most high-profile operations in his 2011 film “The Assault,” based on the 1994 hijacking of an Air France plane. He has since become a regular collaborator of Netflix, directing “The Wages of Fear,” a remake of Henri-Georges Clouzot’s 1953 classic, and co-creating “Ganglands,” a crime series inspired by his 2015 heist thriller “Braqueurs.” The latter ran for two seasons on the streamer.

Sisley, meanwhile, is best known for starring in the franchise “Largo Winch,” adapted from the Belgian comic book series, as well as the French crime procedural “Balthazar” which ran for five seasons on TF1.

107i7b1.title: AI Solved Math’s Most Famous Problem. Now Humans Are Struggling to Understand It
107i7b1.content: Mathematicians are struggling to decode a 17-million-line solution to their field’s most famous problem, published by an Anthropic researcher on Friday.Levent Alpöge released a proof in the programming language Lean of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, which he had created with Claude. While the conjecture, which describes how prime numbers are distributed, is widely assumed to be true, many mathematicians have tried and failed to definitively show this, and the problem has become something of a holy grail of number theory.Since Alpöge published his proof, more than 200 people have been collaborating to verify it. On Saturday, the nonprofit the Lean Focused Research Organization and volunteer-led organization Mathlib said on Saturday they have “full confidence” that the proof is sound. The problem is formulated correctly and the code compiles, they confirmed. Now, “we look forward to all the activity in the mathematical community that will help explain the new ideas in this proof,” they wrote.Lean proofs are written to be checked by machine, while mathematical papers are written to explain the results to the community so that they can be reviewed and advanced. But Alpöge hasn’t released the paper version, which clocks in at 250,000 pages and is, in his own estimation, a “travesty of slop.” (On Monday, he added in an X post that the Lean proof “is full of garbage obviously” but that it still “compiles.” He also said that the 250,000 pages was a “joke … I find big number [sic] extremely hilarious.”) That’s left mathematicians to their own devices as they try to decipher what new findings they can obtain and build from the result.“Knowing there is a proof is one thing,” Abhishek Saha, a professor of mathematics at Queen Mary University of London, tells WIRED, “but when we understand the proof, that would allow us to actually go beyond what has happened, to build new branches of mathematics perhaps or formulate the next conjecture to push the horizon further.”Saha reckons the community effort should be able to simplify the result into a human-readable form of under 10,000, if not 1,000, pages. But complicating this feat is the fact that the proof appears to draw on many advanced branches of number theory in a long and “incredibly counterintuitive” argument. “I don't think this kind of proof would ever come from a human,” says Saha, “but AIs can do something completely different and almost alien, and that breaks our intuition about how very difficult mathematical results might come about.”He was shocked to see even his own corner of number theory utilized by the proof, and has since been trying to understand how. Saha has been using OpenAI’s Astra model to convert sections of the Lean proof into more digestible formats, such as single-page posters like those presented at conferences and shorter documents. But there’s a limit to that approach.“It may well be that no single person has the expertise to understand in detail every part of the proof,” he says.More than 60 other individuals are using AI agents to try to translate the Lean lines into understandable ideas on Principia Math, a collaborative platform designed to facilitate the understanding of AI breakthroughs. So far, they have done this for more than 3,000 pieces of the Lean proof, though platform chief executive officer Anton Shakov expects it will take mathematicians months before they have a good conceptual understanding of the proof Alpöge produced with Claude in roughly six weeks. “I personally believe the picture we will get in the end, once the ideas of this proof have been properly understood, will be astoundingly beautiful," he tells WIRED.Independent mathematicians have already understood and written up one smaller result to have come out of Alpöge’s proof.AI labs have previously been criticized for rushing to publish breakthrough mathematical results, claiming glory while leaving the academic community to digest the results—and clean up mistakes.“No human being can reasonably claim to be responsible for, or even to understand, such a document,” the Association for Human Mathematics, a group of more than 1,000 mathematicians founded in September, wrote in a statement on Friday of the 17-million-line opus. It complained that Alpöge’s announcement “builds upon over a century of human work, but fails to advance mathematical understanding in the same way.”Alpöge, who before joining Anthropic was a researcher at Harvard University, acknowledged on Friday what an “extraordinary” situation it was to present “the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighborhood around its mathematics,” and wrote that he would try his best to help digest the proof, including by writing it up properly. But having had to hold off from making the announcement ahead of Anthropic’s initial public offering on Thursday, “I just could not live if I waited even longer,” he wrote.Anthropic rival OpenAI in October proved a weaker version of the problem, called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. Alpöge had been scooped by OpenAI in September on another Millennium Prize Problem concerning the Navier-Stokes equations, which describe fluid motion. When the company said it had solved part of the problem, Alpöge’s collaborator, New York University professor Tristan Buckmaster, claimed OpenAI had rushed ahead to beat the pair to it after becoming aware of his work. The pair also announced on Friday that they had completed the remaining unsolved parts of the Navier-Stokes problem.
