gh-1459137710.title: GitHub - AOJ222/BlackAndWhite-macOS: Unofficial native Mac (macOS) port of Black & White (2001) for Apple silicon. Needs your own copy of the game.
gh-1459137710.content:
A native macOS port of Black & White (2001, Lionhead Studios) for Apple silicon. It is
an unofficial fan project.
The download holds none of the game's content: the worlds, creatures, sounds, music,
movies and text all come from your own copy of Black & White. On first start the app asks
for your copy, reads the game from it, checks every file, and sets itself up. After that it
starts at once and your copy is not needed again. If you do not own the game, this download
cannot do anything for you.
It does hold the game's program: the game's executable and program libraries for each
version it supports, and Apple silicon code translated from them. See
What is in the download.
Download and play
The latest prebuilt release is on the GitHub Releases page.

Download the release zip and unzip it.
Move Black & White.app into Applications (Black & White Settings.app too if you want it).
Open it. It is not notarised, so on first launch macOS may refuse: System Settings →
Privacy & Security → Open Anyway → Open.
Add your copy of the game: an .iso image of the disc, a folder that is a copy of
the disc, or the folder the game is already installed in.
Set-up takes under a minute and about 3 GB.
Play. Later starts go straight to the game.

Requirements: an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27, about 3 GB free, and your own copy
of the game. It has been tried on one Mac only: an M2 Pro with 16 GB on macOS 27.2. Other
chips are untried, and so are macOS 27.0 and 27.1 (parts of the app were built for 27.2, so
it may not run there).
What you need: your own copy of Black & White in English: the original PC disc as sold,
or a copy patched to 1.10, 1.20 or the unofficial Fan Patch 1.42 (1.10 copies have not been
tried). Other language editions are not supported yet: the import checks the English
voice-over files, so a copy in another language should be refused (not tried).
How it works
The original game's x86 code is statically recompiled to native Apple silicon code
(bw_native) with SwARc, an open-source
recompiler and runtime by JT (MIT licence) that this port builds on and extends. The
recompiled game runs against replacements for its Windows, DirectDraw/Direct3D 7,
DirectInput, audio and Bink layers, over SDL and Metal: a mixture of SwARc's runtime code
and replacements written for this port (see native/NOT-ORIGINAL.md). At run time the only
game files it reads are in ~/Library/Application Support/Black & White: the game content
imported from your copy, and the game's program files, which the app copies there from
inside itself during set-up (the program files in your copy are never used). That is why
every supported copy works the same way: an unpatched copy plays the original 1.00 build,
and a patched copy (1.10/1.20, the Fan Patch) plays the Fan Patch 1.42 build.
What is in the download

The translated game: bw_native (1.00) and bw_native_142 (Fan Patch 1.42), the
game's program translated to Apple silicon code, with the SwARc runtime libraries and the
open-source libraries listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. This code is derived from the
original game program.
The game's program files, one set per version (Contents/Resources/ProgramKit for
1.00, ProgramKit-142 for Fan Patch 1.42): the executable runblack.exe and four
program libraries (DLLs). At set-up the app copies the set for your version into your
game folder. The Fan Patch 1.42 files are those of that unofficial community patch.
A manifest for each version: the name, size and checksum of every file the app expects
from your copy, used to check it. The manifests contain no game files.
Licence texts: a Licenses folder with this project's licence, SwARc's, SoftFloat's
and those of the libraries above, and a written offer of the source code of FFmpeg, the
one library in the download under the LGPL.
None of the game's worlds, creatures, sounds, music, movies or text. They are not in
the download; they come only from your copy.

Building from source
python3 native/app/build-app.py --release --out <folder>

This builds the apps from a bw_native build (the bw-native and swarc trees) and
bundles everything the first start needs, including the disc importer. Nothing that
identifies the building Mac (its folders, user name or disc copy) is baked into a
--release build. The build does bundle the program files described above, which the
builder supplies from outside this repository. The FFmpeg libraries in the download are an
LGPL-only build of FFmpeg 8.1.2 (Licenses/SOURCE-OFFER.txt gives its source and the
configure line); --ffmpeg-dir <folder> bundles the libraries of such a build instead of the
ones bw_native was linked against, and a --release build refuses an FFmpeg built under
the GPL. This repository currently contains the app and importer layer; the separate
bw-native and swarc source trees are also required for a full build and are not
included here yet. See native/app/README.md for the full picture: the launcher, the
settings app, the manifest the game is checked against, and the tests
(native/app/tests/).
Status

1.00 build (an unpatched copy): single-player is playable; Lands 1–5 run, and key
moments are covered by turn-by-turn parity checks against the original game.
The game is checked by hand during development. A full start-to-finish campaign run is the
current testing focus.
Fan Patch 1.42 build (patched copies): new in 0.3.0. Set-up from 1.20 and Fan Patch
1.42 copies has been run, and both started and played the intro. The turn-by-turn checks
have not been run on this build, and 1.10 copies have not been tried.
Creature Isle, the expansion, is not supported yet.
Sound and the opening movies run. On the 1.00 build they have been checked by programs and
by ear and eye; on the Fan Patch 1.42 build, by programs only. Networking (LAN
multiplayer) does not work.
The Settings app and the game's own Options screen change picture size and frame rate.
The Options screen also has Sound and Master Volume rows; the Settings app's window has
no volume row.
Tried on one Mac only (see Requirements).
Known limits are listed in native/app/README.md and native/NOT-ORIGINAL.md.

Legal note
Black & White is a trademark of its respective owners. This is an unofficial fan port,
not affiliated with or endorsed by those owners. This repository holds no game data,
artwork or game executable. The downloadable app does hold the game's program files and
code translated from them (see What is in the download), but
the game's worlds, creatures, sounds, music, movies and text on your Mac come only from
your own copy of the game.
This is a non-commercial fan project. It is free to download, it does not accept
donations, sponsorship or payment of any kind, and nothing in it is for sale.
The MIT licence (see LICENSE) covers original code written for this project only. It
does not cover the original game, the game's program files, code derived from them,
SwARc or the other third-party components, which keep their own terms. Please read
NOTICE.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, and do not upload game files or other
copyrighted material to this project. This is a description of what the download
contains, not legal advice.
Credits and thanks

Lionhead Studios made Black & White. This port exists because the original game is
worth keeping playable.
SwARc by JT — the static recompiler and
runtime this port is built on. The translated game (bw_native) is its output, and the
layers the game runs against are built on its runtime. Released under the MIT licence.
openblack — the open-source engine
project whose years of work documenting the game's file formats (meshes, landscapes,
animations, script bytecode) this project learned a great deal from.
bw1-decomp — the matching
decompilation of the original executables. Its recovered source was an essential
reference for how the original game actually behaves.
The Black & White community — the modders and archivists of
bwgame.net and Planet Black & White, including Daniels118's
challenge-script tools and the decompiled challenge sources shared there, and the
StrategyWiki guide contributors,
whose controls guide served as a checklist for this port's input work.
The open-source libraries bundled with the app are credited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md,
which names the licence each one is under; their licence texts are in the download's
Licenses folder.

Thank you all. Standing on this work is what made a port like this possible; any
mistakes in it are this project's own. (Acknowledgement is not a licence statement:
for what is actually bundled and under what terms, see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.)

gh-1470989861.title: GitHub - hanxl-native/darksiders-native: Darksiders II Deathinitive Edition on Android: a standalone app on the Peanuts Native runtime
gh-1470989861.content:
Darksiders II Deathinitive Edition on an Android phone: one app, one button,
60 fps and the resolution you choose.
This is the app: the screen, the game setup, the build flow, the startup screen and
the icon are this repository's. The runtime underneath is
Peanuts Native, which does the hard
part of running the game's code and graphics (see Credits); the app
shows its own name and art, not the runtime's.
What this app adds

One screen
The game file, the DLC, the pack, the GPU driver, the frame rate and resolution, the saves, the console's keys and firmware. No emulator menus.

Builds the .nup in the app
Pick the game's own .nsp/.xci and any number of DLC packs; BUILD GAME FILE merges them into one .nup with the importer that ships in the APK. A file that already holds an update is taken as it is, and the app warns if the build is not the one its pack was made for.

60 fps and resolution
A present-interval switch that holds 60 fps, and a render scale from 50 % to 200 %, both written as the runtime's switches.

Your keys, your firmware
The APK carries no prod.keys and no console font. KEYS takes your own prod.keys; FIRMWARE takes your firmware folder or .zip and reads the shared fonts from it. Stand-in fonts (Noto, Droid) keep the game working before that.

Imports the pack
The PACK card takes the code and shader data the runtime needs as a .zip (made on a PC, see below) and shows Ready once it is in place.

Turnip, picked for you
Mesa Turnip is selected automatically when it is installed; the GPU driver card installs a driver zip or goes back to the system one.

Saves
Export and import as a zip.

Its own look
The "D II" monogram, the cards and the launcher are this project's; no emulator name or art on any screen.

What you need
The app plays from two files: the .nup (the game) and the pack (the code
and shaders the runtime needs). You can make both on a PC (route A) or on
the phone (route B).
Common to both routes:

an Android 13+ phone with 8 GB of RAM or more (a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2/3 class device);
your own copy of the game (a dump of the card you own), .xci or .nsp;
your console's prod.keys;
the DLC packs, if you want them;
your save as a .zip, if you want to bring one.

There is no update step: this app and its pack are for the base game (v0). A
file that already carries an update is accepted, and the app warns that the pack
was not made for that build.

A — with a PC (recommended)
B — phone only

A computer
Windows with WSL2, Linux or macOS
—

prod.keys on
the PC
the phone

Firmware
not needed
optional (console fonts; stand-in fonts otherwise)

Who builds the pack
the PC tool
the app

Time
~15–40 min on the PC, then minutes
1–2 h on the phone

Nothing is uploaded anywhere: the tools run on your machine and the files stay on
your phone.
Play it — route A (with a PC, recommended)

On the PC, in this repository's tools/, run
build-pack.cmd (Windows) or build-pack.sh with your game and the DLC. It
makes two files: DarksidersII.nup and pack.zip.
Copy both to the phone (USB, SD card or cloud).
Open the app → PACK → choose pack.zip; the card shows Ready.
GAME FILE → choose DarksidersII.nup → Move into the app → wait
(15 GB, a few minutes).
PLAY.

No keys or firmware on the phone with this route: the .nup already holds the
DLC, and the pack holds the shaders.
Play it — route B (all on the phone)

KEYS → your prod.keys. Without it the app cannot read the game files.
FIRMWARE (optional) → your firmware .zip or folder, for the console's
own fonts. Skipping it is fine.
GAME FILE → the base .xci/.nsp. It is only read for now.
DLC (optional) → the add-on .nsp files; you can select many at once.
BUILD GAME FILE → confirm the space, then wait (1–2 h on a phone). You can
cancel.
PLAY.

Your save
SAVES → choose a .zip to restore a save; the same card exports the current
one as a .zip. The save is kept in the app's folder, so it survives updates.
Build the app from source
The app is an overlay on Peanuts Native v0.1.7-1. Two pieces:

patches/0001-darksiders-hooks.patch — turns the upstream launcher into this
app: the single screen becomes the launcher, the build gets the app's name and
its assets folder, the startup screen drops the runtime's art for a named
build, and the firmware picker is made public.
overlay/ — the screen (DarksidersLauncherActivity), the icons and the
redistributable fonts.

apply.sh clones the release, copies the overlay in and applies the patch.
./apply.sh # clones upstream at v0.1.7-1, copies the overlay, applies the patch
cd peanuts-native/android/app
JAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk17 ANDROID_HOME=/path/to/android-sdk \
./gradlew apk -PnxApp=peanuts -PnxAppId=darksiders -PnxLabel="Darksiders II Native" \
-PnxGames=010071800BA98000 -PnxPackEngine=fake
# android/app/out/nxnative-android-peanuts.apk
Needs git, JDK 17 and the Android SDK (build-tools, NDK 28.2). The first build
compiles the native host and takes a few minutes.
A build of your own can carry assets/darksiders/pack.zip (the pack, copied on
first start) and then the PACK card is not needed; a public build must not carry
it — the pack holds the game's own translated shaders.
Tested on
All of the testing so far is on a Samsung Galaxy S24+ (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3,
Adreno 750), Android 16, where it holds a steady 60 fps with Mesa Turnip.
(The phone's own Adreno driver works too, but Turnip is what the app selects.)
That is the only device it has been run on. A Snapdragon 8 Gen 2/3 class phone is
what the app is aimed at; on more modest hardware expect a lower frame rate and a
longer first shader build — the resolution scale in GRAPHICS (75 % or 50 %) is
the first thing to try. Reports from other phones are welcome.
Support
This app is free and will stay free. If it is useful to you, you can buy me a
coffee:

Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/hanxlnative
PayPal: https://www.paypal.com/donate/?business=nmherrerab%40gmail.com&currency_code=USD

Credits

Peanuts Native by seedds and its
contributors: the runtime this app is built on (MIT; its Android host is
GPL-3.0-or-later, see NOTICE).
Mesa Turnip, Noto Sans (SIL OFL) and Droid Sans Fallback (Apache 2.0) for the
pieces shipped with the app.
Not affiliated with THQ Nordic, Gunfire Games or Nintendo. The game's names and
cover art belong to their owners; this app ships neither.

License
This repository's own files are MIT, see LICENSE. An APK built with
them also contains Peanuts Native's Android host, so the APK as a whole is
GPL-3.0-or-later; see NOTICE.

15l43qx.title: Можно ли зимой ездить на «всесезонке»? Да, но есть важный нюанс
15l43qx.content: Вопрос от читателя «За рулем»: – Говорят, этой зимой сотрудники ГАИ будут штрафовать водителей за езду на летних шинах. Однако на Ставрополье снег выпадает крайне редко, необходимость в зимних шинах явно надуманная. Можно ли обойтись летними шинами? Если нет, решают ли проблему «всесезонки»? Расул Ш., Ставропольский крайНа вопросы читателей отвечает начальник Главного управления по обеспечению безопасности дорожного движения МВД России генерал-лейтенант полиции Михаил Черников. – Зимние шины предназначены для того, чтобы обеспечивать надежную управляемость транспортного средства не только на обледеневшем или заснеженном дорожном покрытии, но и на сухой дороге в условиях температур, близких к нулю градусов по Цельсию, а также при их отрицательных значениях. Такие условия встречаются в том числе на территории Ставропольского края, особенно в горных районах. Поэтому в соответствии с пунктом 5.2 Перечня неисправностей и условий, при которых запрещается эксплуатация транспортных средств, в зимний период (декабрь, январь, февраль) легковые автомобили должны быть оснащены зимними шинами. Отличительной особенностью таких шин является маркировка знаком в виде горной вершины с тремя пиками и снежинкой внутри нее, а также знака «M+S», «M&S», «M S». Если всесезонные шины такую маркировку имеют, эксплуатация автомобиля на них в зимний период закону не противоречит. Об особенностях всесезонных шин рассказано тут. «За рулем» можно читать и в Телеграм

gh-1471124262.title: GitHub - MacosPorters/betterxen: BetterXen — experimental Xbox Series X|S emulation research for native Apple Silicon, continued from XenoraOSS/Xenora.
gh-1471124262.content:
BetterXen is a community-maintained continuation. Original Git history, licenses and contributor attribution are retained. See the project history and migration notes for source attribution and imported issue and pull-request records.
Experimental Xbox Series X|S emulation research for Apple Silicon Macs.
BetterXen is an open-source project written primarily in Rust that builds and verifies a native, bounded execution environment on Apple Silicon: an independent x86-64 guest path, original PE32+ loading, AMD RDNA 2 shader translation, and a native Apple Metal graphics backend.
No Wine. No CrossOver. No Rosetta. No Vulkan runtime.
BetterXen is still experimental. Verified work is restricted to independently authored synthetic programs and shaders; authentic Xbox executable loading, system-service compatibility and commercial game execution remain unsupported. See the current limitations.
CautionBetterXen strictly opposes piracy. BetterXen is an independent, clean-room, general-purpose emulation research project that neither distributes copyrighted game files nor supports unauthorized content, DRM circumvention, or leaked materials. Use only legally obtained software. BetterXen is not affiliated with Microsoft or any other publisher or platform holder.

What works today?
BetterXen has progressed from executing individual x86-64 instructions to running original PE32+ guest programs that interact with translated GPU workloads on Apple Silicon.
The latest verified milestones include translated gfx1030 vertex and pixel shaders executing through native Apple Metal, the native Metal blend pass (NativeCompute::render_blend) and indexed triangle draws (NativeCompute::render_indexed) into offscreen targets, with rendered pixels compared against independently calculated reference results.
Development milestones

Milestone
Implementation
Status

X1 — Guest CPU
Bounded x86-64 instruction execution on ARM64 macOS
Verified

X2 — Executable loading
Loading original fixed-base PE32+ test executables
Verified

X3 — GPU compute
Guest-submitted Metal compute workloads and readback
Verified

X4 — Metal rendering
Guest-driven offscreen rendering using authored Metal shaders
Verified

X5 — Guest execution expansion
Additional bounded CPU execution and fixture coverage
Implemented

X6 — Guest control flow
Nested calls, returns, checked memory and synthetic PE execution
Verified

X7 — Imported services
Named imports, guest-to-host service dispatch and result validation
Verified

X8 — Translated compute
Original gfx1030 compute shaders executing on Metal, partial Wave32 handling and BC1 readback
Verified subset

X9 — Translated graphics
Persistent resource handles, translated vertex/pixel stages and offscreen Metal rendering
Verified subset

X10 — Texture sampling
Translated image instructions are still planned; upload, readback and decode of BC compressed formats is implemented (see Texture support)
Planned

X11 — Graphics pipeline
Bounded multi-draw passes into offscreen RGBA8 targets: translated vertex and pixel stages, indexed triangle draws, colour write masks and blend state
Implemented

X12 — Wave execution
Expand Wave32/Wave64 semantics, divergent control flow, cross-lane operations, LDS and barriers
Planned

X13 — Advanced shaders
Mesh, geometry and additional compute shader capabilities with verified Metal execution
Planned

X14 — CPU recompilation
Native ARM64 dynamic recompilation of supported x86-64 instructions in synthetic fixtures
Implemented subset

X15 — Executable compatibility
Static PE inspection reports sections, relocations, thread-local storage (TLS) callbacks, imports and entry-point instructions
Static probe implemented

X16 — Guest memory and threading
Virtual memory mapping, thread scheduling, synchronization primitives and atomic operations
Implemented subset

X17 — System services
Implement a tested subset of Xbox-compatible runtime APIs, memory services, filesystem access and application lifecycle
Implemented subset

X18 — Graphics API translation
Translate supported Xbox graphics commands, resource descriptors, command queues, barriers and fences into Metal operations
Planned

X19 — Advanced GPU features
Indirect rendering, asynchronous compute, additional texture formats and ray-tracing compatibility research
Planned

X20 — Integrated guest runtime
Connect CPU recompilation, executable loading, system services and graphics translation into one persistent runtime
Planned

X21 — Application compatibility
Execute increasingly complex independently authored applications through the complete guest CPU and GPU pipeline
Planned

X22 — First application boot
Establish a reproducible startup and error-reporting path for supported game-like applications
Planned

X23 — Initial game compatibility
Investigate startup and execution of legally supported game software, identifying missing runtime and graphics behavior
Long-term goal

X24 — Gameplay and performance
Expand rendering correctness, input, audio, memory management, shader caching and execution performance
Long-term goal

X25 — Running games
Achieve reproducible, stable execution of compatible games on native Apple Silicon macOS using Metal
Long-term goal

Roadmap note: X10–X25 are proposed engineering milestones, not completed implementations or a guaranteed sequence. Follow the BetterXen development phases for the current work order and existing issue/PR dependencies. Actual priorities will change as compatibility testing reveals new blockers. Successfully completing one milestone does not guarantee that a particular game will run.
All existing verification refers to independently authored synthetic programs and shaders. Commercial-game compatibility remains unverified.
Native graphics translation
BetterXen's graphics pipeline translates a supported subset of AMD RDNA 2 instructions into Metal Shading Language.
The translation process is:

flowchart TD
A["Original gfx1030 Machine Code"]
B["RDNA2 ISA Decoder"]
C["Validated Shader IR"]
D["Metal Shader Generation (MSL)"]
E["Native Metal Pipeline"]
F["Apple Silicon GPU"]
G["GPU Readback"]
H["Independent CPU Validation"]

A --> B
B --> C
C --> D
D --> E
E --> F
F --> G
G --> H

Loading

The initial implementation focused on compute shaders. X9 extends this to actual translated vertex and fragment/pixel shader stages.
Translated rendering
The current graphics subset supports:

Original gfx1030 vertex and pixel shader fixtures.
Decoding and translation into Metal shader functions.
Vertex position transformation.
Constant-color output and clipping.
Interpolated vertex attributes.
Offscreen RGBA8 render targets.
Native GPU readback and pixel-by-pixel validation.
Explicit rejection of unsupported shader forms.
Flat-coloured triangle draws with colour write masks and blending (see Blend pass).
Indexed triangle draws (see Indexed draws).
Depth testing with an optional Depth32Float attachment (see Depth pass).

These are genuine translated shader stages, not merely demonstrations using handwritten Metal vertex and fragment programs.
The current rendering tests are deliberately narrow: original fixtures, a single triangle per draw, and controlled shader inputs and outputs.
Blend pass
NativeCompute::render_blend draws up to 16 flat-coloured triangles in order into an offscreen RGBA8 target. Each draw has its own colour write mask (any subset of R, G, B, A) and either blending disabled or separate RGB and alpha blend factors (Zero, One, source and destination colour and alpha, and their one-minus forms) and operations (Add, Subtract, ReverseSubtract, and Min and Max). Colours are compared per channel against images derived independently (in exact fractions) from the public Metal blend equations.
GPU verification (Metal API and shader validation enabled): 39 Metal-validated passes over two original overlapping triangles — a clear-only pass; blending disabled; each source factor with the destination term zeroed and each destination factor with the source term zeroed; every operation; additive clamping; separate alpha factors; a separate alpha operation; eight write masks; and a pass whose first draw is itself blended and masked. On an Apple M5 Pro every rounded channel matched round-to-nearest exactly.
Indexed draws
NativeCompute::render_indexed issues one real drawIndexedPrimitives call per draw (up to 16) on a 16- or 32-bit index buffer with a start index and a signed base vertex, into an offscreen RGBA8 target. A draw can sample an original BC1 texture uploaded natively.
GPU verification (Metal API and shader validation enabled): 16 Metal-validated passes (both index sizes, 32-bit indices above 16 bits, odd 16-bit start, positive and negative base vertex, reversed winding, flat and textured two-triangle draws, draw order, BC1-textured draws), compared per pixel against images derived independently from the geometry, the public D3D12 and Metal index semantics and the public BC1 rules.
Depth pass
NativeCompute::render_depth draws up to 16 triangles in order into an offscreen RGBA8 target with an optional Depth32Float attachment, a chosen clear depth, a per-draw depth compare function (all eight) and depth write enable. Colour and the stored depth are both read back.
GPU verification (Metal API and shader validation enabled): 30 Metal-validated passes of original overlapping triangles: clear, every compare function at three depths, write enabled and disabled, depth test disabled with an attachment and no attachment at all, and a BC1-textured draw.
Verified Apple M5 results
The X9 native Metal acceptance run reported 20 passing tests, zero failures and zero ignored tests, with Metal API and GPU validation enabled. The newer passes below are separate Metal-validated campaigns, also with Metal API and shader validation enabled.
Representative checks include:

Test
Verified behavior

Constant-color rendering
12 red pixels and 12 clear pixels

Vertex transformation
3 rendered pixels versus 7 for a pass-through control

Perspective interpolation
Exact checks of 16 pixels and another 16 after swapping vertex color channels

BC1 texture handling
33 texels across selected mip levels and array layers

Guest rendering
PE32+ guest receives and checks the translated render output

Blend pass
39 Metal-validated passes over two overlapping triangles

Indexed draws
16 Metal-validated passes (both index sizes, signed base vertices, draw order)

Depth pass
30 Metal-validated passes (all eight compare functions, no-attachment case)

The expected results were calculated independently of the production shader translation path.
Important: Correct output for these fixtures does not prove general RDNA2 compatibility or correctness for arbitrary Xbox shaders.
Persistent GPU resources
X9 introduces a bounded GPU resource-management system for synthetic guest programs.
The implementation includes:

Generation-checked guest resource handles.
Buffer creation, updates, reuse and destruction.
Checked buffer views and memory permissions.
Repeated compute submissions.
Resource lifetime validation.
Snapshot behavior for queued submissions.
Rejection of stale handles and malformed resource requests.
Guest-visible readback and result verification.

The original X9 PE fixtures exercise these services through the guest execution environment.
The resource system remains experimental. Native GPU work already in flight during resource release, persistent Metal texture residency across guest calls, and general asynchronous execution are not yet implemented.
Texture support
BetterXen includes original texture upload, readback and block-compression paths.
Implemented and tested functionality includes:

Validated mip levels and array layers.
Pitched texture uploads.
Block-compressed texture handling, including BC4/BC5 upload and readback and a CPU BC7 decoder for the eight modes.
Native Metal texture readback.
Edge-block and transparency tests.
Invalid descriptor and bounds rejection.

Translated texture-sampling instructions are not yet implemented.
The existing texture readback path uses authored Metal kernels. It should not be confused with executing arbitrary RDNA2 texture-fetch instructions.
Xbox-specific texture layouts and additional compression formats require further research and validation.
Architecture
BetterXen is organized around three connected subsystems: guest execution, shader translation and native GPU execution.

flowchart TD
subgraph Guest["Guest execution"]
A["Original PE32+ test program"]
B["Bounded x86-64 interpreter"]
C["Synthetic imported services"]
D["Validated GPU resources and commands"]

A --> B
B --> C
C --> D
end

subgraph Shader["RDNA2 shader translation"]
E["Original gfx1030 shader bytes"]
F["ISA decoder"]
G["Validated intermediate representation"]
H["MSL generation"]

E --> F
F --> G
G --> H
end

subgraph Metal["Native Apple Metal"]
I["Compute or render pipeline"]
J["Apple Silicon GPU"]
K["GPU readback"]

D --> I
H --> I
I --> J
J --> K
end

subgraph Validation["Correctness verification"]
L["Independent CPU reference"]
M{"Expected output matches?"}

E --> L
L --> M
K --> M
end

Loading

BetterXen's host execution environment is native ARM64. The guest architecture being interpreted is x86-64.
The native graphics pipeline runs translated vertex and pixel stages, the indexed-draw and blend passes and the depth pass into offscreen Metal targets, with GPU readback compared against independent CPU references.
The project does not currently provide a general-purpose x86-64 dynamic recompiler or a complete Xbox operating-system implementation.
See Interface Contracts for the documented execution and resource boundaries.

Current limitations
BetterXen is an engineering research project, not a working commercial-game emulator.
The following remain unsupported or incomplete:

Subsystem
Outstanding work

Guest CPU
Broad x86-64 instruction coverage, multithreading and performant dynamic recompilation

Executable loader
General relocations, TLS, DLL initialization and authentic Xbox startup

Xbox runtime
Console-specific services, system APIs, filesystem and application lifecycle

RDNA2 shaders
General control flow, broader instructions, Wave64, cross-lane operations and mesh stages

Graphics
Translated texture sampling and broader resource binding

Textures
Authentic Xbox memory layouts and translated sampling

Performance
Production-scale workloads, CPU/GPU profiling and optimized execution

Game compatibility
No demonstrated execution of commercial Xbox titles

BetterXen's current shader fixtures target a bounded subset of desktop gfx1030 behavior. This is not equivalent to complete Xbox Series GPU compatibility.
Progress is measured by reproducible tests rather than estimated game compatibility percentages.

Building BetterXen
Requirements

Apple Silicon Mac running native ARM64 macOS.
Rust toolchain with aarch64-apple-darwin support.
Xcode and Metal development tools.
Python 3.11 or newer.
LLVM with AMDGPU support for applicable shader-fixture assembly and verification.

The recorded Apple M5 environment uses Rust 1.100.0 and Xcode 27.2.
Clone
git clone https://github.com/MacosPorters/betterxen.git
cd betterxen
Build
scripts/bootstrap.sh
cargo build --locked -p betterxen
Run core tests
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --workspace
The format, lint and test trio is the standard check set. The native Metal
passes use Metal API and shader validation; scripts/audit/status.py --check
verifies the generated status tables.
Run native Metal tests
These require a Metal-capable Apple Silicon Mac.
scripts/test-gpu.sh
The native test suite enables Metal API and shader validation and tests the supported compute, rendering and texture paths. The full semantic-review batch defaults to a 300-second timeout; set XENORA_SEMANTIC_TIMEOUT to raise or lower it for a slower or faster host. On macOS, the script uses a Python 3 fallback when GNU timeout is unavailable.
Verify guest execution
cargo test --locked \
--manifest-path experiments/x1/Cargo.toml \
--target aarch64-apple-darwin \
--features metal
Run the original guest resource integration tests:
tests/compat_fixtures/verify-resources.sh
Additional checks:
tests/compat_fixtures/verify.sh
tests/compat_fixtures/verify-compute.sh
scripts/assemble-fixture.sh --check
scripts/demo.sh
Some verification paths require additional tools. Refer to the relevant test scripts and documentation before interpreting a missing dependency as a test failure.
Test evidence
Testing distinguishes between:

CPU correctness: Independent expected values and bounded execution.
Shader compilation: Decoding, lowering and valid generated Metal source.
Native GPU execution: Actual GPU work and checked readback.
Guest integration: Original test executables invoking GPU services and checking results.
Unsupported behavior: Explicit rejections and documented missing functionality.

Compiling a shader is not equivalent to proving its GPU output is correct.
Where the work is heading
See the roadmap table for proposed milestones, and the changelog for the current unreleased additions, such as the native blend pass, indexed draws and the depth pass. The remaining research steps are the outstanding items in current limitations.

The goal is to build a trustworthy native Apple Silicon compatibility framework, one verifiable subsystem at a time.

License
BetterXen is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3 or later.
See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for third-party attribution and docs/legal.md for the project's research and legal boundaries.
BetterXen is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with Microsoft, Xbox, Rockstar Games or Apple.

95zkcq.title: Jenna Ushkowitz Says ‘Glee’s Cory Monteith Tribute “Wasn’t The Right Thing”: “It Was Too Soon For That”
95zkcq.content:
Jenna Ushkowitz doesn’t want to remember when Glee did a tribute to Cory Monteith after his death.

In a new interview, the star of the musical comedy explains why it was difficult to film the episode and why she felt they shouldn’t have done it.

“To shoot ‘The Quarterback’ [tribute episode]… I think it wasn’t the right thing,” Ushkowitz said on the We Need to Talk podcast. “And I think everybody collectively agrees that it’s maybe not the thing that we should have done, because we were grieving both privately and publicly.”

Monteith played Finn Hudson in the Ryan Murphy series until his death in July 2013. The show continued and paid tribute with an episode dedicated to the late actor, which also acknowledged that the quarterback from the fictional William McKinley High School had died.

“I think the fans definitely needed something, because they loved Cory so dearly like we did, and [loved] Finn so dearly,” Ushkowitz said. “But it’s a really hard thing to be grieving your friend and be a character grieving their friend at the same time.”

She continued, “It was like, too soon for that. [It] was not fun, [I] don’t want to remember that time. The show itself was never the same. He was the heart of the show, our friend, most importantly, and our leader. He really was the quarterback for us. He held everybody together. He hosted parties for the crew. He was the kindest. He knew everybody’s names. He just was such a good person, a kind person.”

Ushkowitz mentioned that at the time “even our creators, they were dealing with grief too” and “nobody had the tools” to deal with Monteith’s death.

Watch the full interview in the video below.

157slhx.title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Finale Recap: Who Takes Home The Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy?
157slhx.content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the Season 35 finale of ABC‘s Dancing with the Stars.

It’s that time of year again: Another Dancing with the Stars couple is set to take home the mirrorball come end of show on Tuesday.

That’s right, it’s the Season 35 finale. The five remaining couples will be performing not one, not two, but three routines for their final night in the ballroom.

FIRST PERFORMANCE

First up, the couples are tasked with a fresh take on a dance style they performed earlier this season.

Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik. Tatyana made history as the person with the lowest score ever who made it in the finale, but hey! She made it! Carrie Ann stopped by to ask Tatyana and Jan to redo their salsa. She’s pretty happy with the decision, and the challenge with this second go round is to own the execution. Carrie Ann wants to see fire! “Hello, finale! Tatyana is here! You brought the fire,” Carrie Ann gushed. SCORE: 27 out 30

Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov. After being on top of the leaderboard last week, Derek is challenging Amber to take another spin at the quickstep. She says she had a blast last time, but the judges think her tempo was a little off, so she’s got to lock in this time. The music is faster, so she’ll have to really maintain her frame. “Amber, you are a perfect combination of pure class and a little bit of fire in there,” Derek affirms. SCORE: 30 out of 30

Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. Connor’s journey has been quite a rollercoaster, and they’re ready to take on whatever comes for them in the finale. Carrie Ann lets them know they’ll be doing another viennese waltz, meaning that his main focus during this routine is his frame. It’s been a struggle for him all season, and he has one more shot to get it together. “Connor, bravo! You took every note! Look at that frame!” SCORE: 28 out of 30

Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas. These two have had a mixed bag of reactions from the judges, and Maura is quite exhausted, but she’ll have to muster all her energy for this final push. Bruno tasks her and Mark with redoing the tango, which Maura is happy about. She’s confident that she can show some improvement. “That is how you do a proper ballroom tango,” Bruno compliments. SCORE: 30 out of 30

Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. Ezra is closing out the first round of the competition by taking on another salsa. Bruno tells he and Daniella to work on getting fuller engagement in the hips. They got 9s the last time they performed a salsa, so they’re going to need to hone in on the details if they want 10s. “You did what I asked you. You went supernova with those hips tonight!” Bruno tells him. SCORE: 30 out of 30

SECOND PERFORMANCE

Next up is the instant dance round, where each couple will only have five minutes to prepare their routine.

Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik. These two will take on a jive to “Land of 1000 Dances” by Wilson Pickett, better get to work! Tatyana says in rehearsals she’d really prefer to not have a jive, so the universe is definitely throwing a challenge at her with this. “That was so amazing, that was so entertaining! Guys, good job!” Derek says. SCORE: 27 out of 30

Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov. Amber’s instant dance is taking her back to Week 1 as she’s dancing a cha cha to “Tears” by Sabrina Carpenter. Just like Tatyana, she’s inadvertently picked the dance she admits puts her at a disadvantage, but she’s never been afraid of a challenge, and she won’t start now. “Sometimes when you’re under pressure, it brings out the best in you,” Bruno tells her. SCORE: 30 out of 30

Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. Connor gave himself a cha cha for the instant dance round, and they’ll be dancing to “Buttons” by the Pussycat Dolls. Last time they performed a cha cha, the judges loved their connection but did not love Connor’s technique. He’ll have to really pull through to impress the judges this go round. “Connor…that was your best cha cha,” Carrie Ann says excitedly. SCORE: 25 out of 30

Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas. She’s dancing a quickstep to “Tutti Frutti” by Little Richard! Wow, what a task they have on their hands. The last time they took on the quickstep was Week 3, and she was missing some of the finesse, so she’s got a lot to remember to nail the details this time around. “Fantastic quickstep!” Derek chimes. SCORE: 30 out of 30

Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. Closing out this round, Ezra is facing a tango to “Levels” by Avicii. They seem pretty happy about that, so they might be the only ones in this round to not have been handed their least favorite dance style. “What you do, sometimes I cannot even explain it…” Bruno muses. SCORE: 30 out of 30

THIRD PERFORMANCE

The moment everyone has been waiting for has arrived. It’s time for the freestyles.

Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik. The underdog has arrived at her final dance of the competition. She’s extremely emotional talking to Jan in rehearsal about the journey she’s gone through over the last 11 weeks. She says she’s using her final two minutes on this stage to dream her wildest dreams. “When I watch you, I feel something,” Derek says. SCORE: 28 out of 30

Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov. Amber isn’t holding anything back in her finale freestyle. The mirrorball is in sight, if only she can make it through this last performance. “No question, you are a great dancer,” Bruno confirms. SCORE: 30 out of 30

Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. Quite possibly the most anticipated dance of the season, Connor is paying homage to Tom Holland’s iconic lip sync battle dance with a freestyle to “Singin’ In The Rain/Umbrella” for his final time stepping on the ballroom floor. “That’s what you call ‘Give the people what they want’ freestyle,” Derek compliments. SCORE: 29 out of 30

Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas. She’s come so far from her humble beginnings on Love Island, and though she still feels like that girl from Ireland, she’s standing on a national stage again to rep her country. “Exceeding all expectations!” Bruno exclaims. SCORE: 30 out of 30

Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. Closing out the entire competition, Ezra is using it as one last opportunity to illustrate the odds he’s defied by making it to the finale. But, no sob story here! It’s all about bringing power and energy to this last dance. “Ezra, every time you dance, you come out here and you’ve had purpose…you have been the most amazing ambassador for people with disabilities,” Carrie Ann tells him. SCORE: 30 out of 30

Who wins the mirrorball?

After a grueling 11 weeks, Ezra and Daniella take home the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy. That’s a wrap on Dancing with the Stars Season 35!

gh-1469836447.title: GitHub - Recoi1/RE-DEX: RE:DEX: Pokémon X and Y (3DS) recompiled to native PC, with a shared X/Y cross-play online world. Rust. Bring your own dump.
gh-1469836447.content:
RE:DEX turns Pokémon X and Y (Nintendo 3DS) into a native PC game with a shared online world: X and Y players walk Kalos together and see each other's trainers, in the outfits they made. Written in Rust.

Native, not emulated. The game's ARM11 code is translated ahead of time to C and built on your PC from your own decrypted dump on first launch. This repository contains no Nintendo code or assets.
One world, both versions. X and Y cross-play on the official RE:DEX world (sign in from the start screen with a RE:DEX account) or on community-hosted redex-world servers over Steam. If the official service can't be reached, you can still play peer-to-peer with the characters on your PC. Players nearby, whispers, reports and an Ignore list are in; trades, battles and a market come later, each behind server-side legality checks.
Your own front door. A start screen with a game builder, cross-game characters and a 3D character creator, ahead of the 3DS title screen.
PC features. High frame rates with Smooth motion (up to your monitor's refresh rate), resolution scaling, controller support, texture packs.
Discord status. Your Discord profile shows the game, the mode and your play time, if Discord is running.
Fair online. Fast forward, dev tools, local-wireless rooms and game-changing mods are off while you're in a world.

How to play. Download the release folder and run redex.exe. Press Add your game, pick your own decrypted Pokémon X or Y dump (.cci or .3ds), and wait while RE:DEX builds it on your PC (a few minutes, the first time only). Then make a character and press Play. Everything it needs is in the folder; nothing else has to be installed. Maintainers build the folder with tools/release/make-release.ps1.
Your character. The start screen keeps your characters, up to 8. New character opens the creator: pick a boy or a girl, skin, hair style and colour, and eyes, and name them. The preview is the game itself drawing your trainer, so what you see is what you get; drag it to turn the model, scroll to zoom. A character plays in both X and Y: a new game starts as them (their name, gender and look), and Import a save brings in an existing main save (copied, never moved) from RE:DEX's own save folder, Citra or Azahar, or a Checkpoint backup. Remove character takes one off the list (after asking) and leaves its saves on disk. Each character has its own saves, and RE:DEX backs them up before every launch. Clothes you buy in a boutique stay with the character, in the other game too. Online, your characters live on your account, so they are there on any PC you sign in on, and other players see the look you made.
Mods. The start screen's Mods button lists the Pokémon X and Y mods on GameBanana and installs texture packs and skins with one press; turn them on and off there. Skins and texture packs play online (only you see them); mods that change game data are marked Offline only. See docs/mods.md.
Status: early development. Community: Discord.
Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Game Freak, Creatures Inc. or The Pokémon Company.

Como usar / How to use
Baixe a última versão, abra o BlueStinger-Recompiler.exe e
escolha o seu disco. O instalador compila o jogo na sua máquina e nada do disco sai dela. Imagens aceitas: GDI,

Download the latest release, open BlueStinger-Recompiler.exe
and pick your disc. The installer builds the game on your machine and nothing from the disc leaves it. Accepted images:
GDI, CUE/BIN (like Redump's), CHD and CDI, also inside .zip or .7z.
Para compilar, o instalador usa o Visual Studio (ou os Build Tools), se estiver instalado. Se não estiver, ele oferece um
compilador portátil: baixa o Zig, o CMake e o Ninja oficiais (cerca de 125 MB, cada arquivo conferido pelo SHA-256) e
os guarda só no seu perfil, em %LOCALAPPDATA%\BlueStingerRecomp\compilador, sem instalar nada no sistema.
To build, the installer uses Visual Studio (or the Build Tools) when it is installed. Otherwise it offers a portable
compiler: it downloads the official Zig, CMake and Ninja (about 125 MB, each file checked by SHA-256) and keeps them only
in your profile, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\BlueStingerRecomp\compilador, without installing anything on the system.
Pela linha de comando, o Builder faz o mesmo:
From the command line, the Builder does the same:
bs-builder --disc <seu_disco.cdi> --out <pasta> --kit . --sdl3 build/msvc-release/_deps/sdl3-src
bs-builder ... --compilador-portatil

Para desenvolvedores / For developers
Requisitos: Visual Studio 2022 ou mais novo (ou os Build Tools) com CMake e Ninja, ou Clang. O jogo também compila com o
Zig no alvo x86_64-windows-gnu. Abra um Developer PowerShell e rode:
Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 or newer (or the Build Tools) with CMake and Ninja, or Clang. The game also builds with
Zig for the x86_64-windows-gnu target. Open a Developer PowerShell and run:
cmake --preset msvc-debug
cmake --build --preset msvc-debug
ctest --preset msvc-debug

O teste real_disc usa a sua imagem quando BS_DISC_IMAGE aponta para o .cdi, .gdi, .cue ou .chd. Sem essa
variável, ele é ignorado.
The real_disc test uses your image when BS_DISC_IMAGE points to the .cdi, .gdi, .cue or .chd. Without that
variable it is skipped.
Ferramentas de linha de comando:
Command-line tools:
bs-extract --info "ISO/Blue Stinger.cdi" # mostra faixas e hash sem gravar nada / shows tracks and hash, writes nothing
bs-extract "ISO/Blue Stinger.cdi" game-data # extrai e valida o hash / extracts and checks the hash
bs-recomp config/bluestinger_us.toml # gera generated/*.cpp / generates generated/*.cpp
bs-disasm game-data/1ST_READ.BIN 0x8C010000 0x8C010000 64 # disassembly: base, início, quantidade / base, start, count

O executável 1ST_READ.BIN precisa ter o SHA-256 de uma versão suportada (tools/extractor/known_versions.h). Com
--force, a extração acontece mesmo assim, e o resultado fica marcado como não verificado.

TAT-2 — Thick As Thieves rebuilt in Godot 4.7
A private-use, asset-faithful port of the shipped UE5.5 game Thick As Thieves
to Godot 4.7.2 (Forward+, Jolt, 1280×720 reference). The port loads the real
extracted geometry, materials, landscapes, audio, animation and gameplay tables;
the TAT-2 expansion adds The Moth thief, Jaspering Hall and co-op.

Private-use notice. Extracted assets from the Steam install live in
extracted/ and game/assets/ue/, both git-ignored. Only original code, tools
and expansion content are committed. Do not redistribute extracted content.

Status (2026-11-24, bc063d2) — playable end-to-end: startscreen → Den →
contract prep → Guildhall run → two-phase escape → scoring, plus free-play
cleanout, carried-loot capacity and stashing, two-player ENet co-op and all five
E2E tiers.

Gate
Result

GDScript compile (tools/check_scripts_compile.gd)
120 scripts, 0 broken

Unit/integration (tests/run_tests.gd)
278 checks, fails=0 (suites numbered to 90)

M2 traversal/tools (tests/test_m2_player.gd)
fails=0 (11)

E2E (tests/e2e/run_e2e_tests.gd, tiers 1–4 + s2)
278/278 (tier 1: 117)

Door walk · viewmodel truth · Niagara · leak probe
PASS

Steam manifest + content audit (make audit)
exit 0, fail-closed tracked baseline, disk-backed coverage 99.6 % (12657/12703), 13/13 content groups

Gate ratchet (make gate-ratchet)
PASS — floors verified against committed logs

Not yet measured: the perf matrix (no publishable FPS run) and the editor's
per-process VRAM. Do not quote frame rates from any older run.
Quick start
make run # launch the game (native tools/godot, Flatpak fallback)
make test # headless unit/integration suite
make audit # fail-closed content + producer-baseline gate
python3 tools/test_manifest_audit.py # negative controls for the audit
A fresh clone needs the private assets first:
make extract # CUE4Parse dump of the Steam install
make normalize # generated JSON (levels, materials, gameplay, …)
make anims # 995 animation GLBs (Blender, ~30 min)
tools/reimport_assets.sh # Godot import
make desktop-texture-cap # 1024 px cap + mipmaps (rerun after clean extract)
Requirements: Godot 4.7.2 (tools/godot wrapper), Python 3, .NET 10 SDK (extractor),
Blender (anims). Linux x86_64 desktop is the supported target; Android internal
builds are documented in docs/ANDROID.md.
Commands

Command
Purpose

make run
Launch the desktop client (F3 = FPS/draw-call overlay)

make test
Headless integration run (278 checks)

make audit
Fail-closed gate: texture cap, mount/disk coverage, 13 content domains, producer output hashes, errors.log marker, freshness

make gate-ratchet
Assert the gate floors in tools/gate_ratchet.json against the committed logs in docs/reports/logs/

make audit-bootstrap
Explicit first run; writes the tracked tools/audit_baseline.json

make audit-refresh-stamps
Escape hatch after regeneration; missing/decreased outputs still fail

make audit-imports
Separate Godot import gate (.import sidecars + .translation)

make normalize
Run all 21 generated-data producers

make linux-build / make linux-stamp-verify / make linux-run
Linux x86_64 export, its HEAD/PCK provenance stamp, and a run

make android-debug / make android-release
Signed internal APK

make desktop-texture-cap
Re-bake the 1024 px texture cap

make texture-cap-check
Read-only: fail if any over-cap loader texture lacks the cap + mipmaps

make editor
Open the Godot editor with the TAT-2 Review dock

make bake-review MAP=guildhall
Headless bake of one binary LevelLoader scene per sublevel (+ manifest)

make bake-review-core
Bake the single-file core map used for load/VRAM checks

make review MAP=guildhall
In-game free-camera review of the static world (no mission)

build/qa/test_perf_guard.sh
Exercise the perf wrapper's stamp/temperature/RSS contracts without launching a game

tools/audit_baseline.json is tracked and records every producer/infrastructure
hash, external tool version and per-output content digest. A normal run with no
baseline fails; make audit-bootstrap is the explicit first-run path.
tools/audit_allowlists.json holds the 73 known case-only path normalizations,
33 case-only .ubulk companions and 46 known-undumped manifest paths.
Headless gates that are not Make aliases:
tools/godot --headless --path game --script "$PWD/tools/check_scripts_compile.gd"
tools/godot --headless --path game --script res://tests/test_m2_player.gd
tools/godot --headless --path game --script res://tests/e2e/run_e2e_tests.gd
tools/godot --headless --path game --script res://probe_leak.gd
World review
The real Guildhall/Den/Old-Manor world can be inspected without starting a
mission, with the same LevelLoader the game uses:
make bake-review MAP=guildhall # per-sublevel .scn + world.scn + review.tscn + manifest
make editor # TAT-2 Review dock: bake/open, sublevel+kind toggles, bookmarks
make review MAP=guildhall # in-game free camera (WASD/QE, 1-0 toggles, F1-F6 bookmarks, P capture)
make review-capture MAP=guildhall # offscreen six-bookmark PNG sweep (no window presentation needed)
Generated scenes land in game/scenes/review/<map>/ and are git-ignored
(extracted-content derivatives). The in-game camera loads the live world, not
the baked scenes; P saves PNGs to user://review_captures/. Architecture,
tagging vocabulary, measured Den/lobby numbers and limits are in
docs/reports/review-map-baker.md.
Playing

Thieves: The Spider (grapple wire), The Chameleon (disguise integrity),
The Moth (astral scout, TAT-2 expansion).
Gadgets: Slithersap, smoke bomb, pickpocket fairy, blackjack, Thief Vision,
lean left/right.
Contracts: 16 shipped contracts across Old Manor and Guildhall on Novice /
Thief / Master Thief, plus the FTUE tutorial route. The TAT-2 expansion adds
The Moth, the Jaspering Hall prep/tutorial identity and 2-player ENet co-op.
Free play: in the Thieves' Den map table press G (or the
FREE PLAY: GUILDHALL CLEANOUT [G] button) for a score-only Contract Inactive
run of Mission.Guildhall.LootTheRoom. No contract progress or currency is
banked.
Run clock: 55:00 on the main window (the mission's authored duration).
Completing the objectives summons the escape doors and starts a separate
20:00 endgame window; the doors stay open for 4 minutes each, then collapse.
Loot: 12 authored inventory slots — minor loot takes 1, major loot 3, so
four majors fill the bag. A full bag refuses the pickup with the authored
INVENTORY FULL line. Deposit everything at a stash to free slots; stashed
value is banked even if you are caught, while carried loot is only kept if you
escape.
QA autostart: --qa-free-play, --qa-mission, --qa-contract <n>.

Repository layout
game/ Godot project (src/, scenes/, tests/, assets/ue -> extracted)
tools/ extractor (.NET/CUE4Parse), 21 normalizers, audit + gates
build/qa/ tracked capture/probe harness sources (captures ignored)
docs/ architecture, performance, fidelity tracker, wave reports, handoffs
extracted/ private extraction cache (gitignored)

Runtime code lives under game/src/{core,player,ai,stealth,interact,missions,ui};
data under game/data/generated/ (gitignored, produced by make normalize).
Documentation

AGENTS.md — operating rules, gates and traps for coding agents.
docs/HANDOFF_NEXT_AGENT.md — current state,
pipeline gotchas and open work.
docs/FIDELITY_GAPS.md — live 1:1 coverage tracker and
every documented residual.
docs/reports/w7-integration.md — latest
wave: loot capacity/stash/payout and save v8, two-phase run clock and 25 escape
markers, surface-resolved hearing, stair descent, KF11 backdrop and Cotter
wardrobe, export provenance and the Sonar plan.
docs/reports/review-remediation-wave.md
— earlier wave: beams, two-sided materials, albedo recovery, doors, traversal
blockers, FOV, loot grounding, sign, free play.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md,
docs/PERFORMANCE.md,
docs/reports/ — module map, batching numbers, per-area reports.

Known residuals
See docs/FIDELITY_GAPS.md. The visible ones: Guildhall
POI graybox floors/floating furniture, sign lettering low-contrast at 27 m, some
white glass/emissive plates, the Den's 43.5 vs UE 52.6 Lumen GI gap, and a
7-texture probe-exit warning (TAT2_NO_DEN_PROBE=1 is the clean path).
Behavioural residuals: walked descents of 0.18–0.30 m still take 4–12 airborne
frames, the two-phase timer banks local-only in co-op, the post-match haul screen
is not built, and XP still uses the port's invented rule rather than the authored
DefaultGame.ini curve — which brings the 48 level-gated market items far
earlier than authored. Hearing is range-based: walls and closed doors do not
block sound yet.

gonp5g.title: Больше тысячи километров без дозаправки: Haval анонсировал новый кроссовер
gonp5g.content:
Официальная премьера гибридного кроссовера Haval H6L запланирована на 27 ноября. В преддверии премьеры автомобиль с классической гибридной системой HEV впервые показали на официальных изображениях и раскрыли часть информации о модели. Haval H6LКузов насчитывает 4800х1895х1730 мм, колесная база растянута до 2810 мм. Салон строго пятиместный. Колесные диски – 19-дюймовые.Спереди H6L узнается по зауженной светотехнике и трапециевидному воздухозаборнику – в его центральную часть встроены датчики систем помощи водителю. Во всю ширину пятой двери протянулась светодиодная балка с логотипом GWM.По низу кузова идут черные пластиковые накладки, на крыше предусмотрены компактные рейлинги. Ручки дверей сделали классическими, под естественный хват.Haval H6LГибридная система Hi2 приводит в движение только передние колеса. От розетки тяговую батарею заряжать нельзя: установка работает в связке с ДВС и подпитывается за счет рекуперации энергии торможения.Полуторалитровый турбоагрегат выдает 156 л.с. и ассистирует электромотору на 177 л.с. В сумме отдача установки составляет 248 л.с. В качестве трансмиссии используется 2-ступенчатая гибридная DHT.До сотни кроссовер ускоряется за 7,8 секунды, максимальная скорость – 180 км/ч. Средний расход топлива заявлен на отметке 4,9 л/100 км по циклу WLTC, а полного бака хватает на 1082 км.В списке опций – адаптивные амортизаторы и система водительских ассистентов Coffee Pilot 3.Медиацентр получил 15,6-дюймовый тачскрин, мощный чип, голосовое управление, бортовую навигацию и интеграцию смартфонов по нескольким протоколам. Предусмотрены быстрая беспроводная зарядка на 50 Вт, двухзонный климат-контроль, бесключевой доступ и "теплые" опции.Цифровая приборка снабжена солнцезащитным козырьком. На переднем пассажирском кресле есть выдвижная оттоманка.Что до цен и даты старта продаж гибрида, их не уточняют.
