3sui16.title: В Литве задержали пять граждан страны по подозрению в сотрудничестве с ВГТРК
3sui16.content:
В Литве в среду, 25 ноября, задержали пять граждан страны, которых подозревают в сотрудничестве со Всероссийской государственной телевизионной и радиовещательной компанией (ВГТРК). Задержания провели в рамках досудебного расследования по делу об оказании помощи государству в действиях против Литвы, указано в совместном заявлении генпрокуратуры Литвы и главного комиссариата полиции Вильнюсского уезда.

Столичные правоохранители вместе с департаментом госбезопасности Литвы начали расследование после появления информации о том, что группа граждан страны с осени 2024 года "поддерживала контакты" с представителями ВГТРК. Отмечается, что за денежное вознаграждение задержанные выполняли различные поручения по сбору и передаче "информации, представляющей интерес для государства, враждебного настроенного по отношению к Литве".

Кроме того, по данным следствия, задержанные "готовили и распространяли" в стране контент, который "соответствует интересам России и повторяет нарративы российской пропаганды". В рамках расследования также провели более десяти обысков. "В ближайшее время будут приняты решения о применении мер процессуального принуждения", - указано в заявлении.

Задержания связаны с организацией "Кондукторы родины"

Задержаны - Казимерас Юрайтис, Вайда Юозапайтите, Дмитрий Глазков, Лауринас Рагельскис и Миндаугас Рамошка - члены организации "Кондукторы родины" (Tėvynės konduktoriai), подтвердили в прокуратуре агентству BNS.

На прошлой неделе литовское онлайн-издание 15min писало, что участники этого объединения, зарегистрированного в стране как СМИ, злоупотребляли правом получать комментарии госструктур, и направляли в различные ведомства сотни запросов, касающихся обороны, безопасности, миграции, а также других чувствительных тем. "Подавляющее большинство" полученных ответов не публиковались, а при отказе предоставлять комментарии члены организации подавали в суд.

10n3iqa.title: Former FTX COO Constance Wang Slams 'Racist' ‘The Altruists’ Portrayal
10n3iqa.content:
Former FTX COO Constance Wang is calling out Netflix’s “The Altruists.” Wang took to social media on Wednesday to respond to whether the streamer had consulted her about what she describes as a “very stereotypical” portrayal of her by actress Madison Hu.

“People have asked whether Netflix consulted me. They didn’t,” wrote Wang on X. “One conversation would at least have saved Madison Hu, who plays me, the trouble of putting on a Chinese accent I don’t have. It feels very stereotypical, then again, it’s Netflix. What did we expect?”

On Monday, Wang wrote that she and others who had worked at Alameda Research and FTX, the companies the show focuses on, recognized “little beyond the names” in the Graham Moore-created limited series.

“My expectations were low, but I’m still surprised it’s this bad,” she continued. “In short, the story has nothing to do with what actually happened at FTX or Alameda… Maybe you’ll enjoy The Altruists as a romantic comedy. For those of us who watched it together, it felt like someone else’s story with our names attached.”

“The Altruists,” the Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner-led drama inspired by the real-life story of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, hit the streamer on Nov. 19. Per the show’s official logline, “The Altruists” tells the story of Bankman-Fried (Boyle) and Ellison (Garner), “two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye — before they were accused of stealing $8 billion.”

Bankman-Fried founded the failed FTX cryptocurrency exchange in 2019, before ultimately being sentenced to 25 years in prison when a federal jury convicted him on seven counts of fraud and conspiracy related to the collapse of his cryptocurrency company and related hedge fund. The U.S. government alleged that Bankman-Fried had cheated investors and customers out of upwards of $10 billion through FTX and his crytpo trading firm Alameda Research.

Ellison was the CEO of Alameda Research, a trading firm affiliated with FTX, and was in a relationship with Bankman-Fried.

17i5o6y.title: Ms. Rachel Explains How Mr. Rogers’ “Radical” Programming Inspired Her: “A Huge Responsibility”
17i5o6y.content:
As Ms. Rachel continues her mission-driven work, she’s crediting the “radical” influence of Mr. Rogers and her pals on Sesame Street.

The famed YouTube children’s educator and activist (whose real name is Rachel Accurso) recently explained that the “intentional and caring” programming on Mr. Rogers’ Neighborhood when she was a kid has inspired her work on the hit Ms. Rachel series.

“When you see Mr. Rogers sharing the pool [with Officer Clemmons], when you when you see on Sesame Street, Black and white children playing together, you’re not like, ‘Wow, that was radical.’ But it was so radical,” she told Hasan Minhaj. “And it’s amazing that I get to be part of a field that is radical, that was pushing those those boundaries.”

Ms. Rachel continued, “I feel honored to be in children’s media and I don’t know if that deep care for children translates to being progressive and being like, ‘Kids should have SNAP benefits. We want kids to eat. We shouldn’t be killing over 20,000 kids in Gaza. They shouldn’t be losing their limbs. And I’m going to show Rahaf on the show and show that she’s just like any other 3-year-old.’ And I think it’s kind of by design that people want to make us think it’s so long ago, but it’s not so long ago. Ruby Bridges is alive and on Instagram.”

Noting that Mr. Rogers “knew that children’s media is a huge responsibility and he took that responsibility really seriously” on his PBS series from 1968 to 2001, and even “called out everyone once” at the Emmy Awards, Ms. Rachel admires that he “wasn’t afraid” to tackle serious topics on his show.

“He just was so caring and he really had that pause and he just spoke to children about things that were really serious and he wasn’t afraid to tackle death or assassination or war,” she said.

When people question, “What would Mr. Rogers be now?” Ms. Rachel points out that he dedicated multiple episodes in 1983 to call out the government for spending tax dollars on bombs during anxieties around the Cold War.

“He came out and said it in the show,” she said. “And so, sometimes people are like, ‘Oh, he was subtle. He didn’t come out and say things.’ But he really addressed things in the show more than I do because my show is for younger [kids]. I do have Rahaf on the show. You know, I say things by just having people there. But he really tackled things.”

Ms. Rachel’s comments come as she visited children in immigration court earlier this week, having previously been an outspoken advocate for children in ICE detention centers and Palestinian children in Gaza.

xw11dk.content:
Hexmonger представила меха-роглайт-шутер Tin Coffins и назвала дату его выхода. Ролик демонстрирует сражения отрядов, сел-шейдинг, боевых мехов и разрушенные войной города.
Игрок возьмёт роль боевого клона Talon-22, которому предстоят короткие смертельные вылазки против вражеских подразделений. Локации будут генерироваться процедурно, а противники смогут обходить с флангов, подавлять огнём и удерживать позиции.
После гибели в бой отправится следующий клон. Tin Coffins выйдет в Steam.

p5bgko.title: Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea
p5bgko.content:
More than a mile below the surface of the Red Sea, researchers from the University of Miami (UM) Rosenstiel School of Marine and Atmospheric Science discovered rare deep-sea brine pools in the Gulf of Aqaba, a northern extension of the Red Sea. These unusually salty underwater lakes could provide clues to how Earth's oceans formed millions of years ago and help guide the search for life on other planets.
The discovery was made by Sam Purkis, professor and chair of the UM Department of Marine Geosciences, and his colleagues in collaboration with OceanX. The researchers located the pools at a depth of more than one mile (1,770 meters) using a remotely operated underwater vehicle (ROV) deployed from the OceanXplorer, an advanced research vessel equipped to investigate some of the least accessible environments on Earth.
"Until we understand the limits of life on Earth, it will be difficult to determine if alien planets can host any living beings," said Purkis. "Our discovery of a rich community of microbes that survive in extreme environments can help trace the limits of life on Earth and can be applied to the search for life elsewhere in our solar system and beyond."
Life thrives in extreme underwater lakes
Brine pools rank among the harshest environments on our planet. Their waters contain exceptionally high concentrations of salt, feature unusual chemical conditions, and are completely devoid of oxygen. Despite these seemingly inhospitable conditions, the pools support abundant microbial life. Previous research on microbes inhabiting Red Sea brine pools has even identified biologically active molecules with potential anticancer properties.
The findings, published in Communications Earth & Environment, mark the first documented discovery of brine pools in the Gulf of Aqaba. Remarkably, the researchers nearly missed them.
"We were very lucky," said Purkis. "The discovery came in the last five minutes of the ten-hour ROV dive that we could dedicate to this project."
Hidden records of ancient tsunamis and earthquakes

Beyond their biological significance, the pools serve as natural archives of the region's geological history. Situated relatively close to the coastline, their extremely salty waters and absence of oxygen help preserve evidence of tsunamis, flash floods, and earthquakes that occurred in the Gulf of Aqaba thousands of years ago. Regional tectonic activity has produced numerous faults and fractures across the seabed in this part of the gulf.
Earlier in 2022, Purkis and his colleagues uncovered evidence of a 500-year-old underwater landslide that likely generated a substantial tsunami. Understanding the region's history of such events could have important implications for coastal development in Egypt and Saudi Arabia.
The study, titled "Discovery of the deep-sea NEOM Brine Pools in the Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea," was published on June 27, 2022, in Communications Earth & Environment.
The research team included Sam J. Purkis, Hannah Shernisky, Peter K. Swart, Arash Sharifi, Amanda Oehlert, Gaëlle Duchâtellier, James Klaus, Gregor P. Eberli, Larry Peterson, and Graham Kolodziej from the UM Rosenstiel School; Fabio Marchese and Francesca Benzoni from King Abdullah University of Science and Technology's Red Sea Research Center; Giovanni Chimienti from the University of Bari Aldo Moro in Italy; Andrew Craig and Mattie Rodrigue from OceanX; Jürgen Titschack from MARUM -- Center for Marine Environmental Sciences in Germany; and Ameer Abdulla from NEOM.
NEOM, a company developing the Saudi Arabian coastline, provided funding for the four-week research expedition aboard the OceanXplorer.
Watch the NEOM OceanX documentary about the discovery: https://youtu.be/bWNftnYDx9c

rdtb7n.title: Do we really know more about space than the ocean?
rdtb7n.content:
Credit: Particle

New discoveries are made about the world every day—a species of deep-sea fish here, a new galaxy there. There's a saying, "We know more about space than the ocean." But is this true? How do we determine knowing? Is it the number of things we have directly observed, or is it a matter of resolution?

To get to the bottom of this unknown, oceanographer Associate Professor Jeff Hansen and astrophysicist Dr. Kat Ross weigh in.
Mapping the oceans
More than 70% of the Earth's surface is ocean.
A whopping 94% of that water is deep ocean—that is, greater than 200 meters (656 feet) deep—yet only 0.001% of it has been observed.
Most of what we know about the ocean comes from scientists mapping the underwater terrain. "A lot of the technologies that exist to measure and map things don't work well in water," says Hansen.
These technologies often use electromagnetic radiation including lasers, radar or gamma waves.
The problem, Hansen says, is that water absorbs all of these wavelengths. "That's why it's pitch black at the bottom of the ocean; no light can get there," he says.
Oceanographers have opted for sonar, which works by pinging sound into the ocean and then measuring the time it takes for the signal to return after reflection. Unfortunately, Hansen says it's "extremely slow."
"That's why most of the ocean hasn't been mapped in any sufficient resolution."
As of early 2026, only 28.7% of the ocean floor has been accurately mapped using sonar. "It's easier to map Mars," says Hansen.

Mapping the heavens
The technologies that don't work so well in water work wonders in space.
"The web of structure within the universe that links all the galaxies and clusters together requires a different form of mapping," says Ross.
There are optical telescopes for mapping what we can see and radio telescopes for recording what we can't.
For team optical, the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument has plotted a staggering 5.6 trillion-pixel map, accounting for 75% of the night sky.
For radio heads, the Very Large Array Sky Survey has mapped 82% of the sky—it can map places where space dust is too thick for visible light to penetrate.
"Every time we think we've got a grip on things we discover something entirely new that we had not even considered was possible," says Ross.
Fumbling in the dark
While more of the night sky has been mapped, both environments have a unique set of research challenges. "Once you get down to those depths the pressure is just crazy," says Hansen.
In the Mariana Trench—the deepest point in the ocean—pressures reach over 1,000 kg/cm². That's equivalent to having a small car parked on your fingernail.
Pressure aside, very little sunlight penetrates below about 200 meters (656 feet) down, and GPS won't make it past the ocean's surface.
"It's like you walk into a room that is well lit… and then you turn the lights off and try to navigate by remembering where everything was," says Hansen.
Being able to demonstrate what you've seen when you can't even see seems difficult.

Nothing but noise
"Radio astronomy faces an issue called 'confusion,' where we can't measure what's background noise and what's source," says Ross.
This noise comes from every electrical thing around us and interferes with radio telescopes.
"If we put a mobile phone on the moon, that [radio signal] is 300x brighter than the brightest radio galaxies that we look at."
With the ever-increasing number of satellites in Earth's orbit, Ross says we might be approaching a critical tipping point where radio telescopes will cease to cut through the interference.
Unlike the ocean, space is seemingly infinite and you can't just wade in. It takes massive teams with massive budgets years to learn anything new about space.
Will we ever know?
This may have been a fruitless exercise. How can we compare how much we know between two topics if we can't even define "know?"
Where do we draw the line on what counts as ocean or space research? Such enormous fields are difficult to constrain. Both environments are forever changing.
"There are just so many interactions and dynamic processes that are happening in every part of the universe," says Ross.
Hansen expresses a similar sentiment about the ocean: "It's not static, unfortunately; you have to keep measuring it."
How can we know everything there is to know if it's always in a state of flux? Perhaps the uncomfortable truth is, we never will, but at least there's no shortage of new discoveries to be made.

1frsg89.title: 'The Squirrel' Review: An Endearing Futuristic Dramedy
1frsg89.content:
If Finnish master Aki Kaurismäki, with his measured emotional register and stoic humor, were to ever make a science-fiction film taking a page from a seminal text in the genre like “Blade Runner,” it may resemble Markus Lehmusruusu’s endearing dramedy “The Squirrel.”

Before one learns anything else about how the film’s unspecified, seemingly idyllic future operates, Lehmusruusu reveals that even the intimate act of masturbation has been automated here. The opening scene sees Pasi (Miro Lopperi), a lanky man in his early 30s whose face radiates heartwarming innocence, step into a rose-colored room for a machine to help him “regulate his hormones.”

Rather than offering a montage, an introductory title card, or an expository speech on the mechanics of this era, the astute writer-director (with a background mostly in local episodic TV) allows for the most essential of those details to surface as we follow Pasi’s mundane day as part of a team designing the latest robotic pet: a dog that’s only slightly more sophisticated versions of those Poo-Chi toy pups from the early 2000s.

The tone, from the onset, is charmingly deadpan, with the characters acting oblivious to the absurdism. Again, if Kaurismäki needs a homegrown successor, he may have one in Lehmusruusu. Following a September premiere at Fantastic Fest, the film has been picked up for North American distribution by Obscured Releasing.

Every aspect of everyone’s life is monitored under the guise of maintaining collective comfort and happiness above individual satisfaction. Swear words are discouraged by the ominous artificial voice that’s always listening, and even bending machines decide whether one should consume caffeine or not. Each person wears a bracelet that keeps track of their health — not too far from what smart watches already do today. In Lehmusruusu’s vision, these devices and the information they collect have already become instruments of control.

This emotionally sanitized world emerges visually via the formalism of cinematographer Max Smeds’s elegant framing, showcasing the symmetrical spaces and parallel lines in the infrastructure of this reality: escalators at a subway station, the stairs in the building were Pasi works, or the homogenously designed apartment complexes. For the interior of Pasi’s flat, production designer Michael Randel creates a mostly white, brightly lit, nearly antiseptic space where chaos seems unfathomable. Likewise, the muted colors of the costumes enhance the feeling of existing in an oppressively solemn, lifeless timeline.

Pasi’s understanding of this post-stress world, where all his needs are met and nothing unexpected ever occurs, is upended when he comes across the titular rodent one night on his way home. The encounter, which he must report, also introduces him to investigator Emilia (Mimosa Willamo). Attraction is instant between the two, but neither makes a move. Lehmusruusu makes clear that a crime like adultery is punished with a procedure that erases the perpetrator’s memory, implying that spontaneous love might also be off limits.

The streamlined conception of the narrative, with no intel about the characters’ past or specifics on how people are raised in this society to become model citizens, works because it frees the film from having to explicitly justify every choice. Instead, it distills the ideas into situations that offer enough context for the point to come across without being burdened by lengthy explanations. As a bridge to the past, Lehmusruusu provides Jimi (Hannu-Pekka Björkman), a longtime employee at Pasi’s job with knowledge about the animals that once roamed the earth and what’s beyond the bubble that humanity (or at least this segment of it) have trapped themselves in.

It’s only after he secretly adopts the squirrel that Pasi begins to comprehend that it’s precisely the randomness of an organic life, at times acting and reacting on instinct (even if against one’s best interests) that makes the experience of being alive worthwhile, or at least interesting. Those in charge seek to prevent unpredictability at all costs, stopping people from making mistakes, but also from finding greater fulfilment. The ethos that runs through Lehmusruusu’s narrative aligns with the approach to bringing the squirrel character to the screen — the animal is mostly played by four real rescue squirrels under the care of a trainer (with some assistance from a puppet and minimal CGI).

The disarming faint smile that appears on Lopperi’s face when Pasi plays with said squirrel — a playful interaction that an artificial creature cannot match — turns into a frown as the little furball shows signs of heartache. Lehmusruusu takes this newly found relationship between man and nature as the vehicle to encourage Pasi to seek a human bond, not in an intellectual manner, but surrendering to his inherent need for companionship and physical touch. An effectively minimalist, offbeat delight, “The Squirrel” makes a case for organic love in the age of automation.

tdvfr9.title: Astronomers may have discovered a black hole born before the first stars
tdvfr9.content:
On December 18, 2019, astronomers recorded something unusual happening to a star in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way. For approximately one hour, the star gradually grew brighter before fading back to its usual appearance. The change was smooth and symmetrical, with no sudden explosion or flare. It looked as though an invisible object had moved between Earth and the star, bending its light in our direction. Afterward, the star returned to normal and showed no further changes in brightness.
Researchers have named the mysterious object Phoebe, but its true identity remains unknown. The event appears to be an example of gravitational microlensing, a phenomenon predicted by Einstein's general theory of relativity. When a compact object with sufficient mass passes in front of a distant star, its gravity bends the star's light and temporarily magnifies its brightness. This produces a recognizable pattern that differs from the changes caused by variable stars, stellar flares, or passing asteroids.
Astronomers at Swinburne University in Melbourne identified the signal while examining observations from a survey that frequently monitored stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud. The distinctive pattern convinced the team that they had detected a genuine gravitational microlensing event. What remained uncertain was the nature of the invisible object responsible.
Three Possible Explanations for the Mysterious Object
Researchers have identified three potential explanations for Phoebe. One possibility is a rogue planet that was expelled from its original solar system and now travels alone through the Milky Way. Another is a similar wandering planet located within the Large Magellanic Cloud. If the second explanation proves correct, Phoebe would become the first planet discovered through gravitational microlensing beyond our galaxy.
The third possibility is far more extraordinary. Phoebe could be a primordial black hole, an ancient object that formed in the earliest moments of the universe. Unlike ordinary black holes, which develop when massive stars collapse, primordial black holes could have emerged from extremely dense regions of space during the first fractions of a second after the Big Bang. Such objects would have formed long before the first stars appeared.
A One-Hour Signal Reveals a Surprising Clue
The unusually short duration of the brightening provides an important clue about Phoebe's mass. Gravitational microlensing events depend partly on how massive the intervening object is. Generally, lighter objects produce shorter events, although their speed and position also influence how long the magnification lasts.

Phoebe's signal lasted approximately 60 minutes, placing it near the detection limit of current astronomical surveys. Using the observed duration and their models of the event, researchers estimated that the object has a mass roughly three times that of the Moon. That would make it considerably less massive than any planet in our solar system and far too small to be a conventional black hole formed by a collapsing star.
Black holes produced through stellar collapse typically have masses of at least about five times that of the Sun. Phoebe's estimated mass falls enormously below that threshold. If the mysterious object really is a black hole, its tiny mass would point toward a primordial origin rather than the death of a star.
Could Phoebe Be a Primordial Black Hole Linked to Dark Matter?
To investigate where Phoebe might belong, the researchers compared the likelihood that the object originated from different populations. These included stars in the Milky Way, stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud, and objects associated with the surrounding dark matter halo.
The results strongly favored the dark matter halo. According to the team's calculations, Phoebe is approximately 100,000 times more likely to belong to this population than to one associated with ordinary stellar matter. This enormous difference makes a potential connection to dark matter particularly intriguing, although it does not establish that Phoebe is a primordial black hole.
If the primordial black hole interpretation is correct, Phoebe could be among the oldest objects ever detected. It may have formed before the first atoms and stars existed, when the universe was still experiencing the extreme conditions that followed the Big Bang.
For roughly 13 billion years, such an object could have traveled unseen through space, leaving almost no trace of its existence. Then, on a single night in December 2019, its gravity may have briefly magnified the light of a distant star, offering astronomers a remarkable glimpse of something born near the very beginning of the universe.

19qclc0.title: God of War: Sons of Sparta получила неофициальный ПК-порт - поддержка 4K, 240 FPS и ультрашироких экранов
19qclc0.content:
Энтузиасты выпустили первую версию неофициального ПК-порта God of War: Sons of Sparta, позволяющего запускать оригинальную версию игры для PlayStation 4 непосредственно на Windows x64. Экспериментальная поддержка также реализована для Linux и Steam Deck.
Порт предлагает ряд улучшений по сравнению с оригиналом. В частности, появилась поддержка разрешений вплоть до 4K, ультрашироких мониторов с соотношением сторон 21:9 и 32:9, а также частоты кадров до 240 FPS. Доступны режимы 30, 60, 90, 120, 144, 165 и 240 FPS, а также неограниченная частота кадров с корректной синхронизацией.
Среди других возможностей:

Поддержка локального кооператива на двоих в режиме The Pit of Agonies — за Кратоса и Деймоса.
Возможность открыть The Pit of Agonies и Hermes Mode с самого начала, не проходя сюжетную кампанию.
Автоматическое переключение обозначений кнопок между контроллерами Xbox и PlayStation.
Поддержка DualShock 4, DualSense и других геймпадов SDL.
Сглаживание SMAA, анизотропная фильтрация до 16x, масштабирование AMD FSR 1 и повышение резкости RCAS.
Локальная система достижений и сохранений с резервным копированием.
Возможность пропустить вступительные заставки и сразу перейти в главное меню.

Оба режима раннего доступа к дополнительным возможностям отключены по умолчанию. Они не изменяют сохранения сюжетной кампании.
ПК-порт распространяется без игровых файлов: для его использования потребуется собственная легальная копия God of War: Sons of Sparta для PS4 — американское издание CUSA57767 версии 1.00 или 1.01. Установить её можно через соответствующую страницу лаунчера.
Проект доступен в виде нативных сборок для Windows x64 и Linux x86-64 (AppImage), поэтому запускать игру через Proton или Wine не требуется.

1stqiqr.title: Новый компаньон и не только в обзорном трейлере Switch 2-версии Xenoblade Chronicles 3
1stqiqr.content:
Уже через неделю  Xenoblade Chronicles 3 получит отдельную версию для консоли Switch 2. В связи с этим компания Nintendo опубликовала обзорный трейлер, посвящённый грядущим нововведениям.Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition предложит:Повышенную частоту кадров до 60 fps как в стационарном, так и в портативном режиме.Поддержку 4K-разрешения в стационарном режиме и full HD в портативном.Подтянутую графику как в геймплее, так и в катсценах.Новые озвученные фразы в диалогах.Новый игровой режим Heroes’ Vault, выполненный в стиле  Vampire Survivors. В этом режиме игрокам предстоит истреблять бесконечные волны противников, открывать новые комбинации способностей, союзников и сражаться со смертоносными боссами.Новый побочный сюжет, в котором команда Ноа и Мио объединится с таинственной спутницей по имени Шиммер. Героиня отличается сокрушительными и быстрыми атаками, а также даром предвидения, позволяющим видеть отголоски будущего.Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition выйдет 3 декабря. Тем временем не стоит забывать, что студия Monolith Soft уже работает над совершенно новой частью серии, которая носит название  Xenoblade Genesis. Её релиз планируется в течение 2027 года эксклюзивно для Nintendo Switch 2.

b4jefe.title: GTA 6 запустили на старых прошивках PS5 благодаря бэкпорту, несмотря на обязательное обновление от Sony
b4jefe.content:
Всего через шесть дней после официального релиза GTA 6 в сети появились видеоролики, на которых, предположительно, показан запуск игры на взломанной PlayStation 5 с прошивкой 11.60. Это примечательно тем, что незадолго до выхода проекта Sony выпустила обязательное обновление системного ПО до версии 14.23.
Одну из демонстраций опубликовал пользователь omxr, утверждающий, что игра работает на консоли с прошивкой 11.60. Другой пользователь, oBasim, показал запуск GTA 6 на системе с версией 13.40, однако на видео появляется сообщение об ошибке, поэтому подтвердить совместимость с этой прошивкой пока нельзя.
Параллельно сообщается об извлечении файлов коммерческой версии игры, включая расшифрованный исполняемый файл EBOOT.BIN. Контент-мейкер Soflysojoe1 также подтвердил появление соответствующих файлов, но подчеркнул, что информация нуждается в независимой проверке.
Напомним, перед выходом GTA 6 ходили слухи, что для запуска игры потребуется прошивка PS5 версии 14.22. Однако за два дня до релиза Sony выпустила обновление 14.23, в примечаниях к которому упоминались исключительно исправления безопасности. Его появление вызвало предположения о дополнительных мерах защиты игры от несанкционированного запуска.
Сейчас публичный джейлбрейк Relapse поддерживает прошивки от 7.00 до 13.60. При этом наличие взлома само по себе не гарантирует возможность запуска модифицированных игр. До недавнего времени поддержка нативных FPKG-пакетов для PS5 ограничивалась версией 11.60. По данным SceneGaming, разработчики Cryptosensei, Drakmor и EchoStretch уже работают над расширением совместимости до 13.60, но решение пока находится на стадии тестирования.
Бэкпорт представляет собой адаптацию игры, рассчитанной на более новую версию системного ПО, для запуска на предыдущих прошивках. Для этого могут потребоваться изменения исполняемого файла, системных библиотек и других компонентов операционной системы.
Если запуск GTA 6 на версии 11.60 действительно подтвердится, не исключено, что впоследствии игру удастся адаптировать и для более старых прошивок. Однако совместимость с версиями 9.00, 10.01, 13.40 и 13.60 пока не доказана. Минимальная необходимая версия системного ПО также остаётся неизвестной.
Появление расшифрованного исполняемого файла PS5 произошло всего через два дня после утечки файлов версии GTA 6 для Xbox Series, которые уже изучают энтузиасты, заинтересованные в создании нативного ПК-порта. Анализ версий для обеих консолей может помочь лучше разобраться в устройстве RAGE, управлении ресурсами и графических технологиях игры. Эти данные также потенциально пригодятся разработчикам эмуляторов PlayStation 5.

gavm03.title: From solving to 'digesting': How mathematicians can adapt to the dramatic changes AI has brought to their field
gavm03.content:
Credit: Unsplash/CC0 Public Domain

Mathematics is having an existential crisis. On Nov. 20, 2026, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic claimed that while working with the model Claude, he had solved the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the most famous problem in mathematics. This problem has stood unsolved for 167 years, and solving it could easily warrant a Fields Medal—considered equivalent to a Nobel Prize, but for mathematics.

In its current state, however, the solution is roughly 250,000 pages long, so it will take a while before human mathematicians can be satisfied that it is correct.
This proof emerged a month after OpenAI released 722 mathematics research papers that contained results generated by an internal AI model. While it has already retracted some of the papers due to mistakes, others, assuming they are correct, would also be impressive enough to earn a Fields Medal.
If AI can generate papers that would take a human mathematician years to research and write, does that mean mathematics is dead? Many headlines have been asking this question—and some school-age children may be rejoicing.
But it's not that simple. I've been a mathematician for 45 years, and my work has taught me that mathematics is not just about solving problems or proving theorems. It is about understanding why the solutions and proofs work and then extending that mathematics to new contexts.
Fueling this existential crisis is the fact that over the past century, mathematicians have come to attach greater prestige to the solution and the proof than the understanding. Now that an AI can come up with a solution and a proof, the underlying understanding could vanish. Mathematicians are being forced to rethink what they value.

Why should nonmathematicians care?
If you're not a mathematician, this crisis might seem inconsequential. But math isn't all abstract problems. It's used to design and optimize technology that's essential to modern society.
One example is MRI, or magnetic resonance imaging. MRI is a very useful tool in medical diagnosis. X-rays see only your bones, but MRI machines allow a physician to see the soft tissue inside a person in a noninvasive manner.
MRI scans used to require a patient to lie still inside a metal tube for up to half an hour or more while a loud machine made images by scanning back and forth. At the end, it combined the images. This process was difficult for many adults and virtually impossible for children without sedation.
Modern MRI machines require many fewer scans in a shorter period, and they get better resolution. Now, more patients find the procedure no big deal. The key to this vast improvement was the mathematics of compressed sensing, a relatively recent invention.
Compressed sensing allows the machine to construct an image from fewer scans. At first, doing so didn't seem possible. But in the mid-2000s, a mathematician, statisticians and an electrical engineer figured out how to use the fact that many of the scans are very similar to develop the mathematics that made compressed sensing possible.
They showed that images can be reconstructed from far fewer samples than previously thought necessary. This solution required a deep understanding of many different areas of mathematics, and even the development of new mathematics. Moreover, it involved asking the right questions—something I believe current AI models would not have known how to do.
Today's iterations of AI may have been able to speed up the invention of compressed sensing, with humans in the loop. But coming up with the mathematics behind compressed sensing most likely would have been beyond the current capabilities of AI by itself.

'Digesting' the math
AI-led research still requires the involvement of human mathematicians. But mathematicians are now asking each other what they have to change about their approach and the field's norms. Many problems that would have been given to Ph.D. students to solve for their dissertations can now be done by AI.
But most of OpenAI's 722 mathematics research papers are not understandable to a human mathematician, and this is certainly the case for the claimed proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis. Even the outputs from these papers that have gone through the proof-checking software Lean, which can verify a proof, are often incomprehensible to a human. AI's current mathematical writing ability is quite primitive.
In other words, the mathematics will be known to be true by the mathematicians, but they won't have a clue in most cases as to why it is true. And if there is no understanding as to why, then the mathematics loses its value. If you don't know why it works, then you can't apply the math.
As Terrence Tao, the mathematician who solved the MRI problem, has said, mathematicians will now have to place value on the digestion of the proofs. By digestion he means absorbing, simplifying and contextualizing the proof.
Once the proofs are digested, researchers gain understanding, and then the ability to apply the results in new realms. Many mathematicians are now arguing that Ph.D. programs should change their emphasis from solving a problem to solving, digesting and then showing understanding by explaining the solution to other mathematicians and colleagues in other scientific fields.

Looking ahead
Mathematicians will also have to change how they teach their classes. AI can now easily solve any standard math homework problem. To get around this, instructors might try to design their classes around understanding, rather than reaching solutions. They might accomplish this shift using oral exams or class presentations.
Many mathematicians—me included—view this shift in the field as an opportunity to emphasize understanding. The invention of the calculator freed students from computation. AI may do the same at another level.
AI is not just changing mathematics. It will affect other disciplines, too. It is already speeding up the development of new materials and chemicals. In these fields, human scientists will still want to verify that the model yields what they desire.
Four years ago, ChatGPT was incapable of basic arithmetic. These models have progressed very quickly, so it's hard to say where mathematics will be in the future. But regardless, learning math teaches students important problem-solving and critical-thinking skills that AI cannot, at least at this point in time, entirely replace.

ont2dh.title: Colman Domingo Responds to Critic Calling ‘Michael’ Performance Mid
ont2dh.content:
Colman Domingo is firing back at a critic of “Michael” and his performance as Joe Jackson, which some members of the film press forecast will earn him major nominations this awards season.

“Hot take: Awards prognosticators adding Colman Domingo for Michael, you really don’t need to add a mid performance/bad movie. You really don’t,” posted a user to X on Wednesday. Domingo kept his response short, replying simply: “Who hurt you?”

In the musical biopic, released back in April, Domingo plays the domineering father of pop superstar Michael Jackson. His turn as the patriarch of the Jackson family earned him praise from critics when the film first hit theaters, so much so that several awards prognosticators, as the X user wrote, are predicting Oscar and Golden Globe nominations for the actor.

Ahead of the film’s premiere, the “Euphoria” actor told The Wall Street Journal that he focused on finding the father’s “humanity” in order to play him. “He created some of the most iconic artists that have ever walked this earth,” he added. “What goes into the making of that man?” Of the alleged abusiveness of the father, Domingo said: “I will say that he chastised his children. It’s always going to be arguable what’s right and a great method.”

Because of the allegations surrounding Michael Jackson’s alleged sexual abuse of children (which the executors of the Jackson estate, who produced the film, have maintained are false), the film was controversial even before it hit theaters. Speaking about the film with Variety in Nov. 2024, Domingo said that “anything surrounding those ideas about him never came into play with me… It’s about the character, more than anything. And the idea of working with the estate, Antoine Fuqua and Jaafar Jackson — who is exceptional.”

Alongside Domingo, the film stars Jackson’s nephew Jafaar Jackson as the titular pop star, Nia Long as his mother Katherine, Miles Teller as lawyer John Branca, Laura Harrier as Suzanne de Passe, Jamal R. Henderson as Jermaine Jackson, Tre Horton as Marlon Jackson, Rhyan Hill as Tito Jackson, Joseph David-Jones as Jackie Jackson and Jessica Sula as La Toya Jackson.

While the film holds the record for the highest-grossing biopic ever made, Variety exclusively reported that it was not submitted for the 2027 EE BAFTA Film Awards.

1ndt1l2.title: 'Four Seasons in Java' Review: Gorgeous Indonesian Oscar Submission
1ndt1l2.content:
A gloriously executed slow burn of a suspense thriller, mixed with magical realism and other genre tropes, “Four Seasons In Java” connects the themes and concerns of Indonesian writer-director Kamila Andini’s previous films in an exhilarating and emotionally moving way. It follows a formerly incarcerated, sexually abused woman who returns to her remote Javanese village after 20 years and finds the men behind her ordeal still in charge. Issues of female power, self-determination and challenges to the patriarchy connect with questions about trauma, memory and what it takes to reclaim home and identity. After 2021’s TIFF Platform Prize winner “Yuni,” “Java” marks the second of Andini’s films to be selected as Indonesia’s international feature Oscar submission.

When Pertiwi (a magnificent Putri Marino in the present; Shofia Shireen in flashbacks) returns to her parents’ rural home in the shadow of majestic Mount Bromo, she is far from the shy, obedient 16-year-old schoolgirl her mother remembers. No longer afraid or ashamed, she is a fighter, determined to stand up for herself and others.

In contrast, the dynamic at Pertiwi’s parents’ home has not changed: Her weak-willed, alcoholic father (Iswadi Pratama) still racks up gambling debts and her mother continues to make excuses for him. Unwelcome in the village, Pertiwi sets about assembling an alternative family from fellow outcasts and brings them to live with her in an abandoned building outside the village limits. Together with former sex worker and café operator Mak Ira (iconic Indonesian actress Christine Hakim, chewing the scenery a bit here) and village madman/high school friend Kuntet (Dwika Pradnyana), who shares her interest in electrical engineering, Pertiwi develops a catering business, patronized by her one-time boyfriend Bisma (Arya Saloka), and also works on solar generators.

It takes some time for Pertiwi to tell her loved ones about what happened to her (spoiler alert/trigger warning: she was raped), but Andini powerfully uses all the elements of cinema to indicate her severe trauma. Certain people — in particular, village headman/former teacher Fajar (Totos Rasiti) — and places trigger Pertiwi’s memories, which first return as quick, jagged images crackling with horror-movie energy and later as entire devastating scenes that she seems to be able to watch as if they were a vintage TV show. At other times, she feels as if she is being followed by a heavy-breathing monster with sharp claws that only she can see.

When Pertiwi witnesses some young village men sexually abusing deaf schoolgirl Raras (Hanna Aretha O. Ginting), she literally cracks heads and determines to shine a light on the village’s dark doings. Her activism makes her return even more of a threat to Faraj and his patron Sapto (Doni Kus Indarto), the village’s richest man, who aims to keep his clan in power in whatever unscrupulous way he can.

Andini creates many striking visual metaphors. She juxtaposes the majestic nature surrounding the village and the succor that Pertiwi draws from it (her name means Mother Nature) with the evil deeds of Sapto’s family, the village headman and the corrupt police, that take place in dimly lit interiors and darkened spaces. She also contrasts the technology and light that Pertiwi and Kuntet create with their solar energy with the run-down electric plant, long exploited by Sapto and his henchmen, and the wounds it renders in nature. The light metaphor is also cleverly extended into a deus ex machina reveal as well as a magical realist ending.

Although certain scenes many have the look of a Western, as when Pertiwi and Bismas ride through fields, flats and forests, Andini also grounds the film in Javanese culture and tradition. The second of two scenes of traditional dancing and gamelan playing led by a shaman’s family, who are also treated as outcasts by the village officials, evokes a powerful magic that becomes a form of resistance. The striking, mood-setting, percussive score by Ricky Lionardi and Bottlesmoker deserves a shout out amongst the rest of the remarkable tech package.

The chief criticism is that the film is so packed with characters and incident that some story arcs and characters seem neglected and not as well integrated into the overall narrative. This is particularly the case with Pertiwi’s reunion with her fellow ex-prisoners and a striking scene at a Jakarta club where Pertiwi reads a poem accompanied by howling punk band. This critic would welcome a mini-series about Pertiwi and her mates in Jakarta.

1jzxulq.title: Judge Blocks FCC Move on ABC License Renewals
1jzxulq.content:
A judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from seeking early license renewals from ABC stations, finding that the network has faced a “campaign of retaliation” for its protected speech.

The FCC ordered Disney-owned ABC in April to file renewal applications for its eight owned stations, including WABC-TV New York, KABC-TV Los Angeles and WLS-TV Chicago. The FCC’s action came a few days after Jimmy Kimmel, the network’s late night host, joked that the First Lady had “a glow like an expectant widow,” which prompted President Trump to call for Kimmel’s firing.

In a ruling on Wednesday, Judge Loren AliKhan ruled that ABC was likely to prevail on its claim that the renewal process was forbidden by the First Amendment.

“No one doubts that the Commission may enforce the law in the manner it sees fit,” the judge wrote, “But in doing so, Defendants may not retaliate against or punish Plaintiffs and other broadcast license holders for disfavored speech.”

The judge noted that Trump has routinely called for ABC’s licenses to be revoked in response to editorial decisions. Under Brendan Carr, Trump’s appointee to chair the FCC, the agency has opened an investigation of ABC’s daytime talk show “The View” and its interviews of political candidates. Carr also threatened ABC over a Kimmel monologue on September 2025, saying “We can do this the easy way or the hard way.”

AliKhan found that ABC has engaged in self-censorship since the FCC actions began. “The View” has avoided candidate interviews, for fear of running afoul of the “equal time” rule, while Kimmel put an interview with Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico on YouTube, rather than risk airing it on broadcast.

“This is not a close case,” the judge wrote.

ABC sought an injunction blocking the early renewal process, as well as an order barring “any actions, formal or informal, to coerce or threaten Plaintiffs with sanctions in an effort to alter their exercise of editorial discretion.” The judge granted the former but denied the latter, saying the request was too vague.

The FCC also sought to force ABC to post an “appropriate bond” as a condition of maintaining the injunction. The judge ordered the company to post a bond in the amount of $1.

“Today’s decision is an important victory for the First Amendment,” an ABC News spokesperson said in a statement. “We thank the court for its careful consideration.”

An FCC spokesperson said the ruling was mistaken.

“While we appreciate the district court denying in part Disney’s request for preliminary injunctive relief, the portion of the decision granting Disney’s motion is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law — as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear,” the spokesperson said. “The FCC looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter. We will continue to use our lawful authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations.”

Anna Gomez, the lone Democrat on the commission, said that the ruling will bring “badly needed accountability.”

“This decision shows that this FCC is a paper tiger whose threats crumble when challenged by those willing to defend their rights,” she said. “Every broadcaster facing this pressure should take note and choose courage over capitulation because, as I’ve said from the beginning, the First Amendment is on their side.”

14wnjjc.title: Amanda Seyfried Admits She “Told A Lot Of People” About Her ‘You Can See Everything’ Role: “I’m The Most Indiscreet Person”
14wnjjc.content:
Although Amanda Seyfried‘s buzzy new role was a well-kept secret, discretion was maintained with no thanks to her.

The Oscar-nominated actress admitted that although she “was only involved for like a year” in You Can See Everything, she “told a lot of people” about her surprise appearance in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s critically acclaimed documentary about Elizabeth Holmes.

“I’m the most indiscreet person I’ve ever met in my life,” she said on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. “How the hell did I manage to keep it under wraps? I told a lot of people. But I guess I could trust them all.”

Seyfried added, “I mean, I did. I told a lot of people. I mean, one person tweeted something and Nathan was like, ‘What’s this?’ And I was like, ‘I don’t know.’

In You Can See Everything, disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invites Fielder into her and husband Billy Evans’ home to document everything in the month leading up to the start of her 11-year prison sentence on fraud charges.

After portraying Holmes in Hulu’s The Dropout (2022), Seyfried agreed to appear in the documentary, reprising her performance as Holmes in reenactments of moments Fielder was unable to get on camera.

With Seyfried’s appearance revealed during the doc’s surprise September premiere at Telluride, A24 has been building Oscar buzz for the actress, which would be the first time a documentary re-enactor has been nominated in an acting category.

gh-66107014.title: GitHub - fabiangreffrath/woof: Woof! is a continuation of the Boom/MBF bloodline of Doom source ports
gh-66107014.content:
This is Woof!

Woof! is a continuation of Lee Killough's Doom source port MBF targeted at modern systems.
Synopsis
MBF stands for "Marine's Best Friend" and is widely regarded as the successor of the Boom source port by TeamTNT.
It serves as the code base for popular Doom source ports such as PrBoom+/DSDA-Doom or The Eternity Engine.
As the original engine was limited to run only under MS-DOS, it has been ported to Windows by Team Eternity under the name WinMBF in 2004.
Woof! is developed based on the WinMBF code with the aim to make MBF more widely available and convenient to use on modern systems.
To achieve this goal, this source port is less strict regarding its faithfulness to the original MBF.
It is focused on quality-of-life enhancements, bug fixes and compatibility improvements.
However, all changes have been introduced in good faith that they are in line with the original author's intentions and even for the trained eye, this source port should still look very familiar to the original MBF.
In summary, this project's goal is to fast-forward MBF.EXE from DOS to 21st century and remove all the stumbling blocks on the way.
Furthermore, just as MBF was ahead of its time, this project dedicates itself to early adoption of new modding features such as DEHEXTRA+DSDHacked, UMAPINFO and MBF21.
What's with the name?
If you turn the Doom logo upside down it reads "Wood" - which would be a pretty stupid name for a source port.
"Woof" is just as stupid a name for a source port, but at least it contains a reference to dogs - and dogs are the Marine's Best Friend. 😉
Key features

Arbitrary resolutions up to native display resolution with dynamic resolution scaling (DRS) to automatically change the internal resolution to maintain a target framerate.
Widescreen rendering with proper support for widescreen assets.
Rendering with uncapped frame rate and frame interpolation.
Adjustable field of view (FOV).
Support for voxels in KVX format.
3D audio, supporting stereo and up to 7.1 surround sound with an optional HRTF mode, as well as PC speaker emulation.
Several music backends: native MIDI, FluidSynth with a bundled soundfont, built-in OPL3 emulator. Digital music and sound formats supported by libsndfile, module music supported by libxmp.
Modern gamepad support featuring rumble, gyro, flick stick, custom weapon slots, and full control of sensitivities, response curves, and deadzones.
Mouselook.
Autoload directories.
Savegame backward compatibility up to MBF.EXE.
Integration of the Chocolate Doom network code.
Compatibility levels: "Vanilla", "Boom", "MBF" and "MBF21" (default).

Capabilities

Support for additional node types, including DeePBSP and ZDoom's XNOD/ZNOD, XGLN/ZGLN, XGL2/ZGL2 & XGL3/ZGL3 extended formats.
Integration of the NanoBSP node builder (enforce with -bsp) for maps without nodes or with unsupported nodes (not demo compatible).
Tall textures and sprites in DeePsea format.
Support for UDMF maps, in the "Doom" namespace, compliant with version 1.1 of the spec.
Unlimited extra states, sprites, mobjtypes and sounds for use in Dehacked patches (supporting the "DEHEXTRA" and "DSDHacked" specs).
Ambient sounds using SNDINFO and DoomEdNums 14001 to 14064.
In-game music changing using MUSINFO and DoomEdNums 14101 to 14164.
UMAPINFO support, compliant to Rev 2.2 of the spec.
MBF21 compatibility level, compliant to Rev 1.4 of the spec.
Support for PNG graphics.
SMMU-style swirling animated flats.

Usage

Getting Started
Cheat Codes
Command Line Parameters

Releases
Source code, Windows binaries (MSVC builds for Windows 7 and newer) and Linux AppImages for the latest release can be found on the Release page.
The changes currently in progress since the latest release can be found in the Changelog.
Compiling
The Woof! source code is available at GitHub: https://github.com/fabiangreffrath/woof.
Building with vcpkg (Recommended - All Platforms)
Install vcpkg https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg?tab=readme-ov-file#get-started.
git clone https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg.git
cd vcpkg
./bootstrap-vcpkg.sh # Unix/macOS
# or
.\bootstrap-vcpkg.bat # Windows
cd ..

Clone the woof repository:
git clone https://github.com/fabiangreffrath/woof.git

Run the CMake configuration:
cd woof
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="[path to vcpkg]/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake"

During this step, vcpkg will build all the dependencies.
Finally, build the project:
cmake --build build

After successful compilation, the executable will be available in the build/src directory.
Linux, and Windows with MSYS2
The following build system and libraries need to be installed:

CMake (>= 3.15)
SDL3 (>= 3.4.0)
SDL3_net
openal-soft (>= 1.22.0 for PC Speaker emulation)
libsndfile (>= 1.1.0 for MPEG support, optional)
yyjson (>= 0.10.0, optional)
fluidsynth (>= 2.2.0, optional)
libebur128 (optional)
libxmp (optional)
libspng (optional)
discord-rpc (optional)

Usually your distribution should have the corresponding packages in its repositories. If "development" ("dev") versions of these libraries are available, make sure to install them.
Once installed, clone the woof repository, run the CMake configuration and build the project:
git clone https://github.com/fabiangreffrath/woof.git
cd woof
cmake -B build
cmake --build build

After successful compilation, the executable will be available in the build/src directory.
Contact
The canonical homepage for Woof! is https://github.com/fabiangreffrath/woof.
Woof! is maintained by Fabian Greffrath.
Please report any bugs, glitches or crashes that you encounter to the GitHub Issue Tracker.
Acknowledgement
MBF has always been a special Doom source port for me, as it taught me how to implement 640x400 resolution rendering which was the base for my own source port project Crispy Doom.
As the original MBF was limited to run only under MS-DOS, I used its pure port WinMBF by Team Eternity to study and debug the code.
Over time, I got increasingly frustrated that the code would only compile and run on 32-bit systems and still use the meanwhile outdated SDL-1 libraries.
This is how this project was born.
Many additions and improvements to this source port were taken from fraggle's Chocolate Doom, taking advantage of its exceptional portability, accuracy and compatibility. Further sources of inspiration are PrBoom+, DSDA-Doom and The Eternity Engine.
Special thanks to @rfomin and @ceski-1 for implementing the more advanced features of this port, and @JNechaevsky and @MrAlaux for helping to port back some useful features from their own source port projects!

15kaeye.title: FCC Bid Challenging ABC’s TV Licenses Halted in Major Win for Network
15kaeye.content:
Logo text

ABC has won a court order barring the Federal Communications Commission from taking further action against the network amid the government’s efforts to possibly strip the company of its local broadcast licenses.

U.S. District Judge Loren Alikhan on Wednesday rebuffed the FCC‘s bid to dismiss the lawsuit, finding that the agency likely violated ABC’s First Amendment rights by weaponizing its regulatory authority to retaliate against the network for protected speech and pressure it to change its editorial decisions.

“Today’s decision is an important victory for the First Amendment. We thank the court for its careful consideration,” an ABC News spokesperson said in a statement.

The Disney-owned company sued the FCC earlier this year after the Brendan Carr-led agency called for an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses. The renewal prompted concerns of retaliation since it followed an investigation into Disney’s diversity practices and ABC late-night host Kimmy Kimmel angering President Donald Trump with a joke.

In Wednesday’s ruling, the court said that Carr’s conduct is “powerful evidence” of the FCC’s “retaliatory motive.”

“It is no coincidence that President Trump criticized Mr. Kimmel’s skit on social media and the very next day Defendants initiated the early license renewal proceedings,” Alikhan wrote. She pointed to Carr’s comment that “we can do this the easy way or the hard way” and that “these companies can find ways to take action on Kimmel, or there is going to be additional work for the FCC ahead.”

The FCC has maintained that the early license renewal proceedings are merely “in aid” of its investigation into Disney’s employment practices and would’ve occurred regardless.

The court was unconvinced, finding that it “does not find that explanation to be credible.” It stressed that Trump has targeted ABC for several years.

The FCC has also launched a separate inquiry into The View, which it argued is not a “bona fide” news program and therefore is not exempt from FCC equal opportunity rules. This came after an appearance by James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for the Texas Senate, in February. ABC said in an earlier filing that the FCC “now appears poised to find that The View must provide equal opportunities to all legally qualified political candidates if it interviews one candidate on the show, which would represent a reversal of decades of agency precedent.”

Nov. 25, 5:59 p.m. Updated to include statement from an ABC News spokesperson.

1nfompl.content:
Команда Fire & Frost отметила первую годовщину  Of Ash and Steel релизом глобального обновления 2.0, которое вводит целый ряд улучшений и ворох дополнительного контента.В состав свежего апдейта вошли:Новый хардкорный режим сложности «Пепел и Сталь», предназначенный для самых опытных игроков. В этом режиме враги стали заметно сильнее, торговцы жаднее, а голод и жажда смертельнее. Сохраняться можно только в безопасных местах, а уровень здоровья больше не растёт при прокачке. Тем не менее в режиме «Пепел и Сталь» герой получает больше опыта, что значительно ускоряет прогресс.«Железный режим», доступный на любом уровне сложности. По классике в этом режиме игрокам доступно только одно сохранение, которое удаляется при первой же гибели протагониста.

Улучшенное глобальное освещение с устранением раздражающего «шума».Улучшенный липсинк в диалогах с доработанными анимациями лиц.Улучшенная система толпы с полноценными NPC, которые реагируют на действия игроков.Значительные визуальные улучшения города.Переработанная система коротких диалогов между NPC с повышенным разнообразием фраз.Различные улучшения боевой системы:Переработанное парирование с новыми анимациями и более понятной индикацией.Переработанная шкала ошеломления противников, которая теперь видна на экране. При заполнении шкалы можно провести особенно мощный удар.Обновлённый ИИ противников. Теперь враги ведут себя агрессивнее, уворачиваются от стрел, чаще атакуют с расстояния и реже застревают в геометрии.

Глобальная переработка экономики, дабы деньги и лут оставались ценными на протяжении всего прохождения. К примеру, снижено количество золота на локациях, а на уровнях сложности выше сюжетной продажа добычи теперь приносит меньше денег.Совершенно новая система репутации, которая зависит от действий протагониста на протяжении игры. Репутация влияет в том числе на цены у торговцев. При этом скупщики краденого будут лучше доверять герою с низкой репутацией.Переработка взлома. Теперь сложность замка зависит от ценности добычи. Кроме того, за взлом и кражу вещей теперь также начисляется опыт.Полноценный питомец по имени Мун-Мун. Это ручной клыкарь, которого можно найти после постройки собственного дома. Мун-Мун не только лишь помогает в бою, но также собирает травы на локации и подсвечивает контейнеры с добычей. Для его прокачки потребуются те же очки, что и для протагониста.

Восемь новых уникальных боссов, разбросанных по всему острову. За победу над ними игроки получат особые артефакты первопроходцев. В их числе — курительная трубка, которая позволяет проматывать время на манер сигары из  Metal Gear Solid V.Всевозможные исправления багов и ребаланс.Of Ash and Steel пока доступна только на ПК (Steam). В настоящее время разработчики трудятся над консольными версиями для PlayStation 5 и Xbox Series, а также готовят полномасштабное дополнение  Shattered Faith.

cq0u39.title: Judge Sides With ABC In First Amendment Lawsuit Against FCC; Puts Halt To Agency’s Early License Renewal Proceeding
cq0u39.content:
A federal judge has largely sided with ABC in its First Amendment lawsuit claiming that an FCC order to review its broadcast licenses was a retaliatory act by the Trump administration designed to chill its content, whether that be news coverage or jokes from Jimmy Kimmel.

U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan issued a preliminary injunction on Wednesday that prohibits the FCC from taking any further action in its license review, concluding that the network was “likely to succeed in their retaliation claim.

“This is not a close case,” she wrote in concluding that the network had shown that the public interest favors court intervention in agency action.

“No one doubts that the Commission may enforce the law in the manner it sees fit,” AliKhan wrote. “But in doing so, Defendants may not retaliate against or punish Plaintiffs and other broadcast license holders for disfavored speech.”

She also rejected the FCC’s effort to dismiss the lawsuit on jurisdictional grounds.

“Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face – loss of their broadcast licenses – the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness,” the judge wrote.

Read the judge’s decision in the ABC case against the FCC.

In highlighting the urgency of court action, AliKhan cited moves that the network has already taken out of fear of losing their licenses. They include the choice to place James Talarico’s guest appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live on YouTube, outside of the FCC’s authority, as well as ABC’s decision to livestream Trump’s July primetime speech out of fear concern of administration retaliation.

“These alterations to Plaintiffs’ editorial decision making showcase how the Commission’s early license renewal proceedings have already curtailed Plaintiffs’ protected activity,” the judge wrote. “That an objectively reasonable broadcaster faced with the same existential threat would follow suit is beyond debate.”

The network is the first major media conglomerate to challenge the FCC’s wave of investigations since the start of Donald Trump‘s second term.

ABC filed suit against the FCC in August, claiming that the agency was violating the First Amendment as it ordered the network’s broadcast stations to submit their licenses to an early review.

The network noted that the agency’s action was unprecedented, creating a chill to its speech and that of other broadcasters given the risk to losing licenses for their eight owned stations. The first of the licenses was not set to expire until 2028.

In claiming regulatory retaliation, the network cited Trump’s attacks on Kimmel and its news coverage, as well as warnings from the president’s FCC Chairman Brendan Carr.

The judge referenced Trump’s attacks and warnings in her opinion and noted that three of the co-hosts of The View, as well as Kimmel and ABC News reporters have entrires of the White House’s “media offenders” webpage. She said that Trump and Carr’s “call and response” was “no coincidence.”

She also noted the timing of the FCC’s order for ABC stations to submit to the license review, coming a day after Trump posted on Truth Social that Kimmel should be fired for a skit the previous week.

The FCC has argued that the early license renewal was tied to its inability to obtain documents from the network as part of an investigation of its diversity, equity and inclusion practices. But toward the end of a two-hour hearing last month, the judge asked the agency whether there were other, less drastic alternatives it could have chosen rather than the license review. And in her decision, AliKhan wrote that she did not find the agency’s explanation to be credible.

She wrote, “What is more, Chairman Carr has taken President Trump’s rhetoric as his marching orders. The same week he was tapped to be President Trump’s FCC chair, following months of President Trump’s calling for ‘ABC [to] lose its license’ for how it covered the presidential campaign …. then-Commissioner Carr lauded ‘license revocation’ as a ‘remedy’ to ‘deter this kind of conduct.'”

During the hearing, Beth Wilkinson, representing the network, compared ABC’s situation to the French Revolution, with people forced on a guillotine, wondering if anything will come down. Losing broadcast licenses, she said, is akin to a “death penalty” for stations.

The FCC argued that the network had to wait until the review process played out before challenging it, and that the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals, not the district court, is the venue to hear such a case.

But AliKhan concluded that ABC’s First Amendment retaliation claim fell outside the kind of statutory review set up in the Communications Act, directing challenges to the federal appellate court and likely adding months of delay.

The judge wrote, “To be sure, Plaintiffs would face even greater injury if the FCC ultimately denied their renewal applications. But that does not mean that they are not currently being injured by allegedly being singled out for differential treatment—that is, from facing early license renewal proceedings years in advance of the standard expiration dates as a cudgel to stamp out unfavorable content about President Trump.”

Carr has initiated investigations and reviews of all of the major broadcast networks. Among other things, he launched a probe of The View earlier this year and whether it had to comply with the agency’s Equal Time Rule.

The judge’s decision was limited to the license renewal proceeding. She also denied ABC’s request for a broader injunction that would prohibit any FCC actions “to coerce or threaten” ABC with sanctions as a way to influence their content. AliKhan wrote that such an injunction could not be issued to something “merely feared.”

An ABC News spokesperson said, “Today’s decision is an important victory for the First Amendment. We thank the court for its careful consideration.”

A spokesperson for the FCC said in a statement, “While we appreciate the district court denying in part Disney’s request for preliminary injunctive relief, the portion of the decision granting Disney’s motion is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law—as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear. The FCC looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter. We will continue to use our lawful authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations.”

Anna Gomez, the sole Democrat on the FCC, said in a statement, “For nearly two years, the agency has weaponized its licensing authority to retaliate against broadcasters for exercising their right to free expression, and now a federal court has stepped in to put a check on that conduct. That brings badly needed accountability to a Commission and an administration that have politicized the machinery of government in a sustained campaign of censorship and control.”

The case had been closely watched by First Amendment advocates and journalism groups.

Bruce Brown, the president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, called the decision “a big win not only for ABC, but for all broadcasters.”

He said, “As the court recognized, this is ‘not a close case.’ But it is also a novel case forced on ABC because of the administration’s punitive actions and therefore all the more important that the federal judiciary stepped in to vindicate First Amendment rights.

gh-1414429590.title: GitHub - AdrianPol-projects/NotBlood-Chosen: NotBlood (Blood source port) with bots, new match types, co-op saves, online lobbies and a live dashboard - Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iPad
gh-1414429590.content:
NotBlood (a Blood source port) with bots, new match types, co-op saves, internet play without port forwarding, a live game dashboard, a MODS menu and a LAN game finder, for Windows, Linux (PC and ARM), macOS, Android and iPad. Every player in a network game needs the same version; all platforms of one version play together.
Downloads

Windows, Linux, macOS, Android: NotBlood-Chosen releases
iPad (unsigned IPA for sideloading): NotBlood-iOS releases
Older version: 1.3 (1.3 and 1.4 can't play together)
Public server and live games: https://blood.pi-mole.com, map editor: https://blood.pi-mole.com/mapmaker
Web browsers (iPad, phones, computers, no install): every NotBlood server serves it at /play/ (how it works)

Unzip, copy your Blood files (One Unit Whole Blood: CD, GOG or Steam) next to the game and start it. The README in each download explains the rest.
What's new compared to NotBlood (version 1.4, release notes)

Bots that play like people (hide, ambush, flank, take the high ground, ride lifts), 4 difficulties, 6 personalities, fine tuning for all bots and for each one. Offline (PLAY WITH BOTS, CAREER, WATCH BOTS) and in LAN and online games, where the host's PC plays them. Details: BOTS.md.
Match types: gun game, king of the hill, juggernaut (twice as big and red), last man standing, hide and seek; teams: team bloodbath, capture the flag, king of the hill, last team standing; co-op survival, with a WAVES setting from very easy (smaller waves, longer breaks, more ammo, health every wave) to hard. SET TEAMS for any mix of players and bots, mutators (gravity, vampire, one-hit kills, weapon sets, tiny or big players, TNT barrels everywhere, akimbo everything), match rules (rounds, a vote for the next map, only the host starts games) and match stats.
Co-op saves, 8 slots, saved on every player's machine. Load where you saved (positions, keys, enemies) or restart the level with your gear. Players get their saves by name, new players start with the pitchfork, missing players leave the level. The game saves itself when a player leaves.
Online lobbies through your own relay server (how to set it up: SERVER.md): host or find lobbies, protected by a server key, no port forwarding.
Live dashboard in the browser: lobbies, players' health, armor, weapons, keys, a live level map, an event list, big-screen mode, and you choose what it shows.
Blood Map Maker: a map editor for phones and browsers (tools/mapeditor): rooms, heights, sky, starts, weapons and items, saved as a .MAP the game loads.
MODS menu: add-on episodes (addons/, e.g. Cryptic Passage) and mods (mods/ folders, .zip, .grp, .pk3). A mod that breaks the start is switched off again.
FIND LAN GAMES, your address on the host screen, clear messages when versions or mods differ.
Cutscenes from the CD's movie folder in any upper/lower case.
Touch devices: on-screen controls, gyro aiming, resolutions from 100 % down to 25 %, touch buttons hide while a controller is connected.
macOS app for Apple Silicon and Intel that needs no administrator; Android keeps everything in the NotBlood folder of the main storage.

Building: release.yml (desktop and Android), platform/Android, platform/iOS; the relay server is in server/ (SERVER.md).

As of 2026 NotBlood is no longer being maintained and will be archived

No further features or requests will be accepted
2021/Jul/03 - 2026/Nov/22

Overview
NotBlood is a fork of NBlood with gameplay options, optional mutators and multiplayer features, while retaining NBlood mod support
Downloads
Download for Windows/Linux can be found on https://github.com/clipmove/NotBlood/releases
Features

Switch to last active weapon if TNT/spray can is active when entering water
Basic room over room support for positional audio (before/after)
Autosaving support for collecting keys and start of level
BloodGDX style difficulty options for singleplayer
Set item box selection to activated item
Ability to record DOS compatible demos
Drag and drop folder mod support (demo)
Customizable palette adjustment
New singleplayer cheats
Weapon selection bar (demo)
Mirror mode
Auto crouch

Multiplayer Features

Cloak powerup hides player weapon icon
Improved spawning randomization logic
Colored player names for messages
Adjustable spawn weapon option
Adjustable spawn protection
UT99 style multi kill alerts
Uneven teams support

Mutators (Optional)

Difficulty based invulnerability timer for player damage (demo)
Raymarching collision testing for player projectiles (before/after)
Fix blood/bullet casings not being dragged with sectors (before/after)
Fixed missiles colliding with water sector edges (before/after)
Smaller hitboxes for player projectiles (before/after)
NotBlood balance mod for weapons (see README.txt for details)
Randomize mode for enemies and pickups (multiplayer supported)
Quad damage replacement for guns akimbo powerup
Respawning enemies option for singleplayer
Bullet projectiles for hitscan enemies
Fixed bullet casings clipping into walls
Lower gravity of bullet casings and gibs underwater
Allow particle sprites to traverse through room over room sectors
Increased blood splatter duration and improved floor collision accuracy
Make blood splatter/flare gun glow effect slope on sloped surfaces

Installing

Extract NotBlood to a new directory

Copy the following files from Blood (v1.21) to NotBlood folder:

BLOOD.INI
BLOOD.RFF
BLOOD000.DEM, ..., BLOOD003.DEM (optional)
CP01.MAP, ..., CP09.MAP (optional, Cryptic Passage)
CPART07.AR_ (optional, Cryptic Passage)
CPART15.AR_ (optional, Cryptic Passage)
CPBB01.MAP, ..., CPBB04.MAP (optional, Cryptic Passage)
CPSL.MAP (optional, Cryptic Passage)
CRYPTIC.INI (optional, Cryptic Passage)
CRYPTIC.SMK (optional, Cryptic Passage)
CRYPTIC.WAV (optional, Cryptic Passage)
GUI.RFF
SOUNDS.RFF
SURFACE.DAT
TILES000.ART, ..., TILES017.ART
VOXEL.DAT

Optionally, if you want to use CD audio tracks instead of MIDI, provide FLAC/OGG recordings in following format: bloodXX.flac/ogg, where XX is track number. Make sure to enable Redbook audio option in sound menu.

Optionally, if you want cutscenes and you have the original CD, copy the movie folder into NotBlood's folder (the folder itself too).
If you have the GOG version of the game, do the following:

make a copy of game.ins (or game.inst) named game.cue
mount the .cue as a virtual CD (for example with WinCDEmu)
copy the movie folder from the mounted CD into NotBlood's folder

Launch NotBlood (on Linux, to play Cryptic Passage, launch with the -ini CRYPTIC.INI parameter)

Building from source
See: https://wiki.eduke32.com/wiki/Main_Page

See AUTHORS.md
